studi.t: Distill-Mol: Learning unified molecular representations via cross-modal fusion and hierarchical geometric distillation
studi.s: Molecular representation learning aims to link molecular structures to downstream tasks in drug discovery and materials design. Molecules contain multi-level information, including semantic, topological, and geometric features. However, existing methods often rely on single-modality representations or shallow fusion strategies, limiting their ability to capture complex structure-property relationships.

studi.t: Cognitive functions relate to the decision-dependent component of football skill in youth academy players
studi.s: Talent identification in football relies increasingly on objective tests. However, these tests capture physical performance better than decision-making, that is, perceiving a game situation and choosing an action. It also remains unclear whether general cognitive functions relate to decision-making on the pitch, partly because studies usually judge skill by playing level or coach ratings, which do not separate decision-making from athletic ability.

studi.t: Chewing-related changes in ankle muscle activity and spectral power are modulated by oral anesthesia during single-leg stance
studi.s: Mastication can facilitate lower-limb motor output, yet whether its influence on postural muscle control depends on oral sensory feedback is unknown. In a randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study, 27 healthy adults performed sub-maximal single-leg stance trials at baseline, after unilateral buccal lidocaine (n = 12) or placebo (n = 15) spray, and while chewing gum. Center-of-pressure sway and surface electromyography of the tibialis anterior (TA) and medial gastrocnemius (GM) were analyzed during the first 3 s of unipedal support.

studi.t: A Reproducible, Leakage-Aware Machine Learning Pipeline for Antimicrobial Peptide Activity Prediction
studi.s: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are key alternatives to conventional antibiotics, but published machine learning models may overestimate predictive performance because of positive-class sequence redundancy and data leakage. We developed a leakage-aware pipeline using 13,469 peptides from DRAMP v5.0 and UniProt, clustered at 40% sequence identity with CD-HIT to enforce cluster-level splitting.

studi.t: Bone Marrow Polyethylene Microplastics Favour Tet2-mutant Haematopoiesis and Aggravate Atherosclerosis
studi.s: We investigated whether polyethylene microplastics (PE-MPs) in bone marrow influence clonal haematopoiesis and atherosclerosis. Pyrolysis-gas chromatography/mass spectrometry detected polyethylene in bone marrow aspirates from 27 of 31 adults (87.1%). In Ldlr-/- mice competitively transplanted with wild-type and Tet2+/- marrow, intratibial PE-MPs exposure increased atherosclerotic lesion area in the aortic arch and root, the relative contribution of Tet2+/- donor cells, and the abundance of mutant-derived myeloid cells.

studi.t: Can we infer mechanisms governing PMF generation and partitioning from existing experimental data? A model-based identifiability analysis
studi.s: Photosynthesis is a well-studied and essential biochemical process on Earth. It converts light energy into chemical energy by coupling the photosynthetic electron transport chain to the Calvin-Benson-Bassham (CBB) cycle. Central to this coupling is the proton motive force (PMF) across the thylakoid membrane. It drives ATP synthesis, and its partitioning into membrane potential ({Delta}{Psi}) and proton gradient ({Delta}pH) regulates photoprotection and electron flow.

studi.t: Domain-general and domain-specific neural mechanisms underlie metacognition in social and perceptual decisions
studi.s: Metacognition, the monitoring and assessment of our own cognitive processes, plays a key role in our everyday decision-making across a multitude of domains. Despite this, the question of whether metacognition is implemented by domain-general or domain-specific neural processes has not yet been conclusively answered. Theoretical two-layer accounts propose that a shared core network of metacognition, consisting of prefrontal areas, might be functionally coupled with task-relevant brain regions in a domain-specific way. To test this empirically, the present study comprises three experiments.

studi.t: HIV-1 VPR TARGETS BCOR FOR DEGRADATION TO COUNTER POLYCOMB-DEPENDENT PROVIRAL SILENCING
studi.s: Chromatin remodeling complexes such as the Polycomb Repressive Complex (PRC) are recruited to the HIV-1 promoter during latency. Using BioID, we previously identified multiple PRC subunits as potential HIV-1 Vpr-interacting partners. Here, we show that HIV-1 Vpr, but not its paralog Vpx encoded by SIVsmm/HIV-2, targets the non-canonical PRC1.1 core component, BCL6 co-repressor (BCOR), for proteasomal degradation.

studi.t: Defining and Characterizing the Accessory Genome of the Virulent Vibriophage ICP1
studi.s: Bacteriophages (phages) must evade host defense systems and redirect cellular resources to support viral replication. The virulent phage ICP1 is a persistent predator of Vibrio cholerae in both human hosts and aquatic environments, yet the genetic factors underlying its infection cycle remain incompletely defined. Here, we developed a transposon mutagenesis platform for ICP1 and applied transposon sequencing (Tn-seq) to identify genes required for infection across host strains and environmental conditions.

studi.t: The fate of social dilemmas under randomly fluctuating growth rates
studi.s: We study three social dilemmas Prisoner's Dilemma, Hawk-Dove and Coordination games between two phenotypes whose intrinsic growth rates switch randomly with the environment, modeled as dichotomous noise. We derive the exact stationary distributions of the population composition and the fixation probabilities. The persistence of each phenotype is set by its invasion rate, which depend only on the time-averaged environment, hence, zero-mean fluctuations do not alter the invasion abilities.

studi.t: THREAD: a Bayesian nonparametric framework for resolving polygenic risk into multicellular programs
studi.s: Genome-wide association studies have linked thousands of loci to complex disease, yet translating these associations into the cellular mechanisms that generate risk remains difficult. Existing methods relate genetic risk to individual cell types or, at single-cell resolution, to individual cells, yet how that risk is organized across coordinated cellular programs remains less explored.

studi.t: High connectivity of an iconic seabird species may buffer genetic consequences of population declines
studi.s: In an era of biodiversity decline, molecular techniques are increasingly used to inform conservation strategies, including delineating management units, evaluating erosion of genetic diversity, and tracing the origin of individuals. These approaches, however, rely on the ability to distinguish between populations, yet many seabird species show weak genetic structure across large ranges.

studi.t: A Mediator subunit regulates genome stability via direct and indirect transcriptional targets in Candida albicans
studi.s: Gene families often arise for effector proteins that serve critical functions in organismal survival and fitness. Paralogs encoding the MED2 subunit of the transcriptional regulatory complex Mediator, designated the telomere-associated (TLO) gene family, form the largest lineage-specific gene family expansion in the fungal commensal and opportunistic pathogen Candida albicans. Mediator controls global gene expression through site-specific contact with transcription factors in the Tail domain where Tlo resides. The C.

studi.t: Alternative reproductive morphs and sexes differ in DNA methylation along distinct genomic axes in Poecilia parae
studi.s: Biological diversity occurs not only between species and sexes, but also within the sexes. Differences between males and females (intersexual differences) are well known to correspond to distinct DNA methylation differences, suggesting that differences between alternative phenotypes of the same sex (intrasexual differences) may also correspond to such methylation differences. Here, we used the fish Poecilia parae, in which males occur as discrete Y-linked morphs, to ask whether heritable diversity within the sexes corresponds to alternative DNA methylomes.

studi.t: Deconvoluting Latent Erythroid-Mitochondrial Transcriptomic Gradients and Technical Sample Structure in Severe Preeclampsia: A Stratified Sensitivity Framework for Public Placental RNA-Seq Datasets
studi.s: BackgroundBulk placental transcriptomic profiling has been widely deployed to elucidate the molecular pathogenesis of severe preeclampsia (sPE) and to nominate clinical biomarkers across diverse maternal populations. However, human placental tissue exhibits profound cellular heterogeneity and vascular perfusion variability.

studi.t: First in, first folded: evolution of vectorial substrate folding by metazoan Hsp60/10
studi.s: Group-I chaperonins such as GroEL/GroES fold proteins by encapsulating a complete non-native chain within a central chamber. This limits its substrates to proteins that can be accommodated within the cavity. Whether human mitochondrial Hsp60/10, a descendant of bacterial GroEL/ES, serving a larger proteome, retains the size constraint or bypasses it has remained unknown. Here, we show that human Hsp60/10 assists the folding of large multidomain proteins without the size-dependent decline in folding efficiency as observed with bacterial GroEL/ES.

studi.t: Microstructural Analysis of Language Pathways Development in Term Neonates
studi.s: Understanding the early development of language pathways is essential for elucidating how neonatal brain organization supports the acquisition of linguistic skills. In this study, we investigated microstructural changes in term human neonates scanned at postmenstrual ages (PMA) of 37 to 44 weeks. Using diffusion MRI data from 310 healthy infants in the developing Human Connectome Project, we employed q-space diffeomorphic reconstruction to map major language tracts involved in language processing.

studi.t: Age and Visual Contrast Affect Walking Stability on Winding Paths
studi.s: Older adults often experience loss of balance, and potentially falls, when trying to maintain lateral stability while walking. Age-related declines in vision likely exacerbate these challenges. Goal-directed walking to navigate complex environments requires that we clearly see the task-relevant features of our environment, known as visual salience. This study quantified lateral stability of 16 young (10F/6M; Age 22.8{+/-}1.95 yrs) and 16 older (12F/4M; Age 70.3{+/-}1.82 yrs) healthy adults walking on a treadmill within a Motek M-Gait virtual reality system.

studi.t: Evaluation of an Instrumented Helmet for Measurement of Orthosis-Head Interface Forces in Pediatric Craniosynostosis
studi.s: Postoperative cranial orthoses guide skull growth after endoscopy-assisted craniosynostosis surgery in infants, yet the forces they apply at the orthosis-head interface remain poorly characterized. Here, a cranial helmet with 12 soft magnetic tactile sensors is developed to measure these forces. The helmet, a computed tomography (CT)-derived replica of a patients first clinical helmet, is evaluated on patient-derived expandable head phantoms with and without a modeled craniotomy.

studi.t: DASTevolve: Evolving executable protein-design programs with large language models
studi.s: Protein engineering often requires improving one property while preserving others across multiple regions or molecular states. An aggregate score can reveal a poor design yet offer little guidance about which decision to revise. We introduce DASTevolve, which represents a design task as two linked abstract syntax trees. The functional tree specifies objectives and state relationships, and its links to the structural tree identify where edits are permitted for each objective.

studi.t: Identification of HIV-1 infected cells in single-cell multiome datasets using Kraken2
studi.s: Detecting HIV-1-infected cells in single-cell sequencing studies is challenging primarily due to low transcriptional activity, scarcity of infected cells, and high viral genetic variability. Here, we present a novel pipeline integrating multiple HIV-1 subtype B genomes with Kraken2 (K2) for k-mer-based classification, bypassing the need for exact sequence alignment. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells from five individuals were analyzed at three time points: before HIV acquisition, at the time of HIV diagnosis, and after one year on antiretroviral therapy (ART).

studi.t: Recovering Missing Regulations by Multiplex Graph Aggregation of GRN Predictions (Technical Report)
studi.s: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) capture the complex gene interactions underlying biological systems. However, existing GRN inference models face technical challenges in recovering faithful GRNs from single-cell RNA sequencing data in an unsupervised setting. GRN aggregation has been proposed to leverage the wisdom of different GRN models and improve overall performance, but aggregation methods either train on ground-truth edges, overlook the network nature of GRNs, or are computationally expensive.

studi.t: TW-GMProt: Trust-Weighted Semi-Supervised Gated Modulation Protein Language Model for Antimicrobial Peptide Activity Prediction
studi.s: Antibiotic resistance poses a major global health threat, underscoring the need for faster approaches to antimicrobial discovery. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are promising therapeutic candidates, but experimental activity screening remains costly and time-consuming. We introduce TW-GMProt, a trust-weighted semi-supervised gated modulation protein language model for quantitative AMP activity prediction. It integrates pretrained protein language model representations with convolutional neural networks through a gated modulation strategy, complemented by biophysical priors.

studi.t: A multidimensional benchmark of bulk RNA-seq simulators for task-specific evaluation of simulation fidelity
studi.s: Bulk RNA-seq simulators are widely used to develop and evaluate statistical methods, but their suitability depends on whether they preserve the properties of the data required for the intended downstream analysis. We benchmarked seven widely used simulators across five real bulk RNA-seq reference datasets using a unified framework that evaluated five complementary dimensions of simulation fidelity: marginal distribution fidelity, dependence structure, co-expression network topology, stability across repeated simulations, and differential-expression recovery.

studi.t: BioGCD: A Biology-Guided Multimodal Framework for Compound and Combination Discovery
studi.s: Phenotype-based transcriptomic screening provides a powerful approach for therapeutic discovery by capturing how compounds reshape cellular states. However, existing perturbation models lack biological constraints, limiting generalizability, mechanistic interpretability, and the ability to prioritize experimentally validated candidates.

studi.t: COMPASS: In silico reconstruction of single-cell-resolved spatial atlases via cross-omics distillation and coordinate refinement
studi.s: The spatial organization of single cells underlies tissue function, yet most spatial omics protocols capture multiple cells per spot. Recovering single-cell coordinates from spot-level data is underdetermined, and existing methods give only cell-type proportions or heuristic placements while rarely using domain structure, geometric priors, and complementary modalities. We introduce COMPASS, a constrained reconstruction framework that resolves this ambiguity by imposing three mutually reinforcing priors on cell-resolved atlas assembly.

studi.t: p53β, an alternatively spliced isoform of p53, induces tumor-suppressive cellular senescence and suppresses tumor growth in wild-type and mutant R273H TP53 glioblastoma
studi.s: Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most common and aggressive primary brain tumor, with approximately 30% of cases harboring TP53 mutations. TP53 encodes several isoforms, including p53{beta}, which is negatively regulated by the splicing factor SRSF3 and cooperates with p53 to induce tumor-suppressive cellular senescence in normal cells. However, the role of p53{beta} in glioblastoma remains unknown. Here, we showed that increasing wild-type or mutant R273H p53{beta} expression, via SRSF3 depletion or doxycycline-inducible overexpression, induced cellular senescence in GBM cells.

studi.t: Chemotherapy reprograms the breast cancer pericyte secretome from growth-promoting to pro-inflammatory
studi.s: Background: Breast cancer (BrCa) is one of the most common cancers in the United States, and metastatic disease has a 5-year survival rate around 30%. Taxanes such as docetaxel (DTX) are standard of care, but chemoresistance occurs in 30-35% of patients. The tumor microenvironment (TME) shapes both progression and therapeutic response. Pericytes regulate vascular stability and angiogenesis, resemble cancer-associated fibroblasts, and are exposed to chemotherapy in the TME. The metabolites that pericytes secrete, and how chemotherapy changes them, are largely unexplored.

studi.t: Lactylation-related genes prognostic model for triple-negative breast cancer and validation of a lactate-PFKP lactylation-glycolysis positive feedback loop that promotes malignant phenotypes
studi.s: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is an aggressive breast cancer subtype associated with unfavorable clinical outcomes and a shortage of therapeutic targets. By integrating bioinformatic analysis of GEO datasets, we identified a four-gene lactylation-related signature (PFKP, VEGFA, PLOD2, and NDRG1) that effectively stratified TNBC patients by survival risk. In both the training and independent validation cohorts, the signature showed robust prognostic utility, with high-risk patients having worse overall survival.

studi.t: Cell-free DNA from ascites is a suitable source for the identification of driver mutations and aligns well with functional chemoresistance testing in late-stage ovarian cancer patients
studi.s: AimOvarian cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related deaths among gynaecological malignancies. This is mainly caused by late diagnosis and resistance development to standard-of-care chemotherapy consisting of platinum compounds and taxanes. Most patients develop resistance to therapy in the first 2 years, leading to high rates of recurrence. In these patients, surgical therapeutic options are limited, and so is the possibility of resampling of tumour material for precision medicine purposes.

studi.t: Time-resolved single-cell analysis of liver fibrosis resolution reveals a recovery-associated hepatic stellate cell state with prominent intercellular signaling
studi.s: Background & Aims Activated hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) are central drivers of liver fibrosis, but their potential signaling roles during regression remain poorly understood. We investigated whether HSCs persisting after injury withdrawal express paracrine programs that could contribute to tissue recovery. Approach & Results We performed time-course single-cell RNA sequencing of enriched liver non-parenchymal cells during thioacetamide-induced fibrosis and after injury withdrawal in mice.

studi.t: Doubly exponential decay of the ovarian reserve and aging milestones
studi.s: Study questionIs there a simple, quantitatively accurate, and mechanistically plausible framework for understanding the decay of the ovarian reserve and aging milestones across populations of women?

studi.t: Arabinogalactans provide the molecular basis of ice nucleation by plant pollen and spores
studi.s: Biological ice nucleators are thought to influence cloud ice formation, affecting weather and climate. Plants are a major source of atmospheric aerosol, yet the identity of the ice-nucleating molecules they produce remains unclear. Droplet freezing experiments show that pollen, fern spores and moss spores carry similar soluble ice-nucleating macromolecules, indicating that such material occurs across land plants. Selective binding experiments and infrared spectroscopy identify these molecules as Type II arabinogalactans or closely related polysaccharides.

studi.t: Cell-free identification of de novo designed minibinders as building blocks for targeted protein degraders
studi.s: Targeted protein degradation is a powerful strategy for manipulating protein abundance and function, but developing protein-based degraders typically requires laborious screening and optimization of target-specific binders. Recent advances in de novo protein design offer a promising route to accelerate degrader development, although computationally designed binders often exhibit variable binding activity and require extensive experimental validation.

studi.t: Flux-centric coarse-graining of hepatocyte metabolic network captures acute-on-chronic liver failure dynamics in alcohol-associated hepatitis
studi.s: Acute-on-chronic diseases are marked by progressive deterioration bifurcated by sudden shifts in the compensatory state. Alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH) is an acute manifestation in patients with chronic alcohol-associated liver disease. Metabolic decompensation is a hallmark of AH. How the dysfunction of multiple metabolic pathways collectively lead to overall decompensation remains poorly understood. We developed a flux-centric, coarse-grained mathematical framework to represent hepatocyte metabolism as a network of metabolic modules operating under a constrained resource.

studi.t: grassp: A graph-based framework unifies subcellular proteomics across assays and studies
studi.s: Mass spectrometry-based subcellular proteomics is generating a rapidly growing collection of protein localization datasets ("maps") across diverse biological contexts. This offers unique opportunities to understand how localization shapes cellular function at scale. However, differences in experimental assays, data formats, analytical strategies, and compartment vocabularies hinder systematic comparison and integration. Here we present grassp, an open-source computational framework that represents subcellular maps as protein-neighborhood graphs.

studi.t: Genetic Influence on the Sleep EEG is Distributed Across Multiple Traits
studi.s: Sleep spindles are among the most promising neurophysiological biomarkers in sleep research: they support memory consolidation, track healthy aging, are altered in psychiatric, neurodevelopmental, and neurodegenerative disorders, and are highly trait-like, varying between individuals while remaining stable within them across nights.

studi.t: The entorhinal elliptic frame: emergence and persistence of coherent neural representations across contexts as Mordell-Weil sections
studi.s: Entorhinal grid-cell recordings reveal toroidal population activity across environments even as spatial firing maps shift, rescale, and shear. What geometric structure couples cue-evoked phases across contexts, and how can cross-context coherence fail while local toroidal coding remains intact? Extending recent computational accounts of latent oscillatory dynamics in the medial temporal lobe, we introduce the entorhinal elliptic frame (EEF).

studi.t: Ketamine reverses chronic corticosterone-induced changes in dendritic spine morphology in hippocampal but not cortical neurons in vitro
studi.s: Chronically elevated glucocorticoids, such as corticosterone (CORT), reduce dendritic spine density in the prefrontal cortex and hippocampus, and the rapid-acting antidepressant ketamine (KET) reverses this spine loss in the prefrontal cortex. Less is known about how CORT affects spine morphology, whether these effects differ between the cortex and hippocampus, and whether KET counteracts them. Most studies used stress models or systemic CORT, making it difficult to distinguish direct and indirect effects of CORT on neurons.

studi.t: Network Correlates of Shared Experience in Musical Improvisation
studi.s: Shared experiences emerge when individuals feel attuned to one another as they coordinate their actions and mental states, constituting a fundamental part of everyday human life. Yet, the neural mechanisms underpinning these phenomena remain poorly understood. Musical improvisation provides an ecologically valid setting for studying shared experiences, as it combines creativity, joint action, and real-time adaptation.

studi.t: Microscopic Elementary Current Properties Survive Across Scales Shaping Spectral And Non-Linear Features Of Field Potentials
studi.s: The temporal fluctuations of field potentials (FPs) carry information about upstream neuronal dynamics, but their extracellular expression is shaped by the anatomo-functional properties of the receiving population. Inferring upstream dynamics from FPs requires understanding how incoming activity is transformed by the receiving population. We here explored whether elementary synaptic current waveform shape contributes to mesoscopic fluctuations or is diluted during micro-to-mesoscopic integration.

studi.t: Isoflurane Anesthesia under Hyperoxic Conditions Shapes Cortical Hemodynamics and Photothrombotic Injury Severity in Mice: A Wide-Field Optical Imaging Study
studi.s: Background/Objectives: Anesthesia can alter cortical hemodynamics and the severity of experimental brain injury. We investigated how isoflurane under hyperoxic conditions affects these. Methods: Wide-field optical imaging (WFOI) in light-scattering mode (505 and 656 nm) through a chronic cranial window was used to assess hemoglobin dynamics in awake (n = 9) and isoflurane-anesthetized (n = 7) mice with intact cortices.

studi.t: Canine Leishmania infection in communities with notified human visceral leishmaniasis cases in Albania
studi.s: Visceral leishmaniasis (VL) is an important zoonosis in Albania, where dogs are the main reservoir of Leishmania infantum. This retrospective study describes Leishmania infection in dogs sampled in 2015 in communities where human VL cases had been notified. After 16 human cases were notified in the first half of 2015, household and neighbouring dogs were sampled in June and July 2015 in 19 locations across 11 districts.

studi.t: Systems Immunology in Obesity: Uncovering Hub Gene Networks in Macrophage-Specific Drivers of Chronic Inflammation
studi.s: Obesity is marked by chronic low-grade inflammation, with macrophages in adipose tissue acting as key mediators of immune dysfunction. Macrophages play a crucial role in this process, undergoing significant gene expression changes. Understanding the molecular mechanisms driving these changes is critical for developing effective therapeutic strategies, yet the transcriptional regulators driving this immunometabolic reprogramming remain poorly understood.

studi.t: Beyond antigen delivery: tailoring the Coated Bacterial Vaccine platform with a Lentilactobacillus kefiri S-layer protein to modulate vaccine-induced immunity
studi.s: Coated Bacterial Vaccines (CBVs) are a versatile antigen display platform based on chemically inactivated Bacillus subtilis. We previously showed that CBVs induce protective immune responses with a predominant Th2 profile and are effective with both strongly and weakly immunogenic antigens. Here, we explored whether the S-layer protein SLP 83111 from Lentilactobacillus kefiri can be co-immobilized on CBVs to modulate this response. Native SLP 83111 was co-immobilized with the C-terminal fragment of tetanus toxin (TTFC-dSLPA) on inactivated B.

studi.t: Spatial Confinement Promotes Hyphal Morphogenesis and Growth Advantage in Candida albicans
studi.s: Candida albicans is an opportunistic human pathogen that can colonize multiple organs. During the commensal-to-pathogen transition, it often faces mechanical challenges and natural spatial confinement. Using molded agarose structures mimicking the geometry of an intestinal crypt and microfluidic confining devices, we demonstrate that spatial confinement induces a robust yeast-to-hyphal transition. Tip growth persists even after mechanical stress is removed. Furthermore, the hyphal form of C.

studi.t: Choanoflagellates discriminate among Pseudomonas aeruginosa alkylquinolones during pathogen response
studi.s: Choanoflagellates are emerging models for studying host-pathogen interactions, and as the closest living relatives of animals, offer a window into the evolution of immune defense against bacteria. However, investigating mechanisms of pathogen recognition and response in choanoflagellates remains challenging in the absence of defined bacterial effectors. By studying the interaction between the pathogen Pseudomonas aeruginosa and the choanoflagellate Monosiga brevicollis, we identify alkylquinolone HNQ (2-nonyl-4-quinolone) as a potent effector that reduces host viability.

studi.t: Dietary fibre hierarchical structure determines gut microbiota responses to apple (poly)phenols through metabolite-associated microbial guilds
studi.s: Dietary fibres frequently coexist in the colon with vacuole-derived (poly)phenolic compounds following consumption of whole and minimally processed plant foods or combinations of dietary sources. However, whether (poly)phenols can direct microbial community composition and metabolic outputs during fibre fermentation, and whether such effects depend on fibre composition and physical assembly, remains unknown, possibly explaining inconsistent (poly)phenol clinical outcomes.

studi.t: TNF inhibition reveals a reversible component of age-associated sinoatrial node dysfunction
studi.s: Background and Aims: Age-related sinoatrial node (SAN) dysfunction is a principal indication for permanent pacing, yet its mechanisms remain poorly defined, and no disease-modifying therapy exists. This study investigated whether age-related reorganisation of the local immune microenvironment suppresses the SAN pacemaker gene programme and investigated the functional and therapeutic relevance of implicated inflammatory signalling mediators. Methods: Young and aged human SANs were profiled by spatial transcriptomics, integrated with physiological, molecular and immune phenotyping of aged mice.

studi.t: Conserved control of cell differentiation across divergent brown algal body plans revealed by diploid genome editing
studi.s: Brown algae evolved complex multicellularity independently of animals, plants and fungi, yet whether developmental mechanisms are conserved across their deeply divergent and morphologically diverse lineages remains poorly understood. In the filamentous brown alga Ectocarpus, the evolutionarily conserved protein DISTAG (DIS) is required for basal cell identity, but its function in more complex body plans is unknown. Here, we investigate the role of DISTAG in Dictyota, a distantly related brown alga that develops a complex parenchymatous thallus.

studi.t: Diverse ecological pressures govern microbial heterogeneity across dark ocean ecosystems
studi.s: The deep ocean regulates Earths biogeochemical cycles, yet accelerating warming, deoxygenation, and biodiversity loss threaten to fundamentally disrupt these processes. Despite microorganisms central role in global elemental cycling, deep-sea microbial communities remain poorly characterized, limiting our capacity to predict ecosystem responses to ongoing environmental perturbation.

studi.t: Recovering the Impacts of Landscape Changes through the Demographic History of a Western Ghats Endemic Bird
studi.s: Global landscapes are shaped by long-term palaeoclimatic changes and more recent, rapid anthropogenic changes. Changes in the demographic history of a species correspond to responses to changes in its natural habitat. Recent developments in genomics allow the reconstruction of recent historical effective population sizes. Yet only a limited number of studies have linked these changes to specific land-use changes in their natural habitat, especially with known trajectories of habitat change.

studi.t: PhyloRender: an interactive and agent-ready package for reproducible phylogenetic visualization
studi.s: Publication-quality phylogenetic figures are central to evolutionary biology and phylogenomics. Scientific workflows are now entering the AI agent era, where AI agents already automate many routine analytical and plotting tasks. Preparing phylogenetic figures, however, still requires heavy manual work due to three bottlenecks. First, existing tree viewers and plotting packages were not built for AI agents and lack both a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server and a domain agent skill for structured, verifiable editing.

studi.t: Drivers of intraspecies mitochondrial genome evolution revealed by deep population sequencing of a major fungal wheat pathogen
studi.s: Mitochondria play crucial roles in eukaryotic cells, serving as hubs for energy conversion. Despite functional conservation, mitochondrial genomes exhibit astonishing rates of expansion and rearrangement. Genome expansions correlate with the proliferation of selfish elements. However, how such variation arises in its earliest stages within species remains largely unknown. Here, we address this by establishing the largest intra-species survey of mitochondrial genomes focused on the major wheat pathogen Zymoseptoria tritici.

studi.t: Unifying Gene Regulatory Network Inference and Sequence-to-Expression Modeling via Bilinear Sparse Regression for De Novo TF-DNA Interaction Discovery
studi.s: Inferring transcription factor (TF)-DNA interactions from transcriptomic data is key to deciphering the genomic regulatory code. Existing computational approaches generally focus either on identifying trans-regulatory dynamics via gene regulatory network (GRN) inference or cis-regulatory sequence logic via sequence-to-expression (S2E) modeling.

studi.t: Inhibition of the oxytocin system prevents partner preference formation in females of the monogamous goby Trimma marinae: a comparison with its polygamous relative, Trimma caudomaculatum
studi.s: Monogamous mating systems are widespread across vertebrates. Although ecological theories have addressed their ultimate drivers, the extent to which their proximate mechanisms are shared across taxa remains unclear. We investigated the involvement of oxytocin (OT) signaling in partner preference formation in two closely related gobiid fishes with contrasting mating systems: monogamous Trimma marinae and polygamous Trimma caudomaculatum. Females received pharmacological treatments before cohabitation with a male, and partner preference was assessed the following day. In T.

studi.t: Subcellular multiomic profiling with SPACE-immune reveals divergent immune activation states and intracellular signaling of PBMCs
studi.s: Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) represent the most clinically accessible window into systemic immune status, yet many current single-cell technologies, such as flow cytometry and droplet-based sequencing, lack subcellular spatial resolution. Here we present SPACE-immune (SPAtial Cell Exploratory for Immune characterization), which adapts imaging-based spatial molecular profiling to measure the whole transcriptome (18,935 genes) and 64 proteins in the same PBMC at subcellular resolution.

studi.t: whittle: annotation-preserving trimming and filtering of long reads
studi.s: Long reads from Oxford Nanopore and PacBio instruments can carry per-base annotations in unaligned BAM or FASTQ headers. These include base-modification calls, PacBio polymerase kinetics and Nanopore move tables that link bases to raw signal. Trimming and splitting remove bases or change their positions, so annotations that are not updated can refer to removed bases or the wrong positions. We present whittle, which removes adapters, barcodes and primers, splits chimeric reads, filters reads by quality and length, and rewrites the supported annotations of each retained segment.

studi.t: A Calibrated Gate for Evaluating Synthetic Clinical Data
studi.s: Evaluation tools for synthetic patient records score fidelity (resemblance to real patients), utility (performance of models trained on the table) and privacy (exposure of real patients), combining them by arithmetic, geometric or harmonic means. Such scores are compensatory: copied training records can pass with high fidelity despite poor privacy. Under the null that a table is an unaltered sample of the source population, none of seven reviewed frame-works reports its aggregation rules type I error rate or power against injected flaws.

studi.t: Transcription Factor Binding Site Prediction in Microbial Biosynthetic Gene Cluster Families
studi.s: Motivation: Transcriptional regulation of biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) controls secondary metabolite production, yet the regulatory elements governing BGC expression remain largely uncharacterised and unmapped across BGC diversity. Results: We present a comparative-genomic pipeline that partitions genes within each BiG-FAM BGC family into clusters of orthologous genes and discovers motifs conserved in their upstream regions.

studi.t: Conditional Dirichlet Flow Matching for exploring the sequence space of protein families
studi.s: Protein folds have evolved to support a diverse range of functions, and repurposing an existing fold can offer a more effective route to engineering new functions than designing a scaffold de novo. Here, we introduce Syzygy, a generative model that learns the evolutionary sequence patterns of protein families to generate artificial homologues that diverge from natural sequences while preserving family-specific characteristics.

studi.t: PanPPI: ranking-trained protein embeddings for proteome-scale interaction screening
studi.s: Proteome-wide interaction screening requires ranking millions of protein pairs before costly structure prediction. PanPPI trains a cacheable protein encoder with a ranking loss, so each protein is embedded once and pairs are scored at 0.75 million per minute on one H200 GPU. PanPPI matched or outperformed published models on benchmarks, and in five eukaryotes its top 1% of pairs contained 52-88% of AlphaFold-Multimer's confident predictions among STRING-linked pairs.

studi.t: Temperature Scaling as a Free Lunch for De Novo Peptide Sequencing: Further Gains from Training-Free Candidate Rescoring
studi.s: De novo peptide sequencing infers peptide sequences directly from tandem mass spectra without relying on a reference database, enabling the identification of peptides absent from reference collections. Autoregressive models commonly decode with beam search and return the candidate with the highest model score.

studi.t: R implementation of the NORMAgene data-driven qRT-PCR normalization algorithm
studi.s: Effective data normalization is essential in producing meaningful qRT-PCR results. Traditional reference gene normalization has high risk of confounds when poorly implemented, and data-driven normalization is becoming an increasingly used and robust alternative. The NORMAgene least squares-based normalization algorithm is one of the most application flexible of existing data-driven qRT-PCR normalization approaches; however, it is currently only available in the form of an unmaintained Visual Basic for Applications (VBA) macro.

studi.t: Enzymado: Are Protein Language Models Getting Better at Enzyme Tasks?
studi.s: Protein language model (PLM) embeddings are a common representation for enzyme engineering tasks. PLMs are pretrained using vast protein data, and while enzymes are proteins, they are distinguished by their catalytic nature, which is dependent on substrates and reaction mechanisms. Current PLM evaluations test isolated properties with incompatible data, splits, and metrics, leaving open how PLMs can better serve enzymes and what drives their performance.

studi.t: A data engine for AI-assisted labeling of high-density sperm microscopy videos
studi.s: Computer-aided semen analysis (CASA) systems are the standard tools for quantifying sperm motility, concentration, and morphology, but they rely on classical algorithms that struggle with overlapping cells, collisions, and the imaging artifacts that accumulate in long, high-density recordings. As a result, analyses are typically restricted to short videos of diluted samples. AI-based trackers could overcome these limitations, but they require large, accurately labeled training datasets, and manually labeling crowded sperm videos is prohibitively slow.

studi.t: Simultaneous Optimization of Codon Adaptation and Thermodynamic Stability in mRNA Therapeutics via Deep Reinforcement Learning
studi.s: Motivation. The efficacy of mRNA vaccines depends on translational efficiency and molecule stability, commonly captured by the codon adaptation index (CAI) and minimum free energy (MFE), respectively. These objectives are in tension, and codon degeneracy makes their simultaneous optimization in large RNA constructs encoding multiples peptides a combinatorial search problem intractable through brute-force computation. Methods.

studi.t: Conformal Quadrature RF Coils with a Semi-open Architecture for 9.4 T Brain MRI from Mice to Macaques
studi.s: Objective: To develop a semi-open quadrature RF coil architecture that combines brain coverage with low interport coupling at 9.4 T across animal sizes. Methods: Head-conformal high-pass resonators with an adjustable peripheral branch were constructed for four animal head sizes. A shared-rung circuit model, two-capacitance electromagnetic screening, and accepted-power-normalized field analysis guided the implementation.

studi.t: ImmunoCAR Atlas: a pan-immune single-cell resource for dissecting CAR-T therapy response across patient cohorts
studi.s: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy has transformed treatment for relapsed/refractory hematologic malignancies, yet 40-60% of patients relapse within one to two years, and the immune correlates separating durable responders from non-responders remain poorly defined. Single-cell transcriptomics has been widely applied to CAR-T cohorts, but the resulting data remain fragmented across small, underpowered studies with inconsistent metadata, tissue sources, sampling timepoints, and annotation schemes, and existing immune atlases each address only part of this problem.

studi.t: The tell-tale hair: Effects of dam contact and hutch type on hair cortisol concentrations in female Holstein calves
studi.s: Early rearing conditions and the social environment have decisive influences on calves stress responses. The effects of prolonged postpartum cow-calf contact and preweaning housing conditions on hair cortisol concentration (HCC) in Holstein calves are not yet fully understood. This study aimed to understand how different postpartum contact times between calves and their dams and subsequent hutch types affect cortisol concentrations in calf hair.

studi.t: Heliox effect on expiratory flow in master athletes: a comprehensive analysis coupling experimental measures and computational modeling
studi.s: Introduction. Expiratory flow is determined by airway geometry and inhaled gases properties. Maximal expiratory flow-volume (MEFV) curves decrease with aging that reduces airway caliber and increase resistance. However, the independent contributions of airway geometry and gas properties to expiratory flow remain difficult to quantify experimentally. We combined experimental measurements and mathematical modeling to evaluate these contributions in master athletes a model of successful aging. Methods. Spirometry was assessed in 14 master athletes (69.3+/-5.7yr) breathing air or heliox (HeO2).

studi.t: Comparative Chloroplast Genomics of Henbit (Lamium amplexicaule) Reveals Diagnostic Plastid Markers in Lamium.
studi.s: Lamium amplexicaule (henbit deadnettle) is a widespread member of Lamiaceae, but plastome-level comparisons within Lamium are still limited. In this study, we characterized the complete chloroplast genome of an L. amplexicaule accession collected in Turlock, California, and compared it with other available Lamium plastomes. The L. amplexicaule_Turlock plastome was 150,642 bp in length and had the typical quadripartite structure, with 113 distinct chloroplast genes. Phylogenomic analysis based on 79 shared protein-coding genes across 31 taxa placed the three sampled L.

studi.t: Lung tissue organization shapes influenza spread and immune control
studi.s: Type I interferon (IFN) is a central defense against influenza A virus, yet its effectiveness depends on lung tissue organization, often simplified in mechanistic models. We investigated four IFN mechanisms--blocking infection, inducing a refractory state, suppressing virion production, and amplifying IFN production--using a homogeneous reaction-diffusion model and a spatial agent-based model reconstructed from murine lung histology. The latter represented approximately 233,000 detected cells in a single section or 4.1 million across a reconstructed volume.

studi.t: Baseline Predictors of Craving Reduction Following Non-Invasive Neuromodulation: A Computational Modeling Approach
studi.s: BackgroundAlcohol craving is a clinically relevant symptom with an established neurobiological basis and has emerged as a treatment target. Non-invasive neuromodulation has shown potential for reducing craving, but substantial inter-individual variability in response is a pervasive challenge. This study examined whether baseline computational parameters predicted treatment response following neuromodulation.

studi.t: Enhanced KNa1.1 Channel Underlies Cortical Hyperexcitability and Seizure Susceptibility after Traumatic Brain Injury
studi.s: Pathogenic variants of the sodium-activated potassium channel KNa1.1 have been reported in multiple epileptic disorders. However, whether and how KNa1.1 channel is involved in epileptogenesis after traumatic brain injury (TBI) remains unknown. Firstly, we used behavioral monitoring and EEG recording to examine physiological property, spontaneous seizure activity, and seizure susceptibility after TBI. We explored the changes of KNa1.1 channel following TBI, including changes of subcellular distribution and expression pattern.

studi.t: EpiState-T for representing epigenetic states across time
studi.s: Epigenetic information is central to cellular identity, aging and rejuvenation. Unlike the relatively stable genomic sequence shared by most somatic cells, epigenetic states vary across cells and time, making their dynamics difficult to reconstruct from sparse experimental measurements. We introduce EpiState-T, the Temporal Epigenetic State Tensor, to represent selected epigenetic states across intervals and distinguish an observed trajectory from the use of a retained record. In a ten-cell simulation, an explicit reader can act on each cells surviving baseline record.

studi.t: Understanding robustness and enabling remediation of neuroimaging-based deep neural networks for digital security: Semantic segmentation of brain tumors as illustrative study
studi.s: BackgroundApplications of deep learning models in neuroimaging have significantly advanced translational neuroscience, offering substantial benefits to human health. However, recent cybersecurity threats have undermined the reliability of digital neuroscience tools, posing challenges to the clinical neuroscience community. A critical issue is the automated semantic segmentation of malignant or premalignant brain tumors, essential for neurosurgery and radiotherapy planning.

studi.t: Dynamic hippocampal and cortical signatures of naturalistic event memory
studi.s: Remembering temporally extended experiences requires integrating information over time into coherent event representations that can be stored and later retrieved. This process places changing demands on memory as an event unfolds: event representations must be reset at the beginning, connected into a unified model during the event, and stored in long-term memory at the end. We hypothesized that oscillatory dynamics, by coordinating communication across regions and organizing neural activity in time, provide a flexible mechanism for meeting these changing demands.

studi.t: Sex-Related Associations Between Precuneus Volume and Subjective-Objective Memory Discrepancy in Amyloid-Positive Individuals
studi.s: INTRODUCTIONThe precuneus, a metamemory-related parietal region with sex-specific vulnerability in Alzheimers disease (AD), may contribute to reduced insight of memory deficit. We investigated whether precuneus structural integrity explained sex differences in subjective-objective memory discrepancy.

studi.t: Mapping the neural circuitry of cognitive restructuring in depressive and anxiety disorders
studi.s: Cognitive restructuring, the process of identifying and challenging negative thoughts, is a key technique in the treatment of depressive and anxiety disorders. However, findings regarding its underlying neural circuitry remain inconsistent, potentially reflecting opposing effects of depressive and anxiety symptomatology that obscure disorder-specific dysfunction.

studi.t: Terminal Schwann Cells Are Required for Presynaptic Vesicle Homeostasis but Not for Gross Neuromuscular Junction Architecture in Mice
studi.s: Terminal Schwann cells (tSCs) are specialized glial cells persistently residing at the neuromuscular junction (NMJ), where they are widely held to participate in synaptic transmission and maintenance. However, elucidating their precise in vivo roles has been hindered by a lack of models for tSC-specific genetic manipulation, as conventional tools simultaneously targeted axonal Schwann cells. Here, we identify Col20a1 as a gene highly specific to tSCs through single-cell transcriptomic analysis and generate a novel Col20a1-CreERT2 knock-in mouse model.

studi.t: Olfactory-Visual Integration Facilitates Scene Perception through Modulation of the Parahippocampal Place Area
studi.s: Visual scenes anchor our experience of the world, yet the places in which scenes unfold are defined not only by what we see but also by what we smell. Whether and how odors contribute to the neural representation of visual scenes remains poorly understood. Here we asked whether a semantically congruent odor facilitates scene perception and identified the neural mechanisms supporting this facilitation. In two behavioral experiments, participants judged whether briefly presented, masked images depicted intact or scrambled scenes while continuously smelling an odor.

studi.t: A Deep Learning Model for Quantifying and Mapping Human Spiral Ganglion Neurons (SGNs): The SGN Base Model
studi.s: IntroductionSpiral ganglion neurons (SGNs) transmit auditory information and are a histological marker that have been quantified for decades to study various hearing loss pathologies in human temporal bone (hTB) specimens. Historically, quantification of SGNs has been labor-intensive and subject to manual bias and error. With the advent of digital microscopy, this study introduces and assesses the accuracy of a deep learning model for SGN quantification, providing an efficient approach that enables in-depth analysis of SGN distribution through three-dimensional frequency mapping.

studi.t: Global weight-Ranked cluster-grOWing (GROW): A Cluster-Growing Framework for Robust Functional Coordinate Network Mapping
studi.s: Coordinate Network Mapping (CNM) has become an important approach for translating scattered neuroimaging findings into circuit-level models of brain disorders such as Alzheimers disease (AD). But conventional CNM uses fixed-radius spheres and pools heterogeneous studies without accounting for confounders. We developed Global weight-Ranked cluster-grOWing (GROW), which reconstructs clusters behind reported peaks using cluster information and a reference statistical weight map, without original imaging data.

studi.t: Robustness of a connectome model of the fly walking rhythm generator to modelling choices
studi.s: Connectome-constrained models are increasingly used to attribute behaviour to wiring, but their conclusions rest on modelling choices that the connectome does not fix. We independently replicated the rate model of the Drosophila nerve cord in which descending neuron DNg100 drives a walking rhythm generator (Pugliese et al., 2026), and asked which of its conclusions survive defensible alternatives to eleven such choices. Changed one at a time, 19 of 20 alternatives left the rhythm intact, including transfer of the wiring to a second connectome.

studi.t: Dynamic remodeling of hybrid BBB-fenestrated capillaries in the hypothalamic arcuate nucleus
studi.s: The hypothalamic arcuate nucleus (Arc) is a central regulator of metabolism. We show that capillaries with sparse fenestrae enable direct and rapid hormone transport into the Arc. Arc fenestrae are virtually absent during pregnancy and obesity, but reform postpartum and upon weight-loss. Fenestrated Arc endothelial cells display a unique hybrid BBB-permeable structural and molecular phenotype, which can be regulated by Wnt signaling. The Arc endothelium exhibits functional plasticity that may affect hypothalamic sensing of systemic metabolic signals.

studi.t: Fecal virome-enriched fractions are associated with increased biofilm biomass and distinct bacterial responses in biofilm and planktonic communities in an in vitro colon model
studi.s: The gut microbiota is spatially organized, yet microorganisms at the intestinal mucus surface remain understudied in virome microbiota research. We investigated how addition of fecal virome enriched fractions was associated with biofilm biomass and bacterial composition in surface associated and planktonic communities using a biofilm adapted in vitro colon model, CoMiniGut. Fecal samples were collected from three healthy human donors at two time points approximately one year apart.

studi.t: Myotendinous junctions form dynamic three-dimensional architectures during development and growth
studi.s: The myotendinous junction (MTJ) is a specialized extracellular matrix-rich interface that transmits contractile force generated by skeletal muscle to tendon, but how the MTJ is assembled as developing skeletal muscle connects to tendon, and how the mature tissue-level architecture subsequently emerges, remain incompletely understood. Here, we generate a Col22a1-EGFP knock-in mouse that enables direct visualization and quantitative analysis of MTJs from embryonic development to postnatal growth.

studi.t: Genome-wide Cell-free DNA Fragmentation Profiling at Transcription Start Sites Detects Cancer Without Cancer-Type-Specific Region Selection
studi.s: Accurate discrimination between healthy individuals and patients with cancer using minimally invasive liquid biopsies could improve cancer diagnosis and monitoring. Circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) is a promising biomarker, since its fragmentation patterns reflect chromatin organization at regulatory regions such as transcription start sites (TSSs). Classification approaches typically rely on hypothesis-driven selection of genomic regions based on literature or external tissue data.

studi.t: Emergent particle collection by cyanobacteria through gliding motility and filament buckling
studi.s: Cyanobacterial macrostructures such as mats, aggregates, and stromatolites are observed in diverse habitats. These structures incorporate organic and inorganic matter and form microenvironments enabling biochemical transformations. Macrostructures are found to be associated with motile, filamentous cyanobacteria, but how, and to what extent, filament motility can drive macrostructure formation are unclear. To address this question, we study macrostructure formation in a well-characterised freshwater cyanobacterial community dominated by the filamentous cyanobacterium Fluctiforma draycotensis.

studi.t: Haplotype-resolved genome assemblies and population resequencing reveal no evidence for genetic sex determination in the dioecious conifer Taxus baccata
studi.s: Hundreds of plant lineages have independently evolved dioecy, the separation of female and male reproductive organs on different individuals. In all dioecious plants investigated at the molecular level to date, sex is determined genetically through a sex-determining region (SDR). However, SDRs have mostly been characterized in angiosperms, even though dioecy is far more common among gymnosperms. Here, we investigate sex determination in the dioecious conifer Taxus baccata L. (European yew).

studi.t: Active sensory exploration is a major driver of dopamine neuron activity
studi.s: Novel stimuli promote arousal, orienting, and learning-related plasticity. Many of these effects have been attributed to dopamine (DA) release, yet whether individual DA neurons encode novelty remains controversial, and the circuit origin of novelty-related signals is unknown. Here, we recorded and manipulated neurons in the ventral tegmental area and substantia nigra (VTA/SNc) of mice exposed to novel and familiar odors while monitoring active sensory exploration, including sniffing and facial movements.

studi.t: Adaptation to postural perturbations under fatigue produces persistent changes in neuromuscular coordination
studi.s: Postural control depends on the ability to adapt motor responses to changing environmental and physiological conditions. Neuromuscular fatigue (NMF) is known to alter balance and muscle activation patterns, yet its effects on motor adaptation during whole-body postural tasks and on the persistence of learned strategies remain unclear. This study investigated whether localized NMF of the ankle dorsiflexors influences adaptation to a novel postural perturbation task and whether learning under fatigue induces persistent changes during subsequent re-exposure.

studi.t: Cross-Stream Self-Supervised Learning Inspired by Feature-Biased Visual Processing in the Brain
studi.s: Humans and other animals develop rich visual representations without explicit object-category labels. Self-supervised learning (SSL) offers a computational framework for studying how such representations emerge from visual experience. Many contrastive SSL models, such as SimCLR, learn by being robust to augmented views of the same image, which may fail to preserve visual attributes such as color and orientation.

studi.t: Heatwaves rescue a mosquito host from parasitism across a large geographic gradient
studi.s: The impacts of increasingly frequent and intense heatwaves on parasitism are an important frontier for understanding disease risk under climate change. These impacts are complex because parasitism arises from multiple interacting host and parasite traits that can vary in thermal sensitivity, across the ontogeny of infection, and among populations exposed to different historical temperature regimes.

studi.t: Nanoscale spatial-omics via contrastive embedding of single-molecule localisation data
studi.s: Omics approaches have transformed biology by characterising cells at the genomic, transcriptomic and proteomic levels. An additional layer of cellular information is provided by the nanoscale spatial organisation of molecules, which can be measured using super-resolution microscopy. We present a self-supervised contrastive learning framework that embeds single-molecule localisation microscopy (SMLM) point patterns into a learned representation of nanoscale organisation.

studi.t: Ion-channel transcript loss and variable firing in SCA1 Purkinje cells: a modelling test
studi.s: In spinocerebellar ataxia type 1 (SCA1), Purkinje cells fire with more variable interspike intervals before they degenerate, and reduced ion-channel expression is a proposed cause. We asked whether their channel transcript changes, applied as conductance changes, could produce this firing. We analysed public single-nucleus RNA-seq from male and female Atxn1 154Q/2Q knock-in and wild-type mice (24 discovery mice, 5-30 weeks; six held-out, 12 weeks). Knock-in Purkinje nuclei showed a reproducible transcriptional shift from 5 weeks.

studi.t: An expanded GRAB sensor palette for multiplexed imaging of purinergic dynamics in vivo
studi.s: Extracellular ATP and adenosine operate as tightly coupled purinergic signals, yet tracking both molecules simultaneously in vivo has been limited by the performance and spectral range of existing sensors. We describe an expanded set of genetically encoded GPCR-Activation-Based (GRAB) sensors for ATP and adenosine that together support multiplexed imaging of purinergic signaling in the intact brain.

studi.t: Behaviorally driven increased glutamatergic activity from lateral entorhinal cortex to hippocampus supports object and spatial memory recall
studi.s: Interactions between the entorhinal cortex (EC) and hippocampal area CA1 are vital for episodic memory formation, but their role in recall is less clear. Canonically, spatial processing -- the "where" of an experience -- is attributed to the medial entorhinal cortex (MEC), whereas the lateral entorhinal cortex (LEC) processes the "what": non-spatial sensory cues and objects. Though these inputs are anatomically segregated in CA1, multimodal memory processing requires integrating spatial and contextual information, and recent work suggests greater MEC-LEC crosstalk than previously thought.

studi.t: Dynamic Weight Signatures as a Novel Biomarker of Motor Dysfunction in Mouse Models
studi.s: Motor dysfunction is typically assessed through clinical examination and manual scoring, with gait analysis and accelerometry providing objective measures of subtle abnormalities. The observable 4-6 Hz resting tremor of Parkinsons disease highlights the importance of capturing motor fluctuations at relevant timescales. Using a high-precision industrial weighing module, we tested whether high-frequency weight recordings of freely moving mice could provide a simple, noninvasive means of detecting disease-associated motor abnormalities.

studi.t: One More Night: Investigating the Stability of Verbal Overnight Memory Consolidation and Sources of Variability
studi.s: Sleep-Dependent Memory Consolidation (SDMC) plays a vital role in facilitating the retention of newly learnt information. However, retesting in the literature is scarce and thus little is known regarding the daily stability of the SDMC process. The present study investigated whether overnight memory consolidation performance is stable (reflecting a trait) or variable (reflecting a state) across two nights using a novel word-pair smartphone application.

studi.t: Giant bacteria in gut microbiomes
studi.s: The advent of sequencing-based omics has transformed our understanding of the gut microbiome, enabling microbial communities to be characterised at unprecedented scale and resolution. However, these approaches provide limited information about cellular traits such as size and morphology. Giant bacteria remain largely overlooked in gut microbiome research, despite their extraordinary cell size, extreme polyploidy and unusual reproductive strategies.

studi.t: Structural Landscape of MHC Complexes through Fold Mining
studi.s: Major histocompatibility complex (MHC) proteins share a characteristic structural platform formed by two -helices positioned above a {beta}-sheet (1-2 domain), which can accommodate ligands and provide an exposed surface for recognition by protein binding partners. This interaction system is best characterized for classical MHC-I molecules presenting peptides to T-cell receptors (TCRs), one of the most extensively studied mechanisms of immune recognition.

studi.t: Forecasting Human Sleep Dynamics with a Latent-State Framework
studi.s: Sleep is essential for health, and forecasting its evolution could clarify its temporal organization and guide intervention timing. We developed a representation-forecasting model using electroencephalography from 5,419 participants. From 30-minute histories, 10-minute forecasts achieved 90.71% four-class accuracy in the 10% of windows with lowest predicted risk and averaged 72.11% overall. Direction-specific encoder feature axes had spectral correlates.

studi.t: Local sleep in wake is widespread across the rat cortex and tracks sleep need
studi.s: During non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep, cortical neurons alternate between ON periods of firing and OFF periods of silence, the latter accounting for the slow waves of the EEG. Converging evidence indicates that OFF periods can also occur locally during extended wake ("local sleep"), at a behavioral cost, but whether this phenomenon is ubiquitous across the cortex, whether some areas are more resilient than others, and whether it can also provide any benefit, remain open questions.

studi.t: Inferred interactions transform values into lattice-patterned choice attractors in orbitofrontal cortex
studi.s: Economic decisions require transforming option values into choices, a process involving the orbitofrontal cortex (OFC), but the circuit mechanism remains unclear. We recorded OFC activity in monkeys performing a juice-choice task, fitted graphical Ising models to spike data, and simulated the inferred networks. Offer inputs shifted the networks toward attractor states favoring the choice representation supported by relative value.

studi.t: From cellular synaptic input profiles to population-level respiratory circuitry
studi.s: Breathing depends on coordinated activity among brainstem neurons. Their discharge patterns show when populations are active but do not specify the synaptic inputs that generate these patterns. Assuming that respiratory pattern generation involves a small number of interacting populations distinguished by discharge timing and excitatory or inhibitory output, we used synaptic conductances as readouts of their convergent activity.

studi.t: Evidence supporting resting-state power spectrum exponent as a non-invasive measure of neural-circuit excitation:inhibition balance in children with and without autism
studi.s: IntroductionAn ongoing neural circuit excitation (E) and inhibition (I) imbalance is thought to be a major contributor to clinical conditions such as autism, schizophrenia, and epilepsy. Current methods for directly measuring E:I dynamics require invasive procedures that are difficult to perform in non-human animals and nearly impossible in humans. A non-invasive measure of E:I balance is of great interest as a diagnostic as well as therapeutic marker, and as a means of studying relevant pathological and intervention mechanisms.

studi.t: Closed-loop control of sensorimotor aperiodic neural dynamics can manipulate excitatory-inhibitory balance in humans
studi.s: A ubiquitous property of physical and biological systems is scale-free dynamics in which spectral power decreases as a function of frequency, showing a 1/f spectral slope. The 1/f slope of neural power spectra has been proposed as a marker of cortical excitation-inhibition (E/I) balance, based on pharmacological experiments and computational models of synaptic activity in cortical networks. However, whether or not the spectral slope in the human population recordings, influenced by biophysical or experimental factors, can be utilized as an index of cortical E/I is debatable.

studi.t: Lifespan Remodeling of Cerebral Biomechanical Network Organization Reveals Coordinated Maturation and Aging-Related Convergence
studi.s: Brain biomechanical connectivity (BC) captures shared regional viscoelastic properties that may support functional interactions. Although functional and structural brain networks are well characterized, the systems-level organization of brain biomechanics remains unknown. Using in-vivo magnetic resonance elastography (MRE) and community detection, we established BC and its network organization across the mouse lifespan, spanning seven stages from early adolescence (4 weeks) to old age (72 weeks).

studi.t: Prethalamus integrates neocortical and hypothalamic input to promote courage
studi.s: Courage, the ability to act despite potential danger, is essential for adaptive behavior, yet the circuit mechanisms that balance caution and risk-taking under threat are not fully understood. Here we identify the ventral lateral geniculate nucleus (vLGN), an inhibitory prethalamic structure, as a key node in this process. High vLGN activity predicts courageous behavior, such as leaving a shelter to enter a potentially threatening environment, and optogenetic activation of vLGN neurons promotes risk-taking under diverse aversive conditions.

studi.t: ProteoBridge Connects Proteomics Quantification Outputs to Reusable Analysis Workflows
studi.s: Quantification tools for bottom-up label-free proteomics, including DIA-NN, Spectronaut, MaxQuant, and FragPipe, use different table layouts, column headers, modification notations, and parameter files. Downstream applications maintain separate readers for these outputs. ProteoBridge lets an application request the same quantity, such as unnormalized ion intensity, across reports from different quantification tools. JSON parsing rules describe each tools tables, and software-specific parameter parsers read the settings. The rules currently cover 14 tools and are tested on public inputs.

studi.t: Paternal transmission of the APPPS1 transgene is associated with increased amyloid pathology and a small Thy1.2-APP methylation difference
studi.s: Maternal transmission of the APP transgene lowers amyloid burden in 5xFAD mice. We examined whether APPPS1-21 shows a similar parent-of-origin association and whether Thy1.2 methylation contributes. F1 offspring inheriting the transgene from the mother had less A{beta}42, fewer plaques, less gliosis, and less human APP at intermediate ages. The A{beta}42 difference was not detected in the F2 cohort at 100 days. Non-transgenic off-spring of APPPS1 mothers did not differ in glial counts, and serum anti-A{beta} antibody levels were not higher at 40 days.

studi.t: Top-down prefrontal connectivity accompanies perceptual breakthrough after interocular suppression
studi.s: The role of the prefrontal cortex (PFC) in the emergence of visual stimuli into conscious awareness remains contested. Additionally, whether top-down prefrontal connectivity is shaped by prior expectations during this process is not well understood. To address these questions, we applied dynamic causal modelling (DCM) to an EEG dataset during breaking continuous flash suppression (bCFS), which offers tight control over when a stimulus breaks into conscious perception. Our network comprised bilateral PFC, primary visual cortex, fusiform gyrus and motor cortex.

studi.t: Spatiotemporally regulated transcriptional networks control the plasticity of chickpea root exodermis
studi.s: Abscisic acid (ABA) regulates plant responses to stress and influences the differentiation of root barrier cell types, such as the endodermis and exodermis. Despite the importance of the exodermis in limiting water and solute fluxes, its regulation remains poorly understood in legumes. Here, we characterize suberization and lignification induced by exogenous ABA in tissues across eight galegoid legumes to identify exodermis-forming species in the clade. Chickpea deposited suberin lamella specifically in the outermost cortex and formed a functional apoplastic barrier, i.e. an exodermis.

studi.t: Predictive coding networks capture human neural representations missing in supervised DNNs
studi.s: Neuroscientific learning theories propose that the brain acquires knowledge by constructing internal world models. Supervised learning, the dominant approach in deep neural networks (DNN), relies on external category labels, making it difficult to reconcile with biological learning. There is an increasing trend towards more biologically valid approaches, such as predictive (minimize future surprise) or contrastive (minimize response to expected, maximize to unexpected inputs) objectives, but these approaches typically rely on pretrained DNN models that vary widely in architecture, size, and…

studi.t: An integrative model of AMPA receptor trafficking reveals the central contribution of local translation in subtype-specific kinetics
studi.s: AMPA-type glutamate receptors (AMPARs) underlie most of the excitatory synaptic transmission in the brain and are crucial for implementing long-term synaptic plasticity. AMPARs form multi-protein complexes containing pore-forming subunits GluA1-4 and auxiliary subunits that regulate AMPAR function and trafficking. Here we show that protein synthesis and trafficking mechanisms determine distributions of AMPAR subtypes across neuronal compartments and their distinct responses to long-term potentiation.

studi.t: Loss of Tau in the adult brain causes progressive disruption of neuronal homeostasis and behavioral performance
studi.s: Tau has been extensively studied in neurodegenerative disease, yet its physiological role in the adult brain remains elusive. Here, we generated an inducible conditional Tau knockout mouse model to selectively delete Tau in adult brain and investigated the consequences of Tau loss across multiple levels. Tau knock-down in the forebrain induced progressive emotional and cognitive deficits, accompanied by dendritic remodeling, impaired spine maturation, and disrupted neuronal network activity.

studi.t: Resource-State Modulation of Prefrontal Value Processing during Earning-Spending Decision Making
studi.s: Money mediates earning and spending, and accumulated monetary holdings constitute both a basic form of wealth and an external resource state that shapes economic decisions. Unlike internal physiological states such as hunger or satiety, external resources persist outside the body, can be acquired or depleted through choice, and preserve access to future consumption. Although money and wealth are human constructs, balancing resource acquisition and consumption may rely on evolutionarily conserved neural computations.

studi.t: Expression of human-specific SRGAP2C increases representational capacity in mice
studi.s: The brain of modern humans has evolved remarkable computational abilities enabling higher cognitive functions. Recent progress in evolutionary genomics and experimental neuroscience has identified several human-specific genetic modifiers of brain development that underlie the emergence of human-specific traits of cortical circuit connectivity and function. The human-specific gene SRGAP2C emerged by partial duplication of the ancestral gene SRGAP2A, which encodes a postsynaptic protein regulating synaptic development.

studi.t: The IFN-γ Paradox: Mechanistic Modeling Uncouples Cytokine Abundance from Influenza Pathogenesis
studi.s: IFN-{gamma} has both pathogenic and protective roles during influenza infection, yet its value as a biomarker remains unclear because both increased and decreased levels associate with greater severity. To resolve this, we developed a mechanistic mathematical model of IFN-{gamma} and IFN-{gamma}-producing cell kinetics. The model was calibrated using murine data and validated against immune perturbation experiments, murine transcriptomics, human influenza challenge, and critically ill patient data.

studi.t: NAD(P)H-FLIM reveals spatial and temporal epithelial metabolic heterogeneity in live intestinal organoids
studi.s: Metabolism contributes globally to energy production at cell and tissue levels, but its cell-specific metabolic states also support tissue function and architecture. Conventionally used bulk metabolic flux assays however provide only the average readouts across cell populations, while fixed-sample and destructive spatial analysis methods result in endpoint.

studi.t: A long-lived human gastric tissue model defines regulators of lineage maturation
studi.s: The gastric epithelium maintains barrier function against food-borne pathogens and executes metabolic activities through specialized cell types. The niche signals and gene-regulatory networks governing gastric specification remain poorly understood, partly due to the lack of mature human in vitro models. Here we develop long-lived engineered gastric epithelia that recapitulate gland-pit topography and, upon extended culture, give rise to all known gastric epithelial lineages including rare enteroendocrine and tuft cell subtypes.

studi.t: Phenotypic and molecular convergence of a cancer-associated pigmentation trait in Xiphophorus evelynae
studi.s: Cases of phenotypic convergence are common across the tree of life, and often reflect shared ecological pressures. Studying such cases can provide insights into the repeatability of evolution in nature and help uncover the degree to which similar morphological phenotypes tend to also be driven by convergent molecular mechanisms. Here, we investigate the genetic basis of a convergent phenotype in Xiphophorus, a genus of fish known to possess a wide variety of polymorphic pigmentation traits, which have been shown to play important roles in their behavioral and ecological environments.

studi.t: Stress-responsive enhancer RNAs couple chromatin reprogramming to post-transcriptional control of senescence
studi.s: Background: Cellular senescence is accompanied by extensive epigenomic reprogramming leading to changes in enhancer RNA levels, yet how enhancer activity is translated into functional RNA-level regulation remains unclear. Here we investigate how enhancer reprogramming during senescence impacts functional RNA-level regulation by eRNAs. Results: By integrating time-resolved transcriptomic analyses across multiple primary human cell types, we identify a set of recurrently dysregulated senescence-associated enhancer RNAs (SAeRs).

studi.t: A sequence context-unbiased approach to enable precise inference of mutational processes in cancer.
studi.s: Mutational signatures are recurring patterns of somatic mutations observed in cancer genomes, resulting from the activity of endogenous and exogenous mutagenic processes. Their investigation has significantly advanced our understanding of cancer etiology, informing prevention strategies and supporting clinical stratification. Although analytical approaches facilitate the identification of mutational signatures, their biological interpretation can be challenging, as some signatures may reflect methodological artifacts rather than distinct underlying mutational processes.

studi.t: Genomic insertion sequence populations of an ancient chemosynthetic symbiont
studi.s: Genetic isolation as a consequence of host restriction of bacterial symbionts can lead to reductive genome evolution resulting in small, functionally streamlined genomes that are biased toward high AT contents. Frequently, reductive genome evolution leads to the loss of transposable elements, which are one of the major initial drivers of symbiont genome evolution through massive expansion events following initial host restriction.

studi.t: Digital news consumption as an information foraging problem
studi.s: News feeds are digitally available all around us, yet the cognitive mechanisms by which we decide what to spend time on, and what to skip, are not well understood. We formulate digital news consumption as an information foraging problem. In this formulation, users move between news articles, formalized as information patches, exploited them like agents consuming food in a canonical patch foraging task. The switching time between news article can be seen as a navigational process that happens at a time akin to the travel time in the canonical patch foraging formalism.
