studi.t: GinsengMind: An evidence-grounded AI research agent for integrative molecular research in Panax ginseng
studi.s: Panax ginseng C. A. Meyer is one of the most extensively studied medicinal plants, with substantial pharmaceutical and economic importance owing to its diverse bioactive constituents, particularly ginsenosides. Despite considerable advances in ginseng molecular research, the fragmentation of genomic, transcriptomic, protein structural, and biochemical information remains a major challenge for investigating gene function and specialized metabolism.

studi.t: Measuring and reducing segmentation-driven cell-type labeling errors in imaging spatial transcriptomics
studi.s: Imaging spatial transcriptomics labels each segmented cell from transcripts that include some of its neighbors RNA. We labeled each cell from its nucleus and its whole mask at equal depth, with two nuclear halves as a null. Whole-cell counts drew small, RNA-poor cells toward their larger neighbors labels. On three platforms, relative to nuclear labels at equal depth, T and NK cells lost 23-53% of their labels in six datasets of five tissues and 4-9% in renal cell carcinoma; this label-only measure matched same-cell protein markers in five donors and, where it differed, understated the loss.

studi.t: Large pan-cancer cell screen coupled to (phospho-)proteomics underscores high-dose vitamin C as a potent anti-cancer agent
studi.s: Increasing preclinical and clinical evidence has positioned high-dose vitamin C as a promising anti-cancer treatment that merits more clinical attention. Multiple cytotoxicity mechanisms have been described, including pro-oxidant effects. To contribute to the preclinical understanding of the broad pan-cancer effects of high-dose vitamin C in a global manner, we determined the IC50s of a large panel of cancer cell lines (n=51) representing 7 solid tumour types, and generated proteome data.

studi.t: Multimodal profiling resolves the functional and spatial organization of colorectal cancer liver metastases
studi.s: BackgroundColorectal cancer (CRC) is the second leading cause of cancer-related mortality, largely because of liver metastases (LM). Despite advances in perioperative treatment and surgery, recurrence after resection of CRC liver metastases (CRC-LM) remains common. The cellular complexity of treatment-exposed CRC-LM and the interactions among malignant, stromal, immune, vascular and liver-resident populations remain incompletely understood, limiting the identification of biological vulnerabilities associated with disease progression and recurrence.

studi.t: Confirmation of preclinical findings across laboratories identifies robust effects and factors limiting reproducibility
studi.s: A fundamental challenge in drug development is the frequent failure of early laboratory research to translate into clinical benefit. One proposed solution is to confirm findings from exploratory single-laboratory studies across multiple laboratories before clinical testing. We investigated this approach by prospectively following the conduct of twelve preclinical multi-laboratory studies across different fields of medicine and by systematically identifying previously published multi-laboratory studies in the literature.

studi.t: Optogenetic Kindling Model Reveals Functional Synaptopathy as a Driver of Temporal Lobe Epilepsy and Associated Comorbidities
studi.s: Temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) is one of the most prevalent and pharmaco-resistant forms of focal epilepsy in adults. The precise cellular and network mechanisms underlying TLE progression remain elusive. Animal models are essential for studying molecular and cellular mechanisms of TLE; however, widely used models largely rely on acute seizure induction and fail to recapitulate the gradual, progressive course of human TLE. Here, we present an optogenetic kindling mouse model of TLE, in which repeated stimulation induces a progressive increase in seizure susceptibility.

studi.t: Aiolos is specifically altered in schizophrenia, is expressed in hippocampal neurons and regulates structural synaptic plasticity through complement-mediated mechanisms
studi.s: Aiolos (Ikzf3), a member of the Ikzf family, has been primarily characterized in the immune system, whereas other Ikzf family members have reported roles in the brain and have been implicated in schizophrenia. However, the potential role of Aiolos in the brain remains broadly unexplored. Combining human samples, translational and gain and loss of function mouse models we characterized Aiolos expression in the brain and investigated its potential involvement in schizophrenia.

studi.t: Gaze and Pupil Patterns in ADHD and ASD during Naturalistic Viewing
studi.s: BackgroundAutism spectrum disorder (ASD) and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) frequently co-occur, and both are associated with atypical attention and arousal. Whether these associations arise from shared or distinct processes remains unclear because the conditions are rarely modeled jointly and attention and arousal are rarely measured simultaneously.

studi.t: PICALM deficiency exacerbates amyloid pathology in murine and nematode Alzheimers disease models
studi.s: Alzheimers disease (AD), characterized by the accumulation of amyloid {beta}-peptide (A{beta}) plaques, is a progressive age-related neurodegenerative disorder affecting more than 35 million people worldwide. The risk of developing AD is significantly influenced by genetic factors. Deciphering their molecular functions has substantially advanced our understanding of the pathogenic mechanisms underlying AD. The PICALM gene represents a highly validated AD risk factor, and the encoded endocytic adaptor CALM is critical for endothelial A{beta} clearance and microglial A{beta} phagocytosis.

studi.t: Accurate and Interpretable Prediction of Antidepressant Treatment Response from Receptor-informed Neuroimaging
studi.s: Conventional antidepressants show moderate efficacy in treating major depressive disorder. Psychedelic-assisted therapy holds promise, yet individual responses vary, underscoring the need for predictive tools to guide treatment selection. Here, we present graphTRIP (graph-based Treatment Response Interpretability and Prediction) -- a geometric deep learning architecture that enables three advances: 1) accurate prediction of post-treatment depression severity using only pretreatment clinical and neuroimaging data; 2) identification of interpretable biomarkers; and 3) causal analysis of…

studi.t: Dissociation of Reward Incentive and Motivational Drive by Distinct Neural Circuits in Mice
studi.s: The generation of reward incentive value and maintenance of motivational drive are distinct processes in reward-related behavior. However, how neural circuits differentially process these components remains poorly understood. Although intracranial self-stimulation (ICSS) paradigms have been utilized to identify reward-related circuits, ICSS measures may conflate reinitiated actions attributed to learned incentive value with ongoing motivated behavior sustained by concurrent stimulation.

studi.t: Continued genomic surveillance of Vibrio cholerae O1 isolates from cholera cases in Europe, 2023-2024
studi.s: Background: Following the global resurgence of cholera in 2022, 59 cholera cases were reported by 11 European countries in 2023-2024. Aim: We aimed to confirm that V. cholerae O1 isolates associated with these cases belonged to the epidemic seventh pandemic El Tor (7PET) lineage rather than to non-epidemic V. cholerae O1 lineages, and to characterise their virulence and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) determinants and phylogenetic relationships.. Methods: Fifty V. cholerae O1 isolates were available for whole genome sequencing, of which 49 yielded genomes of sufficient quality for analysis.

studi.t: A Comparative Metagenomic Analysis of the Viral Diversity in Faecal Samples from Malnourished and Non-malnourished Children with Gastroenteritis Admitted at Victoria Mxenge Hospital in Durban, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa
studi.s: Viral gastroenteritis and malnutrition remain major health burdens among children under five in South Africa. Malnourished children are particularly vulnerable to prolonged enteric viral infections, yet their gut virome remains poorly characterised in South Africa. This study compared gut virome diversity among malnourished and non-malnourished children with gastroenteritis, and children without gastroenteritis and malnutrition (healthy controls).

studi.t: RFoldSearch enables fast RNA structure search beyond sequence similarity
studi.s: The rapid growth of predicted RNA structure databases demands fast and sensitive structural search methods. Sequence-based approaches lose sensitivity for divergent homologues, whereas exhaustive coordinate alignment is computationally expensive. Analogous to Foldseeks 3Di representation, we introduce RFoldSearch and 3Dr, a learned 80-state structural alphabet encoding local RNA tertiary environments. RFoldSearch combines indexed prefiltering, structure-aware token alignment and optional coordinate-based reranking.

studi.t: RingNet: An Interactive Platform for Multi-Modal Data Visualization in Networks
studi.s: The exponential growth of data in biomedicine has created an urgent need for intuitive visualization tools. These tools must be able to effectively represent complex biological networks and remain accessible to domain experts without extensive computational training. Current network visualization approaches often require specialized programming skills and/or cannot handle the scale and complexity of modern biomedical datasets, which creates significant barriers to biological discovery.

studi.t: kRISP-meR: A Reference-free Guide-RNA Design Tool for CRISPR/Cas9
studi.s: Designing specific guide RNAs for CRISPR/Cas9 typically relies on reference genomes, which limits the applicability in non-model organisms and fails to account for individual-specific genomic variations. To address this, we present a reference-free method for single-guide RNA (sgRNA) design that operates directly on raw sequencing reads, implemented in a tool called kRISP-meR.

studi.t: A systematic benchmark evaluation of algorithms for 3D tissue alignment and registration with spatial omics
studi.s: Recent advances in spatial omics have enabled tissue atlases spanning serial sections, donors, and experimental technologies. Aligning these datasets is essential for comparing spatial organization, reconstructing three-dimensional tissue architecture, and registering sections to a common coordinate framework. However, systematic comparisons of alignment accuracy, computational efficiency, and usability remain limited.

studi.t: Single-cell transcriptomics reveals conserved embryonic-like cell populations in different human cancers
studi.s: Background Embryonic development is governed by coordinated transcriptional programs that shape cellular differentiation and can be reactivated in cancer. However, whether tumors of distinct ontogenetic origins contain conserved tumor cell populations that recapitulate features of these developmental programs remains unclear.

studi.t: Reconciling the tempo and timing of eukaryote emergence with clade dynamics and the fossil record
studi.s: The timing of the last eukaryotic common ancestor (LECA) remains a fundamental ques- tion in evolutionary biology and palaeontology. Fossils with morphologies compatible with a eukaryotic-grade affinity are reported as early as 1780 Ma, but no crown-group supergroups are confidently identified before the end of the Mesoproterozoic (ca. 1050 Ma). Recently, the late LECA hypothesis suggests that this absence of crown-assignable fossils implies a late Mesoproterozoic origin of the crown.

studi.t: The ear receives only weak parametric information about saccade directions
studi.s: Eye movement-related eardrum oscillations (EMREOs) are acoustic signals recorded in the ear canal induced by saccades, whose amplitude and time course relate to the saccade vector. While horizontal saccades evoke robust, and largely opposing EMREO signals in the two ears, the reliability and informational content of vertical EMREOs has remained more elusive. Here, we analyzed bilateral EMREOs in human participants performing visually guided horizontal and vertical saccades. Consistent with previous work, horizontal saccades induced stereotyped, opposing waveforms across ears.

studi.t: Sequential predictive learning is a unifying theory for hippocampal representation and replay
studi.s: The hippocampus represents an animal's position in the environment and generates "replay" proposed to support recall, planning, and memory formation. Recently, it's been found that artificial neural networks trained to predict sensory inputs develop spatially-tuned cells, however, whether predictive learning can account for the ability to produce replay, or the hippocampus' representation of non-spatial variables, is unknown.

studi.t: Altered striatal dopamine dynamics and behavior in Grin2a mutant mice, a genetic mouse model of schizophrenia
studi.s: Schizophrenia (SCZ), a complex psychiatric disorder with a strong genetic basis, is thought to involve, at least in part, dopamine dysregulation in the striatum. Recent large-scale exome sequencing has identified multiple SCZ risk genes, including GRIN2A (encoding an NMDA (N-methyl-D-aspartate) receptor subunit) and AKAP11 (encoding a protein kinase A binding protein), which is also a risk gene for bipolar disorder (BD). However, the mechanisms by which these genetic risk factors perturb dopamine circuits and cause psychotic symptoms remain poorly understood.

studi.t: A signature of deep credit assignment in the human Orbitofrontal cortex
studi.s: Humans are remarkably efficient at learning from limited experience because they can generalize quickly. Doing so, however, requires first learning about the latent structures that govern outcomes. The dominant theoretical framework to understand this interactive cycle between learning task representations and generalisation is deep learning, which updates parameters throughout multi-layered neural networks using deep credit assignment. Yet, whether the brain uses a similar "deep" approach to learning is unclear.

studi.t: High basal autophagic activity in the brain revealed by systemic quantitative analysis using GFP-LC3-RFP mice
studi.s: Autophagy is a fundamental intracellular degradation pathway with vital physiological functions. Although it is well known that autophagy is activated during starvation, the extent of basal autophagy remains unclear owing to challenges in measuring autophagic flux in vivo. In this study, we developed autophagy reporter (GFP-LC3-RFP) mice and quantified basal autophagic flux across tissues by comparing normal and autophagy-deficient conditions. Comparative analyses revealed uniformly low basal autophagic flux during embryogenesis, but significant tissue-specific variation in adult mice.

studi.t: Multi-omic cardiac adaptation to exercise training identifies adaptive and disease-opposing signatures: findings from MoTrPAC
studi.s: BackgroundEndurance exercise reduces cardiovascular disease risk, but how this protection is mediated at the molecular level remains incompletely understood.

studi.t: Social Behavior in Mice Relies on a Capacity to Phosphorylate the Serotonin Transporter
studi.s: The biogenic amine 5-hydroxytryptamine (serotonin, 5-HT) regulates social behavior across the animal kingdom. Although drugs that promote 5-HT transporter (SERT)-mediated 5-HT efflux within the nucleus accumbens (NAc) enhance sociability, the extent to which endogenous mechanisms regulating SERT contribute to normal social behavior is unknown. Prior in vitro studies have shown that SERT trafficking and activity are controlled by transporter phosphorylation, with the Thr276 site required for rapid, protein kinase G (PKG)-dependent increases in SERT function.

studi.t: Quantal release through the fusion pore
studi.s: Exocytosis of neurotransmitters and peptides begins with the formation of a fusion pore that connects the vesicle lumen to the extracellular space. Release is completed when vesicles undergo full fusion. Here we show that full quanta of serotonin are released through a slowly closing fusion pore without full vesicle fusion. Amperometric recordings of serotonin release from dense-core vesicles in the axons of isolated Retzius neurons of the leech contained a subset of small release currents with a long biexponential decay.

studi.t: Modeling natural HIV-1 infection and immunopathogenesis in a lymphoid organ-chip
studi.s: Secondary lymphoid organs are the principal sites of HIV-1 replication, immune dysfunction and reservoir persistence, yet physiologically relevant human models of this microenvironment remain limited. Here we show that a microfluidic lymphoid organ-chip supports productive HIV-1 replication without exogenous T cell activation or cytokine supplementation. All six HIV-1 strains tested, including three CXCR4-tropic (X4) and three CCR5-tropic (R5) viruses, replicated productively in the chip, whereas matched static three-dimensional cultures supported only three.

studi.t: RNA structure probing with 4-base-recognizing RNA cutters
studi.s: To elucidate dynamic higher-order structures of RNA in human cells would be important not only to deeply understand the physiological functions of mRNA and non-coding RNA but also to establish precision medicine. tRNase ZL together with hook-type sgRNA works as a 4-base-recognizing RNA cutter. We thought that RNA structure probing using the RNA cutters with hook-type sgRNAs of various 4-base recognition sequences would provide valuable information on the higher-order structures of cellular RNA. In this study, we investigated the feasibility of this method in vitro.

studi.t: Requirement for the Sts1 Adaptor in Proteasome Nuclear Import Elucidated in a DNA Origami NPC Mimic
studi.s: The 26S proteasome, which is essential for eukaryotic protein homeostasis, comprises a 19S regulatory particle (RP) and 20S core particle (CP). Most proteasomes localize to the nucleus in exponentially growing cells, but their import mechanisms remain poorly understood. We have employed a nuclear pore complex (NPC)-mimic system to investigate translocation of the yeast proteasome in vitro. The system is built from DNA origami-based channels ("NuPODs") containing densely grafted Nsp1, a Phe-Gly (FG)-rich nucleoporin.

studi.t: Relative distance change rather than absolute distance drives auditory alerting
studi.s: The function of hearing as an early warning system relies partly on detecting the distance and motion of an object based on sound. Approaching - or looming - objects activate the human alerting system, but it is debated whether sounds in the immediate vicinity of the body achieve the same irrespective of the direction of motion and of sound intensity. We addressed this question by examining distance perception of and phasic alertness states evoked by virtual sonic motion into and within peripersonal and extrapersonal space, at high and low intensities, in normal-hearing adults.

studi.t: Dopamine shifts striatal ramping dynamics
studi.s: Diseases that disrupt dopamine impair cognition; however, it is unknown how dopamine affects neuronal networks that instantiate cognitive processing. We studied this problem in the dorsomedial striatum during interval timing, an elementary cognitive task requiring working memory and attention to estimate an interval of several seconds. Interval timing requires medium spiny neurons (MSNs) that ramp up or down over temporal intervals. While these neurons receive prominent dopaminergic input from the substantia nigra, it is unknown how dopamine modulates MSN activity during interval timing.

studi.t: DualBranchEEG: A Dual-Branch CNN BiLSTM Network with Temporal Attention and Spectral Features for Three Class EEG Seizure Classification
studi.s: Automated seizure detection from electroencephalography (EEG) is a key step toward closed-loop brain-computer interface (BCI) systems and clinical decision support. We present DualBranchEEG, a dual-branch network that fuses (i) a temporal branch--a three-block 1-D convolutional encoder, a two-layer bidirectional LSTM and an additive attention layer--operating on the raw z-scored waveform, with (ii) a spectral branch--an MLP on log-power spectral density (PSD) features from Welch's method.

studi.t: Causal dissociation of occipital and mid-fusiform contributions to human visual experience
studi.s: Visual experiences can arise without corresponding retinal input, as in imagery, dreams, and hallucinations. Influential models of visual mental imagery propose that mental images acquire their visual quality in early visual cortex. Direct intracranial electrical cortical stimulation (DIECS) causally probes which cortical sites can evoke visual experiences, and of what kind.

studi.t: Human hematopoietic development during the first year of life and its remodeling by neonatal Bacillus Calmette-Guerin vaccination
studi.s: Hematopoiesis and immune development are well defined in adults but remain poorly understood in early life, despite the neonatal period being critical for immune maturation. We map hematopoietic and immune programs across the first year of human life using single-nucleus epigenomic and transcriptomic profiling of circulating hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (cHSPCs), including Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) vaccinated infants to illustrate a controlled immune challenge.

studi.t: Retron-Eco9 ADP-ribosylates release factors to disrupt translation during phage infection
studi.s: Retrons are a major form of anti-phage defense in bacteria, but how they provide defense remains incompletely understood. The most common retron effector is a predicted nucleoside 2'-deoxyribosyltransferase (NDT). Here, we demonstrated that the NDT of retron-Eco9 is, in fact, a protein histidine ADP-ribosyltransferase that associates with the bacterial ribosome through an interaction with the stalk proteins bL7/bL12.

studi.t: Colibactin-induced DNA damage activates cGAS-STING signaling that is amplified by mitochondrial DNA release
studi.s: The microbiome-derived genotoxin colibactin induces oncogenic mutations that contribute to the development of colorectal cancer. Colibactin exposure also elicits inflammatory and senescence-associated responses. However, the cellular pathways that link colibactin-induced genotoxic stress to inflammation and senescence are poorly defined. Here, we show that colibactin causes cytoplasmic DNA accumulation and activates pro-inflammatory cGAS-STING signaling in human cells.

studi.t: NUP62 acts as T cell activation-dependent switch to regulate post nuclear import steps of HIV-1 replication in primary CD4 T cells
studi.s: Resting CD4 T cells resist productive HIV-1 infection. T cell activation licenses replication, increases nuclear pore complex (NPC) density, and alters chromatin organization. Paradoxically, HIV-1 nuclear import is more efficient in resting than in activated CD4 T cells, despite lower NPC abundance. Using activation-neutral gene editing in primary human CD4 T cells, we show that T cell activation reshapes nucleoporin (NUP) contributions to infection. The FG-nucleoporin NUP62 switches from an inhibitor of HIV infection in resting cells to a dependency factor in activated cells.

studi.t: A novel engineered T7 RNA polymerase produces therapeutic mRNA without inflammatory dsRNA byproducts
studi.s: The therapeutic application of in vitro transcribed (IVT) messenger RNA (mRNA) is constrained by double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) impurities generated by wild-type (WT) T7 RNA polymerase (RNAP). These impurities trigger innate immune responses via RIG-I and MDA5, suppressing protein translation. Conventional polymerase engineering often trades dsRNA reduction for lower transcription processivity. Here, we report engineered T7 RNAP variants that limit this trade-off.

studi.t: Physiological Culture Modulates the Cargo and Wound-Healing Potential of MSC Extracellular Vesicles
studi.s: This study demonstrates that animal-free 3D culture and long-term hypoxic conditioning modulate mesenchymal stromal cell-derived extracellular vesicle (MSC-EV) production and cargo composition without compromising MSC identity. Mimicking the in vivo microenvironment through hypoxic 3D culture increased MSC-EV yield and altered EV molecular composition, highlighting the potential of culture engineering as a strategy to optimise MSC-EV manufacturing.

studi.t: Cell type specific Rab Munc13-4 coupling defines divergent exosome fusion mechanisms and post-docking fusion pore opening
studi.s: Munc13-4 operates as an intracellular Ca2+ sensor for regulated secretion in both immune and cancer cells. Its capacity to physically engage multiple Rab GTPases and SNARE proteins places it at the center of membrane reorganization upon intracellular Ca2+ elevation. Here, we define the mode of action of Munc13-4 during Ca2+ evoked exosome secretion in RBL-2H3 mast cells. We show that Munc13-4 coupling to Rab27a is essential to retain Munc13-4 on secretory membranes for exosome release in mast cells, contrasting with cancer cells where the Munc13-4 Rab11 axis predominates.

studi.t: Sex differences and multiregional variation in placental gene expression in late-onset gestational hypertension
studi.s: Placental dysfunction has been associated with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy which are primarily characterized by high maternal blood pressure newly diagnosed after 20 weeks of gestation (gestational hypertension). Of these, early-onset preeclampsia ([≤] 34 weeks) has dominated previous research because it is associated with more severe adverse outcomes for the mother and fetus, but late-onset preeclampsia with mild features or late-onset gestational hypertension (>34 weeks) is much more common and can be life-threatening for the mother during pregnancy and increase the risk of…

studi.t: Functional Right Ventricular and Atrial Cardiomyocytes Generated from Human Pluripotent Stem Cell-derived Second Heart Field Progenitors
studi.s: Second heart field (SHF) progenitors give rise to distinct populations of cardiomyocytes (CMs) in developing heart including right ventricular (rv) and atrial (a) CMs, but robust methods to generate these CM types from human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) are lacking. Here we differentiated hPSCs to SHF progenitors, rvCMs and aCMs identified by scRNA-seq transcriptome analysis in comparison to FHF-derived left ventricular (lv) CMs. The hPSC-CM single cell transcriptomes overlapped human fetal heart transcriptomes supporting the chamber-specific identity.

studi.t: Biodiversity turnover in coastal marine eukaryotic plankton revealed by a 20-year metabarcoding time series
studi.s: Long-term observations are essential to resolve how ecosystems respond to environmental variability, yet decadal-scale molecular time series of marine plankton communities remain rare. Here, we analysed a >20-year (2001-2023) high-frequency 18S rRNA gene (V9) metabarcoding time series of eukaryotic plankton from a coastal observatory in the Western English Channel. Community composition exhibited recurrent seasonal cycles driven primarily by seawater temperature and water column stratification.

studi.t: Heritable variance in fitness in wild vertebrates accounts for a small share of their missing neutral diversity and exceeds what recurrent mutation is estimated to maintain
studi.s: Pedigree-based estimates show that wild populations carry substantial additive genetic variance in lifetime fitness. In classical theory, such variance reduces neutral diversity and is maintained by recurrent deleterious mutation. This variance is not expected to explain the missing genetic diversity of abundant species, but neither its share of that deficit nor the share maintained by mutation has been measured in individual natural populations.

studi.t: Population-scale measurement of human centromere array length variation from short-read sequencing
studi.s: Alpha-satellite higher-order repeat (HOR) arrays at human centromeres vary several-fold in length across individuals and have been linked to kinetochore function and chromosome missegregation. However, their repetitive megabase-scale architecture has largely restricted length measurement to a few hundred long-read derived genome assemblies, leaving short-read cohorts uncharacterized. Here we introduce cenlen, an alignment-free method that estimates active centromeric array lengths across all 24 human chromosomes directly from short-read or long-read CRAM files.

studi.t: Genomic conformation reflects epigenetic programming rather than gene expression
studi.s: Genome function is regulated temporally and tissue-specifically through coordinated interplay between epigenetic modifications and genomic elements, however, the extent to which chromatin conformation shapes or is shaped by epigenetic programming and transcriptional activity in vivo, remains largely unresolved. Through analysis of the well-characterised Dlk1-Dio3 imprinted domain, we have identified tissue and parent-of-origin specific conformations and taken a genetic approach to determine the hierarchical relationships between conformation, epigenetic state and transcription.

studi.t: A Framework for Identifying Determinants of Epigenomic State: Decoding Variable CTCF Occupancy and Contact Frequency
studi.s: CTCF binding is essential for delineating topologically associated domains, constraining enhancer-promoter interactions, and controlling gene expression. Many CTCF peaks are bound in all cell-types, but the mechanisms regulating cell-type-specific CTCF occupancy are not fully understood. Here, we present a general framework to comprehensively discover factors driving variable epigenomic state and TF occupancy. We apply this framework to CTCF ChIP-seq binding across hundreds of cell/tissues, and we identify five distinct mechanisms regulating CTCF occupancy.

studi.t: A hydrocarbon pheromone mediates ant group cohesion
studi.s: Social insect colonies are among the most cohesive groups in the animal kingdom, yet we know little about the signals and sensory mechanisms that underlie their collective unity. Here, we show that cuticular hydrocarbons (CHCs), low volatility compounds present on the insect body surface, play a central role in social cohesion in the clonal raider ant, Ooceraea biroi. CHCs are transferred from the body to the nest substrate, where they are sufficient to induce aggregation. Nest associated CHCs elicit aggregation across distinct O.

studi.t: Maillard reaction-derived furan aldehydes act as positive allosteric modulators of the calcium-sensing receptor CaSR
studi.s: Maillard reaction products contribute to flavor formation and flavor-enhancing effects during food processing; however, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. We previously identified 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (5-HMF), a major Maillard reaction intermediate, in heated shio-koji lees and showed that it prolongs the umami aftertaste. We investigated its effect on the calcium-sensing receptor (CaSR), implicated in kokumi perception, and the umami taste receptors T1R1/T1R3.

studi.t: BPQ_RNA: A Thermodynamically Informed, Hybrid Quantum-Classical Framework for RNA 2D Structure Prediction Including Chemical Modifications
studi.s: Predicting RNA secondary (2D) structural folds remains a Nondeterministic Polynomial-time (NP)-hard challenge. Existing quantum approaches predominantly rely on coarse-grained heuristics or classical stem pre-estimation, shifting core thermodynamic computations outside the quantum workflow and limiting localized structural precision. Here, we present a Base-Pair QUBO framework for RNA (BPQ_RNA), a hybrid pipeline that directly maps experimental Nearest Neighbor Database (NNDB)-derived free energies onto a gate-based quantum framework strictly at the base-pair level.

studi.t: Learning Protein Structure Representations through Joint-Embedding Prediction
studi.s: Motivation: Protein structure representations are often learned by reconstructing coordinates, yet reconstruction quality does not necessarily track performance on biological prediction tasks. We therefore investigate whether joint-embedding prediction can capture information useful for biological prediction while retaining recoverable backbone geometry. Results: We introduce PS-JEPA, a self-supervised model that learns protein structure representations by predicting masked residue embeddings from visible backbone context.

studi.t: GRACE: Discrete Biological Sequence Optimization with Gradient-Resolved Adaptive Constrained Exploration
studi.s: Machine learning increasingly enables biological sequence redesign for therapeutic and biotechnological applications by optimizing sequences for desired properties. However, improving one property can compromise another: for example, increasing enzyme activity may reduce stability, while enhancing regulatory DNA activity may diminish cell-type specificity.

studi.t: scXOrGAN: A Generative Framework for Cross-Organ Single-Cell Transcriptomic Translation
studi.s: Gene expression profiles of organs provide important insights into their health and disease states. However, while some organs can be sampled only through invasive procedures, others, such as blood, are readily accessible. Existing methods for predicting gene expression in one organ from another typically work with bulk or averaged profiles, obscuring cell specific differences. Translation at single-cell resolution is more challenging, because individual cells in the source and target organs lack direct correspondence.

studi.t: Bonds, a neighbourhood field and missing hydrogens: a transferable electron-density model of proteins
studi.s: A compound that has not been made has no diffraction data to refine against. A model of electron density that is to be used in drug design must therefore be transferable: the same numbers for every protein and every ligand, nothing fitted per structure. The independent-atom model (IAM) is transferable, but it places no density in bonds and lets no atom respond to its surroundings.

studi.t: Brillouin microscopy detects treatment-associated biophysical responses in live triple-negative breast cancer spheroids
studi.s: Mechanical changes are increasingly recognised as an integral component of tumour response to therapy and can be effectively used as a tumour biomarker in designing and testing new anticancer therapies. Assessing these changes in situ in a live tumour model, however, without disturbing cellular function, remains a challenge. We investigated dose-dependent responses to anticancer drugs in live three-dimensional triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) spheroids using label-free Brillouin microscopy, complemented by bulk compression testing and biological assays.

studi.t: ProFORGE: a composable sequence structure dynamics workflow validated by mechanoprotein design
studi.s: Designing a protein to resist tension requires identifying the contacts that bear the load. We developed ProFORGE to track residues as a scaffold changes length and to select designs by steered molecular dynamics. Starting with the 56-residue GB1 domain, we generated 14,542 candidates using protein language models for scaffold expansion and fixed-backbone design for sequence refinement. Of 182 sequences that passed the initial screen in the final round, 19 also met the AlphaFold 3 confidence threshold.

studi.t: Space partitioning by microtubules and molecular motors
studi.s: Cells contain radial arrays or polar bundles of microtubules that support their main functions. Active matter made of microtubules and molecular motors can transiently assemble radial asters or form nematic structures that continuously extend and fold. Whether such networks can reach dynamic steady states, as seen in cells, is not known. Here we asked whether confining two oppositely directed motors could generate dynamic, stable and regular organizations.

studi.t: A BMP-to-GREM1 cancer-associated fibroblast switch at the colorectal cancer invasive front, revealed by histology-anchored spatial transcriptomics
studi.s: Which fibroblast state signals to tumour cells at the colorectal cancer invasive front, and from what distance, has not been resolved in human tissue, and spatial transcriptomics obscures the answer whenever tumour regions are defined from the expression being analysed and RNA is assigned to the wrong, neighbouring cell. We introduce a histology-anchored framework that segments cells from H&E (OmiCoreSeg), maps the tumour from H&E alone (OmiCoreTumorDetector; area under the ROC curve 0.91 against pathologist annotation) and returns RNA to the cell that made it (OmiCoreCloud).

studi.t: Cost-information trade-offs partially rationalize the feed-forward loop census
studi.s: Gene transcription regulatory networks let cells encode an internal representation of their environment as patterns of protein expression. Among the thirteen connected directed subgraphs on three nodes, the feed-forward loop (FFL) is the one consistently over-represented in transcriptional networks relative to randomizations that preserve the node degrees, yet its eight structural variants occur very unequally: in Escherichia coli and Saccharomyces cerevisiae the C1 and I1 variants dominate and the other six are rare.

studi.t: Chinese hamster tissue and CHO cell transcriptomes reveal immortalization signatures and the factors driving lineage divergence
studi.s: Chinese Hamster Ovary (CHO) cells dominate biotherapeutic manufacturing but still have a few limitations in post-translational modifications such as N-glycan branching, O-glycan core extension and inefficient protein folding/processing. It is yet unclear whether these CHO-specific traits reflect general Chinese hamster biology or arise specifically from cell line immortalization. We assembled a uniformly processed transcriptome compendium of 350 RNA-seq samples from 24 studies, integrating nine native Chinese hamster tissues with four CHO lineages (CHO-K1, CHO-S, CHO-DG44, CHO-DXB11).

studi.t: Brain rhythms during Instagram Reels viewing and subsequent performance on sustained attention and working memory: an EEG study
studi.s: What does even a short scrolling 'snack' do to the brain? Short-form video feeds such as Instagram Reels have been rapidly becoming a near-universal phenomenon, used widely by people around the world, especially young adults. However, this is a very recent development, and yet their immediate effects on brain activity, attention, and working memory remain unclear. In a counterbalanced, within-subject experiment, we examined whether 10 minutes of Instagram Reels altered electroencephalographic (EEG) activity, cognitive performance, and subjective fatigue.

studi.t: Optimisation of femtosecond dispersion compensation at the sample using side-view two-photon fluorescence imaging
studi.s: Efficient two-photon absorption depends on compensating the dispersion of the whole excitation path. Building on established fluorescence-based adjustment, we describe a practical procedure that uses side-view images of fluorescence in a dye cuvette, independently of the microscope's scanning and detection, with reference records, stability warnings and open analysis software. For a 1045 nm laser, maxima lay between 21 and 24 screw turns in 11 of 13 sweeps.

studi.t: Acute Effects of Prolonged Intermittent Theta Burst Stimulation on Cortical Excitability: A Randomized Crossover TMS-EEG Study
studi.s: Background: prolonged intermittent theta burst stimulation (piTBS), as used in Stanford Neuromodulation Therapy (SNT), achieves antidepressant efficacy, yet its acute single-session mechanisms remain elusive. EEG can capture online oscillatory dynamics during piTBS and pre- to post-stimulation changes in TMS-evoked cortical reactivity. Methods: in a randomized, sham-controlled crossover trial, 40 healthy males completed two visits ( [≥]7-day washout), receiving active or sham piTBS over the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex.

studi.t: Scale-dependent predictability of microscopic brain structure from MRI using paired PS-OCT
studi.s: Cortical layering, fascicle geometry and tissue texture of the mouse brain lie in the mesoscopic range. That range sits below the hundred-micrometre sampling of a whole-brain magnetic resonance (MR) volume and above the micrometre structure of individual fibre bundles. Polarization-sensitive optical coherence tomography (PS-OCT) reaches into it, and MRI does not. Super-resolution models can enlarge an MR volume to any grid, but the grid size does not decide what the volume contains.

studi.t: Focused Ultrasound Neuromodulation: Disentangling Neural Signals from Mechanical Artifacts
studi.s: Transcranial focused ultrasound (tFUS) can noninvasively modulate neural activity in the human brain (Blackmore et al., 2019; Fomenko et al., 2018; Legon et al., 2014), and EEG, with millisecond resolution, is well suited to track the timing of cortical engagement. In humans, tFUS aimed at primary visual cortex (V1) has been reported to evoke phosphenes, with EEG peaks (N55, P100) during sonication (Lee et al., 2016).

studi.t: Conditional feature importance with error control for machine-learning-based biomarker discovery in Alzheimer's disease
studi.s: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is characterized by complex biology captured by proteomics, transcriptomics, genetics, and brain imaging. These high-dimensional and correlated data make biomarker discovery challenging. To disentangle biomedical AD data, we propose Conditional Feature Importance (CFI), a theory-grounded framework quantifying the unique contribution of individual or grouped variables in any machine learning model while controlling false discoveries.

studi.t: Microglia target parvalbumin-expressing interneurons and tune gamma oscillations through P2Y12-dependent IL-1 receptor signaling
studi.s: Adaptation of neuronal network activity is critical for maintaining brain homeostasis and coping with changing computational demands. Microglia, the brain's innate immune cells, are increasingly recognized to shape neuronal function in the healthy brain, yet their contribution to inhibitory circuit dynamics and network synchronization remains largely unexplored.

studi.t: Ongoing activity in anatomically recurrent cortex is predominantly feedforward
studi.s: The cerebral cortex is the major site of computation in the brain, and its recurrent wiring has motivated models in which repeated neuronal activation maintains information in stable attractor states. Large language models illustrate an alternative principle by transforming information layer by layer during each forward pass. A first step toward understanding what cortex and these models can teach us about each other is to establish whether feedforward dynamics can predominate in recurrent cortex.

studi.t: Functional balance between inhibitory and disinhibitory pathways predicts the heterogeneous effects of arousal on cortical timescales
studi.s: Cortical activity exhibits diverse timescales that vary with behavioral state, but the underlying circuit mechanisms remain unclear. Analyzing Allen Institute Neuropixels recordings from mouse primary visual cortex, we found that the fraction of excitatory neurons activated by optogenetic stimulation of somatostatin (SST) interneurons varied across mice. Intrinsic timescales lengthened during arousal in mice with a lower fraction of activated excitatory neurons and shortened in those with a higher fraction.

studi.t: SHANK3-actin cytoskeleton coupling regulates nanoscale remodelling of the postsynaptic density
studi.s: Dynamic remodelling of multiprotein signalling complexes allows cells to rapidly adapt signalling strength. At synapses, neurotransmitter receptors and scaffolds concentrate in subsynaptic nanoclusters that govern synaptic signalling strength and that are dynamically remodelled by synaptic activity. However, although this distinct nanoscale organization of synaptic protein complexes is well-established, the mechanisms that control the activity-induced reorganization of these complexes remain elusive.

studi.t: Mechanical role of dural structures and tumor material heterogeneity in brain tumor mass effect
studi.s: Brain tumor growth induces considerable deformation of the surrounding tissue, yet the mechanical contribution of intracranial dural structures and the influence of tumor material heterogeneity on mass effect remain poorly understood. In this study, we developed a heterogeneous finite element model of the brain to investigate the mechanical role of the falx cerebri and tentorium cerebelli and to determine how variations in tumor subregion stiffness influence the mechanical response of the brain. Two complementary analyses were performed.

studi.t: Neutrophil lectin-like oxidized low-density lipoprotein receptor (LOX-1) limits inflammatory injury during bacterial pneumonia.
studi.s: Pneumonia is an inflammatory condition that is caused by myriad microorganisms, necessitating broadly applicable therapeutics. Yet, host determinants of pneumonia severity remain poorly understood, demanding a more complete understanding of the cells and signals that control tissue homeostasis. Our group previously showed that the class E scavenger receptor lectin-like oxidized low-density lipoprotein receptor-1 (LOX-1) limits pneumonia-induced lung injury without affecting bacterial clearance, contrasting its well-established injurious effects in the setting of atherosclerosis.

studi.t: Stk11 deficiency promotes tumor CXCL16 secretion and a CXCL16-dependent expansion of Aregpos CXCR6pos Vγ6 γδT17 in lung cancer
studi.s: IL-17-producing gamma delta ({gamma}{delta}T17) T cells can promote tumor growth and metastasis. How the tumor microenvironment controls the activation, expansion, and function of {gamma}{delta}T17 in different cancers remains unclear. Using an autochthonous model of KrasG12D/Stk11-driven lung adenocarcinoma coupled with scRNAseq and V(D)J profiling, we found that KrasG12DStk11-loss tumors induced a rapid expansion of lung CXCR6+ V{gamma}4 and amphiregulin-expressing CXCR6+ V{gamma}6{gamma}{delta}T17 cells.

studi.t: CNS-derived SerpinA3n restricts pathogenesis during WNV encephalitis via suppression of inflammatory protease activity
studi.s: Proteolytic activity is integral to host immune defense, yet little is known about how proteolytic homeostasis is maintained in the central nervous system (CNS) during viral infection. Here, we investigated roles for the serine protease inhibitor SerpinA3n in promoting host protection during West Nile virus (WNV) encephalitis. WNV neuroinvasion was accompanied by widespread induction of serpin expression, including SerpinA3n.

studi.t: CD33-CAR iNKT cells overcome acute myeloid leukemia heterogeneity by activating CD8+ T cells and enhancing tumor immunogenicity
studi.s: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) exhibits extensive inter- and intra-patient antigenic heterogeneity, representing a major obstacle for chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-based therapies. Cellular platforms that combine potent direct cytotoxicity with the ability to engage endogenous immune responses may help overcome this limitation. Invariant natural killer T (iNKT) cells are particularly attractive for allogeneic immunotherapy because of their lack of alloreactivity and their capacity to promote cross-priming of conventional T cells.

studi.t: From Substrate to Short Chain Fatty Acids: An In Vitro Investigation of Bacterial Dynamics in the Porcine Colon using the Modified Hohenheim Gas Test
studi.s: Background: Research on the development of pig colonic bacteria under in vitro conditions is limited. In this in vitro study, the modified Hohenheim Gas Test (modHGT) was used to improve the understanding of fermentation processes in the pig colon with respect to the underlying microbial community, in particular how different substrates modulate the microbial community structure during fermentation.

studi.t: Maternal periconceptional nutrition is associated with the vaginal microbiome along pregnancy
studi.s: The human vaginal microbiome has been repeatedly associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, and therefore understanding lifestyle factors associated with it may provide insights into strategies for improving pregnancy and reproductive health. The periconceptional period is a critical time window in pregnancy, with nutrition seen as a key factor for pregnancy health. However, the associations between periconceptional nutrition and the vaginal microbiome along pregnancy remain underexplored.

studi.t: Caspase Activity Affects Cell Cycle and Chromosome Integrity after Genome Editing in Human Hematopoietic Stem and Progenitor Cells
studi.s: Therapeutic genome editing introduces DNA double-strand breaks into hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs), making chromosome integrity an important consideration for edited cell function. We investigated how caspase activity influences cellular responses to genome editing in primary human HSPCs. Caspase inhibition increased the fraction of phospho-histone H3-S10-positive cells and reduced micronucleus formation and DNA damage after editing. Genome editing was associated with reduced detection of BUB1 and H2A-T120p at centromeres, with partial restoration after caspase inhibition.

studi.t: A bacterial pathogen reveals a new mechanism of micron-scale nucleocytoplasmic transport
studi.s: In addition to its canonical role as a selective barrier, the nuclear envelope is increasingly recognized as a dynamic structure, remodeled to integrate mechanical cues. Here, we discover that the bacterial pathogen Rickettsia parkeri deforms the nuclear envelope to an unprecedented degree to invade and exit human cell nuclei through large membrane protrusions.

studi.t: Buildings act as barriers to insects, decoupling the bacterial-dominated and insect-dominated phases of carcass decomposition
studi.s: The dynamics of necrophagous insect communities and the decomposition of the cadavers they colonise can be modulated by ecological filtering limiting insect access. We examine how different degrees of confinement influence the decomposition of animal carcasses, their colonisation by necrophagous insects, and the link between these two processes. To this end, vertebrate carcasses were placed either outdoors or in sheds with open or closed windows in a replicated experiment. Over two weeks, decomposition and insect abundance were documented daily.

studi.t: Beyond suppression: a stand-off effect of mitigation measure reduces seabird bycatch in pelagic longline fisheries
studi.s: Bycatch in longline fisheries is one of the causes of population decline in albatrosses and other pelagic seabirds worldwide, and tori-lines and weighted branch lines are the mitigation measures most widely deployed to address this threat. Despite their widespread use, it remains unclear exactly how these devices reduce bycatch and whether combining them provides added protection beyond either device alone.

studi.t: Evolutionary dynamics with directed updating rules
studi.s: Evolutionary game theory describes how the frequencies of strategies change in a population when individuals imitate others who have higher payoffs. Models of imitation typically assume that updating is undirected, so that any individual may adopt the strategy of any other. But in many systems some replacements occur in one direction only: in a food chain, for example, a predator species can replace its prey but not the reverse. Here we study replicator dynamics with directed updating rules in a generalized Rock-Paper-Scissor game, in which each strategy can replace only one of the other two.

studi.t: A small set of morphological metrics describes wing-planform plasticity: a correlational analysis in a population of the European grapevine moth Lobesia botrana (Lepidoptera: Tortricidae)
studi.s: The insect wing is a complex morpho-functional organ, and it remains unclear whether a set of well-defined metrics can fully capture wing-planform variation. To address this question, we digitised 339 male forewings of the European grapevine moth, Lobesia botrana (Lepidoptera: Tortricidae), an economically important grapevine pest. Specimens came from two non-overlapping seasonal flight generations.

studi.t: Limited biological identifiability of dominance-labelled variance components in polyploid genomic prediction
studi.s: Genomic prediction models for polyploid crops often partition genetic variance into additive and dominance-labelled components, but a fitted dominance component is not necessarily identifiable as digenic dominance (D2). We combined known-truth simulations with a panel-conditioned diagnostic workflow on 11 public datasets from alfalfa, potato, blueberry, guinea grass, rose, Miscanthus, sweetpotato and sugarcane. The workflow uses kernel geometry, permutation references, structure controls, planted-D2 spike-ins, posterior uncertainty and paired prediction tests.

studi.t: AHCY inhibition reshapes DNA methylation and transcriptional regulation in colorectal cancer cells
studi.s: DNA methylation is an important epigenetic mechanism regulating gene expression, and its maintenance depends on cellular methyl group metabolism. Adenosylhomocysteinase (AHCY) is a key enzyme in the methionine cycle that hydrolyzes S-adenosylhomocysteine (SAH), thereby preventing its accumulation and inhibition of methyltransferase activity. Although AHCY has been implicated in cancer cell proliferation and transcriptional regulation, the effects of its inhibition on genome-wide DNA methylation and their relationship to gene expression remain poorly understood in colorectal cancer (CRC).

studi.t: Genotoxic stress and clonal expansion shape the somatic genome of systemic sclerosis skin
studi.s: Background: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a life-limiting inflammatory disease characterised by skin and visceral fibrosis. We previously showed that fibrotic skin from patients with diffuse cutaneous SSc (dcSSc) accumulates a large number of somatic mutations, although the mechanisms that generate them and their disease-related consequences remain poorly understood.

studi.t: The genome sequence of the reef-building coral Cyphastrea microphthalma from the Persian/Arabian Gulf
studi.s: We present a genome assembly from the coral species Cyphastrea microphthalma from the southern Persian/Arabian Gulf (Cnidaria; Anthozoa; Hexacorallia; Scleractinia; Merulinidae). The assembly is 681.2 Mb in size, spanning 5,554 scaffolds with a contig N50 of 244.4 kb. The assembly has a BUSCO completeness of 94.1% (single = 85.1%, duplicated = 9%, fragmented = 1.6%, missing = 4.3%) using the metazoa_odb10 reference set (n = 954). Genome annotation identified 24,716 protein-coding genes (including 10 pseudogenes) and a high repeat content of 63.4%.

studi.t: A stratified benchmark reveals distinct short- and long-read performance gradients within difficult genomic regions
studi.s: Accurate detection of small variants underpins population, functional and clinical genomics, yet short-read sequencing remains unreliable in repetitive and duplicated regions of the human genome, where long reads provide substantially greater sequence context. Although this disparity is well documented, aggregate accuracy metrics delineate where short- and long-read callsets diverge but not the mechanisms that give rise to these differences.

studi.t: HDX-MS for Analysis of Protein Dynamics in Complex and Crowded Cellular Environments
studi.s: Hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS) offers potent insights into protein conformational dynamics and interactions but traditionally requires proteins to be purified to near homogeneity and to be removed from their native cellular context which is often challenging for unstable, untagged, or difficult-to-purify targets. Here we present crude-HDX (crHDX) a workflow that we used to extend HDX-MS analysis progressively from purified proteins to unfractionated cell lysates and, ultimately, intact cells.

studi.t: Scalable direct mapping of signal-transduction dynamics using protein-assembly recorders
studi.s: The timing and coordination of signaling events within signal-transduction cascades shape cellular behavior. Protein-assembly recorders empower signaling dynamics study by scalable spatiotemporal mapping of downstream transcriptional outputs, yet we still lack a general mechanism to directly write signal-transduction dynamics.

studi.t: Transient mRNA-LNP Delivery of the Tardigrade Protein Dsup Protects Airway Epithelium from Bleomycin-Induced Injury
studi.s: Bleomycin is an essential component of chemotherapy regimens used for Hodgkin lymphoma and germ cell tumors, but its clinical utility is restricted by pulmonary toxicity that forces dose reduction or discontinuation in around 10% of patients. There are currently no approved strategies that prophylactically protect the lungs, representing a significant unmet clinical need. Bleomycin generates reactive oxygen species (ROS) within the alveolar epithelium, causing alveolar cell death and senescence and driving maladaptive crosstalk with stromal cells.

studi.t: Robust single-cell analysis through subsampling reveals hidden naive T cell states in aging
studi.s: Single-cell genomics has been instrumental for studying the variation between cell states. Yet, the use of single-cell technologies to study variation between sample groups remains challenging, with findings often failing to replicate across cohorts. Here, we introduce a general framework for robust single-cell analysis that uses subsampling of individuals to identify statistical patterns that hold regardless of which unmeasured characteristics of those individuals covary with the condition of interest.

studi.t: Argonomics Explorer: an interactive database for dissecting Argonaute-RNA regulatory networks
studi.s: Argonaute (AGO) family proteins associate with small RNAs (sRNAs) to form complexes that direct sequence-specific regulation of target RNAs. Recent studies in Caenorhabditis elegans, Drosophila melanogaster, and human cell lines have systematically characterized the repertoire of sRNA associations and targets for individual AGOs in these organisms; however, the lack of an accessible, searchable platform limits efficient comparison of the specificity and redundancy of Argonaute functions.

studi.t: Automated benchmarking with structured variant effect data
studi.s: Protein variant effect prediction (VEP) has a wide range of applications, from describing the role of mutations in human disease to improving enzymes for industrial applications. VEP is now predominantly powered by machine learning models and high-throughput experimentation. Progress in this field depends on fair and systematic model comparison, which is complicated by the heterogeneity of VEP tasks and the diversity of model implementations. ProteinGym is the most widely used VEP benchmark, but it does not have a standard representation for datasets or models.

studi.t: RBAi Scholar: Semantic and Hybrid biomedical literature Search for Researchers and AI assistants
studi.s: Motivation: A keyword search for mitochondrial dysfunction can miss a paper that says impaired mitochondrial function, so an empty result does not show that no such paper exists. Search by meaning addresses this mismatch, but it blurs exact strings such as gene symbols. Results: We present RBAi Scholar, which lets researchers and AI assistants search a growing corpus of biomedical abstracts by meaning (semantic search), by keyword, or by meaning among the papers that contain a required term (hybrid search). We tested it on a fixed version of 11.1 million records.

studi.t: Adaptive Representations for Real-World Enzyme Optimization
studi.s: Protein fitness landscapes are highly rugged, giving rise to complex optimization landscapes. Bayesian optimization (BO) with Gaussian processes (GPs) is widely used in protein engineering for its sample efficiency and calibrated uncertainty estimates. Here, we study a joint fine-tuning framework of a protein language model (PLM) and a GP across enzyme fitness landscapes that span various distinct mutation regimes encountered in real-world engineering campaigns.

studi.t: AUTOENCODIX: powering a hub for biological representation learning models
studi.s: Autoencoders are a foundational architecture for biological representation learning and empower methods for denoising, multi-modal integration, explainable embeddings, and synthetic data generation. But, new architectures are scattered across isolated repositories, which hampers benchmarking, the reuse of pretrained models, and the transfer to new data modalities. Here, we present the next generation of AUTOENCODIX, a Python package and model hub for biological representation learning.

studi.t: Resplitting LIT-PCBA with MolSCISSOR: A Memory-Efficient, Quasi-Deterministic Framework for Reducing Structural and Physicochemical Biases
studi.s: Reliable training-test partitioning is essential for developing and evaluating virtual screening (VS) methods, particularly in the era of machine learning (ML). However, existing molecular dataset splitting approaches do not simultaneously address key challenges in rigorous VS evaluation: cross-partition structural bias, test-set inter-class physicochemical bias, high memory requirements, limited scalability, stochastic allocation, a lack of automated optimization and of flexible training-test similarity control.

studi.t: Capturing human expertise for AI-assisted molecular structure annotation
studi.s: We developed a large language model-based tool that captures expert reasoning in bile acid structure elucidation, drawing on hand written notebooks, scientific literature, and recorded voice-to-text analytical sessions. It generates human-readable reports detailing evidence for and against candidate structures, tracing each inference to its source and identifying ambiguities. When applied to data, the tool proposes bile acid conjugates lacking reference spectra.

studi.t: A Genome-Scale Virtual Escherichia coli in the L++ Language
studi.s: A virtual organism is a computational model, mechanistic or learned from data, that predicts how a living system grows, adapts and responds to genetic edits, drugs and environments. As a first step toward such a model, we are building a virtual Escherichia coli, and here we present its first version, E. coli version 1.0, written for K-12 MG1655 in the L++ programming language. The model writes the cell as a biologist reads it, in one cell definition that compiles to 33,246 species and 41,649 reactions over 4,484 gene loci.

studi.t: HapAdapter: A Transfer Learning Protocol for DNA Foundation Models Adapted to Diploid Personal Epigenomes
studi.s: The rapid rise of large language models (LLMs) has spurred the development of genomic language models (gLMs) that capitalize on the key features of natural language present in biological sequences. Moreover, DNA foundation models, a sub-class of gLMs, have demonstrated impressive accuracy in predicting a wide range of functional tracks from DNA sequence input. However, current DNA foundation models are exclusively trained on haploid reference genome sequences -- despite personal and graph genomes becoming the new standard for genomic analyses.

studi.t: Inferring transcriptional bursting dynamics from scSLAM-seq data
studi.s: Transcription is a bursty, stochastic process. How transcriptional regulators reshape bursting dynamics during cellular responses remains poorly understood, largely because most single-cell RNA sequencing experiments measure only steady-state RNA abundance. Here, we present buRst, a probabilistic framework that infers burst frequency, burst size, and RNA degradation rates from metabolically labeled single-cell RNA sequencing (scSLAM-seq) during acute perturbations, without assuming steady state.

studi.t: GeneArbiter improves plant genome annotations while preserving established gene models
studi.s: As plant genome resources expand, updating established annotations requires incorporating improved gene models without disrupting correct structures or stable identifiers. We developed GeneArbiter, an evidence guided framework that treats annotation updating as a correction preservation problem. GeneArbiter uses the current annotation as a backbone, integrates alternative models with RNA splice junction and homologous protein evidence, and applies constrained language model arbitration followed by deterministic release and identifier reconciliation.

studi.t: Length and Mg2+ dependent conformational changes in homopolymeric single-stranded RNA sequences
studi.s: Despite the important functional roles of single-stranded RNA molecules in a number of biological processes, relatively little is known about their conformational ensemble, especially in divalent cations. We use the coarse-grained Three Interaction Site model for RNA (TIS-RNA) to determine the structural changes in rA30, rA120, and rU30 as a function of Mg2+ concentration at a fixed monovalent concentration. The Mg2+-dependent excess ions around rA30 and rU30, obtained in simulations, are in good agreement with experiments.

studi.t: A single LIM domain is sufficient for strain-selective binding of zyxin to F-actin
studi.s: Cells sense mechanical cues through force-dependent changes in protein binding and activity, and the actin cytoskeleton is a central conduit for these forces. Zyxin and other LIM (Lin-11, Isl-1, Mec-3) domain proteins accumulate on strained F-actin through their LIM containing region (LCR), a process we term strain-selective binding.

studi.t: Fundamental limits on fluorescence lifetime estimation using optical gating
studi.s: Fluorescence lifetime imaging (FLIM) is a promising approach for quantitative measurement in biology. Traditional lifetime measurements have limited photon throughput and slow acquisition speed due to photon counting electronics and point-scanning detectors. Wide-field imaging with optical gating can overcome these limitations. We analyze lifetime estimation precision for both single- and bi-exponential decays with optical gating waveforms.

studi.t: MembraneCurvature: A Python tool to calculate membrane curvature from molecular dynamics simulations.
studi.s: Biological membranes are complex structural and functional assemblies that play central roles in many cellular processes. They are primarily composed of lipids and proteins, whose dynamics and interactions are commonly investigated at the molecular level using Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations. Local membrane curvature, arising from changes in lipid composition and lipid-protein interactions, is an important property linked to lipid and protein sorting as well as protein mechanisms of action.

studi.t: Clustering conformations from molecular dynamics simulations by gradient flow segmentation of projected free energy landscapes
studi.s: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations sample a continuum of conformations whose populations can reveal distinct protein structural states and substates as well as different ligand binding states. Determining which conformations belong to each state remains a central challenge in interpreting protein structural dynamics and ligand binding. Building on our framework for constructing free-energy surfaces from principal component projections of MD trajectories, we treat these surfaces as images.

studi.t: Virtual Transcriptomics from Routine Histopathology Reveals Metastasis-Associated Programs and Molecular Risk States in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
studi.s: Background: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is a highly aggressive and biologically heterogeneous disease for which reliable biomarkers of metastatic progression remain limited. Although transcriptomic profiling can reveal clinically important molecular programs, its routine implementation is constrained by cost, tissue availability, and workflow complexity. We hypothesized that metastasis-associated transcriptional states are encoded within routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) histopathology and can be recovered using artificial intelligence enabled virtual transcriptomics.

studi.t: Pharmaceutical agent cetylpyridinium chloride modulates mitochondrial dynamics to enhance calcium-stimulated immune mast cell function
studi.s: The public is routinely exposed to quaternary ammonium compound cetylpyridinium chloride (CPC) through myriad personal care, food, and cleaning products. However, at exposure-relevant and non-cytotoxic doses, CPC exerts mitochondrial- and neurotoxicity, even crossing the blood brain barrier. Previously, our lab showed that CPC inhibits IgE-mediated mast cell function (degranulation) by hampering early tyrosine phosphorylation events and signaling of the lipid PIP2, though direct CPC effects on the downstream portion of the pathway remained unknown.

studi.t: A Novel Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme 2 Fusion Protein Reduces Cardiotoxic Effects of Doxorubicin
studi.s: Background: Anthracyclines, such as doxorubicin, are a cornerstone of chemotherapy and are the first-line therapy for high-risk breast cancer. Doxorubicin, however, induces dose-dependent cardiotoxicity that can lead to acute and chronic heart failure. In clinical studies with serial measurement of left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), targeting the Renin-Angiotensin System (RAS) with angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors was effective in ? 40% of patients (responders), but in 45% of patients, there was no response in LVEF.

studi.t: Isoflurane and Injectable Anaesthesia Differentially Affect Optoretinography Signals in C57BL/6J Mice
studi.s: Abstract Purpose: Anaesthesia is commonly required to immobilise mice in preclinical ophthalmic studies but also alters systemic physiology. We investigate the effects of three anaesthetics on optoretinography (ORG) measurements obtained by functional optical coherence tomography (OCT). Methods: A total of 14 adult C57BL/6J mice (5 female and 9 male) were grouped in three cohorts. Each cohort was alternatingly exposed to isoflurane (ISO), ketamine-xylazine (KX) and a mixture of medetomidine, midazolam, fentanyl and ketamine (MMFK).

studi.t: Multi-scale three-dimensional visualization and analysis of barley anatomy using X-ray computed tomography
studi.s: Methods of determining plant anatomy often rely on time-consuming preparation techniques and targeted sampling of tissues of assumed importance. This typically involves single plane 2D examination over small profiles of sub-sampled plant tissue with limited ability for 3D extrapolation of internal anatomies of plant organs. This limitation can create phenotyping bottlenecks. These bottlenecks are particularly acute in plant species that are larger than commonly used model systems, which have typically been selected for their small size and suitability for high-density growth.

studi.t: The thylakoid K+ exchange antiporter KEA3 affects NPQ dynamics and growth in the green algae Chlamydomonas reinhardtii
studi.s: The highly variable environmental conditions that photosynthetic organism experience in nature require rapid and long-term acclimatory responses. Light and CO2 availability are tightly linked within the cell. When light intensity rises, CO2 fixation accelerates, causing intracellular CO2 to become limiting for photosynthesis. Nonphotochemical quenching (NPQ) mechanisms prevent over excitation of the photosynthetic electron transport chain and consequent damage by reactive oxygen species.

studi.t: Methamphetamine acute exposure induces mitochondrial fragmentation in ventral tegmental area dopamine neurons
studi.s: Methamphetamine (METH) is a potent psychostimulant that primarily acts on the dopaminergic system and has strong reinforcing effects. It also induces oxidative stress, impairs mitochondrial function, and causes neurotoxicity at high doses. We previously showed that long-term METH self-administration increases mitochondrial respiratory metabolism and reduces antioxidant capacity in the mesolimbic dopaminergic circuit. However, the effects of METH exposure on mitochondrial structure in dopamine neurons remained unexplored.

studi.t: Repeated transcranial ultrasound is associated with altered temporal organization of spontaneous wheel activity during sleep disruption in mice
studi.s: Background: Motor-cortex-targeted transcranial ultrasound stimulation (tUS) can influence neural activity and motor responses, but its relationship to spontaneous behavior during sleep disruption (SD) remains unclear. Objective: To examine how repeated tUS during sustained SD relates to the temporal organization of spontaneous running and inactivity bouts. Methods: We recorded wheel activity in 36 mice for 17 days. On Days 13-17, mice in control (Ctrl) or wheel-confinement SD housing received bilateral motor-cortex-targeted tUS or sham.

studi.t: A Cross-Tissue Multi-Omics Atlas of Brain Transcriptomes and Liquid Biopsy EV Proteomes in Parkinson's Disease and Multiple System Atrophy
studi.s: Parkinson's disease (PD) and Multiple System Atrophy (MSA) are progressive synucleinopathies characterized by widespread molecular alterations across neuronal and glial populations. While brain tissue provides direct insight into disease mechanisms, liquid biopsies, particularly extracellular vesicles (EVs) in plasma, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), and urine, offer a minimally invasive avenue for clinical diagnosis and monitoring. However, the extent to which cell-type-specific brain transcriptional changes translate into detectable circulating protein signatures remains unclear.

studi.t: Ultra-Fast Signals during Spreading Depolarizations
studi.s: Spreading depolarizations (SDs) are major pathophysiological events implicated in various brain diseases. Hallmarks of SD include a negative DC shift, reflecting near-complete neuronal depolarization, and the depression of cortical activity. Using microelectrode field potential recordings from the rat cortex, we found that, in contrast to the depression of activity in conventional AC frequency bands (0.5-1000 Hz), high-potassium-induced SDs were associated with increased local field potential power at ultra-fast frequencies (4-8 kHz), which we term the Ultra-Fast Signal (UFS).

studi.t: Non-Ordinary Visual Spaces, Self-Motion and Sense of Agency in Near-Death Experiences
studi.s: Near-death experiences (NDEs) are a subset of non-ordinary states consciousness in which people frequently report unusual perceptions of space and self-motion. How the occurrence of self-motion varies across the visual-field boundary configurations described in first-person accounts remains underinvestigated. Alongside a semi-structured digital questionnaire, participants represented their NDE visual spaces schematically, outlining visual-field boundaries and marking self-location and self-motion direction.

studi.t: A Spatiotemporal Code for Cognitive Flexibility in the Mid-Posterior Cerebellar Cortex
studi.s: Cognitive flexibility is the critical ability to adapt behavior in changing environments. Although traditionally associated with the prefrontal cortex, behavioral, lesion, and functional imaging evidence suggests the cerebellum contributes to cognitive flexibility. To test the role of the cerebellum at the circuit level, we paired widefield calcium imaging of single-cell Purkinje cells with a cognitive flexibility task and computational behavioral model.

studi.t: Network size regulates the balance between reuse and reconstruction of neural dynamics during reversal learning
studi.s: Neural system size is a fundamental quantitative property that may influence cognitive function. While larger neural systems have been associated with enhanced cognitive performance, how system size contributes to cognitive flexibility remains poorly understood. In particular, it is unclear whether size influences not only how efficiently a system learns but also how previously established neural dynamics are reorganized when learned associations must change. We addressed this question using recurrent neural networks trained on a reversal learning task.

studi.t: Contextual Guidance and Suppression in Visual Search: Probing Learned Attentional Settings With a Color Singleton
studi.s: How does learning a spatial context shape the selection of a newly salient distractor? In two eye-tracking experiments (26 participants each), observers searched for a T among Ls in repeated (Old) or novel (New) configurations. A designated distractor occupied a fixed or variable location and became a red color singleton in the second session. Repeated configurations predicted a stable target location in Experiment 1 but not in Experiment 2. Familiar configurations yielded faster responses alongside an increased probability of initial saccades toward fixed-location singletons.

studi.t: Assessing gait control from short time series using a geometric characterization of stride-by-stride corrections
studi.s: Gait variability in healthy adults exhibits Long-Range Autocorrelations (LRA), reflecting long-term statistical dependencies between stride intervals. Previous studies have interpreted LRA within an optimal control framework, where stride length and duration are regulated in a coordinated manner to maintain a constant walking speed. Such objective offers redundancy among gait parameters that achieve success. In this context, imposing constraints on the walking cadence reduces this redundancy and leads to a loss of LRA.

studi.t: Prior Experience Alters Exploration in Standard Behavioral Assays More Robustly Than Sex or Light/Dark Cycle in C57BL/6J Mice
studi.s: Circadian phase during testing, biological sex, and repeated exposure to the same testing apparatus are all experimental variables known to impact outcomes in neurobehavioral studies. However, the combined, interactive effects of these intrinsic and extrinsic variables on common behavioral tests are not well established, and the effect of repeated testing is particularly understudied.

studi.t: Angiostrongylus cantonensis fifth-stage larvae Excretory-Secretory Products Induce Presenilin-1-Associated Molecular Changes and Inflammatory Responses in Mouse Astrocytes
studi.s: Background Parasite infection may cause significant effects on the immune response in the host brain. Previous studies have demonstrated that excretory-secretory products (ESPs) released by fifth-stage larvae (L5) of Angiostrongylus cantonensis induce inflammatory responses in mouse astrocytes. However, the underlying molecular mechanisms involved in ESP-induced neuroinflammation remain unclear. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying inflammatory responses in mouse astrocytes following treatment with A. cantonensis L5 ESPs.

studi.t: Hepatocyte NMD restrains inflammation and is impaired in alcohol-associated hepatitis
studi.s: Nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (NMD) limits the abundance of transcripts containing premature termination codons (PTCs) and regulates other endogenous mRNAs. How distinct transcripts respond to reduced NMD capacity in liver disease remains poorly understood. Here, we found that hepatic UPF1 and UPF2 protein abundance was markedly reduced in human alcohol-associated hepatitis.
