Hepatocyte-specific Upf2 deletion in mice caused liver injury, cell death, and macrophage accumulation, with innate immune gene induction evident by day 11.

studi.t: A novel simultaneous RNA extraction workflow from mouse Retinal Pigmented Epithelial (RPE) and retina
studi.s: Purpose: In Posterior Segment Eye Diseases (PSEDs), the homeostatic relation between retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and retina is disrupted. A better understanding of the transcriptomic changes occurring in different ocular cell types can help to elucidate disease mechanisms. Currently, there is no complete detailed workflow describing the process of simultaneous RNA isolation from RPE and retina separately. In this paper, our aim was to develop an easy, reproducible protocol for simultaneous isolation of RNA from both murine RPE and retina.

studi.t: Transgene-free immortalisation of bovine satellite cells by genetic disruption of CDKN2A
studi.s: Production of cultivated meat demands a supply of cells that differentiate into muscle, even after extended proliferation. As primary bovine satellite cells (PrimSCs) lose proliferation and differentiation capacity over prolonged culture, immortalised cell lines are necessary for rapid commercialisation. Here, we report the first evidence of a transgene-free single knockout mRNA-hit-and-run-based strategy that yields immortalised bovine satellite cells (ImmSCs). We demonstrate targeted disruption of CDKN2A alone is sufficient to immortalise SCs from three cow breeds.

studi.t: A Tunable Centromere-inheritance Switch Links DNA Replication to Germline Regeneration and Reproductive Aging
studi.s: Centromeres direct chromosome segregation and are defined not by DNA sequence but by CENP-A-containing chromatin, raising the question of how centromeric identity is faithfully transmitted through DNA replication, and whether this process influences stem cell behavior. In the Drosophila male germline, germline stem cells (GSCs) assemble asymmetric sister centromeres linked to non-random sister-chromatid segregation, but how this asymmetry is established and whether it contributes to germline function remain unclear.

studi.t: Spiny mice are resistant to retinal fibrosis and display a capacity for ganglion cell recovery after NMDA-induced injury
studi.s: Degenerative eye diseases affect millions of people and can ultimately lead to blindness. Facilitating regeneration of retinal neurons in mammals could prevent or slow vision loss. Spiny mice (genus Acomys) display remarkable regenerative abilities across many tissues, including the spinal cord. Utilizing the neurotoxin NMDA to damage inner retinal neurons, we assessed the response to retinal damage in Acomys using the well documented response of Mus musculus as a baseline for comparison.

studi.t: Non-structural carbohydrate pools suggest nitrogen limitation of photosynthesis in drought-limited boreal forest
studi.s: Boreal forests were commonly known to be limited in their productivity by low temperatures and low nitrogen (N) availability. Recently, evidence has accumulated that an increasing boreal forest area has switched from temperature limitation to drought limitation. Co-limitation by N in drought-limited boreal forests is hardly studied.

studi.t: Genomic signatures of cognitive evolution in birds
studi.s: The ability to invent novel behavioral solutions was a crucial factor in the success of Homo species. Beyond humans, high levels of innovation have evolved independently across several animal lineages, including birds. Birds provide a particularly striking example, with highly innovative species distributed across multiple clades, creating an opportunity to investigate whether independent origins of this phenotype involve recurring evolutionary mechanisms.

studi.t: Slow mitochondria, long life: a phylogenetic comparative analysis in 41 avian species
studi.s: Mitochondrial aerobic metabolism is thought to play a central role in the mechanisms underlying aging. However, because metabolism scales with body mass, which strongly predicts lifespan, disentangling the relationship between mitochondrial metabolism and lifespan from the shared allometric scaling of both traits with body mass remains a persistent challenge.

studi.t: Comparative Metagenomic Analysis of Chondrosia and Chondrilla Sponge Microbiomes Reveals Distinct Symbiotic Communities, Functional Potential, and Contrasting Environmental Responses
studi.s: Marine sponges frequently maintain distinct, host-specific microbial communities despite inhabiting overlapping or identical environments. In this study, we performed comparative shotgun metagenomic sequencing on two sympatric sponge taxa, Chondrilla and Chondrosia, collected from the same shallow-water habitat in the Florida Keys to examine whether differences in microbiome composition and functional potential persist under shared environmental conditions.

studi.t: Structural Complexity in the Maize Pangenome Graph Is Generated by Transposable Elements and Sorted by Selection
studi.s: Pangenome graphs capture the structural variation that linear references miss, but what generates their complex regions, whether these are targets of selection and whether the structural context of a gene affects its expression is unknown. These questions were addressed with a graph of 58 chromosome level maize assemblies (57 inbred lines and a teosinte accession), a genome dominated by transposable elements (TEs).

studi.t: Structure-guided discovery of zinc enzymes and prediction of acetophenone reduction activity
studi.s: Advances in artificial metalloenzyme design have expanded the range of reactions accessible to enzymes, yet the diversity of available scaffolds remains limited. Experimental activity data for individual non-native reactions are scarce, making it difficult to establish how the environment around a metal center shapes catalysis across scaffolds. Using phenylsilane-driven asymmetric reduction of acetophenone as a model reaction, we developed a workflow that combines structure-guided mining, experimental activity assays, and small-sample machine learning.

studi.t: Chia Oil-Derived α-Linolenic Acid Supports Brain Docosahexaenoic Acid Concentrations with Turnover Approaching That of Preformed DHA in Mice
studi.s: -Linolenic acid (ALA) is a dietary precursor of docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) but estimates of its conversion to DHA generally rely on circulating measurements rather than brain DHA turnover. We investigated whether increasing dietary chia oil-derived ALA supports brain DHA concentrations and turnover compared with preformed DHA from fish oil. Male C57BL/6J mice received diets containing 0.2%, 0.9%, 1.8%, 4.5%, or 9% ALA, or a reference diet containing 1.8% ALA and 0.9% DHA, expressed as percentages of total dietary fat.

studi.t: Localizing and labeling contamination in electron micrographs with cryoFILTER
studi.s: Single-particle cryoEM is increasingly applied to compositionally complex, coarsely purified samples, whose micrographs often contain contaminants, including crystalline ice, aggregates, grid support material, and residual ethane. This contamination is spatially localized, occupying only part of an otherwise usable image such that rejecting whole micrographs would discard usable particles along with the contaminant.

studi.t: The allometry of ground reaction forces in Atta vollenweideri leaf-cutter ants.
studi.s: As animals get larger, their weight increases faster than the cross-sectional area of geometrically similar muscles. How, then, do the forces exerted by individual legs change with body size to keep up with this demand? We measured three-dimensional ground reaction forces exerted by individual legs of freely walking leaf-cutter ants (Atta vollenweideri), sampling workers across a fivefold range in body mass. Forelegs exerted the largest peak vertical and propulsive forces, whereas midlegs exerted the largest braking forces.

studi.t: Simulation-based inference of a multiscale reversible-electroporation model reveals how population variability shapes atrial cardioversion
studi.s: Electrical therapies remain a cornerstone for terminating cardiac arrhythmia, but they are painful, require sedation, and may fail in complex cases. Reversible electroporation, traditionally seen as an unwanted side effect of electrical stimulation, may itself help terminate arrhythmia. However, its dual and potentially proarrhythmic effects remain poorly understood and largely unexplored in silico.

studi.t: Confident but misplaced: a model-free ruler for post-translational modification placement by AI structure predictors
studi.s: AI structure predictors accept post-translationally modified (PTM) residues, but whether they place the added atoms where crystallography finds them, and whether their confidence reveals when they do not, is unknown. We first built a ruler from experiment alone: independent crystal structures of the same site reproduce the added atoms of oxidised cysteine and methionine to 0.32 [A], the closest pre-cutoff library rotamer lies at 0.41 [A] and a model-free guess at 4.17 [A].

studi.t: ComProg resolves spatial cell-cell communication into dynamic communication programs and receiver responses
studi.s: Spatial transcriptomics enables cell-resolved inference of ligand-receptor (LR) signaling, but the resulting communication maps are highly redundant, sensitive to LR database choice and difficult to relate to receiver-cell transcriptional responses while accounting for cell identity and spatial context.

studi.t: StrucMind links protein contacts and ligand environments to atoms in PyMOL
studi.s: StrucMind provides two PyMOL plugins for comparing protein contact maps and examining the interactions around a bound ligand. A contact seen in only one structure can reflect a difference in packing or a gap in the coordinates needed for comparison. Contact Maps aligns corresponding residues, identifies retained, gained and lost contacts, and records why a comparison remains unresolved. Structure Analysis measures direct ligand-protein contacts, traces paths through individual water molecules, and characterizes aromatic packing and pocket geometry.

studi.t: Tumor2Line: population-aware tumor-cell line alignment for cancer cell line selection
studi.s: Abstract Cancer cell lines are widely used in cancer research and drug development, yet their representativeness of patient tumors varies across models and biological contexts. Here, we introduce Tumor2Line, a population-aware framework that reframes cancer cell-line selection as an alignment problem between tumor and cell-line populations using unbalanced optimal transport. Tumor2Line improved the recovery of documented tumor-cell line pairs over conventional similarity-based approaches.

studi.t: Pretrained Decision Models in Bioinformatics: Comparable to Active-Learning Screening, Baseline-Dependent in Cell-Type Annotation, Behind a Trained Mass-Spectrometry Re-scorer
studi.s: Much of biomedical research rests on small, repeated decisions with a fixed set of answers: whether a study belongs in a systematic review, whether two trial claims contradict each other, which type a cell is, whether a peptide-spectrum match is correct. Pretrained decision models answer such questions without training on the data at hand, but how far they can replace the methods established for each task is unknown. Here we tested two such models, Jev and d3-ultra, against an established tool or, where none exists, published benchmark results.

studi.t: rnaModScan: context-aware deep learning-based filtering of nanopore m6A and inosine calls
studi.s: Nanopore direct RNA sequencing (DRS) can detect multiple RNA modifications, but falsepositive background calls complicate transcriptome-wide analysis. We developed rnaModScan,a deep learning filter that integrates Dorado scores for all eight modification types with local sequence, repeat, and per-read alignment features to distinguish N6-methyladenosine (m6A) and inosine candidates from background calls.

studi.t: L++: A Language for Programming Life
studi.s: Living systems run on a code written in DNA or RNA, but expressing that code as a model that scientists can write, run and read remains difficult. We present L++, a holistic programming language in which life can be described, simulated and, beyond that, designed; its nouns are biological, and people and AI systems can both write it. Molecules, reactions, compartments, cells, organs and populations are written directly and nest by containment, so one grammar spans a reaction and the population around it. Quantities carry units, objects take places in space, and values can be set in time.

studi.t: Reconstructing regulatory histories of cell fate decisions from single-cell lineage and multi-omics
studi.s: Understanding how distinct cell identities emerge from common progenitors requires access to regulatory histories that molecular snapshots cannot directly reveal. We introduce RegArch, a probabilistic framework integrating transcriptomic profiles, chromatin-derived evidence, and time-scaled cell lineages to reconstruct terminal and unobserved ancestral gene regulatory networks (GRNs).

studi.t: FunDLM: A Foundation DNA Language Model for Fungi
studi.s: Background: Fungi are important pathogens and biotechnology resources, but lack a broadly applicable fungal DNA language model. Models trained on diverse fungal genomes can support functional interpretation of genomic variants and a broad range of genomic tasks. Results: We introduce FunDLM, a family of four DNA language models pre-trained on 426 fungal reference assemblies spanning 217 genera and 14.3 Gb of sequence.

studi.t: Adult gut microbiomes single out individuals at population scale
studi.s: Gut microbiome DNA is shared openly under the assumption that only human host DNA poses an ethical risk. Here we show that querying all publicly available metagenomes with one stool sample recovered another sample from the same person for 94% of 483 adults. Extrapolated to the world population, recovery rates remain well above the re-identification risk threshold advised for public release.

studi.t: Leukocyte content accounts for most microRNA-immune associations in cutaneous melanoma: a confounder-adjusted reassessment
studi.s: Loss of antigen presentation allows tumours to escape T cells and resist immune checkpoint blockade. In melanoma cell lines, several microRNAs repress genes of the antigen-presentation machinery, and many microRNAs have been proposed as immune biomarkers in melanoma tissue. Most tissue evidence comes from bulk biopsies, in which both microRNA profiles and immune-gene expression depend on the immune-cell content of the sample.

studi.t: Thin2Seg: Single-cell Segmentation of Label-free FLIM at Low Photon Counts
studi.s: Significance: Fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) of NAD(P)H can measure the metabolism of single cells without labels. However, its weak autofluorescence requires long acquisitions that can lead to phototoxicity, while shorter acquisitions leave too few photons for current cell segmentation methods. This trade-off is aggravated in 3D live-cell models, such as spheroids and organoids, and in thin, highly adherent 2D cultures. Aim: We develop Thin2Seg to adapt a generalist segmentation network to low-photon FLIM using unlabeled recordings and a single annotated training image.

studi.t: Structure-Guided Design of a c-Src-Inspired Polypeptide Inhibitor Targeting KRas4B-G12D
studi.s: Kirsten rat sarcoma viral oncogene homolog (KRas) is among the most frequently mutated oncogenes in human cancers, so that its direct inhibition remains a major therapeutic challenge. Here, we present a comprehensive computational investigation of a 41-residue chimeric polypeptide proposed as a potential binder of KRas4B-G12D.

studi.t: Molecular mechanisms driving the Arctic E22G-induced amyloidogenicity switch between Aβ40 and Aβ42
studi.s: Amyloid fibrils formed by amyloid-{beta} (A{beta}) in Alzheimer's disease (AD) are characterized by parallel in-register (PAIR) interpeptide {beta}-sheets. Although A{beta}42 is more amyloidogenic than the more abundant A{beta}40 isoform, the familial Arctic E22G mutation disproportionately enhances the amyloidogenicity of A{beta}40, effectively reversing this relationship.

studi.t: The C-tail governs isoform-specific local and global conformational dynamics of non-visual arrestins in aqueous and membrane environments
studi.s: Non-visual arrestins, {beta}-arrestin 1 ({beta}-arr1) and {beta}-arrestin 2 ({beta}-arr2), regulate GPCR desensitization, internalization, and signaling, making them potentially attractive therapeutic targets in several diseases. However, their high sequence similarity complicates isoform- specific targeting. Their C-tails exhibit considerably lower sequence conservation, but they remain poorly characterized due to their disordered nature, limiting our understanding of how C-tail conformational dynamics influence arrestin structure and function.

studi.t: Predicting the antigenic peptidome
studi.s: Antigenic peptides are short protein sequences that are recognized by the immune system. The Major Histocompatibility Complex (MHC) transports intracellular peptides to the cell surface, where interactions with CD8+ T cells are induced. Peptide presentation involves a complex transport pathway, which has several key checkpoints and involves kinetic proofreading. Here, we show that cell metabolism, by modulating transport checkpoints, can strongly affect antigen presentation.

studi.t: Deciphering the synthetic route and apoptotic mechanisms of oxime ester (UAH-4): A potent ursolic acid derivative targeting colorectal cancer
studi.s: The study aimed to synthesize a novel derivative of ursolic acid (UA) and evaluate its anticancer efficacy against Colorectal Cancer (CRC) cells, with a focus on elucidating its mechanism of action. The derivative, UAH-4, was synthesized through a multi-step chemical process and characterized using spectroscopic techniques. In vitro cytotoxicity of UAH-4 was assessed using the SRB assay, while its impact on colony formation, cell migration, Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) generation, Mitochondrial Membrane Potential (MMP) loss, and nuclear morphology were evaluated.

studi.t: The Impact of Highly Effective Modulator Therapies on the ABCG5 ABCG8 Sterol Transporter and Hepatobiliary Function
studi.s: Sitosterolemia (STSL) is a monogenic, recessive disorder characterized by the accumulation of xenosterols in plasma and tissues. STSL is caused by mutations in either ABCG5 or ABCG8, genes that encode ABC half-transporters that form an obligate heterodimer (G5G8) that opposes sterol absorption and promotes biliary cholesterol secretion in the small intestine and liver, respectively. Like STSL, Cystic Fibrosis (CF) is caused by mutations in an ABC transporter, the CF transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR, ABCC7).

studi.t: Serum responses to acute vigorous intensity exercise: vesicle analysis with an omics approach
studi.s: Exercise-induced temporal responses in serum components, such as extracellular vesicles (EVs), remain incompletely characterised. Here, serum was collected from healthy, physically active participants (n=20; 10 males, 10 females) before and at 3-minutes, 1-hour and 2-hours after a 30-minute cycle ergometer bout performed at 70% of maximal oxygen uptake. EVs were characterised by transmission electron microscopy, nanoparticle tracking analysis and mass spectrometry; serum cytokines were quantified in parallel. The main effect of time on EV concentration and size was not significant.

studi.t: Exposure-driven modulation of neural response to novel word forms in toddlers
studi.s: An enhancement of an early brain signal in response to novel word forms has been associated with lexical learning in adults. Here, we measured neural responses to novel pseudowords in 24-month-olds to investigate whether a similar early modulation occurs in young children. Participants were presented with familiar French words (e.g., bateau, boat) and novel pseudowords (e.g., bamon). Event-related potentials were time-locked to the word disambiguation point (i.e., the onset of the second syllable) and analyzed across three time bins (4 minutes each) during the experiment.

studi.t: Target-dependent modulation of finely tuned gamma by transcranial ultrasound in Parkinson's disease
studi.s: Background: Finely tuned gamma (FTG) is a narrowband oscillation associated with dopaminergic ON states and dyskinesia in Parkinson's disease (PD), although its physiological significance remains debated. While deep brain stimulation (DBS) can entrain gamma oscillations, whether noninvasive ultrasound can modulate endogenous FTG across motor circuits remains unclear. Methods: We analyzed local field potentials recorded using sensing-enabled DBS systems in two cohorts of patients: 17 with subthalamic nucleus (STN) and 10 with globus pallidus internus (GPi) electrodes.

studi.t: Neuronal Culture Media Shape Protein Abundance and Turnover in Human iPSC-Derived Neurons
studi.s: Cultured neuron models are essential for studying neuronal biology and disease, yet it remains unclear how neuronal culture media shape the global proteome and protein turnover. Here, we compared human iPSC-derived neurons cultured in four different media: BrainPhys, DMEM/F-12, Neurobasal, or a 1:1 DMEM/F-12:Neurobasal mixture using label-free and dynamic SILAC proteomics. To enable protein turnover measurements in BrainPhys, we developed an in-house SILAC-compatible BrainPhys formulation that supported comparable viability and proteome coverage to commercial BrainPhys.

studi.t: Non-invasive Topographic Sculpting of the Mammalian Auditory Cortex with Low-intensity Focused Ultrasound: A Platform for Personalized Editing of Sensory Representations
studi.s: Background: Topographic maps organize the mammalian cortex, and their maladaptive reorganization underlies conditions like chronic tinnitus and focal dystonia. Low-intensity focused ultrasound (FUS) produces offline neuromodulation, yet its submillimeter spatial distribution within sensory maps remains poorly understood. Objective: To determine how offline FUS-induced amplitude changes are spatially organized within the mouse primary auditory cortex (A1) tonotopic map and depend on sonication intensity.

studi.t: Human lipidomics guides brain-inspired lipoprotein particle approach to ameliorate Alzheimer's disease pathology
studi.s: APOE encodes the principal lipid-transporting protein in the brain, and lipid dysregulation is increasingly implicated in Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathogenesis. The APOE4 allele, together with advanced age and female sex, are major risk factors for late-onset AD. Yet how these risk factors interact to reshape lipid composition and transport in the brain remains unclear. Herein, we characterize lipidomic profiles in the brain, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), and blood of individuals with or without AD, as well as of mice expressing humanized APOE.

studi.t: Modeling Speech-in-Noise Performance Using an Auditory-Nerve Manifold
studi.s: Speech-in-noise difficulties often exceed audiometric profile-based predictions, suggesting suprathreshold neural coding deficits limit understanding even when audibility is preserved. A major limitation of clinical speech tests is that reduced performance can reflect either hair-cell loss or cochlear neural degeneration (CND). We propose a computational framework estimating each factor relative contribution at a population level.

studi.t: Neuronal heparan sulfate controls the brain accumulation and glymphatic clearance of pathogenic α-synuclein
studi.s: In Parkinson's disease and dementia with Lewy bodies, fibrillar aggregates of the -synuclein (-syn) protein are released into the extracellular space and drive disease progression, yet the mechanisms governing their in vivo neuronal uptake and clearance remain poorly understood. Heparan sulfate proteoglycans (HSPGs) act as receptors for -syn fibril internalization in iPSC-derived dopaminergic neurons and could therefore advance synucleinopathy progression in patients.

studi.t: Instruction Timing Governs Representational Competition in Behavioral Timescale Synaptic Plasticity
studi.s: Neurons can form new representations within a single experience through behavioral-timescale synaptic plasticity (BTSP), yet how such rapid learning affects previously established representations remains unclear. We present an analytically tractable theory of BTSP, constrained by experimental measurements in hippocampal CA1, to examine how successive learning events interact within individual neurons. Competition between temporally narrow potentiation and broader, weight-dependent depression generates nonmonotonic interference as a function of the separation between instructive events.

studi.t: One genome, two connectomes: genetic encoding of synapse drive to specify environment-appropriate wiring
studi.s: The form of neural wiring must be robust as well as appropriate for the environment. In resource-rich environments, C. elegans larvae rapidly mature into reproductive adults; otherwise, they enter dauer diapause, a state with altered physiology and behaviors for survival and dispersal from harsh environments. By comparing the electron microscopic reconstruction of multiple dauers and non-dauers, we define two consensus connectomes that stereotypically differ in approximately 1/3 wiring partnerships.

studi.t: The degree of Amyloid β pathology determines the impact of autophagy deficiency
studi.s: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is characterized by amyloid {beta} (A{beta}) deposition, tau aggregation and impaired proteostasis, including autophagy dysfunction. However, how autophagy deficiency affects A{beta} pathology and disease progression remains unclear. We crossed excitatory neuronspecific Atg7 knockout mice with App knock-in mice (AppNL-F/NL-F and AppNL-G-F/NL-G-F) and assessed A{beta} pathology, extracellular vesicle (EV) release, cognition, gamma oscillatory activity, cell death, brain atrophy and proteomic changes.

studi.t: The body as a network, rhythm as the principle: a FREQ-NESS analysis of human movement
studi.s: Humans spontaneously move together to rhythm, yet how the body organizes its movements is poorly understood and determining which aspects of this organization support interpersonal coordination requires state-of-the-art analysis methods. By applying for the first time Frequency-resolved Network Estimation via Source Separation (FREQ-NESS) to movement data, we reveal a rhythmic architecture of human movement and show how it shapes coordination between individuals.

studi.t: Single-molecule motion profiling reveals direct and indirect effects of PolyQ expansion on huntingtin dynamics and molecular engagement
studi.s: Huntingtons disease (HD) is caused by CAG expansion in HTT, but how PolyQ expansion alters huntingtin behaviour in human neurons remains unclear. We combined live single-molecule imaging and tracking with transformer-based motion profiling to resolve full-length HTT dynamics in pluripotent hESCs and their derived cortical- and MSN-like neurons. HTT occupied three behavioural states: bound, confined, and exploratory. PolyQ expansion progressively shifted molecules from bound and confined states toward the exploratory state.

studi.t: The unfolded protein response in alveolar type II cells is a therapeutic target in ischemia-reperfusion injury and chronic lung allograft rejection
studi.s: Although lung transplantation is life saving for patients with end-stage lung disease, its long-term outcome is poor owing to an inexorable process of chronic rejection that culminates in chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD) and death or the need for re-transplantation at a median of 6 years post-transplant. Current immunosuppression fails to prevent CLAD, suggesting the existence of alternative pathways not susceptible to these drugs. Lung-directed autoantibodies have been shown to predict CLAD and reduced post-transplant survival.

studi.t: A modular intranasal Nm-nOMV RBD concatemer vaccine induces broad betacoronavirus-neutralizing antibodies
studi.s: Betacoronaviruses pose a major threat to human and animal health due to their propensity to cause spillover infections. Broadly protective vaccines that induce mucosal immunity may strengthen pandemic preparedness by limiting infection and onward transmission. Here we have developed intranasal betacoronavirus vaccine candidates combining AdJane Biosciences' Neisseria meningitidis native outer membrane vesicle (Nm-nOMV) platform, a self-adjuvating mucosal delivery platform recently shown to be safe and well tolerated in a first-in-human Phase 1 trial, with multivalent coronavirus spike…

studi.t: Human Lung Mast cell Diversity Across Anatomical Compartments Defined by Single-Cell Transcriptomics
studi.s: Background: Mast cells are key regulators of inflammatory lung diseases, including asthma. Yet, the heterogeneity of lung mast cells and their specialization in different lung compartments remain poorly defined. Traditional protease-based classifications fail to capture distinct mast cell states relevant to airway pathology, highlighting the need for high-resolution, compartment-resolved analyses. Objective: To determine the heterogeneity of human lung mast cells in different lung compartments.

studi.t: Whole-blood and PBMC-based assays reveal hidden inflammatory responses to decellularized materials for heart valve replacement
studi.s: Reliable assessment of inflammatory activity is essential for the development of biological heart valve materials. However, the responses detected depend critically on the assay system. Following inconsistent and weak responses in standard macrophage assays, we systematically compared human whole blood with isolated immune-cell models to evaluate laboratory-prepared decellularized aortic valves from human donors and clinically used biological valve materials.

studi.t: Viral-bacterial arms race in the marine sponge Halichondria panicea
studi.s: Sponges are complex holobionts/metaorganisms and important models for host-microbe interactions, yet their viral communities remain poorly understood. Here, we characterized the diversity of viruses associated with the marine sponge Halichondria panicea from different locations in the North Atlantic and Baltic Sea. Most sponge-associated viruses were also detected in the surrounding seawater, while little evidence was found for a shared sponge-specific core virome across locations. A subset of viruses that were enriched in sponges over seawater was explored further.

studi.t: Structures of human adenoviruses D36 and D56 provide insights into adenovirus diversity and cement protein networks
studi.s: 83 out of 118 human adenoviruses (HAdVs) belong to species D, which includes respiratory viruses, recombinants associated with rare, fatal neonatal infections, and viruses developed as vectors for clinical applications. The structural basis for variability in capsid-host interactions, and the complex network of cement proteins stabilizing the inner face of the capsids are incompletely understood. We report cryo-EM structures of HAdV-D36 and HAdV-D56 at 2.5 and 2.6 A resolution, respectively. Capsid surface features are well resolved, allowing structural comparisons of hypervariable regions.

studi.t: Advancing Cyanobacterial Toxin Monitoring Capacity: A Large-Scale Multi-Year Comparison of ELISA, LC-MS/MS, and qPCR in Temperate Waters
studi.s: Cyanobacterial toxins are an increasing environmental and public health concern, driven by rising temperatures and anthropogenic pressures such as eutrophication. Due to the colder climate, Northern Europe is generally believed to be less vulnerable, however, cyanobacterial blooms have increased in recent years in many areas including Arctic lakes and Northern Baltic Sea. Yet, monitoring remains challenging due to toxin diversity, variable bloom dynamics, and the differences in analytical targets among methods.

studi.t: High-resolution cryo-EM of ribosomes in mammalian neurons
studi.s: Brain function depends on protein synthesis (translation), which controls neurodevelopment, synaptic plasticity, and memory formation. To understand the molecular mechanisms of translational control, the functional states of neuronal ribosomes must be determined. We visualized the translational apparatus within induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSC)-derived human neurons and in human and mouse neuron-derived lysates, using cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) with high-resolution 2D template matching (2DTM) and large-area imaging (DeCo-LACE).

studi.t: A human-accelerated enhancer rewires FOXC1-dependent skeletal development
studi.s: The evolution of human skeletal morphology involved modifications to conserved developmental programs, but the underlying regulatory mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here we integrate single-cell transcriptomic atlases of developing human, macaque and mouse limbs with comparative chromatin interaction maps of chondrocytes. We identify human-biased transcriptional programs within conserved osteochondral lineages and link divergent chromatin interactions to human-specific sequence changes.

studi.t: Contrasting taxonomic and functional diversity of tropical anuran communities across crude oil-contaminated and reference streams in a biodiversity hotspot
studi.s: Conservation assessments of chronic anthropogenic disturbance increasingly ask whether changes in species composition translate into comparable changes in ecological function. This distinction is central to anticipating the long-term consequences of disturbance for ecosystem processes. Crude oil spills are a recurrent but understudied source of chronic disturbance in tropical freshwater ecosystems.

studi.t: Trade-offs between sexual and clonal reproduction differ within versus among populations
studi.s: Plants exhibit large variation in reproductive strategies, from obligately sexual to exclusively asexual. Clonal vegetative reproduction is common among plants, and despite theory assuming that trade-offs exist between sexual and clonal reproduction, empirical demonstrations of trade-offs remain elusive. Here we examined whether the strength of genotypic trade-offs in white clover (Trifolium repens) depends on spatial scale of sampling, and the environmental factors that favour sexual versus clonal reproduction.

studi.t: Reference genomes for Australian Cryptosporidium hominis and C. parvum from humans
studi.s: Cryptosporidium hominis and C. parvum are important protozoan pathogens of humans worldwide, and genomic surveillance is increasingly being used to investigate transmission and outbreaks. However, no complete Cryptosporidium genome is available from Australia, and many common Cryptosporidium gp60 subtypes lack high-quality genome assemblies worldwide. This study generated the first Australian reference genomes for two clinically relevant, zoonotic Cryptosporidium species, C. hominis and C. parvum from human hosts, as well as a scaffold-level genome for Australian C. meleagridis.

studi.t: A Benchmark for Generative Modeling of High-Dimensional Enzyme Kinetic Parameters of Metabolic Networks
studi.s: Large-scale kinetic models predict how metabolism responds to genetic and environmental perturbations, but building them at scale is limited by the scarcity of experimentally determined enzyme kinetic parameters. Generative machine learning has been proposed to address this bottleneck, yet prior work has each introduced a single, bespoke architecture, leaving open which generative paradigm suits this problem and why.

studi.t: EHRMENEIA: A Benchmark for Foundation Models on Longitudinal Electronic Health Records
studi.s: Electronic health record foundation models are evaluated using heterogeneous targets, vocabularies, and adaptation procedures, preventing systematic characterization across model families. We introduce EHRMENEIA (https://ehrmeneia.upc.edu/), a benchmark that provides a multidimensional evaluation framework for next-event prediction, multi-horizon event occurrence, trajectory fidelity and few-shot representation transfer. EHRMENEIA preserves each model's native vocabulary and temporal representation while mapping clinical outputs to shared evaluation objects.

studi.t: Task-aligned foundation model representations enable single-cell cytokine response inference
studi.s: Inferring cellular responses from single-cell transcriptomes requires interpreting changes relative to an appropriate baseline while retaining cell-type context. Here we present CYTAP, which adapts frozen single-cell foundation model embeddings for cytokine-response inference by combining donor-adjusted receiver states with deviations from matched control centroids. CYTAP uses a shared classifier to assign relative single-cell response scores across 90 cytokines and supports unpaired analyses using counterfactual control references.

studi.t: GNEval: A Context-Specific Benchmark for Gene Network Inference with Single-Cell Foundation Models
studi.s: Gene network (GN) inference plays a critical role in understanding gene relationships and their roles in biological functions and diseases. Existing single-cell GN inference methods often rely on limited data from individual studies. Single-cell foundation models, pretrained on large and diverse datasets, provide a range of gene-gene association signals that offer a promising basis for GN inference. However, it remains unclear which GN properties these signals capture and how they compare with domain-specific methods.

studi.t: CellTouch: Learning to separate touching nuclei in anisotropic 3D cell cultures
studi.s: 3D-oids, such as spheroids and organoids, are essential models in drug discovery and precision medicine, and quantitative analysis requires every nucleus to be segmented separately. Accurate 3D instance segmentation remains challenging, because nuclei are densely packed and touching, and volumes are sampled more coarsely along the Z-axis than laterally. Most existing methods were developed for near-isotropic data and tend to merge neighbouring nuclei.

studi.t: Elucidating the membrane-binding mechanism of the ALPS-like motif of the Osh4 protein
studi.s: Transport of lipids within cells is crucial for cellular functions and is facilitated by lipid transport proteins, like the Saccharomyces cerevisiae oxysterol-binding homologue (Osh) proteins. Among these, Osh4 is of particular interest, due to its role in lipid trafficking at the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and trans-Golgi network (TGN).

studi.t: Influence of interindividual variability structures on implied priors and population predictions in pharmacogenetic models
studi.s: Interindividual variability (IIV) defines part of the prior distribution used in Bayesian parameter estimation. However, the dependence of model-implied priors on IIV and covariate model specifications is rarely examined explicitly. We evaluated empirical support for pooled versus phenotype-specific IIV structures and their consequences for predictive distributions in a CYP2D6-dependent population pharmacokinetic model.

studi.t: Humidity detection after blood feeding in ticks is required for oviposition site selection and egg survival
studi.s: Immediately following a blood meal, the female tick must locate conditions that allow successful egg development. A contributing factor is that conditions must be sufficiently moist to prevent egg dehydration. Previous studies show that humidity detection occurs through the forelegs and that interference with this process leads to tick mortality; however, this effect has not been examined in fed tick stages. Here, we show that female ticks exhibit a distinct attraction to higher humidity, directing them to locations where they arrest and subsequently deposit eggs.

studi.t: The relationship between heart rate variability and cerebral autoregulation at elevated intracranial pressure
studi.s: Objective. Altered intracranial pressure (ICP) is a key biomarker for traumatic brain injury (TBI). However, obtaining ICP measurements is a highly invasive process. Heart rate variability (HRV) has demonstrated potential as a useful biomarker for ICP changes, but few studies have investigated the relationship between ICP changes and HRV. This work examines how HRV and ICP interact in cases of TBI and whether HRV metrics can be informative of the state of autoregulatory control at elevated ICP. Approach. Electrocardiogram signals were recorded in seven non-human primates under anesthesia.

studi.t: Time-resolved multi-omics reveals constitutive defense preparedness and early responses to soybean cyst nematode in wild soybean
studi.s: Soybean (Glycine max), a versatile cash crop, is the largest global source of plant-based protein and second-largest source of vegetable oil. However, soybean cyst nematode (SCN; Heterodera glycines) is the most economically damaging pest of soybean worldwide, causing substantial yield losses annually. Currently, the effectiveness of widely deployed genetic resistance in soybean cultivars is increasingly challenged by evolving SCN populations; therefore, identifying new sources and mechanisms of SCN resistance is critical.

studi.t: Disrupting translation in CA1 pyramidal cells blocks novelty-induced increases in population firing rate while preserving newly formed assemblies
studi.s: Long-term memory depends upon the translation of the plasticity-related proteins required for synaptic consolidation. Whether learning-related changes in hippocampal CA1 coding and synchrony require local synaptic consolidation or reflect plasticity elsewhere remains unknown. We used the inducible protein kinase R (iPKR) chemogenetic system to downregulate cap-dependent translation in CaMKII-expressing dorsal CA1 neurons through intracerebral infusion of an actuator that activates the integrated stress response.

studi.t: Complex IV Subunit C15orf48 Integrates Electron Transport Chain Function with Amino Acid and Lipid Metabolism to Regulate Innate Immunity
studi.s: Despite extensive recognition of immunometabolism in innate immune regulation, how mitochondrial bioenergetic and metabolic pathways in monocytes interface to control inflammatory responses remains poorly understood. Here, we uncover that C15orf48 (MOCCI/NMES1/COXFA4L3), an inflammation-associated mitochondrial complex IV (CIV) subunit, orchestrates electron transport chain (ETC) function, fatty acid oxidation (FAO), and branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) catabolism to control monocyte activation.

studi.t: Dual-loop DogTag engineering enables modular antigen display on human vault nanoparticles
studi.s: Self-assembling protein nanoparticles can enhance immune responses by displaying multiple copies of an antigen on their surface. Most previous studies using vault nanoparticles have focused on loading proteins inside the particle or modifying its ends. Here, we introduced two DogTag peptides into separate surface-exposed loops of human major vault protein (MVP), creating up to 156 potential attachment sites on each 78-subunit vault.

studi.t: Rare Epithelial Sentinel Cells Establish Functional Domains of the Airway
studi.s: Organs exposed to the environment must sense threats in order to evoke protective physiologic responses. Recent single-cell sequencing studies of the airway epithelium have led to the identification of a suite of rare epithelial cells, many of which are unified by their ability to sense stimuli1,2. Herein, we explore how organized networks of epithelial sentinel cells transduce distinct stimuli to alter tissue function by employing a combination of cell type-specific calcium indicators, optogenetics, chemogenetics, cell ablation, and live ACh and ATP sensors.

studi.t: Transient telomerase mRNA delivery extends the proliferative capacity of patient-derived Duchenne muscular dystrophy myogenic progenitors
studi.s: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is an X-linked disease, characterised by progressive skeletal and cardiac muscle degeneration and impaired regeneration. Repeated regenerative cycles contribute to muscle stem cell exhaustion, potentially driven by telomere shortening under chronic proliferative demand. Here, we tested whether transient delivery of hTERT mRNA can increase the relative telomere signal (Q-FISH) in patient-derived DMD myogenic progenitors (CD56+) and interstitial (CD56-) cells from two DMD donors, compared with one control donor.

studi.t: A gene-edited chicken model of ocular coloboma reveals Netrin-1 is required for pioneer cell detachment during optic fissure closure
studi.s: Coloboma, a leading cause of childhood blindness, results from failed OFC. Variants in NTN1 (Netrin-1) are linked to coloboma and other tissue fusion defects, but how Netrin-1 influences epithelial fusion is unknown. We generated a germline NTN1 knockout chicken and analysed the fissure margins by immunofluorescence, in situ hybridisation, single-nucleus RNA sequencing and micro-CT. NTN1-/- embryos developed highly penetrant bilateral colobomas.

studi.t: Chromosome-level genome assembly of the hydrozoan jellyfish Cladonema pacificum
studi.s: The hydrozoan jellyfish Cladonema pacificum, which possesses experimentally tractable polyp and medusa stages, is an emerging cnidarian model for studies of regeneration, development, physiology, and behavior. Although experimental techniques have been established for this species, the lack of a chromosome-level reference genome has limited genome-wide and comparative analyses. Here, we present the first chromosome-level genome assembly of C. pacificum generated using HiFi long-read sequencing and Hi-C technology.

studi.t: Programming Continuous, High Framerate, and Long-Duration Data Acquisitions on the Verasonics Ultrasound System
studi.s: The ultrasound community has seen a rise in popularity of highly demanding imaging acquisition sequences, such as those for super-resolution ultrasound localization microscopy and functional ultrasound imaging, which push the boundary of ultrasound system hardware limits. However, subtle errors in sequence programming can lead to corrupted data, inaccurate timing, and slow data throughput, which impact the performance of these modalities.

studi.t: SPECTRAM: three-dimensional full-vector simulation of coherence-tunable microscopy images
studi.s: We present SPECTRAM, a physics-based framework for three-dimensional simulation of coherence-tunable microscopy image formation. Combining finite-difference time-domain solutions of Maxwell's equations with a coherence-tunable, polarization-dependent image-formation model, SPECTRAM captures full-vector light scattering and modality-specific optical processing in brightfield, differential interference contrast, and phase-contrast microscopy. It supports arbitrary three-dimensional sample geometries and generates volumetric image stacks under configurable illumination and objective parameters.

studi.t: StarCrew: A pipeline for exploratory analysis of Starship cargo
studi.s: BackgroundStarships are giant cargo-mobilizing mobile elements within the fungal subphylum Pezizomycotina that harbor diverse gene content, including genes for virulence and heavy metal resistance. Although Starship elements carry a vast array of cargo genes, the overall composition and function of this cargo remain largely uncharacterized for most elements. While existing bioinformatic tools have been designed for the identification of these elements, a gap remains in tools for characterizing their gene content while accounting for its specific characteristics.

studi.t: Standard benchmarking inflates gene-prioritization accuracy estimates
studi.s: Benchmark results tell clinics which gene-prioritization system to trust and the field what counts as progress. Standard benchmarking practice --- testing each system using its latest knowledge databases --- can inflate system accuracy estimates and invite data leakage. We formalize the Fairbench protocol: testing may use only knowledge available strictly before the patient's assessment.

studi.t: Distance-stratified benchmarking of variant-effect predictors on β-lactamase deep mutational scanning data
studi.s: Mutations far from the active site of antibiotic-resistance enzymes can change resistance, but it is unclear what information predicts their effects. We asked how the performance of a protein language model (ESM2), a structure-based stability predictor (ThermoMPNN) and simple structural descriptors changes with distance from the catalytic residues, using deep mutational scanning data for the {beta}-lactamases TEM-1 (four assays) and VIM-2 (one assay). We measured Spearman correlation and AUROC within distance bins, with bootstrap intervals over positions.

studi.t: Input Construction Accounts for Most PoseBusters Clash Failures on RNA-Ligand Complexes
studi.s: PoseBusters, a widely used test of the physical validity of ligand poses, was calibrated on protein-ligand crystal structures, and whether its checks transfer to RNA has not been measured. Applied without filtering the input to 2,970 deposited RNA-ligand poses, the receptor-clash check failed 527 of 2,931 (18.0%), and all but 7 of the failures were in covalently bonded nucleotides or in entries that contain protein, were solved by cryo-electron microscopy or were resolved at worse than 2.0 [A], so most failures are associated with which structures and ligand records entered the input set.

studi.t: De Novo-Designed Alpha-Helical Proteins Enable Ligand-Directed Spectral Tuning
studi.s: Canonical green fluorescent proteins typically regulate chromophore photophysics through a rigid beta-barrel environment, while spectral tuning often relies on protein engineering or directed evolution. Here, we design a compact alpha-helical protein pocket that activates a GFP-chromophore-derived fluorogen and accommodates a series of chemically modified ligands. A co-crystal structure reveals shared anchoring interactions for fluorogen activation and contacts that enable ligand-dependent spectral tuning.

studi.t: Stromal mitochondrial reprogramming and transfer reveal a chemotherapy-associated tumor state in ovarian cancer
studi.s: Mitochondrial transfer from stromal cells promotes ovarian cancer progression, yet the functional state of donor mitochondria remains poorly understood. Here we define a stress-adapted mitochondrial state in carcinoma-associated mesenchymal stem cells (CA-MSCs), characterized by increased respiratory and glycolytic activity despite increased mitochondrial proton leak and inefficient coupling of respiration to ATP production, oxidative stress, and elevated mitochondrial DNA variant burden.

studi.t: Podocyte-to-Parietal Epithelial Cell Senescence Drives Experimental Focal Segmental Glomerulosclerosis and is reversed by Dasatinib Plus Quercetin
studi.s: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) is a progressive podocyte-depleting glomerular disease and a leading cause of chronic kidney disease, yet the contribution of cellular senescence to its pathogenesis remains poorly understood. Here, we identified senescent parietal epithelial cells (PECs) in human FSGS, revealing a previously unrecognized component of glomerular injury. In experimental FSGS, podocyte senescence preceded PEC senescence, which was associated with glomerulosclerosis. Conditioned medium from senescent podocytes induced secondary senescence in PECs.

studi.t: Alpha-synuclein overexpression induces sex-dependent alterations in striatal autophagic-lysosomal markers in a Parkinson's disease mouse model
studi.s: Parkinson's disease (PD) is characterized by pathological alpha-synuclein (-syn) accumulation and alterations in autophagy. While biological sex is increasingly recognized as a modifier of PD susceptibility and pathophysiology, its relationship with striatal autophagic-lysosomal alterations remains incompletely understood. In this study, we investigated sex-dependent changes in related molecular markers in a mouse model overexpressing -syn. Male and female C57BL/6J mice received bilateral intranigral injections of adeno-associated viral vectors encoding mutant A53T -syn or empty vectors.

studi.t: TAOK1 restrains cerebral cortex size and determines neural progenitor fate through YAP1 suppression
studi.s: The size and complexity of the human cerebral cortex results from precisely coordinated neural progenitor expansion, differentiation, and fate trajectories for which the controlling molecular programs are not well understood. Pathogenic missense and deletion variants in the protein kinase TAOK1 cause a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by intellectual disability and macrocephaly. We generated human cortical organoids harboring catalytically-inactive TAOK1 disease variant and utilized quantitative phosphoproteomics along with single-cell transcriptomics to uncover disease mechanisms.

studi.t: The temporal dynamics of same vs. different relational integration in the adult brain
studi.s: Humans readily abstract common relations across situations that look entirely different. For example, when reading a map, we align relations between landmarks on a screen with those in the world around us. Relational comparison forms the basis of analogical reasoning. Here, we investigated how recognising same and different relations instantiated by various simple shapes unfolds in the brain over time.

studi.t: Mucosal B Cell Aggregates are Associated with Non-response to JAK1 Inhibitor Therapy in Ulcerative Colitis
studi.s: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease with considerable interindividual variation in treatment response and limited efficacy of available therapies in some patients. Predicting individual responses is therefore essential for personalized treatment selection. Filgotinib, a preferential JAK1 inhibitor, induces clinical remission in approximately 40% of patients after 1 year, but mechanisms underlying response remain unclear.

studi.t: Agonistic anti-CD40 monoclonal antibody improves the antitumor efficacy of a clinical chemo-immunotherapy regimen in a refractory mouse neuroblastoma model.
studi.s: Background: The current standard regimen for relapsed-refractory high-risk neuroblastoma (HR-NB) is the combination of chemotherapy agents -Temozolomide and Irinotecan - and anti-GD2 antibody dinutuximab (TIG). This treatment results in an overall response for ~40% of patients, but the remaining 60% are resistant to TIG. We hypothesized that agonistic anti-CD40 monoclonal antibody (aCD40), which activates antitumor NK cells and macrophages as we found in previous studies, will improve the efficacy of TIG.

studi.t: Integrated multi-omics framework mapping Myeloid associated cellular states (M.A.C.S.)
studi.s: Functional specialization of myeloid cells in vivo aligns poorly with historic binary classifications. Moreover, inconsistent annotations hinder comparisons across studies. Here, we present Myeloid Associated Cell States (M.A.C.S.), an integrated multiomics framework combining a human Myeloid Cell Atlas (MCA) comprising 498,642 cells from 581 donors across 7 tissues in health and disease with probabilistic mapping of cell populations. Batch-aware variable gene selection preserves tissue-imprinted and disease-associated programs, resolving 24 core states with consensus gene signatures.

studi.t: A cross-species single-cell spatial atlas of kidney allografts
studi.s: Kidney allografts with the same Banff diagnosis differ in their immune microenvironments and functional recovery after treatment, yet the tissue features distinguishing recovery from non-recovery remain unclear. We constructed SPECTRA (Spatial Etiology and Coordination of Transplant Rejection in Allografts), which comprises spatial multi-omic data from 1,011,984 cells in 83 human allograft biopsies. We also profiled 442,320 cells from 34 mouse grafts across experimental groups and time points by single-cell sequencing, and integrated a public human single-cell reference of 352,911 cells.

studi.t: Programmed Cell Death-1 marks TOX+ T Regulatory Cells that Inhibit Autoimmunity and Anti-Tumor Immunity
studi.s: Regulatory T cells (Tregs) are important for the maintenance of immune homeostasis. A proportion of peripheral Tregs constitutively express the coreceptor programmed cell death-1 (PD1), but the importance of this subset is yet to be investigated. We found PD1 marks TOX expressing Tregs. In both PD1 germline deficient and peripheral deficient Tregs, an increase in TOX+ Tregs were noted in steady state which was reproduced in antibody-based blocking studies. We next investigated if TOX+ Tregs were present in disease states.

studi.t: HDAC6 inhibition rewires carbon metabolism to expose an asparagine dependency in multiple myeloma.
studi.s: Multiple myeloma (MM) remains a challenging malignancy with limited therapeutic options upon relapse/refractory disease, necessitating novel combination strategies. Malignant plasma cells sustain continuous immunoglobulin production, a biosynthetic and secretory burden that places heavy demand on central carbon metabolism and creates potentially targetable metabolic vulnerabilities. Previously, we found a role for HDAC6 in modulating glycolytic metabolism. Our goal here was to find induced metabolic vulnerabilities that could be targeted after HDAC6 inhibition or knockdown.

studi.t: EpiCycle: A flexible approach for scalable, three-dimensional reconstructions of complex epithelial tissues
studi.s: Understanding organ development and repair requires methods to precisely describe cell geometry. Recent image analysis methods allow increasingly accurate segmentation of simple epithelial tissues. However, many vertebrate organs contain more complex stratified epithelia, for which accurate 3D cellular segmentation remains challenging. Here, we describe EpiCycle, an iterative, user-friendly approach developed to address the unique segmentation challenges posed by stratified epithelia.

studi.t: Environmental Noise and Lag Select Distinct Phenotypic Bet Hedging in Microbial Metabolic Allocation
studi.s: Genetically identical microbial cells often differ in their growth rate and metabolic state, and in how long they take to resume growth after a shift of conditions. Preparing for uncertain future conditions is costly: cells that allocate part of their proteome to a future nutrient grow more slowly on the present one. Bet hedging offers a complementary strategy: a genotype whose cells occupy different metabolic states makes it likely that some of them are suited to whatever condition follows and resume growth quickly.

studi.t: Changes in the wing spot pattern of the endangered butterfly Phengaris teleius thirty years after its reintroduction
studi.s: 1. Reintroduced insect populations founded by few individuals can change in phenotype through founder effects, genetic drift and new environmental conditions. Butterfly wing spot patterns, their fluctuating asymmetry and their variability can reflect such changes and population stress. 2. We studied the spot pattern of the hindwing underside of 267 Phengaris teleius butterflies from the Polish source metapopulation at the time of their reintroduction to the Netherlands in 1990, and from the current Polish and Dutch metapopulations (2019-2020).

studi.t: Allocating maternal-tree collections to conserve genetic diversity of Lumnitzera littorea in southern Vietnam
studi.s: Mangrove restoration nurseries often raise seed from a limited number of maternal trees, and how those trees are split among source populations affects which alleles reach the nursery. We genotyped 110 Lumnitzera littorea trees from two mainland and two island sites in southern Vietnam at 11 nuclear microsatellite loci and then enumerated all 5,236 ways of dividing a 30-tree collection among the four sites. With sample sizes matched, the mainland sites had consistently higher expected heterozygosity than the islands.

studi.t: Uncovering mitochondrial diversity and candidate taxonomic lineages of Hypostomus (Siluriformes: Loricariidae) in Colombia
studi.s: Molecular data for Colombian Hypostomus remain sparse, limiting assessments of species boundaries. We combined two mitochondrial markers (cox1 and D-loop) with morphological, morphometric, geographic, and taxonomic evidence to evaluate diversity among Colombian populations. Using ASAP, bPTP, and GMYC, cox1 recovered 16-17 Molecular Operational Taxonomic Units (MOTUs), whereas D-loop yielded 32-37, indicating finer mitochondrial lineage partitioning in D-loop that was not consistently mirrored by phenotypic differentiation.

studi.t: Chromosome-scale comparative genomics reveals a genomic mosaic across the documented Hattan sake-brewing rice lineage
studi.s: Background: Breeding pedigrees record crosses and selections but do not reveal how the documented relationships are reflected in descendant genomes. Therefore, whole-genome summaries can mask local inheritance patterns generated by recombination and segregation. To examine how documented relationships are reflected across genomic scales, we generated chromosome-scale assemblies of the Hattanso landrace and four cultivars from the documented Hattan sake-brewing rice lineage of Hiroshima, Japan.

studi.t: ChondroMap: A Spatially Resolved Framework for Quantifying the Mechanical Exposure Between Cartilage and Bone Surfaces in Knee Osteoarthritis
studi.s: Objective: This study presents ChondroMap, a spatially resolved framework for quantifying articulating cartilage- and bone-based contact interactions, demonstrated across various knee osteoarthritis (OA) severities. Design: Through probing the interactions between segmented high-resolution, spatially resolved cartilage/bone MRI scans and articulating kinematics from biplanar video-radiography (BVR), the ChondroMap framework aggregates cartilage-on-cartilage (CoC), cartilage-on-bone (CoB), and bone-on-bone (BoB) interactions to form a cumulative heatmap of mechanical exposure.

studi.t: Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analyses of lysine isonicotinylation-related gene expression in diabetic foot ulcer healing
studi.s: Diabetic foot ulcers have heterogeneous healing outcomes. We integrated public single-cell and bulk RNA-sequencing datasets to identify cell-type-specific lysine isonicotinylation (Kinic)-related transcriptional patterns and exploratory candidates associated with healing. The atlas comprised 56,568 cells across 14 cell types, with Kinic-related signature scores differing by cell type and healing group.

studi.t: VS-Suite: Automated Consensus Virtual Screening Platform for Improved Screening of Small Molecules
studi.s: Growing the recent advances in artificial intelligence and machine leaning (AI&ML) approaches accelerated small molecules screening against targeted proteins with limited computational resources and time. Finding accurate binding pose and affinity prediction is challenges task and traditional docking tools and lacks the reproducibility. Development of the Co-folding model is paradigm shift in drug discovery and development, allowing to predict protein ligand complexes without experimental crystal structures.

studi.t: RecurSieve: A Python Package to Detect Subtle Gene Expression Differences Across Single-Cell RNA-seq Comparisons Using Iterative Machine Learning
studi.s: Most existing methods for performing differential expression testing using single-cell RNA-seq data evaluate genes independently and primarily detect shifts in mean RNA levels. These methods may thus miss RNAs that distinguish experimental groups jointly or through changes in the shape of genes' expression distributions. To address this limitation, we developed RecurSieve, an iterative ensemble learning method that combines shared expression classification with unsupervised clustering to recursively identify gene sets with group-based expression differences.

studi.t: Extracting generator-specific information from irregular brain field potentials: a comparative study of feature-based and deep learning approaches.
studi.s: Brain field potentials (FPs) reflect the combined activity of multiple neural sources, challenging the accuracy of their temporal series and their spatial origin difficult to establish from waveform inspection alone. However, FP generators obtained by independent component analysis exhibit characteristic temporal patterns and unique spatial profiles that allow their identification, even during apparently irregular activity.

studi.t: Malaria in Pregnancy and Endotoxemia Disturb Maternal Thyroid Function and Remodel the Expression of Placental Thyroid Hormone Transporters in Mice
studi.s: Thyroid hormones (TH) are essential for fetal development. We hypothesized that malaria in pregnancy (MiP) and lipopolysaccharide (LPS) challenge would disrupt the expression of placental TH transporters. Pregnant dams were infected with Plasmodium berghei ANKA at gestational day (GD) 13.5 or challenged with lipopolysaccharide (LPS) at GD17.5. Maternal thyroid parameters, fetal outcomes, placental inflammatory markers, TH transporters and deiodinases expression were assessed at GD18.5.

studi.t: Endothelium-released Dll4 drives sarcopenia and systemic aging
studi.s: Lifelong preservation of skeletal muscle function is essential for healthy aging. Sarcopenia, the age-related loss of muscle mass and strength, arises from aging itself (primary sarcopenia) or chronic diseases (secondary sarcopenia). Although these forms frequently coexist, whether they share a therapeutically targetable mechanism remains unclear. Here we identify soluble, full-length Delta-like ligand 4 (Dll4), released from endothelial cells, as a common driver of both forms of sarcopenia.

studi.t: Regulation of antigen presentation by p38a in alveolar macrophages controls lung immunity
studi.s: The lung is constantly exposed to environmental challenges, so its immune status must be tightly regulated. Alveolar macrophages (AMs) are myeloid cells that play a key role in maintaining lung homeostasis and preventing excessive inflammatory responses. Here, we report that AMs rely on the protein kinase p38a to regulate the major histocompatibility complex class II (MHCII) expression, identifying one way in which AMs may contribute to allergic and malignant lung disease.

studi.t: Bile acid-mediated ileal barrier function deficits in primary sclerosing cholangitis
studi.s: Background: Given a high prevalence of ulcerative colitis (UC) in primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC-UC), research into the pathophysiology of the gut-liver axis has focussed on the large intestine. However, reduced bile flow from the liver has the potential to impact on homeostatic functions of the small intestine, including the main site of bile acid reuptake - the terminal ileum. Objective: Define ileal barrier changes in PSC-UC that are future treatment targets.

studi.t: Concordant genomic, chemical and morphological divergence reveals two cryptic species in the paper wasp Polistes dominula (Hymenoptera: Vespidae)
studi.s: The paper wasp Polistes dominula (Christ, 1791) is one of the most widespread vespid species in Europe and has become invasive in temperate regions on other continents. In Central Europe its mitochondrial genomes fall into two distinct haplotype groups with overlapping distribution. Whether these groups are reproductively isolated, and thus two bona fide species, is an open question. We sampled P. dominula in southern Germany and the Netherlands, where both haplotypes occur syntopically.

studi.t: ManualQC: A MATLAB toolbox for visual EEG quality control and rater calibration
studi.s: ManualQC is a MATLAB toolbox for visual quality control (QC) of epoched electroencephalography (EEG) data. It provides structured QC records of each raters selections and comments on epochs, channels, and independent components (ICs). The RaterTool module combines agreement summaries with waveform replay, displaying their epoch and channel markings on the same pre-QC recording for joint review.

studi.t: Multiple classes of spindle-like oscillations reveal stereotyped lifespan dynamics amid individual variability
studi.s: Sleep spindles, 9-16 Hz transient oscillatory bursts in the sleep electroencephalogram (EEG), are linked to memory consolidation and are altered in aging and disease states. Recent work suggests that traditionally detected spindles are only a subset of a larger class of spindle-like events, and that beyond spindles exist several classes of spindle-like transient oscillatory activity. Together these classes have been shown to comprise individualized signatures of brain activity linked to disease states including schizophrenia and REM behavior disorder.

studi.t: Bridging the Babble: A Method to Correlate Varying Nomenclature and Surface Marker Definitions Across the Human Splenic B Cell Literature
studi.s: IntroductionFlow cytometry-based immunophenotyping is widely used for identifying memory B cell subsets associated with disease or immune responses. For simplicity, multi-feature surface marker vectors are often reduced to a single subset label for cell sorting, functional tests, and understanding immune cell interactions. Across the literature however, the same label is often used with significantly different phenotype feature vectors. Unfortunately, this babelization of phenotype definitions, makes it difficult to compare experimental results across studies.

studi.t: In vivo screening identifies SLC38A3 as a metabolic booster for CAR T cell therapy
studi.s: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells are highly effective against certain blood cancers, but struggle in the hostile tumor microenvironment (TME) of solid tumors. We developed the CARGO method for in vivo gain-of-function screening in CAR T cells and used it to equip CAR T cells with enhanced access to nutrients inside the TME, by overexpressing 452 solute carrier (SLC) transmembrane transporters.

studi.t: The MRE11-Rad50-Nbs1 complex acts on 3 DNA-protein covalent complexes
studi.s: DNA-protein crosslinks (DPCs) are complex lesions that block replication, transcription, and other DNA transactions. Here we investigate repair of 3 DPC lesions using the site-specific Flp tyrosine recombinase H305L mutant that forms stable covalent complexes. In human cells, removal or catalytic inhibition of MRE11 stabilizes Flp DPCs in parallel to a proteasome-dependent pathway. High levels of Flp DPCs are also observed in budding yeast, where MRE11 deletion or mutation of the nuclease domain increases covalent Flp DPC accumulation.

studi.t: Effects of insulin supplementation on senescence-associated markers and cellular phenotype of human dental pulp stem cell spheroids during long-term serum-free culture
studi.s: BackgroundIn vitro expansion of human dental pulp stem cells (DPSCs) in serum-free, three-dimensional suspension culture is important for scalable, clinically relevant manufacturing. However, this approach is limited by reduced proliferative capacity and passage-dependent senescence accumulation. In this study, we evaluated whether insulin supplementation could address these limitations while maintaining mesenchymal immunophenotype and stemness-related gene expression across serial passages in a downscale model as a reference for further DPSCs upscaling.

studi.t: AI-Driven Prediction of Drug-Target Interactions for New Chemical Entities
studi.s: BackgroundModels that Ranking compounds may improve efficiency in drug discovery; however, due to similar chemistry in train/test sets, performance is often measured using random data splits. Here, we assess the predictive performance on completely novel compounds.

studi.t: Molecularly defined olfactory bulb neuron subtypes form broad and selective pathways to cortex
studi.s: Early sensory processing decomposes rich signals into elemental features that can be conveyed through parallel neural pathways defined by cell types, each with unique local circuit organization and long-range projection targets. Outputs from the olfactory bulb are typically categorized into two broad pathways corresponding to mitral and tufted cells. Previous high-throughput molecular profiling identified finer classes, but their morphology, projection patterns, and downstream convergence remain unclear.

studi.t: A Distinct Enzyme Family Catalyzing Methyllanthionine Sulfoxide Formation in Anti-phage Lanthipeptides
studi.s: Lanthipeptides are one of the largest classes of ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptides (RiPPs). The coi biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) from Streptomyces coelicolor A3(2) encodes a canonical class I lanthipeptide dehydratase (CoiB) and cyclase (CoiC), a bifunctional enzyme (CoiSA) with an O-methyltransferase (MT) and glutamyl lyase (GL) domain, and a protein of unknown function (CoiH). The product of the coi BGC was recently shown to impart anti-phage activity, but its structure is still unresolved.

studi.t: pH selects latent allosteric states in insulin glargine assemblies
studi.s: How protein assemblies couple environmental triggers to controlled assembly and disassembly remains a central question in structural biology and biophysics. Insulin glargine provides a clinically important model for pH-triggered assembly-disassembly coupling, yet the structural pathway linking isoelectric depot to delayed release has remained unresolved. Here we combine ambient-temperature serial femtosecond crystallography, solution biophysics, and multiscale network analyses to define the pH-dependent conformational landscape of hexameric glargine across pH 8.4, 7.3, 6.4, and 5.1.

studi.t: Germ-cell restricted antigens are presented on HLA-I in premalignant colorectal lesions
studi.s: Tumour-restricted antigens displayed by HLA class I proteins are potential targets for T cell recognition, but whether they are present before a lesion becomes invasive is unknown. Here we applied high-sensitivity HLA-I immunopeptidomics to 105 individual colorectal lesions and normal mucosa from 24 donors with hereditary polyposis. We identify peptides from germ-cell-restricted genes presented in premalignant lesions, confirmed against synthetic standards, and absent from reference immunopeptidomes of benign colon. These source genes are hypomethylated in polyps relative to normal mucosa.

studi.t: Semenogelin-1 Inhibition of Mouse Sperm Hyperactivation Reveals Two Functional Domains Modulating CatSper Channel
studi.s: Seminal plasma is essential for sperm survival and function after ejaculation. Semenogelin-1 (SEMG1), the predominant seminal plasma protein, transiently suppresses sperm motility and hyperactivation after ejaculation through epididymal protease inhibitor (EPPIN) binding. However, the molecular mechanism underlying SEMG1-mediated inhibition of hyperactivation remains unclear. Here, we tested the hypothesis that SEMG1 inhibits CatSper, a sperm-specific Ca2+ channel crucial for hyperactivation.

studi.t: APOE isoforms shape brain network organization and its coupling with cardiac phenotypes in mice
studi.s: BackgroundApolipoprotein E (APOE) isoforms influence Alzheimers disease susceptibility and cardiovascular physiology, but their roles in functional brain network organization and brain-heart relationships remain incompletely understood. We investigated whether APOE genotype modifies functional brain networks and their cardiovascular, behavioral, and molecular correlates.

studi.t: Protein fitness landscapes are simpler under evolutionary distributions
studi.s: High-order epistasis is often taken as evidence that protein fitness depends on complex interactions among many mutations. The classical Walsh--Hadamard transform quantifies these interactions by weighting all genotypes equally, yet many questions in protein evolution and engineering concern fitness variations among evolutionarily plausible variants. Here we show that weighting genotypes by site-specific amino acid frequencies inferred from antibody and protein language models yields sparser, lower-order representations of protein fitness.

studi.t: WISER: spectral whitening of fixed effects for improved breeding value estimation in structured, unbalanced, and genotype-environment-confounded populations
studi.s: This work introduces WISER (whitening and successive least squares estimation refinement), a whitening-based method designed to improve breeding value (BV) estimation by accounting for population structure and genetic covariance within experimental designs. WISER provides a generalized framework applicable across diverse experimental designs, species, and omics datasets, including single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), metabolomics, and near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) used as phenomic predictors.

studi.t: Innate immune stress pathway activation underlies heterochromatin dysfunction pathology
studi.s: Heterochromatin loss disrupts nuclear architecture, gene regulation and repetitive element silencing, and is associated with diverse human diseases. However, mechanisms linking heterochromatin dysfunction to pathological phenotypes remain unclear. Through large-scale genetic interaction screens and genomic analyses in C. elegans, we identify secondary activation of an innate immune stress pathway, the Intracellular Pathogen Response (IPR), as a major contributor to heterochromatin mutant phenotypes.

studi.t: Microscopic PhotoSelection (MiPS) of single cells in mother machine microfluidic devices
studi.s: Techniques for selecting or sorting single cells within large populations of genetic variants are central to synthetic biology and biotechnology. Widely-used methods such as Fluorescence Activated Cell Sorting (FACS) enable rapid processing of large libraries, but are restricted to low-dimensional measurements taken at a single time point. As a result, sorting based on dynamic or multi-trait phenotypes---such as transient properties and properties that occur on fast timescales or in response to dynamic actuating signals---remains fundamentally challenging.

studi.t: VINE: Variational inference for scalable Bayesian reconstruction of species and cell-lineage phylogenies
studi.s: Bayesian methods are now widely used in reconstructing both species and cell-lineage phylogenies, but they remain heavily reliant on computationally intensive Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling. Phylogenetic variational inference (VI) circumvents this dependency but so far has been limited in speed and scalability. Here we introduce Variational Inference with Node Embeddings (VINE), a computational method that combines an embedding of taxa in a high-dimensional space and a distance-based "decoder" with several algorithmic innovations to dramatically improve phylogenetic VI.

studi.t: Promise and Limits of Hierarchical Dynamical RNNs for Individualized Resting-State fMRI
studi.s: Modeling individual brain dynamics from resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) remains challenging due to substantial inter-subject variability, noise, and limited data length per subject. Here, we systematically evaluate whether hierarchical shallow piecewise-linear recurrent neural networks (shPLRNNs), recently introduced as interpretable dynamical system reconstruction models, can generate individualized rs-fMRI time series while preserving subject-specific functional connectivity structure.

studi.t: Psilocybin Reconfigures Cortical Dynamics Across Temporal, Spatial, and Hierarchical Scales
