While several counterions have been explored for DNA nanostructure assembly, polyamines are particularly attractive candidates because they could support intracellular assembly of DNA nanostructures. However, a systematic analysis of natural and synthetic polyamines for DNA nanostructure assembly is currently lacking.

studi.t: Metabolism-Informed Bioreactor Model for Transferring Knowledge from Fed-batch to Continuous Biomanufacturing
studi.s: Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells remain the dominant platform for monoclonal antibody (mAb) manufacturing, and rising demand is pushing the industry from fed-batch toward continuous operation. Continuous cultures promise sustained high cell densities and volumetric productivities, but their operation depends on reliable real-time monitoring, prediction and control. Limited intracellular observability and sparse extracellular measurements hinder this, leaving a persistent gap between mechanistic understanding and predictive models used in practice.

studi.t: A spatiotemporal perturbational atlas of the post-pneumonectomy lung
studi.s: Perturbational spatial atlases have begun to map regenerative dynamics in a variety of tissues, yet lung remodeling has not been characterized at comparable spatial and temporal resolution. Post-pneumonectomy lung regeneration (PPLR) provides a tractable mammalian model for tissue regeneration that can be studied in situ. Here, we present a spatiotemporal perturbational atlas of PPLR in Rattus norvegicus, combining single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNAseq), high-resolution spatial transcriptomics (10x Genomics Xenium), and NICHES-based spatial tissue connectomics.

studi.t: Multi-omics analysis reveals how the natural compound bostrycin induces iron starvation and ferroptosis
studi.s: The development of novel anticancer drugs remains urgent due to limited efficacy of existing therapies. Natural products are a rich source for discovery of anticancer agents, yet their mechanisms often remain elusive. Bostrycin, a fungal anthraquinone with broad cytotoxicity, is one such compound. Here, we combine global and nascent proteomics with metabolomics to elucidate the mechanism of bostrycin-induced cell death.

studi.t: Tritrophic Interactions among Crapemyrtle, Crapemyrtle Aphids, and the Green Lacewing Chrysoperla rufilabris (Burmeister)
studi.s: Tritrophic interactions can have considerable impact on biological control systems, therefore, it is imperative to consider these interactions when implementing or evaluating biological control agents. Crape myrtles, Lagerstroemia indica L. x L. fauriei L., are important non-native ornamental plants from Asia that are widely planted and a major woody landscape species in the southern U.S. Six alkaloids have been identified from L. indica, mostly in the seeds and leaves.

studi.t: A spatial transcriptomic map of subcutaneous adipose tissue aging in male mice
studi.s: Aging alters adipose tissue composition and function, but the spatial organization and gene expression dynamics during lifetime remain incompletely characterized. Here we profiled spatial transcriptome-wide changes in the aging male murine inguinal white adipose tissue (iWAT). We describe ten different cell type clusters and three distinct adipocyte states. Further, we detected lipid-associated macrophages (LAMs), the cell type-enriched cluster with the largest number of genes upregulated in old age.

studi.t: Subsequent Phases of Gene Expression Leading to Commitment and Differentiation in a Eukaryotic Cell
studi.s: Cell differentiation requires the specific control of gene expression for each cell type. However, the mechanism by which robust developmental outcomes arise from inherently noisy single-cell dynamics remains unclear. To address this question, we performed a formal analysis of longitudinal time series during the commitment and differentiation of giant single cells. We tracked how the discrete expression states of individual genes changed relative to each other.

studi.t: Spectral analysis of gene-dependency networks reveals emergent organization across scales in CAR T biology
studi.s: CAR T-cell infusion products are commonly characterized in terms of their cellular populations and transcriptional programs, but these descriptions do not fully capture how a product is organized as a system. We analyzed single-cell RNA sequencing data from the infusion products of 163 patients across eight cohorts to investigate how system-level transcriptional organization relates to both clinical outcome and how cellular features vary together across patients.

studi.t: Representational geometry shapes noise-driven working memory errors
studi.s: Humans and other animals have strictly limited working memory capacity. When asked to recall one or more presented items after a delay period, subjects will occasionally recall an apparently random item: a "guess'' response. Where do these guesses come from? Using electrophysiological recordings from across monkey neocortex during the performance of a color working memory task, we show that the neural correlates of guess responses emerge during the memory delay -- and that variable encoding precision makes guesses more likely, especially in one of our two animals.

studi.t: Information Content of Cortical Recordings During Deep Brain Stimulation in Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
studi.s: Objective: This study aimed to evaluate network brain activity across both cortical and deep brain (ventral-capsule/ventral-striatum; VC/VS) sites in patients with Obsessive Compulsive Disorder (OCD) that were receiving DBS treatment. We sought to identify relationships between activity in both brain sites, and interactions between them, with evolution of OCD symptomology over treatment. We hypothesized that recordings from cortical sites would carry unique informational content that could predict symptoms and support future adaptive stimulation designs.

studi.t: Shank3 loss heightens social engagement among sibling cagemates and antagonism toward strangers
studi.s: Autism spectrum disorder is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition with strong genetic contributions and diverse social impairments. However, it remains unclear how autism-linked mutations alter social behavior across social contexts and relationships. Using SLEAP multi-animal pose tracking, we followed complete Shank3 knockout (exon 4-22 deletion) mice with adult male and female sibling cagemates over four weeks and with strangers. Unexpectedly, knockouts initiated more social contact and allogrooming with familiar cagemates.

studi.t: Nanobody-guided proximity proteomics reveals conformationally encoded molecular neighborhoods of LRRK2
studi.s: Leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2) is a multidomain signaling protein implicated in Parkinson's disease whose activity is closely linked to conformational state. How these structural transitions shape the cellular molecular environment of LRRK2 remains poorly understood. Here, we combined nanobody-mediated conformational control with miniTurbo proximity proteomics to define molecular neighborhoods associated with inhibitory, neutral, and activating LRRK2 states.

studi.t: Multimodal dynamics during naturalistic learning are associated with subsequent performance
studi.s: Learning from continuous material involves dynamic coordination of visual sampling, autonomic arousal, and neural activity, yet how these signals jointly organize during successful learning remains unclear. Here, we analysed synchronized eye-tracking, pupillometry, and EEG recordings from 86 participants from the Brain, Body, and Behavior Dataset. Using hidden Markov modelling, we identified recurrent multimodal states after accounting for stable recording-level differences and stimulus-shared responses. Three reproducible states with distinct psychophysiological profiles emerged.

studi.t: Striatal lateral inhibition regulates abnormal movements in a mouse model of levodopa-induced dyskinesia
studi.s: Striatal medium spiny neurons (MSNs) integrate convergent cortical, thalamic, and dopaminergic inputs to shape motor output. In addition, MSNs form local inhibitory synaptic connections with one another. Striatal lateral inhibition may contribute to the regulation of motor output, but its role in pathological motor function remains incompletely understood. Disruptions in motor function characterize several movement disorders, including levodopa-induced dyskinesia (LID), a complication of Parkinsons disease (PD) therapy characterized by involuntary movements.

studi.t: Frequency modulation of organelle calcium-dependent voltage oscillations provides an essential memory trace of operant conditioning in Aplysia
studi.s: Spontaneous voltage oscillations in neuronal ensembles play a critical role in memory formation and storage. Although oscillatory activities arising endogenously within central pattern-generating (CPG) networks underlie many rhythmic motor behaviors, the contribution of such autonomous signals to motor learning and memory remains poorly understood.

studi.t: Gentle touch modulates late spinal and cortical somatosensory responses without detectable changes in spinal component N13 and nociceptive flexion reflex amplitude
studi.s: Affective and gentle touch have been associated with changes in pain and somatosensory perception, but it remains unclear whether these effects reflect early spinal gating or later cortical and descending processes.

studi.t: Longitudinal Increases in Ventral Attention Network Connectivity Predict Heightened Reward and Punishment Sensitivities via Self-Control Decline in Emerging Adulthood
studi.s: Emerging adulthood is a critical developmental window for the maturation of executive control and the reorganization of intrinsic brain networks. However, the longitudinal neurobiological mechanisms underlying changes in cognitive control?and their associations with trait sensitivities?remain poorly understood. In a two-year longitudinal study, 332 emerging adults underwent behavioral assessments and resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI).

studi.t: Developmental timing of gene expression predicts dosage dominance, which tracks neuronal-glial fate in the developing human brain
studi.s: Genes implicated in brain disorders have diverse functions, but how altered dosage shapes their effects on developmental cell fate remains unclear. In a cell-state dynamics model of the developing human brain, genes expressed earlier in development responded more strongly to knockout than to overexpression, and this dosage dominance tracked neuronal-glial fate. Fate responses of 14,044 genes formed 31 modules across 21 lineages. Stronger perturbations could reverse fate responses despite correlated predicted expression changes across neuronal destinations.

studi.t: Altered ultrasonic vocalizations in mouse models of FOXG1 syndrome
studi.s: FOXG1 syndrome is a severe neurodevelopmental disorder with communication impairment as a defining clinical feature, yet vocal behavior has not been characterized in animal models of FOXG1. We examined neonatal ultrasonic vocalizations in two mouse models that disrupt Foxg1 in distinct developmental and cellular contexts: a NEX-Cre-driven conditional heterozygous model targeting postmitotic cortical and hippocampal excitatory neurons, and a W300X/+ knock-in model carrying a patient derived truncating mutation at the endogenous Foxg1 locus.

studi.t: Estradiol enhances sensory-evoked dilation of cortical penetrating arterioles in a mouse model of menopause despite pre-existing metabolic dysfunction
studi.s: Estrogen loss during menopause is a risk factor for cardiometabolic and neurovascular dysfunction, cognitive decline, and Alzheimers disease. Rodent studies of menopause have shown neuroprotective effects of 17{beta}-estradiol (E2) treatment when administered within a critical period, though these benefits have not been fully demonstrated in clinical trials of hormone therapy. A proposed explanation for this mismatch is the "healthy cell bias," where estrogen is only beneficial when initiated in physiologically intact systems.

studi.t: Objective markers of altered neural gain dissociate tinnitus and self-reported listening problems in individuals with exceptional hearing thresholds
studi.s: Many individuals experience problems that are undetected by standard hearing tests, such as persistent tinnitus and difficulties understanding speech in background noise. Here, we report evidence of altered neural gain in young adults with self-reported listening problems despite exceptional hearing thresholds.

studi.t: Automated neuroimaging meta-analysis through LLM-guided selection improves recovery of published spatial patterns
studi.s: Systematic meta-analysis enables cumulative science, but expert-led, manual workflows do not scale with the growing literature. In neuroimaging, automated frameworks are widely used but typically sacrifice precision by using coarse article selection and pooling reported results, combining different tasks, populations or comparisons even when only a subset is relevant.

studi.t: Loss of TTC5 impairs cortical development, disrupts tubulin homeostasis and progenitor mitosis in vivo
studi.s: Objective Loss-of-function mutations in the multifunctional scaffolding protein tetratricopeptide repeat domain 5 (TTC5) cause Neurodevelopmental Disorder with Cerebral Atrophy and variable Facial Dysmorphism (NEDCAFD), a recently described neurogenetic syndrome. TTC5 autoregulates tubulin translation in vitro; however, the role of TTC5 in brain development in vivo is poorly understood. Here, we define the function of TTC5 in neocortical development.

studi.t: Learning human-robot collaboration reshapes biological motor coordination
studi.s: Wearable augmentation robots expand human motor capabilities, but every added degree of freedom creates a new coordination problem for the biological body. Although previous studies have made substantial advances in robot sensing, control, and safety, they have largely overlooked how the users own movement changes: individuals adapt their body movements when they start using an augmentation robot, even when control does not require it, and this coordination pattern continues to change as they gain proficiency.

studi.t: Spatial specificity of the functional gradient echo and spin echo BOLD signal across cortical depth at 7 T
studi.s: Functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) at high magnetic field strengths ([≥]7 T) is a promising technique to study the functioning of the human brain at the spatial scale of cortical columns and layers. However, measurements most often rely on the blood oxygenation level dependent (BOLD) response sampled with a gradient echo (GE) sequence, which is known to be most sensitive to macrovascular contributions that limit their effective spatial resolution.

studi.t: Age-dependent brain pigmentation drives early neuroinflammatory molecular signatures linked to neurodegeneration
studi.s: Background: Neuromelanin (NM) is a pigment that progressively accumulates with age in catecholaminergic neurons, particularly in the substantia nigra, ventral tegmental area, and locus coeruleus. These neuronal populations are especially vulnerable to degeneration in Parkinson s disease (PD). Elevated intracellular NM levels have been linked to neurodegeneration and PD-like phenotypes in experimental models.

studi.t: Auditory cortical population codes for pitch are cue dependent
studi.s: Pitch provides a powerful example of perceptual invariance, enabling us to recognize the same melody across different instruments. The fundamental frequency (F0) at which a pitch is heard can be derived from either the harmonic spacing of frequency components (spectral cues), the waveform periodicity (temporal cues), or both. It is unclear whether population codes for F0 in auditory cortex are invariant across these acoustic cue classes.

studi.t: β-Adrenergic regulation of mGluR5-dependent Ca2+ signalling in reactive astrocytes
studi.s: Astrocytes support neuronal function and brain homeostasis and undergo structural and functional remodelling under pathological conditions. Here, we compared astrocytes maintained in serum-containing medium, modelling a blood-brain barrier-compromised reactive state, with serum-free conditions that promote a more physiological arborised phenotype.

studi.t: The Developing Human Connectome Project: Fetal Data Release
studi.s: The Developing Human Connectome Project (dHCP) represents a large open science resource designed to enable detailed investigations of typical and atypical brain development across the perinatal period. It consists of 1228 multimodal magnetic resonance image examinations of the fetal and/or neonatal brain from 1173 participants, together with collateral demographic, clinical, family, neurocognitive and genomic data.

studi.t: The metacognitive signatures of imposterism
studi.s: The imposter phenomenon (or imposterism) is a commonly reported psychological pattern in which individuals persistently doubt their abilities and accomplishments despite objective evidence of their competence. Imposterism is associated with chronic self-doubt and reduced well-being, yet its cognitive mechanisms remain unclear. In a large online sample (N = 602), we investigated how self-reported imposter feelings relate to decision-making, confidence and information search in a perceptual decision-making task.

studi.t: Fibronectin binding and non-canonical transcription factor signature distinguishes lung and bone marrow megakaryocytes
studi.s: Recent evidence has demonstrated the unique morphology and function of lung megakaryocytes (MKs), yet the source of the differences between lung and bone marrow (BM) MKs remains unclear. While BM MKs are large, polyploid, BM-resident cells primarily known as platelet producing cells, lung MKs are smaller, less polyploid, and known for immunomodulation.

studi.t: Nsg2 deficiency attenuates intestinal inflammation and colitis-associated tumorigenesis through microbiome-dependent metabolic remodeling
studi.s: Background & Aims Neuron-Specific Gene 2 (NSG2) is a neuronally expressed protein that facilitates excitatory synaptic transmission through the regulation of AMPA receptor trafficking. While its function has been characterized in the central nervous system, whether NSG2 plays a role in enteric neuronal signaling and intestinal pathology has yet to be explored. We therefore investigated whether Nsg2 deficiency modulates intestinal inflammation and tumorigenesis through gut microbiome-dependent mechanisms.

studi.t: Single cell mapping reveals phenotypic, immunometabolic and functional heterogeneity among age-associated B cells in systemic lupus erythematosus and aging
studi.s: Abstract/Summary Introduction: Age-associated B cells (ABCs) comprise an antigen-experienced memory B-cell population that expands during aging but has also been implicated in autoimmune diseases, particularly systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Cell immunometabolism has emerged as a key determinant of immune-cell function, linking metabolic adaptation to both protective and maladaptive immunity or pathological inflammation, thereby providing a platform for therapeutic intervention.

studi.t: Cholesterol and high concentration serum cooperatively enhance canine CAR T cell transduction and expansion
studi.s: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell immunotherapy is emerging as a promising adjunct treatment option for refractory canine cancers. Unfortunately, clinical trials thus far have failed to meaningfully reduce tumor burden, highlighting the need for improved CAR T cell manufacturing strategies. Effective autologous therapy requires highly viable, efficiently transduced T cells capable of robust expansion, sustained CAR expression, and long-term persistence. Although these parameters have been extensively investigated in humans, comparable optimization in canine systems remains limited.

studi.t: The immunogenic 33-mer gliadin peptide attenuates flagellin-induced TLR5/NF-kB signaling
studi.s: Wheat gluten is the main trigger of gluten-related disorders such as celiac disease, in which the proteolysis-resistant, 33-mer peptide is a key immunodominant factor. It has been reported that the 33-mer forms oligomers and thin-plate superstructures that accumulate in the Caco-2 intestinal epithelial cell line, although their biological effects remain only partially understood. Here, we screened the effects of these nanostructures on Toll-like receptors (TLRs) in Caco-2 cells to investigate their effect on the early innate immune response.

studi.t: Intravenous BCG Elicits a Sustained Myeloid IFNG Response Signature Associated with Early TB Control
studi.s: Bacille Calmette-Guerin (BCG) administered intravenously (IV) to rhesus macaques can prevent pulmonary tuberculosis (TB) infection. To establish transcriptional correlates of protection, we generated longitudinal CITE-Seq data across blood and lung after IV BCG in macaques and compared it to clinically approved intradermal (ID) BCG. We define an interferon gamma (IFNG) response signature in alveolar macrophages (AMs) comprising 61 genes with diverging expression between IV and ID BCG from 4 to 16 weeks after vaccination that was also enriched in AMs early after TB challenge.

studi.t: Alternative splicing links sex to neutrophil inflammatory vulnerability
studi.s: Mammalian females generally live longer than males, yet the immunological drivers governing sex-biased inflammatory mortality remain unclear. Neutrophils, among conserved immune cells across species, exhibit marked sex differences in inflammatory and age-related diseases. We identified conserved male-biased CD11b expression in resting neutrophils of wild-type mice, Rag2 KO mice, and in human cohorts. Male neutrophils selectively displayed CD11b-dependent transendothelial migration.

studi.t: Elucidating and Overcoming Lignin-Mediated Growth Suppression in Anaerobic Fungi
studi.s: Native to the gastrointestinal tract of herbivores, anaerobic gut fungi (AGF) (Neocallimastigomycetes) have evolved highly efficient enzymatic machinery for lignocellulose degradation. While AGF are capable of degrading lignocellulose, they more readily degrade its cellulose and hemicellulose components. Lignin is the most recalcitrant component of lignocellulose that serves as both structural support and a microbial defense strategy within plants.

studi.t: A tricomponent mRNA pertussis vaccine elicits superior protective immunity over licensed acellular pertussis vaccine against emerging antibiotic-resistant variants
studi.s: Pertussis remains a major global health burden and has been resurging rapidly over the past decade. The causes of pertussis re-emergence are multifactorial, including vaccine-induced pathogen evolution, antimicrobial resistance, and crucially suboptimal protective immunity elicited by the widely used acellular pertussis vaccine (aPV). In this study, we developed a tricomponent mRNA pertussis vaccine formulated with lipid nanoparticle (LNP), designated mPervax, which encodes inactive pertussis toxin subunit 1 (PTS1), truncated filamentous hemagglutinin (FHA) and pertactin (PRN).

studi.t: Global evolutionary and spatiotemporal transmission dynamics of human respiroviruses and orthorubulaviruses
studi.s: Human parainfluenza viruses (HPIVs) cause recurrent epidemics and are a major cause of hospitalization worldwide. However, the evolutionary and transmission dynamics driving HPIV persistence remain unclear. We analysed 1,161 archived samples representing four HPIV types from seven countries using genomic sequencing and Bayesian phylodynamic inference. We show that Respirovirus (HRV-1 and HRV-3) displayed greater fluctuations in genetic diversity whereas Orthorubulavirus (HOV-2 and HOV-4) showed more gradual changes.

studi.t: A hydrolysis operon in Lachnospiraceae provides a genetic basis to understand castalagin metabolism by the human microbiome in a clinical study.
studi.s: Gut microbes metabolize the ellagitannin castalagin to ellagic acid and urolithins, a process associated with host benefits. Despite clinical trials with the castalagin-rich camu camu extracts, the genes and taxa responsible for castalagin metabolism remain elusive. We discovered a castalagin hydrolase (cah) operon sparsely distributed in Lachnospiraceae using multi-omics.

studi.t: Calcium Signaling and Glycerol-3-Phosphate Metabolism Coordinate Extracellular Vesicle Biogenesis in Cryptococcus neoformans
studi.s: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are increasingly recognized as important mediators of fungal physiology and host-pathogen interactions, but the mechanisms governing their biogenesis remain poorly understood. Here, we combined time-course RNA sequencing with genome-wide genetic screening to define the regulatory network controlling EV production in the human fungal pathogen Cryptococcus neoformans. Transcriptomic analysis identified an EV-associated regulon enriched in genes involved in vesicular trafficking, cell wall remodeling, lipid metabolism, mitochondrial function and ion homeostasis.

studi.t: Olfactory epithelium local proteomic during SARS-CoV-2 infection in hamsters
studi.s: SARS-CoV-2 has been extensively studied since its recent emergence. It has proven to be an excellent model of respiratory virus impact on nasal epithelium for its massive impact notably on the olfactory epithelium using the hamster animal model. We and others have previously observed that following infection, the nasal epithelium is massively infiltrated by innate immune cells followed by desquamation leading to release of cellular debris in the lumen of the nasal cavity.

studi.t: CurveKinetix: A user-friendly application for analysis of biological time series data
studi.s: Of interest to many biologists is how organisms change over time: their growth, their

studi.t: Dynamic interactions of the coronavirus PEDV nucleoprotein with its viral partner nsp3 and RNA
studi.s: Summary While coronavirus genome replication and transcription occur inside double-membrane vesicles (DMVs) in infected cells, nucleocapsid assembly of genomic RNA takes place at their cytoplasmic (external) face. Neosynthesized viral mRNAs (including genomic RNA) are exported from the DMV through nsp3/nsp4 pores and genomic RNAs are believed to be selected for encapsidation through an essential interaction of the nucleoprotein N with the amino-terminal domain of nsp3.

studi.t: Strain-resolved metagenomics shows gut microbiome signatures in a case-control study of Malawian children with zoonotic schistosomiasis
studi.s: In 2024, Mangochi District, Malawi, we identified unexpected cases of zoonotic schistosomiasis associated with faecal egg excretion of Schistosoma haematobium, Schistosoma mattheei and hybrids thereof (S. haematobium x S. mattheei). Schistosomiasis is associated with gut microbiome alterations, but these associations remain unexplored in zoonotic schistosomiasis. Whether people with schistosomiasis are colonised with more closely related gut bacterial strains than people without schistosomiasis is also unclear.

studi.t: Toxoplasma gondii-induced NETs are mediated by CR3 engagement and the vital non-lytic NETosis pathway
studi.s: Approximately one-third of the global human population harbors an infection with the protozoan parasite Toxoplasma gondii. The immune system exploits neutrophils and one of their effector mechanisms, neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs), as an attempt to capture and neutralize T. gondii. NETs, composed of DNA, myeloperoxidase, citrullinated histone 3, and elastase, play a dual role in pathogen entrapment and amplification of the immune response. Traditionally, NET release was considered to result in neutrophil cell death.

studi.t: Early Corneal Host-Response Signatures Associate with Disease Severity and Etiology-Related Clinical Outcomes in Fungal Keratitis
studi.s: Background: To advance host-based predictive marker development for individual risk assessment in fungal keratitis (FK), we investigated corneal host-response gene-expression signatures associated with etiology-related disease course and clinical outcomes. Methods: We compared severity, healing, and visual outcomes in 1,304 patients with Fusarium spp., Aspergillus flavus, or culture-negative keratitis. Presentation-stage corneal scrapings from 70 prospective patients underwent bulk RNA sequencing stratified by etiology, severity, and outcome.

studi.t: H19 isoform switching during neuronal differentiation reveals a distinct pluripotency-associated non-canonical transcript
studi.s: H19 is one of the earliest discovered and most extensively studied lncRNAs, yet most studies have focused on the canonical 2,315-nt transcript arising from the IGF2/H19 locus on chromosome 11. We examined H19 isoform usage during the pluripotency-to-neuronal transition using NGN2/ASCL1-induced neurogenesis in KOLF2.1J human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs). We show that a smaller, non-canonical isoform, variant 3, is the predominant H19 isoform in the pluripotent cells examined.

studi.t: Human Precision-Cut Kidney Slices as a Translational Platform for Modelling Fibrotic, Inflammatory, Metabolic and Drug-Induced Kidney Injury
studi.s: Introduction. Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is characterised by progressive fibrosis and inflammation. Preclinical models of these processes translate poorly to human CKD. Animal models are limited by species differences, while two-dimensional cultures and organoids do not reproduce the three-dimensional, multicellular environment of the human kidney. We sought to develop and characterise precision-cut human kidney slices (PCKS) as an ex-vivo platform for studying renal disease and testing therapeutics. Methods.

studi.t: Structural basis for m2,2G27 formation and tRNA remodeling by human TRMT1L
studi.s: tRNAs acquire complex chemical signatures through ordered maturation pathways in which some enzymes contribute both catalytic and non-catalytic activities. Human TRMT1L installs m2,2G27 in tyrosine tRNA and has been reported to support D-loop acp3U20 formation, but the structural basis connecting these functions is unknown. Here, cryo-electron microscopy and mutagenesis show that TRMT1L is a homodimer that extensively reshapes its tRNA substrate. One protomer clamps the acceptor and T arms and supplies the catalytic pocket, while the other engages the anticodon loop.

studi.t: Explaining an early ground-nesting bee emergence with climate and occurrence data: Temperature, not precipitation, advances onset
studi.s: Understanding the drivers of bee phenology is important for predicting how climate change may alter the temporal overlap between bee activity and plant flowering, with consequences for pollination. We documented unusually early emergence of Melissodes tepidus timberlakei Cockerell, 1926 at a perennial nesting site in spring 2026 and examined the relationship between emergence and climatic conditions with (1) five years of nesting observations at a single site, and (2) 119 years of M. tepidus occurrence records from across the western United States.

studi.t: Publicly Available Genomic Evidence for Nipah and Avian Influenza Viruses in Bangladesh: A Scoping Assessment of Metadata Completeness and Surveillance Representativeness at the Human-Animal Interface
studi.s: Bangladesh experiences recurrent Nipah virus (NiV) outbreaks and sustained avian influenza virus (AIV) activity. Whether public genomic records contain metadata needed to assess surveillance representativeness across hosts, locations, and time is unclear.We conducted a structured, source-based scoping assessment of publicly documented NiV and AIV genomic records from Bangladesh (2001-2025), drawing on NCBI GenBank/INSDC and cited peer-reviewed and public-health sources. A pilot registry contained 108 entries (55 NiV, 53 AIV).

studi.t: RepeatViewer: a platform for explorative analysis of repetitive DNAs
studi.s: RepeatViewer is a graphical user interface application designed for repetitive sequence inspection and curation, especially focusing on, but not limited to, transposable elements (TEs). It automatically identifies structural features of TEs, including long terminal repeats (LTRs), terminal inverted repeats (TIRs), and target side duplications (TSDs). All detected and user-defined annotations can be interactively inspected, edited, and exported. RepeatViewer also integrates a TE curation workflow intended to facilitate their manual refinement.

studi.t: ONTOLOGY™: Streamlined DNA Barcoding and Metabarcoding on Nanopore
studi.s: Nanopore sequencers have unlocked the potential for a distributed network of DNA barcoding and metabarcoding laboratories. However, the realization of this potential confronts two challenges--one molecular, one computational. First, rigorous indexing protocols are critical to correctly associate sequences with their source specimen or sample; and second, data interpretation often demands processing millions of indexed reads in a structured fashion via complex bioinformatic pipelines. ONTOLOGY addresses these challenges.

studi.t: High-resolution omics and functional profiling of fatty-acid-driven metabolic modulation reveal enhanced physiological relevance of engineered heart tissues
studi.s: Background: Human pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hPSC-CMs) hold vast potential for cardiovascular disease modeling and drug discovery, yet their immaturity limits their ability to recapitulate adult cardiac physiology. Three-dimensional engineered heart tissues (3D-EHTs) provide a functional and more physiologically-relevant model for disease modeling and drug screening. However, EHTs typically retain an immature metabolic phenotype.

studi.t: RIPPLE: learning nucleotide relations in an RNA foundation model
studi.s: RNA function depends on interactions between nucleotides that can be widely separated in sequence, yet capturing these relationships remains challenging for RNA language models. Existing approaches primarily learn nucleotide relationships implicitly from individual nucleotide reconstruction or rely on external structural information to model nucleotide interactions. Here we introduce RIPPLE, an RNA foundation model that learns to identify and represent sparse, predictively useful nucleotide relationships directly from sequence.

studi.t: gPlace: fast, memory-bounded phylogenetic placement with results identical to pplacer
studi.s: Phylogenetic placement methods such as pplacer attach query sequences to a fixed reference tree, thereby establishing their evolutionary relationships to the reference sequences. These relationships can then be used to infer taxonomic classifications or likely metabolic functions. gPlace is a drop-in replacement for pplacer that produces identical results while reducing memory requirements by >3-fold and computation time by >30-fold under typical usage. These improvements are achieved by storing less data per node and streamlining the calculations used to position each query sequence.

studi.t: Cell-type label errors inflate neighborhood effects and can reverse niche claims in spatial transcriptomics
studi.s: Niche analyses ask how a cell's neighbors shape its expression beyond its type. The type comes from a label, and labels are imperfect. Here we show that label errors inflate neighborhood effects and can reverse niche claims. A mislabeled cell still expresses its true type, and because cells of a type sit near one another, the neighborhood is credited with what the label misses. Standard practice, which calls labels on the modeled counts and selects cells by them, hid, exaggerated, or reversed this inflation.

studi.t: Substrate rigidity suppresses the NRF2 antioxidant program in breast cancer cells
studi.s: Matrix stiffness rises as breast tumors progress, but whether rigidity raises or lowers activity of the KEAP1-NRF2 antioxidant pathway is contested: work in breast cancer cells places the antioxidant response on soft matrix, while work in liver cancer places response on stiff. We used publicly available transcriptome data to ask the question across laboratories rather than within one system. Of eleven series identified, four dataset arms passed quality criteria fixed before any biological analysis.

studi.t: Aggregate-Bound Chaperone Complexes Promote Disaggregation through J-Domain-Driven Hsp70 Recruitment
studi.s: Protein disaggregation by Hsp70 chaperone is essential for maintaining cellular proteostasis, particularly under stress and in proteotoxic diseases. J-domain proteins (JDPs/Hsp40s) interact with Hsp70 through their signature J-domain, stimulating ATP hydrolysis and substrate binding. Disaggregation of stress-related aggregates and amyloid fibrils strictly depends on Class B JDPs. In these specialized co-chaperones, J-domain is autoinhibited and requires activation through JDP interaction with the C-terminal EEVD motif of Hsp70. This mechanism is critical for aggregate disassembly.

studi.t: Multi-area Decision Dynamics Across Human Cortex Shape Confidence
studi.s: Theories of the neural basis of decision-making postulate a competition between choice-selective populations of neurons. Mounting evidence shows that choice-selective neural activity is distributed across many brain areas. We hypothesized that these distributed choice codes shape agents' confidence in their decision. To test this idea, we tracked the distributed dynamics of candidate neural decision variables via magnetoencephalography while human participants reported their decisions and the associated confidence in a challenging visual evidence accumulation task.

studi.t: Therapeutic signature mapping of paired direct and indirect LPS injury in an ex vivo human lung perfusion platform reveals injury-specific druggable programs
studi.s: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) remains highly morbid and lacks approved disease-modifying pharmacotherapies. Direct (pulmonary) and indirect (extrapulmonary) insults may initiate biologically distinct early injury programs, but human tissue-level evidence from the first hours is scarce. Here we establish a paired, acellular ex vivo lung perfusion (EVLP) platform using human donor lungs unsuitable for transplantation to model direct (endobronchial) and indirect (perfusate) lipopolysaccharide (LPS) injury within the same donor.

studi.t: Robust ORF Deconvolution from Multiple Ribo-seq Datasets with Group LASSO Penalty
studi.s: Ribo-seq has provided compelling evidence that there are many translated but unannotated ORFs. Despite a growing body of peptidomic support for cryptic ORFs, the computational discovery of weakly translated, short and mutually overlapping ORFs has remained a major bottleneck. Here we introduce PRICE 2, a method designed to resolve these challenging translation events by adapting concepts from isoform deconvolution. PRICE 2 employs a generative model combined with group LASSO regularized regression to jointly infer active ORFs across multiple sequencing runs.

studi.t: Artificial light at night and concealment level affect detection probability of stranded seabirds: a study with 3D-printed puffin decoys
studi.s: Fledglings of burrow-nesting seabirds are vulnerable to disorientation by artificial light at night (ALAN) and grounding in coastal human settlements, where most individuals presumably perish if not rescued. Accurate estimates of the effects of stranding on seabird populations remain elusive due to several levels of uncertainty, such as the number of stranded seabirds estimated to remain undiscovered by rescuers. One species subjected to stranding is Fratercula arctica (the Atlantic puffin). We hypothesized that the detection probability of F.

studi.t: Distinct experience-dependent reorganization of rhythmic syllable tracking in 6-month-old term and preterm infants
studi.s: Preterm birth increases the risk of later language difficulties, yet its impact on early neural mechanisms supporting language acquisition, including speech rhythm tracking, remains understudied. Using EEG, we measured neural tracking of delta- and theta-rate syllable sequences produced by the infant's mother or an unfamiliar speaker in term and preterm 6-month-old infants, modeling how oscillatory responses evolved over the course of a testing session.

studi.t: Pre-anaesthetic anxiety phenotype stratifies anaesthesia EEG, acquired navigation, and post-anaesthesia sleep in sevoflurane-exposed mice
studi.s: Preoperative anxiety is common and has been associated with postoperative delirium, yet whether an anxious phenotype changes the brain's response to anaesthesia is unknown. Here, 42 mice are classified as low-anxiety (LA) or high-anxiety (HA) by fear-retrieval freezing and exposed to sevoflurane without surgery. When adequate anaesthetic effects are reached, HA mice show a higher aperiodic spectral edge frequency than LA mice.

studi.t: 3'UTR-mediated mRNA heterodimerization eventspre-organize protein interactions to drive Wnt gene activation
studi.s: Stem cell differentiation is controlled by transcription factors that are often encoded by mRNAs with highly conserved 3'UTRs. To identify 3'UTRs with the potential to drive differentiation, we partially deleted endogenous 3'UTRs. This altered stem cell differentiation efficiency in 7/10 cases without affecting encoded protein expression in 6/7 cases. For mechanistic investigation of abundance-independent regulatory roles of 3'UTRs, we focused on CTNNB1, an mRNA that encodes the essential Wnt co-activator {beta}-catenin.

studi.t: Learning interpretable rules of protein binding from a trillion interactions
studi.s: Protein binders are invaluable as research tools and therapeutics, yet why some targets readily yield binders while others resist discovery remains poorly understood. Here we quantify this variability through more than 1,300 independent selections against 96 protein targets, experimentally surveying over one trillion protein-protein interactions. We find that binder density-the probability that a random protein variant binds a target is reproducible, varies by at least five orders of magnitude, and depends primarily on target identity rather than library design.

studi.t: A NOD2-Encoded Toggle Switch Resolves the Host-Microbe Battle Over Cyclic AMP Control
studi.s: Pathogens hijack macrophages by triggering pathological cAMP surges that block phagolysosomal killing, a defect mirrored in phagocytes from refractory colitis. We identify a host-encoded, pathogen-specific surgeprotector comprised of a three-protein toggle: The innate sensor NOD2 binds and masks an evolutionarily conserved motif in GIV that activates trimeric-GTPase Gai, enforcing a biphasic surge-to-plunge cAMP program: early, NOD2-GIV assembly permits a brief, tolerogenic cAMP rise, whereas subsequent GIV-Gai engagement collapses cAMP to drive phagolysosomal fusion and microbial clearance.

studi.t: pCASPR: A Single-Plasmid Platform for Scarless Bacterial Genome Editing
studi.s: Scarless bacterial genome editing enables the construction of stable chromosomal genotypes free of residual selectable-markers or recombination site scars, but practical workflows can be limited by plasmid handling, guide retargeting, curing, and host-specific implementation. CRISPR-Cas9/lambda-Red systems such as no-SCAR, pREDCas9/pGRB, and pCas/pTargetF established efficient donor-templated editing in Escherichia coli, but many workflows still require multi-plasmid handling, repeated guide-plasmid construction, separate curing steps, or host-specific redesign.

studi.t: Efficient 3D Cell Tracking by Integer Programming Guided by Self-Supervised Division Scores
studi.s: Recognizing divisions in cell tracking is difficult when cells are densely packed and divide frequently. A daughter can lie closer to a neighbor than to its mother, misleading distance-based linking. Visual cues can reduce such errors, but learning them often requires manual lineage annotations, which are particularly costly for 3D data. We propose an efficient self-supervised tracker trained without manual lineage annotations, using biological priors to extract reliable divisions from its distance-based tracks as labels.

studi.t: Gut bacteria-derived succinate drives enteric neuron recovery following microbiota perturbation
studi.s: Enteric neurons control gut physiology by regulating peristalsis, nutrient absorption, and secretion. Disruptions in microbial communities caused by antibiotics or enteric infections lead to loss of enteric neurons and long-term motility disorders. However, little is known about the signals and underlying mechanisms of microbiota-neuron communication. We found that both enteric neurons and glia are lost after antibiotic treatment but recover when the pre-treatment microbiota is restored.

studi.t: High-resolution, high-throughput screening reveals potent target sites for RNAi and Cas13 systems
studi.s: RNA interference (RNAi) and CRISPR-Cas13 are widely used for targeted RNA degradation, yet identifying optimal target sites remains a major bottleneck. Furthermore, it remains unclear whether these mechanistically distinct platforms share target sites because high-resolution comparative RNA knockdown data are lacking. To address this, we developed a high-throughput screening platform utilizing shRNAone, an engineered scaffold that generates highly homogeneous small RNAs.

studi.t: SuSiE 2.0: improved methods and implementations for genetic fine-mapping and phenotype prediction
studi.s: SuSiE 2.0 is a redesign of susieR for statistical fine-mapping in genetics. Its shared fitting algorithm handles individual-level data or summary statistics paired with LD matrices or genotype sketches. We used this algorithm to implement several SuSiE extensions, including SuSiE-inf, mvSuSiE, mfSuSiE, and SuSiE-rRSS, speeding up SuSiE-inf by more than 30-fold in some benchmarks. In simulations with polygenic backgrounds, SuSiE-inf substantially lowered the credible set false discovery rate relative to SuSiE, with some loss of power.

studi.t: tensorOmics: Data integration for longitudinal omics data using tensor factorisation
studi.s: Longitudinal multi-omics studies track molecular changes across biological layers and over time, but repeated measurements from the same subject introduce dependencies that must be accounted for. Conventional matrix-based approaches often flatten the data, obscuring this temporal structure. Tensor methods preserve the multi-way organisation; however, existing approaches are either unsupervised or limited to a single omic, leaving few options for phenotype-guided analysis across multiple longitudinal omics datasets.

studi.t: PCNA-Pol κ-Polδ /USP18 axes stabilize replication fork and restart to reduce cisplatin cytotoxicity
studi.s: Cisplatin and its analogues are valuable anti-cancer drugs that target the genome, block DNA replication, and induce apoptosis. As a counteractive response, cancer cells activate several mechanisms to maintain uninterrupted DNA replication, and these are yet to be fully elucidated. This study using head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) demonstrated the involvement of DNA polymerase Kappa (Polk), a translesion DNA synthesis (TLS) polymerase that primarily functions as a mismatch extender, in cisplatin resistance.

studi.t: Module-selection balance in the evolution of modular organisms
studi.s: Fitness of an organism depends on different combinations of its traits in different environments. Therefore, how a population traverses the trait space during an adaptive walk in the current environment determines its fitness in future conditions. These trait dynamics depend on two fundamental features of the genotype-phenotype-fitness map (GPFM), its degree of pleiotropy and the entropy of the trait space (i.e., how densely different regions of the trait space are populated by genotypes), but these dependencies are not well understood.

studi.t: Development and validation of LC-MS/MS bioanalytical methods to support the clinical pharmacology studies of COMP360, a form of synthetic psilocybin
studi.s: COMP360, a form of synthetic psilocybin (PSY), is being developed for the treatment of treatment-resistant depression (TRD) and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Orally-administered PSY is rapidly cleaved to the active moiety, psilocin (PSI), which undergoes further metabolism to psilocin-O-glucuronide (PSIG) and 4-hydroxyindole-3-acetic acid (4-HIAA).

studi.t: Presynaptic inhibition switches hippocampal mossy fiber computations and limits vesicle pool plasticity
studi.s: Hippocampal mossy fiber synapses act as powerful teacher synapses in CA3 memory networks, yet how their detonation properties are regulated remains unclear. Combining presynaptic and paired recordings, electron and expansion microscopy, and optogenetic stimulation in mouse hippocampal slices, we show that both exogenously applied baclofen and {gamma}-aminobutyric acid (GABA) synaptically released from inhibitory interneurons control transmission and plasticity at hippocampal mossy fiber synapses via presynaptic GABAB receptors.

studi.t: Non-fatiguing physical exercise induces sustained changes in motor unit discharge patterns and estimated synaptic inputs to motoneurons
studi.s: Non-fatiguing exercise modulates neural excitability in motor pathways controlling both exercised and unexercised muscles. Whether these effects also alter the synaptic control of spinal motoneurons remains unclear. This study investigated how acute non-fatiguing exercise influences motor unit discharge patterns and the estimated contributions of neuromodulatory input and excitation-inhibition balance, depending on muscle activation during exercise.

studi.t: Deciphering lung microbial EV pneumotypes in acute respiratory distress syndrome proteome wide
studi.s: Background. Pneumotypes hold potential predictive value for pathogenesis, outcomes, and interventions. Lung microbiome releases extracellular vesicles (EVs). However, EV-derived pneumotypes in acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) have not been studied yet. Objectives. We aimed to identify pneumotypes in ARDS patients by comprehensively profiling lung microbiome-released EV proteins in bronchioalveolar lavage fluid (BALF). Methods.

studi.t: Benchmarking sequence-to-function models and mapping enhancer-gene interactions with E2GScore
studi.s: Sequence-to-function models predict gene expression and chromatin features directly from DNA sequence and are increasingly used to infer enhancer-gene regulatory interactions. However, differences in attribution procedures and benchmarking datasets complicate comparisons between models, while the biological information captured by their enhancer-gene scores remains poorly understood. Here we introduce E2GScore, a unified framework for extracting and benchmarking enhancer-gene predictions from sequence-to-function models.

studi.t: Epstein-Barr Virus Load in Lymphoblastoid Cell Lines and Its Association with Schizophrenia
studi.s: Background: Blood Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) DNAs are reported to have genetic determinants and correlate with prevalence of autoimmune, neurological, respiratory and cardiovascular condition. However, whether a patient is more susceptible to EBV virus infection is unknown. Lymphoblastoid cell lines (LCLs) are often immortalized by infecting individuals' peripheral lymphocytes by EBV in a dish, providing an ex vivo model to address this question.

studi.t: Characterization of Natural Killer Cell-Associated Prognostic Signature Reveals Immune Landscape and Prognostic Value in Uterine Corpus Endometrial Carcinoma (UCEC)
studi.s: Background: Natural killer (NK) cells are critical in eliminating virus-infected and cancer cells. Uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma (UCEC) is a common malignancy in women, and the role of NK cells in UCEC has attracted significant attention. This study aims to develop an NK cell-related gene signature (NRGs) to improve immunotherapy response and prognosis evaluation in UCEC. Methods: Consensus clustering classified UCEC samples based on NRGs. Univariate Cox regression, differential expression, and Lasso regression were used to build a prognostic model.

studi.t: MidasTUI: Instant Tangible User Interfaces for Wearable Displays using Everyday Objects
studi.s: While wearable displays can bring digital workspaces anywhere, interaction remains limited by mid-air gestures that lack tactile feedback and induce fatigue, or controllers that are cumbersome to carry. We present MidasTUI, a system that instantly transforms arbitrary everyday objects into opportunistic tangible user interfaces through brief interaction demonstrations. For example, a user can slide an earbud case across a table as a mouse, enabling opportunistic interaction without carrying a dedicated input device.

studi.t: The Look-Elsewhere Effect in Searches for New Physics: from Classical Methods to Machine Learning
studi.s: The look-elsewhere effect (LEE) arises when the location of an effect in parameter space is not specified in advance: scanning many locations inflates the significance of the largest excess, and the local $p$-value must be corrected into a global one. A well-established framework, rooted in the work of Davies and operationalised for particle physics by Gross and Vitells, provides this correction for scans over continuous parameters. Some aspects, however, remain unsettled. The definition of "elsewhere" is ambiguous and ranges from a single distribution to an entire experimental programme.

studi.t: Atheism and Cross-Country National Cognitive Skills: Evidence from a Beta Regression Analysis
studi.s: This study performs a beta regression analysis to investigate how country-level cognitive skills---measured using harmonized large-scale international educational assessments and expressed on an IQ-type scale---are associated with the prevalence of atheism in 131 countries. We find that this association is nonlinear: at low levels of cognitive skills, increases are associated with lower expected levels of atheism, whereas beyond a threshold, they are associated with higher expected atheism rates. This turning point is estimated to occur at approximately 65 on the IQ-type scale.

studi.t: A Survey of Security, Privacy, and Ethics of Large Language Models in Telecom
studi.s: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into telecommunications for customer service, network analytics, and operational support. While offering efficiency and innovation, their deployment raises critical privacy, security, and ethical challenges due to the uniquely sensitive and longitudinal nature of telecom data. This paper presents a survey of LLM risks and safeguards in telecom context.

studi.t: Model Weights, Airlocks and Sandboxes: A Call for Technical Validation of Re-identification Tests under the EDPB Anonymisation Guidelines
studi.s: The Guidelines 02/2026 on anonymisation of the European Data Protection Board (EDPB), published for consultation in July 2026, assess anonymity relative to the entities that may access data. They bring AI models into scope and call for testing, but do not say how a re-identification test should be designed or validated, or how far its result counts as evidence.

studi.t: Proverbs As A Window On Collective Prescriptions
studi.s: Proverbs, as repositories of traditional wisdom, have informed human reasoning for millennia. Yet the collective prescriptions they encode have remained largely unquantified. We introduce a computational framework to analyze nearly 50,000 English-language proverbs. Using large language models, validated against human judgments, we map the topical landscape of proverbs, assess their prescriptive power, and quantify their recommendations on key dimensions of human judgment and behavior.

studi.t: Modeling time series of high-resolution spectra using the asymmetric Hilbert-Schmidt decomposition with application to radial velocity exoplanet searches
studi.s: We describe a framework for building low-rank separable expansions to model spectroscopic data from systems with time-varying spectra, in settings where the spectral dimension is finely sampled (in wavelength), but the temporal dimension is sparsely and possibly irregulary sampled. The motivating application is detection and characterization of small exoplanets, e.g., Earth-like planets around Sun-like stars.

studi.t: A multi-patch model for sylvatic hematophagous vector dynamics: the impact of landscape anthropization
studi.s: We develop a multi-patch model for sylvatic hematophagous vector--(wild) animal interactions with nonlinear migration terms that depend on landscape anthropization. Every patch is a suitable habitat for both animals and vectors, but anthropization reduces the animal carrying capacity and induces animal and vector displacement. We considered three dispersal types. Under unconstrained global dispersal, displaced individuals can move to any other patch.

studi.t: How Large are Monetary Policy Effects? dentifying the Shocks in a VAR also Identifies the Constants
studi.s: Restrictions on the contemporaneous effects matrix used to identify fundamental shocks in a structural VAR, also determine the mapping from the structural constant terms to the reduced form constant terms. In some models one will have priors about these structural constant terms and these should therefore be included in a Bayesian estimation procedure. We illustrate the potential significance of this using the analysis of monetary policy by Baumeister and Hamilton (2018) as a motivating example.

studi.t: ENSO-linked redistribution of post-monsoon tropical cyclone energy between the Arabian Sea and the Bay of Bengal: 1982--2025
studi.s: Tropical cyclones in the North Indian Ocean (NIO) form in two sub-basins, the Arabian Sea (AS) and the Bay of Bengal (BoB), which are usually studied separately, with their relationship to the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) treated as stationary. We develop a joint inter-basin statistical framework and apply it to 416 disturbances from quality-controlled IBTrACS best tracks for 1982--2025, with harmonised IMD and JTWC intensities, ERA5 and ERSSTv5.

studi.t: Decision and Support Mechanisms under Platform Information Overload: A Generative-Agent Experiment on College Application
studi.s: People now make major personal decisions surrounded by far more online information than they can read, yet research says little about why information overload affects some people more than others. We study this question in Chinese college applications, a high-stakes decision made amid heavy online content where each list can be scored objectively once admission cutoffs are released. We simulated 90 applicants using language-model agents with family backgrounds from a national household survey.

studi.t: Who Fills the Gap? Role Similarity and Teammates' Minutes When NBA Players Are Ruled Out
studi.s: When a core player is ruled out before an NBA game, do teammates whose statistical role resembles that of the removed set (every rotation player ruled out, about three per case) play more? Using injury reports stamped at least six hours before tip-off and rosters reconstructed after the season, we study 2,441 team-games from 2023-24 to 2025-26 in which a core player was ruled out for a medical reason.

studi.t: Supporting Without Taking Over: AI Support in Gratitude Writing
studi.s: Gratitude writing can support well-being, but independent practice may lack guidance. Generative AI could help while shaping reflection, agency, and ownership. We investigated how gratitude-writing format and AI-assistance mode influence well-being and writing experiences. In a 2x2 between-subjects study (N=401), participants completed a gratitude reflection or a gratitude letter using two AI-assistance modes: scaffolding, which provided reflective questions after inactivity, or co-writing, which offered inline text suggestions.

studi.t: Atunda: Building an Afrogenic Dance Movement Dataset for AI-Driven Classification
studi.s: This paper introduces Atunda, the first systematically collected video dataset of Afrogenic dance moves, designed for training and evaluating deep learning models for movement classification. The first phase of the dataset includes nearly 400 videos covering 13 distinct dance moves from African and African Diaspora performative culture, making it the first AI-ready resource of its kind. Using this dataset, we train and evaluate various configurations of temporal convolutional neural networks, achieving a classification accuracy exceeding 95%.

studi.t: The Hawkes Hypergraph Copy Model: A Semi-mechanistic Generative Model for Temporal Hypergraphs
studi.s: Many complex networks involve time-varying relations between more than two nodes. Such networks are naturally modeled by temporal hypergraphs. We propose the Hawkes Hypergraph Copy Model (HHCM), a semi-mechanistic model for temporal hypergraphs that combines a Hawkes process to model the timestamps of hyperedges with a noisy copy mechanism to model the nodes present in hyperedges. Each hyperedge is either generated as an exogenous event with a baseline rate or an endogenous event as a noisy copy of a previous hyperedge.

studi.t: Procedure Inference as Memory: Learning Recruiter Decision Procedures from OKF-Structured Episodes in Multi-Session Hiring Assistants
studi.s: Multi-session hiring assistants must infer evolving recruiter preferences and decision patterns across projects and time. We introduce Open Knowledge Format (OKF)-indexed episodic memory to organize interactions and retrieve related events through their lineage. We also introduce Procedure Memory, which learns reusable decision procedures from these episodes through prompted reflection or reinforcement learning.

studi.t: The Last Expectation: Sampling Measurement Outcomes in Value of Information Analysis
studi.s: In decision-making under uncertainty, additional information can improve decisions but is often costly to acquire. The Value of Information (VoI) quantifies the expected benefit of different information-gathering strategies. The main computational burden in VoI analysis arises from evaluating the expected utility of a strategy over possible outcomes. As each outcome entails solving a computationally expensive optimization problem under uncertainty to determine the optimal decision, efficient estimation of this expectation is crucial.

studi.t: Where Does the Asymmetry Enter? Staging a Fairness Audit Across a Fused Multimodal Moderation Pipeline
studi.s: Almost every short-video upload now passes through a classifier that fuses video, speech, and on-screen text into one decision about whether it may be seen. It moderates every language community on the platform at once, and fairness across them is judged, if at all, from one accuracy score. That score is compatible with error falling almost entirely on one language group. An audit that goes looking reads the model's decisions, the last stage of a long pipeline and the one whose test has the fewest items.

studi.t: Decision-Aligned Value Learning for Selective Adoption of EEG Fusion in Human-Robot Collaboration
studi.s: Electroencephalography (EEG) captures neural activity associated with human perception and decision-making. It provides human-robot collaboration (HRC) systems with measurable evidence for event recognition, situation assessment, and action preparation. External sensing cannot easily provide such evidence. However, the quality and complementarity of this evidence vary across samples, and existing EEG fusion methods do not explicitly determine when EEG improves a prediction.

studi.t: Towards Democratized Academic LLM Hosting: Practical insights from needs, implementations, and governance across Dutch institutions
studi.s: Academic LLM hosting is emerging as an operational infrastructure domain with recurring socio-technical patterns, tensions, and governance requirements across institutions. Based on a workshop with academic infrastructure, research-support, education, and policy-adjacent stakeholders, this paper synthesizes current practices and open questions around institutionally governed LLM services for Dutch academia.

studi.t: RecField: Embedding Recommendations into Spatial Movie Organization as Affordances for Serendipitous Encounters
studi.s: Research on serendipity-oriented recommender systems has focused on algorithms that recommend unexpected yet useful items. However, serendipity is increasingly viewed as a user experience shaped by both algorithmic outputs and system features. This study positions recommendations not as the primary goal users pursue but as an environmental affordance that creates opportunities for discovery during other activities. We propose RecField, a spatial movie organization interface where users freely arrange movies into collection zones.

studi.t: The cost of being seen as AI in group bargaining
studi.s: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes embedded in collective decision-making, people's perceptions of AI may shape who reaches agreement and what they receive. We studied this in a repeated three-player majoritarian bargaining game with 2,234 participants. Players saw each opponent identified as Human or AI. The instructions described AI as acting either independently or on behalf of a human. Human participants made every decision.

studi.t: Data Centers: The Error of Generalizing Environmental and Socioeconomic Impacts. The Need for a Contextualized Assessment of Computing Infrastructure in Brazil and Worldwide
studi.s: The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence and cloud computing has intensified debates about the environmental and socioeconomic impacts of data centers, including electricity and water consumption, noise, land use, and employment. A recurring methodological problem in these debates is the use of global data, or of evidence produced in a particular country, to draw conclusions about facilities located in very different settings.

studi.t: Gadd45 regulates fate decisions of myeloid-type blood cells in Drosophila
studi.s: Growth arrest and DNA damage-inducible 45 (Gadd45) is a conserved, stress-responsive regulator linking cellular stress and cytokine signaling to cell-cycle control, DNA repair, apoptosis, and differentiation. Altered Gadd45 expression has been associated with mammalian solid tumors and hematopoietic malignancies. Gadd45 also supports cytokine-induced myeloid differentiation, though the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Using the Drosophila hematopoietic system and in vivo genetic and cell-biological approaches, we investigated Gadd45's role in myeloid-type blood cell development.

studi.t: FastHer: a fast and accurate estimator of local heritability from summary statistics
studi.s: We present FastHer, a method for estimating local heritability using GWAS summary statistics and linkage disequilibrium (LD) matrices. FastHer performs exact restricted maximum-likelihood estimation matching the accuracy of individual-level methods. Analytical transformations ensure high computational efficiency. FastHer incorporates SNP weights that define the contribution of each SNP to heritability. The introduction of a model-data concordance parameter enables the adaptation of reference LD matrices when in-sample LD matrices are unavailable.

studi.t: Auxin and cytokinin antagonistically regulate Arabidopsis root distal stem cell fate through opposing pairs of HD-Zip II transcription factors
studi.s: The antagonistic action of auxin (IAA) and cytokinin (CK) regulates several aspects of plant development including stem cell specification and maintenance. In the Arabidopsis thaliana root, the fate of distal stem cells (DSCs) is mainly regulated by IAA, while the function of CK is still ill-defined. Here, by investigating the role of the HD-Zip II transcription factor family in distal tissues, we uncover CK as a proliferative input for DSCs, acting in opposition to IAA. We show that opposing pairs of HD-Zip II proteins regulate DSCs fate by integrating IAA and CK signals.

studi.t: Structured stabilization in recurrent neural circuits through inhibitory synaptic plasticity
studi.s: In cortical circuits, inhibitory interneurons play a dual role: they regulate overall activity levels to prevent runaway excitation, and contribute to diverse computations. While unstructured inhibitory synaptic connections achieve the first role by homeostatically regulating firing rates, computational tasks often require structured excitatory-inhibitory (E/I) connectivity.

studi.t: A hydrogenase-like activity associated with mitochondrial Complex I under hypoxia in vascular plants
studi.s: Abstract Molecular hydrogen (H2) evolution by higher plants under oxygen limitation was reported more than six decades ago, yet its origin, biochemical basis and physiological significance remain unresolved. Here, we localize this activity to a mitochondrial, Complex I-associated electron-transfer system: fractions from etiolated Vigna radiata hypocotyls accumulated H2 under hypoxia at mildly acidic pH. H2 accumulation was nearly abolished by rotenone and sensitive to perturbations of Complex II, quinone-pool turnover, terminal oxidases and protonmotive force.

studi.t: Common excluder barley has more than one mechanism to remove Cd from chloroplasts.
studi.s: Chloroplasts comprise photosynthesis and other important processes. Plants protect chloroplasts from stresses including Cd accumulation. Common terrestrial plants, excluders apply a set of mechanisms to restrict Cd penetration to chloroplasts. Removal of accumulated Cd from chloroplasts should also be a beneficial strategy. However, we do not know whether excluder plant species have ability to remove Cd from chloroplasts. We used barley as a common excluder plant species.

studi.t: Neurofeedback enhances a neural signature of selective attention to speech in cocktail-party settings
studi.s: Understanding speech in noisy situations is challenging and often fails due to attentional rather than sensory deficits. We report here that neurofeedback can enhance a neural signature of selective attention to speech in a cocktail-party setting. Neural responses to speech were quantified in participants' electroencephalogram (EEG) while they attended to one of two audiobooks, presented simultaneously. After each 22s-segment of speech, the participants' N1 component was extracted from the temporal response function (TRF). The N1 component is known to be sensitive to attention.

studi.t: Dysregulated SETX activity at R-loops links transcriptional and splicing alterations to compromised neuronal identity in ALS4
studi.s: RNA dysregulation is an increasingly recognized driver of neurodegenerative diseases, yet the mechanisms linking defects in RNA metabolism to selective neuronal vulnerability remain poorly understood. Alterations in R-loop homeostasis have been observed in neurodegeneration, but it is unclear how these contribute to neuronal dysfunction. To address these questions, we investigate ALS4, a juvenile form of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis that is caused by mutations in the helicase SETX, which functions in R-loops resolution and transcription termination.

studi.t: Pollinator specificity among three co-flowering Mediterranean Aristolochia species pollinated by Diptera
studi.s: Attracting species-specific pollinators can be favoured by natural selection to avoid reproductive interference between sympatric plant species. However, the ways in which fine differences in floral traits lead to the attraction of species-specific pollinators are diverse and unknown in most pollination interactions. We surveyed pollinators on three Aristolochia species that can occur in pairs in sympatry (A. clematitis-A. rotunda and A. pistolochia-A.

studi.t: A spatially patterned Gdf15 response links maladaptive nephron remodeling to polyuria during toxic exposure
studi.s: Lithium impairs renal water conservation and induces microcystic remodeling. Whether these functional and structural complications of treatment share a common mechanism is unknown. Using high-definition spatial transcriptomics, we identify renal growth differentiation factor 15 (Gdf15) induction in vivo along a corticopapillary gradient paralleling lithium accumulation. This response accompanies epithelial stress signatures and persists despite vasopressin V2 receptor blockade.

studi.t: Space-based and object-based saccadic selection in visual working memory
studi.s: Saccades made during memory maintenance prioritize memory for the saccade target, but it is unclear if this benefit is specific to a location or extends across memorized objects. In three experiments, we examined whether saccadic selection spreads to other locations within the same object. In Experiment 1, we asked observers to remember three oriented Gabors presented either within contour-defined objects or without object structure. A subsequent movement cue prompted observers to move their eyes to the indicated location.

studi.t: Development of microsatellite markers with the SSRseq method on Glossina palpalis gambiensis, and G. p. palpalis, and analysis of corresponding field samples from three sleeping sickness foci: Boffa, Dubreka (Guinea), and Bonon (Cote d'Ivoire).
studi.s: Tsetse flies are strictly found is sub-Saharan Africa where they are responsible for the transmission and maintenance of African trypanosomiases in humans (HAT) and animals (AAT). Vector control has been recognized as an essential tool to fight against these diseases. Nevertheless, it requires the best possible knowledge of the biology of the targeted population. Population genetics tools can prove very useful to obtain such information but require the use of polymorphic and reliable genetic markers.

studi.t: Transcriptomic-Methylation Integration and Machine-Learning Prioritization of Candidate Prognostic Biomarkers in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer: A Retrospective Computational Study
studi.s: Background: Triple-negative breast cancer is molecularly heterogeneous, complicating prognostic stratification. We aimed to derive a gene panel and clinical-genomic survival nomogram and assess cross-platform performance. Methods: This retrospective computational study analyzed The Cancer Genome Atlas breast cancer data, identifying 197 primary-tumor transcriptomic aliquots from 190 patients. Differential gene-expression and deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) methylation analyses comparing Dead versus Alive vital status were performed separately.

studi.t: The compartmentalized activity of a legume subtilase SBT12a allows symbiosome stabilization
studi.s: The stabilization of rhizobia in specialized organelles, called symbiosomes, is an evolutionary hallmark for maintaining high rates of nitrogen fixation in legumes. This is achieved by releasing thousands of bacteria from nodular infection threads into a single plant cell, which poses a great challenge for the host to keep control over these differentiated bacteria. Considering the importance of proteolytic degradation of antimicrobial proteins or generation of symbiosis-promoting signalling factors, proteolytic activity may represent a key regulatory system in this process.

studi.t: Human iPSC-derived Olfactory Sensory Organoids model olfactory function and drug response
studi.s: Intranasal drug delivery is being explored as an alternative approach to overcome the blood-brain barrier in the treatment of central nervous system diseases. However, little is known about how therapeutics administered through this route affect human olfactory tissue. Here, we develop human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived olfactory sensory organoids that reproduce key cellular and functional features of the developing olfactory system.

studi.t: A functional analysis of action potential generation in the axon initial segment in two autism mouse models with loss-of-function mutations of the Nav1.2 sodium channel
studi.s: Loss-of-function (LoF) mutations of the SCN2A gene, coding for Nav1.2 Na+ channels, are among the leading genetic contributors to autism spectrum disorders and intellectual disability (ASD/ID). The haploinsufficient Scn2a knock-out mouse (Scn2a+/-), displaying ASD/ID-like phenotypes, is commonly used as model for this channelopathy, although this specific mutation has not been identified in patients.

studi.t: Frequency-Selective Responses to Temporal Interference Stimulation in Hippocampal Neurons
studi.s: Temporal interference (TI) stimulation aims to engage deep brain structures noninvasively by superimposing two slightly detuned high-frequency electric fields (e.g. > 2 kHz), producing a low-frequency envelope (1-120 Hz) where they overlap. Existing accounts explain why a neuron responds to the envelope, but none identifies what determines which beat frequency a given neuron amplifies most.

studi.t: Developmental timeline of the lateral olfactory tract innervation of piriform cortex
studi.s: The development of the lateral olfactory tract (LOT) begins embryonically and is closely linked to the differentiation of olfactory bulb (OB) projection neurons, mitral and tufted cells, whose axons form the LOT. Here, we implemented calretinin (CR) as a proxy to characterize LOT development. Immunohistochemistry (IHC) for CR revealed expression in most mitral/tufted cells, with lower levels in the dorsal OB. This mirrored a reduced CR labeling in a restricted ventral LOT domain, suggesting topographic organization of OB projections.

studi.t: Functional and Neurotransmitter Organization of Cortical Gray Matter Remodeling During Pregnancy
studi.s: Pregnancy is a period of profound neuroplasticity, marked by widespread, spatially heterogeneous reductions in cortical gray matter volume (GMV). Yet, whether this remodeling affects cognition is unclear: subjective memory complaints are common during pregnancy, but objective findings are mixed. Using densely sampled longitudinal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) across pregnancy, we examined whether gestational GMV change corresponds spatially with normative maps of cognitive function and neurotransmitter receptors.

studi.t: Separating robust from fragile cell-type changes in spatial transcriptomics using screening label uncertainty to identify composition effects
studi.s: Imaging-based spatial transcriptomics platforms such as 10x Xenium measure thousands of genes in intact tissue at single-cell resolution, making them attractive for screening which cell populations change between experimental conditions. In small studies, however, apparent changes in cell-type composition can arise from misannotated cells rather than biology, and the reliability of individual cell-type calls is rarely reported.

studi.t: Mapping the invisible: Incidental spatial encoding through haptic exploration
studi.s: Active touch provides rich spatial information about object shape. Whether this haptic information can be retained without an explicit memorisation goal remains unclear. Participants explored an unfamiliar two-dimensional raised-dot contour under different sensory conditions and memorisation instructions. Two haptic groups traced the contour hidden from view, either without advance knowledge of the memory tasks (Haptic-Naive) or with explicit memorisation instructions (Haptic-Informed).

studi.t: Modelling mouse barrel cortex: from anatomical structure to cortical dynamics
studi.s: Detailed biophysical simulations of neuronal networks might help understand brain function.
