Here, we built a model of mouse barrel cortex focused on its somatotopic map, comprising 33 barrel columns. We investigated dendritic polarity in layer 4 and implemented it in the model, building two circuits differing in a single property of basal dendritic synthesis. In the polarised circuit, layer 4 dendrites were confined to their home barrel; in the symmetric circuit, they were not.

studi.t: Sex differences in corticostriatal regulation of alcohol drinking following chronic intermittent alcohol exposure
studi.s: Background: Sex differences in alcohol use disorder (AUD) suggest that the neural circuits regulating alcohol intake may differ between males and females. We examined whether infralimbic neurons projecting to the nucleus accumbens shell (IL-NAcSh) regulate alcohol self-administration and anxiety-related behavior following chronic intermittent alcohol (CIA) exposure.

studi.t: Supplier-associated variation in motor performance and cerebrospinal fluid-contacting neuron anatomy in C57BL/6 mice
studi.s: Cerebrospinal fluid-contacting neurons (CSF-cNs) are an evolutionarily conserved population of spinal sensory neurons positioned around the central canal and characterized by expression of the ion channel PKD2L1. CSF-cNs contribute to locomotor control, but little is known about variation in this sensory system among commonly used laboratory mouse populations. We compared motor performance and CSF-cN organization in closely related C57BL/6 mice obtained from The Jackson Laboratory (Jackson), Charles River Laboratories (Charles River), and Taconic Biosciences (Taconic).

studi.t: Severity of Addiction-like Behaviors and Sex Distinctly Promote Oxycodone-Related Behaviors in Heterogeneous Stock Rats
studi.s: The opioid epidemic continues to impose substantial public health burdens. Critical gaps remain in understanding how sex and individual differences contribute to opioid addiction-like behavior. Although previous clinical and preclinical work has identified sex and other individual differences in opioid-related outcomes, it remains unclear whether the magnitude of sex differences varies across behavioral domains and levels of individual addiction-like vulnerability.

studi.t: Linking Molecular Changes in the Hypothalamus to Alzheimer's Disease Phenotypes
studi.s: In many individuals with Alzheimer's disease (AD), sleep disruption and weight loss emerge years before the onset of memory decline and dementia. However, the cellular and molecular bases of these early events are not well understood. The hypothalamus is a critical brain region for the regulation of these behaviors, but its response to amyloid has not been systematically characterized.

studi.t: How Experience Becomes a Program: Episodic Memory as a Difference Engine
studi.s: A child who has seen a few sums can add numbers of any length: finite experience has become a program, a procedure with memory that holds for inputs of every size. Networks learn procedures by passing errors backward through every step of a computation, over many examples, and what they learn on short inputs seldom holds on long ones. Brains keep something networks discard, the experiences themselves, and we propose that they keep them in order to compare them. When two remembered experiences differ in one place, the first answer at which they differ depended on that place.

studi.t: Brain pericyte lineages converge on a shared molecular profile
studi.s: Brain pericytes arise from two embryonic lineages, neural crest and mesoderm, but it is unknown whether these origins produce molecularly distinct pericyte populations. Using zebrafish lineage-tracing transgenics, we mapped neural crest- and mesoderm-derived pericytes across the brain from larval to adult stages. Neural crest-derived pericytes occupied the forebrain and mesoderm-derived pericytes occupied the midbrain and hindbrain at early stages. A population of neural crest-derived pericytes then appeared in the dorsal midbrain by 10 days post-fertilization and persisted into adulthood.

studi.t: Methods for precise targeting and modulation of the axon initial segment
studi.s: The axon initial segment (AIS) is fundamental to action potential initiation, neuronal polarity maintenance, and plasticity. Despite its functional importance, AIS remains understudied partially due to the lack of molecular tools with high subcellular specificity. By engineering an ultra-high affinity (Kd ~0.37 nM) small binder (16 kDa) that exclusively targets 480-kDa ankyrin-G, the master scaffold of AIS, and integrating neuronal type-specific promoters with feedback-regulated expression elements, we developed an efficient, portable method for delivering tightly controlled amounts of…

studi.t: Multicellular nodules form at subacute time points following closed-head diffuse traumatic brain injury in pigs
studi.s: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a leading cause of long-term neurological impairments and is associated with persistent neuroinflammation. Multicellular nodules, composed of densely aggregated myeloid cells, have been reported in human post-mortem tissue following TBI but remain poorly characterized. Here, we utilized a clinically relevant porcine model of closed-head diffuse TBI generated through rotational acceleration to characterize the temporal and spatial distribution of these nodules.

studi.t: Neurogenic archetypes and diversifiers configure the molecular and functional organization of corticofugal output channels
studi.s: Cortical extratelencephalic neurons (ET) derive from either direct neurogenesis from radial glia cells (ETd) or indirect neurogenesis through intermediate progenitors (ETi), but whether and how neurogenic origin contributes to ET diversity and function remains unknown. Using genetic strategies that differentially target ETd and ETi, we profiled their transcriptomes across the isocortex and imaged their activity in motor cortex during a reach-grasp-drink (RGD) task.

studi.t: Reciprocal 16p11.2 Copy Number Variants Differentially Alter Regional Brain Anatomy and Allometric Scaling
studi.s: Reciprocal 16p11.2 copy-number variants (CNVs) confer substantial risk for neuropsychiatric disorders and produce opposing effects on brain size, with larger brain volume in deletion carriers and smaller volume in duplication carriers. Regional alterations broadly parallel this global phenotype, but because regional brain measures scale nonlinearly with brain size, it remains unclear whether regional differences reflect expected consequences of altered brain size, regional anatomy disproportionate to brain size, or fundamental alterations in allometric scaling.

studi.t: An Open, Evolving Brain and Cognitive Aging Simulator Enabled by Agentic Artificial Intelligence
studi.s: An agentic AI simulator was built to advance our understanding about how the human brain and cognition change with age. The simulator generates worlds based on hypothesized age-linked cascades and then simulates studies across varied experimental designs and selection criteria. Each simulated world begins with 120,000 individual lives initiated by baseline parameters (e.g., genetic risk, birth year) and then changed by age-dependent cascades (e.g., amyloid-dependent, cardiovascular).

studi.t: Neuronal communication subspaces arise across prefrontal-striatal circuits prior to gaze-directed object selection and develop with learning
studi.s: How neuronal ensembles determine the most relevant object to attend to remains unresolved but likely involves coordinating information across multiple brain areas. We found support for this hypothesis in latent firing co-variations across the prefrontal cortex (PFC), anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), and head of the caudate (CD) during and after attention-set learning. Before gaze shifted to an object, neuronal communication subspaces emerged across area pairs.

studi.t: Excitation/Inhibition Balance in People at Clinical High Risk for Psychosis: A Functional MRI Study
studi.s: Excitation/inhibition (E/I) imbalance is implicated in the pathophysiology of psychosis, but the extent to which this is evident before the onset of illness is unclear. Here, we investigated E/I-related brain dynamics using the Hurst exponent (HE) derived from resting-state MRI in two longitudinal cohorts of individuals at clinical high risk for psychosis (CHR-P): PSYSCAN (190 CHR-P individuals and 115 controls) and Accelerating Medicines Partnership(R) Schizophrenia (826 CHR-P individuals and 241 controls).

studi.t: The computational cost of explicit strategies in force-field adaptation
studi.s: Sensorimotor adaptation is often attributed to an implicit, cerebellar-based process, particularly when learning to compensate for novel limb dynamics. However, recent evidence suggests that explicit strategies can also contribute to force-field adaptation, although how these strategies are represented and implemented is unclear. In visuomotor adaptation, explicit strategies can rely on an algorithmic-like process in which the time required to prepare a movement increases with the magnitude of the required correction.

studi.t: Mouse pup ultrasonic vocalization repertoires shift with age and behavioral context across the first postnatal week
studi.s: Pup ultrasonic vocalizations (USVs) are thought to communicate and elicit maternal care, yet the structure of the pup call repertoire and how it changes across the vulnerable first postnatal week remain poorly characterized. Here we analyzed approximately 59,000 USVs emitted by wildtype mouse pups (postnatal days P0-P5) during a pup retrieval paradigm that included habituation, pup isolation, and retrieval phases, performed with wild-type (WT) and Mecp2-heterozygous (Het) female mice as alloparental surrogates.

studi.t: A Platform for Semi-automatic Segmentation, CharacteristicShape Analysis and Simulation of Neuronal Nuclei
studi.s: Segmenting neuronal somas in 3D brain images obtained through techniques such as tissue clearing and Light Sheet Fluorescence Microscopy promises to advance our understanding of healthy brains and the pathophysiological roots of neurological diseases. However, manual segmentation methods are often costly and time-consuming. Automating the segmentation through deep neural networks shows promise, but requires labeled ground-truth data that is also labor-intensive and expensive to obtain.

studi.t: Joint Representation of Valence and Arousal in the Human Brain
studi.s: Scenes varying in emotional content are commonly characterized along two affective dimensions: hedonic valence, reflecting pleasantness, and emotional arousal, reflecting intensity. Although prior studies have examined neural representations of valence and arousal separately, it remains unclear how these dimensions are represented jointly and how their representation relates to low-level visual and scene-level properties.

studi.t: Benchmarking machine learning across development reveals stage-specific neuroanatomical sex signatures.
studi.s: Machine learning (ML) offers powerful approaches for identifying multivariate patterns in neuroimaging data, yet the biological validity and interpretability of the discriminative patterns learned by such models remain incompletely understood. Here, we benchmarked multiple ML approaches for sex classification across development (8-21 years) on structural neuroimaging data and investigated the effects of age on model performance and feature stability.

studi.t: Sampling the Training Trajectory of Vision Models Reveals a Mismatch with Human Visual Development
studi.s: We compare time-resolved EEG representational geometry across seven age groups, from 6 months to adulthood, with representations sampled throughout training from supervised and self-supervised ResNet-50 and ViT-B/16. Previous model-brain comparisons mostly used adult brain recordings and untrained or fully trained networks. We find that successive training stages do not systematically progress from child- to adult-like neural representations: alignment with every age group from 4 years onward emerges early in training and remains stable.

studi.t: Does Denoising Reduce Cross-Vendor Variability in Diffusion MRI? A Travelling Heads Evaluation
studi.s: Between-scanner variability in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-derived features can be comparable to biological between-subject variability, even for the same individual scanned at different sites. MRI harmonisation is therefore an essential tool to ensure studies are generalisable across sites, reducing between-scanner variability and enabling pooling of data to achieve large sample sizes and more representative population samples.

studi.t: Jump: Making Large-Scale Connectomics Accessible
studi.s: Large-scale connectomic resources generated from volumetric electron microscopy (EM) have transformed neuroscience by enabling detailed 3D reconstructions of cellular and subcellular morphology and connectivity across hundreds of thousands of cells in diverse tissues and organisms. Recent advances in machine learning-based cell classification and automated segmentation have enabled large-scale annotation of these datasets, yet barriers remain in validating automated classifications and extracting biological insights.

studi.t: Childhood Trauma Severity Compounds Reward Anticipation Disruption in Substance Use Disorders
studi.s: Background: Substance use disorders (SUD) are associated with reward circuit disruptions and high rates of trauma. Trauma has been found to reduce propensity to engage frontal, limbic, and striatal regions during reward anticipation. However, the interactive effect of trauma and SUD on anticipatory reward circuitry remains unclear.

studi.t: Extracellular tumor-derived IL-33 promotes ST2-dependent tumor control
studi.s: Interleukin-33 (IL-33) is a pleiotropic cytokine with both nuclear and extracellular functions as well as context-dependent roles in tumor immunity. Although tumor-derived IL-33 can promote anti-tumor immune responses, the contribution of its subcellular localization and extracellular availability to tumor control remains poorly understood. Here, we generated MC38 mouse adenocarcinoma cells overexpressing distinct IL-33 isoforms to dissect the relative contribution of IL-33 nuclear retention versus extracellular activity in a model of heterotopic tumors.

studi.t: Mitochondrial fatty acid synthesis (mtFAS) fuels iron-sulfur cluster production essential for type I immunity
studi.s: Mitochondria orchestrate the metabolic programs that drive T cell-mediated immunity, yet the specific mitochondrial activities that license T cell effector function remain unclear. Here, we identify mitochondrial fatty acid synthesis (mtFAS) as a critical mitochondrial pathway that supports T cell effector function and limits T cell dysfunction. Upon activation, human and mouse T cells robustly induce mtFAS enzymes in a Myc-dependent manner.

studi.t: Structural basis of human antibody recognition of linear and conformational epitopes on the peanut allergen Ara h 2
studi.s: IgE-mediated food allergy requires allergens to crosslink FcERI-bound IgE on mast cells, yet how individual allergen epitopes organize pathogenic IgE complexes remains poorly understood. We defined the structural basis of antibody recognition of Ara h 2, a major peanut allergen, using three human monoclonal antibodies isolated from IgG1 memory B cells of peanut-allergic children. As IgE, the DPYSPS repeat-specific antibody P4EC10 alone induced degranulation in vitro and passive cutaneous anaphylaxis in vivo, whereas P1BC6 and P1EC5 elicited both responses only when combined.

studi.t: Recognition of β-D-glucose by surfactant protein D and structural evidence for an extended carbohydrate binding site
studi.s: Human surfactant protein D (hSP-D) is an innate immune protein involved in pathogen recognition in the lungs. Structural definition of the recognition of small carbohydrates by rfhSP-D, a biologically and therapeutically active recombinant homotrimeric fragment of hSP-D, has previously revealed the details of calcium dependent binding in the carbohydrate recognition domain and the influence of residues flanking the binding pocket.

studi.t: Transient fetal type 2 bovine viral diarrhea virus infection protects beef cattle from postnatal challenge with type 1b bovine viral diarrhea virus and Mannheimia haemolytica
studi.s: Bovine respiratory disease (BRD) is the most significant disease in feedlot cattle, impacting animal growth, performance, and profitability. Acute bovine viral diarrhea virus (BVDV) infections have been shown to increase the occurrence of BRD. Fetal infection with BVDV during late gestation results in transient fetal infections (TI). At birth, TI calves are negative for BVDV but positive for BVDV-specific antibodies. The objective of this experiment was to determine the effect of TI status on the susceptibility to BRD and the subsequent rate of gain in feedlot cattle.

studi.t: An RNase bacterial toxin family cleaves the anticodon loop across diverse tRNA isotypes
studi.s: Characterized bacterial tRNase toxins typically recognize individual tRNAs or restricted tRNA subsets. Here, we identify TloR (tRNA loop-targeting RNase), a tRNase with an unusually broad substrate range but a strong positional preference for exposed tRNA loops. Comparative genomic analyses identified TloR homologs across diverse bacterial lineages, where they are frequently embedded in conflict-associated loci.

studi.t: Lateral interactions between antiparallel filaments drive self-assembly of the FtsZ ring in bacterial cell division
studi.s: The Z-ring is the organiser of cell division in most archaea and bacteria, arriving early at mid-cell and recruiting downstream proteins. While FtsZ protofilaments and their treadmilling dynamics are well understood, how FtsZ assembles into condensed Z-rings remains unknown. Here we determined the Escherichia coli in-cell electron cryotomography (cryo-ET) structure of FtsZ to 6.9 [A] resolution, showing antiparallel double filaments with the C-terminus facing the membrane. Electron cryomicroscopy (cryo-EM) of purified E. coli FtsZ showed these double filaments self-assemble.

studi.t: PL25_M23: Salt-enhanced antibacterial activity of a plasmid-encoded SLT-M23 hydrolase from Virgibacillus salarius against Gram-positive bacteria
studi.s: Antimicrobial resistance has intensified interest in peptidoglycan hydrolases as potential alternatives to conventional antibiotics. However, halophilic and halotolerant bacteria remain underexplored sources of these enzymes. Here, we characterized PL25_M23, a predicted 370-amino-acid, dual-domain cell wall hydrolase encoded on a candidate closed circular plasmid from Virgibacillus salarius PL25, a halotolerant Gram-positive isolate.

studi.t: Acquisition of phthiocerol dimycocerosates enabled extension of fused mycomembranes for cellular cording in Mycobacterium tuberculosis
studi.s: Mycobacterium tuberculosis and its pathogenic relative Mycobacterium marinum form virulence-associated serpentine cords. Using live imaging and cryo-electron tomography, we show that cording involves extensive outer membrane enmeshment, such that adjacent cells share a single outer membrane. Importantly, analysis of diverse non-cording Mycobacteriales species, including the poorly virulent saprophyte M. smegmatis, reveals some membrane enmeshment in the clumped colonies. Our analyses suggest that cording was acquired in two evolutionary steps.

studi.t: Phage integrons are vaults of privatized counterdefense genes
studi.s: Integrons facilitate the adaptation of microbes by capturing beneficial gene cassettes, including antiphage defense systems, but their role in phage adaptation remains unclear. Here, we identify reversed integron cassette organization in phages, with 96% of reverse-oriented cassettes lacking detectable homologs in surveyed bacterial and plasmid integrons. Phage cassettes are enriched in counterdefenses, including viral sponge-like proteins.

studi.t: A microbiota-dependent fitness locus promotes intraspecies competition and cell envelope resilience in gut bacterium Phocaeicola vulgatus
studi.s: A central question in gut microbial ecology is how dominant bacterial species establish and occupy their niches amid inter- and intraspecies competition. Phocaeicola vulgatus (Pvu) is a Gram-negative anaerobe and prevalent member of the human gut microbiome that can integrate into established gut communities without antibiotic pretreatment, yet mechanisms underlying this competitive success remain poorly understood.

studi.t: AtVPS13M1 regulates subcellular lipid distribution and lipid remodeling in phosphate-deprived plants
studi.s: VPS13 are conserved lipid transporters with multiple subcellular localizations playing key roles in many fundamental cellular processes. While the localizations and functions of VPS13 have been extensively investigated in yeast and animals, little is known about their counterparts in plants, particularly regarding their role in stress response. Here, we characterized AtVPS13M1, one of the four VPS13 paralogs in Arabidopsis thaliana. We show that AtVPS13M1 is expressed in young dividing and vascular tissues as a single major splice variant.

studi.t: Distinct chaperones coordinate the type III secretion system assembly and effector secretion in Vibrio parahaemolyticus
studi.s: Many Gram-negative bacterial pathogens rely on the type III secretion system (T3SS) to deliver virulence factors or effectors into host cells. In Vibrio parahaemolyticus, the leading cause of seafood-borne gastroenteritis, one of the two T3SSs, the T3SS2, is essential for intestinal colonization and infection in the human body. While many T3SS2 effectors have been extensively characterized, the chaperones that guide their biogenesis and coordinate assembly of the T3SS machinery remain poorly understood.

studi.t: SimpleP2G: Importance of Image Encoders for Gene Expression Prediction from Pathology Images
studi.s: Pathology-image-to-gene-expression (P2G) studies often change the prediction head, image encoder, and spatial context together, making performance differences difficult to attribute. We examine these factors through paired image-input controls and explicit input regimes. Our main comparison covers five HEST-1K datasets, two 200-gene panels, and three selected held-out slides per dataset, using validation-selected checkpoints.

studi.t: Salmonella MgtC promotes polymyxin B resistance and systemic infection by activating LpxO-mediated lipid A hydroxylation
studi.s: The intracellular pathogen Salmonella Typhimurium modifies the lipid A moiety of lipopolysaccharide through various lipid A-modifying enzymes, thereby acquiring resistance to host cationic antimicrobial peptides during infection. While regulation of these enzymes at the transcription level has been extensively studied, however, regulation at the activity level remains poorly understood.

studi.t: PAannotate: Software for Exploring Pseudomonas aeruginosa Gene-Expression Associations from Transcriptomic Data
studi.s: With the proliferation of transcriptomic data for Pseudomonas aeruginosa there is a need for software programs able to efficiently analyze both individual transcriptomes as well as large, publicly available compendiums of arrays. PAannotate is an R package and native macOS application capable of analyzing the Whiteley Lab database of 5,821 transcriptomes from 470 BioProjects. In the application, researchers can use recorded metadata such as strain, medium or treatment to select experiments or genes associated with particular expression patterns.

studi.t: Inhibition of Bacteriophage Infection by Natural and Synthetic DNA-binding Compounds
studi.s: The arms race between bacteria and phages involves a wide range of immune and anti-immune systems on both sides. One of the long-known mechanisms of antiphage defense involves DNA intercalators such as daunorubicin and its analogues. Daunorubicin was also shown to inhibit bacterial growth as well as eukaryotic cell division, underlying its use in chemotherapy. Other DNA intercalators and minor groove binding dyes are widely used for nucleic acids staining, but have not been studied for their effects on viral infection.

studi.t: High dietary sucrose reveals distinct roles for the BBSome subunits BBS1 and BBS9 in Drosophila development
studi.s: Insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes occur in Bardet-Biedl syndrome, and BBSome proteins regulate insulin receptor abundance at the cell surface in mammals. We asked how loss of two structurally related BBSome subunits, BBS1 and BBS9, affects development on a high-sucrose diet in Drosophila melanogaster. Sequence comparisons identified the seven-bladed beta-propeller and gamme-adaptin ear domains of human BBS1 and BBS9 in their respective fly orthologues. High sucrose (1 M) delayed pupariation in both single mutants, with the longest delay in flies lacking both subunits.

studi.t: Paraburkholderia endosymbionts with streamlined genomes are disadvantaged during interspecific competition
studi.s: Trait loss and genome size reduction are classic evolutionary signatures of obligate bacterial endosymbiosis. However, many bacteria are facultative endosymbionts and so experience a trade-off between adaptation to living within their hosts and apart from them. A central tension in this transition is whether traits required for independent life, including adaptations for interspecific competition, are maintained or lost.

studi.t: Evolutionary dynamics of Gag-restricted prion-like domains in LTR retroelements
studi.s: Background: Prions are proteins that can self-template, giving rise to non-Mendelian inheritance. They are functionally diverse and have been found in all domains of life and even beyond cellular life within viruses, a distribution that suggests an ancient evolutionary origin. Testing that origin has been difficult, as prions are identified by composition, such as an enrichment of Q/N residues, and are carried by rapidly changing disordered domains that are difficult to study phylogenetically.

studi.t: Puya: A new example of adaptive radiation in the Northern Andes
studi.s: Most documented examples of plant adaptive radiations occur on oceanic islands, but high-elevation mountain systems offer similar ecological opportunities. Here, we investigate the genus Puya (Bromeliaceae), a rapidly diversifying Andean lineage associated with high-elevation ecosystems, to assess how ecological opportunity and biotic interactions shape diversification and morphological evolution in fragmented mountain landscapes.

studi.t: isoGS: A genomic method to navigate the breeder's dilemma of diversity versus eliteness
studi.s: Global networks of public crop breeding programs exchange germplasm to share traits and increase diversity for genetic gain. There is a fundamental dilemma in crop breeding between the need to expand the genetic variation in elite gene pools while avoiding disruptions to essential traits required for eliteness.

studi.t: A switch in Nrg1-Rtg3 promoter recruitment coordinates mitochondrial cristae remodeling during the diauxic transition
studi.s: During the diauxic transition, Saccharomyces cerevisiae must preserve mitochondrial genome integrity while remodeling mitochondrial architecture for respiratory growth. The transcription factors Nrg1 and Rtg3 form a heteromeric regulator previously shown to be required for mitochondrial DNA maintenance, but its mitochondrial targets remained unknown. Here, we identify ILV5 and MGM101, which encode mitochondrial nucleoid proteins, as Nrg1-Rtg3 targets.

studi.t: Alignment-Aware Genomic Coordinate Encoding for Long-Range DNA Modeling
studi.s: Current genomic foundation models (GFMs) largely inherit the language-modeling paradigm over contiguous token sequences, treating DNA as ordinary text. The genome, however, is a coordinate-based system of sparse signals: variants, regulatory elements, and distal gene interactions occupy a vanishing fraction of chromosome-scale sequences and are defined by their positions in the reference coordinate system rather than by linear proximity. This mismatch limits pure sequence modeling on individualized, non-contiguous genomic tasks.

studi.t: Molecular switch mediates the glucocorticoid receptor transition from tumor suppressor to oncogene in the prostate
studi.s: Glucocorticoids are widely used to alleviate inflammation and treatment-related side effects in prostate cancer (PCa), particularly to counteract abiraterone-induced cortisol suppression. However, the glucocorticoid receptor (GR) exhibits a dual role exerting tumor-suppressive effects by inhibiting early-stage PCa cell proliferation, while also promoting oncogenic progression by mediating antiandrogen resistance. The molecular mechanisms underlying this functional dichotomy have remained elusive and poorly characterized.

studi.t: Genomic variation of Dutch traditional cattle breeds captured in a Dutch cattle pangenome
studi.s: Traditional livestock breeds are reservoirs of genetic variation lost elsewhere by selection for productivity, yet are rarely represented in reference genome resources. Traditional cattle (Bos taurus) in the Netherlands are severely endangered, with some populations having declined by up to 95 % between 2020 and 2026.

studi.t: Structural and functional reference maps of transcriptional enhancers in the developing human cortex
studi.s: Non-coding regulatory variation is the major driver of human phenotypic diversity, yet maps of cis-regulatory elements (CREs) and their variability across developmental cell types remain limited. Here, we integrated single-nucleus chromatin accessibility data from 54 mid-gestation human prenatal cortical donors to generate a CRE atlas comprising 1,165,697 candidate CREs across 104,266 cortical nuclei.

studi.t: Heterogeneous Effects Across Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) Driver Mutations Challenges a Unified Model of CHIP
studi.s: Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) is an age-associated expansion of hematopoietic stem cells harboring somatic mutations in the absence of overt malignancy. CHIP driver genes impart divergent effects on many biological processes, yet the mechanisms underlying these gene-specific effects, particularly in non-hematologic disease contexts, remain poorly understood. We analyzed 466 samples from the Multi-Ancestry Genomics, Epigenomics, and Transcriptomics of Alzheimer's Disease dataset, and identified function-specific differences between CHIP categorizations.

studi.t: Detail: species-agnostic, generalizable animal behavior analysis using foundation model embeddings
studi.s: Automated tools for quantifying and classifying animal behavior from video data are crucial for neuroscience, medicine, and biology. Automated analysis of animal behavior from video usually starts with pose estimation, which needs manually annotated training frames for each new species or setup and reduces an animal to a small number of biased keypoints. Here we present Detail, a behavior analysis package built on foundation vision models, for species- and context-agnostic analysis of animal behavior.

studi.t: scOnion: Cross-Modal Concordance-Aware Joint Analysis of Cells and Features in Single-Cell Multiomic Data
studi.s: Single-cell multiomic assays jointly profile gene expression and chromatin accessibility in the same cells, enabling direct analysis of cross-layer coordination. However, agreement between modalities varies across cells, and existing integration methods often emphasize shared structure, potentially averaging away cell-specific cross-modal discordance that carries biological signal. Here we present scOnion, a concordance-aware computational framework that quantifies cross-modality agreement and propagates this information into downstream analyses.

studi.t: Reference-based assignment of aerolysin nanopore signals to peptide sequences from tryptic protein digests
studi.s: Rapid, cost-efficient and miniaturized protein analysis is essential for point-of-care clinical diagnostics. Nanopores offer a promising alternative to mass spectrometry by enabling label-free, single-molecule sensing with a minimal footprint. However, peptide-level protein identification remains challenging because of the difficulty of assigning nanopore signals to peptide sequences and the incompatibility of conventional proteolysis workflows with nanopore sensing.

studi.t: Human De Novo Microproteins are Intrinsically Disordered and Contain Short Linear Motifs
studi.s: De novo genes, arising from previously non coding regions, have defied our view of gene birth and proteome evolution. Advances in ribosome profiling and comparative genomics have uncovered widespread translation of de novo small open reading frames (sORFs), many of which encode previously unrecognized microproteins. Despite increasing evidence demonstrating translation of de novo sORFs, it remains poorly understood how their encoded microproteins acquire molecular functions.

studi.t: Suprathreshold suppression underlies spatial selectivity in temporal interference stimulation
studi.s: Temporal interference stimulation (TIS) has been proposed for non-invasive deep-brain targeting using temporally interfering kilohertz-frequency electric fields, but the neuronal basis of its spatial selectivity remains unclear. Here we show that differential suppression of suprathreshold firing can support spatially selective recruitment. Multiscale simulations revealed no activation-threshold advantage for TIS over unmodulated high-frequency stimulation (HFS).

studi.t: Extracellular matrix-enriched human induced chondrocyte organoids as living building blocks for scalable cartilage tissue engineering
studi.s: Articular cartilage defects are common and often develop into painful and debilitating osteoarthritis due to the low innate healing capacity of cartilage. However, current regenerative treatments are limited as they depend on large autologous cell numbers and poor scalability. Here, a novel approach for rapid and plentiful cartilage organoid production is introduced for modular and scalable cartilage tissue engineering, by combining an off-the-shelf cell source with a natural matrix supplement in spinner flask cultures.

studi.t: RoWS Biofabrication of Neuromuscular Tubuloids from Human Neuromesodermal Progenitors
studi.s: Combining multicellular self-organization with defined tissue architecture remains a challenge in human neuromuscular modeling. Here, we use rotary wet-spinning (RoWS) biofabrication to encapsulate human neuromesodermal progenitors (NMPs) within fibrin-based cores surrounded by alginate shells, generating neuromuscular tubuloids (nmTubs). NMPs derived from a human embryonic stem cell and an induced pluripotent stem cell line were cultured for up to 50 days and assessed by gene expression analysis, immunofluorescence, tissue orientation measurements, and calcium imaging.

studi.t: A One-Year In Vivo Study of a Braided Pure Molybdenum Stent: Favorable Biocompatibility and the Critical Challenge of Vascular Biomechanics
studi.s: Background: This study aims to evaluate a newly developed biodegradable stent made of pure Molybdenum (Mo) for treating intracranial aneurysms. Unlike traditional permanent metal stents that remain in the body indefinitely, this new device aims to provide temporary support during the healing process and then safely dissolve. Methods: A 30.48 {micro}m braided Mo stent was developed, and its mechanical performance and degradation process were tested in vitro. The stent was then implanted into the arteries of Beagle dogs for a one-year observation period.

studi.t: XenoType: Decoding cellular identity in breast cancer histology through molecular supervision
studi.s: Characterizing the cellular composition of the tumor microenvironment from histological images is fundamental to understanding cancer biology and informing treatment decisions. Deep learning has enabled automated nuclear detection and classification from hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) images, yet cell classifiers remain largely confined to broad morphological categories owing to a reliance on manual annotations.

studi.t: A pangenomic approach identifies new structural variants associated with gene expression in the CARTaGENE cohort
studi.s: Structural variants (SVs) are major contributors to the genetic diversity of human populations. While many small variants have been associated with human traits and diseases, the challenge to genotype SVs using short-read DNA sequencing and a linear reference genome has made association testing with SVs more difficult.

studi.t: Evaluating the Generalizability of Machine-Learning-Guided Directed Evolution Across Protein Fitness Landscapes
studi.s: Machine-learning-guided directed evolution (MLDE) prioritizes promising protein variants for experimental testing, but performance depends on campaign design. We present MLDEx, a systematic benchmark of 557,143 simulated campaigns across 16 protein fitness landscapes, covering 28 representations, eight regressors, three acquisition rules, four initial training-set sizes, and four batch sizes. Going beyond previous benchmarks, MLDEx jointly evaluates these design choices and tests whether recommended configurations generalize to unseen protein landscapes.

studi.t: MEAM-OWL for browser-based analysis of motif enrichment and associations with gene expression
studi.s: Motivation: Identifying functional regulatory motifs (such as cis-regulatory elements) remains challenging because conventional motif enrichment relies on binary comparisons between target and background sequences, overlooking quantitative relationships between motif copy number and gene expression or other quantitative traits. Existing tools for such analysis require specific and inconsistent input formats, incompatible with a streamlined workflow. Results: We present MEAM-OWL (Motif Enrichment Analysis Modules on the Web, Lite) to overcome those issues.

studi.t: Phirefly: hierarchical quantum haplotype phasing at the chromosome scale
studi.s: Motivation: Read-based phasing links alleles on the same homologous haplotype. It plays a critical role in long-read variant calling and variant analysis. Many phasing algorithms have been developed. This includes QHap, the only quantum-inspired algorithm for read-based phasing. QHap does not run on quantum hardware due to the scale of the practical problems. Results: We developed Phirefly, the first practical quantum algorithm for read-based phasing with the key phasing step executed on quantum hardware.

studi.t: A method to disentangle enhancer-gene interactions from latent factors in single-cell multi-omics data
studi.s: Mapping regulatory elements to their target genes in the cell types relevant to disease is essential for interpreting non-coding variants identified by genome-wide association studies. Single-cell multiome data, which simultaneously measure accessible chromatin and gene expression per cell, allow such peak-gene links to be inferred within individual cell types.

studi.t: ChronoClone links temporal clonal behavior to lineage output and mutation responses
studi.s: Distinct stem cell clones can yield similar lineage outputs via different developmental trajectories or dynamics and respond differently to perturbation. Here, we introduce ChronoClone, an unsupervised method that groups single-cell clones by time-resolved cell-state composition into metaclones. Benchmarked against simulated ground-truth scenarios, ChronoClone demonstrates high noise tolerance compared to existing methods.

studi.t: Does embedding impact classification performance ? A small sample perspective
studi.s: Deep learning (DL) methods can address many challenges posed by high-dimensional and sparse microbiome data. In this study we applied and compared deep (DNN) and shallow (SNN) feedforward neural networks combined with five dimensionality-reduction techniques: Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), Non-negative Matrix Factorization (NMF), Autoencoder based Embeddings (AE), and convolutional layers (Conv).

studi.t: CyteArc: in-place analysis and reuse of remote atlases at 100-million-cell scale
studi.s: Public repositories hold hundreds of millions of single-cell profiles, yet analyzing them still requires downloading full files. We present CyteArc, a framework that analyzes remote atlases in place, scaling to nearly 100 million cells on standard CPUs faster than benchmarked workflows, with the lowest memory from 10 million cells upward. Without copying counts, CyteArc integrates millions of cells across studies using 1% to 4% of the disk space of other tools.

studi.t: BRIDGE: inter-tissue imputation with contrastive learning improves recovery of donor-specific gene expression
studi.s: Multi-tissue transcriptome resources are central to understanding tissue-specific regulation and inter-individual variation. Realistically, most tissues are measured in only a subset of donors, especially for less accessible tissues such as brain and heart. Accurately imputing gene expression values for such tissues, while accounting for individual heterogeneity, remains a daunting challenge.

studi.t: GASTON-VI efficiently quantifies spatial axes and molecular gradients from multi-sample, multi-modal spatial-omics data
studi.s: Many tissues exhibit an underlying spatial axis along which fundamental biological processes occur due to continuous spatial gradients of cell type and molecular state. Modern spatial-omics technologies measure molecular features (e.g. gene/protein expression) at 100,000s-1,000,000s of locations within a two-dimensional (2-D) tissue slice, with large-scale atlases profiling multiple tissue slices of the same organ type across different individuals and biological conditions (e.g. healthy versus diseased).

studi.t: BRISANCE: A GPU-Accelerated Pipeline for Somatic Short-Variant Detection in Whole-Genome Sequencing Data
studi.s: Post-sequencing computational processing of tumor-normal whole-genome sequencing (WGS) remains computationally intensive and can delay somatic variant detection in clinical and translational workflows. We developed and evaluated BRISANCE, a graphics processing unit (GPU)-accelerated pipeline based on NVIDIA Parabricks for detecting somatic single-nucleotide variants and short insertions/deletions, using matched tumor-normal WGS data from the Cancer Genome in a Bottle HG008 pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma model.

studi.t: SYNDRI: Context-aware removal of transcript spillover in imaging-based spatial transcriptomics
studi.s: Imaging-based spatial transcriptomics (ST) measures gene expression at single-cell resolution, but imperfect segmentation often misassigns transcripts between neighboring cells, a problem known as transcript spillover. This spillover is niche-dependent and can therefore confound downstream analyses that rely on niche-specific differential expression. True spillover cannot be directly quantified in experimental ST data, so existing correction methods infer contamination indirectly from transcript positions or expression structure.

studi.t: SPECTRE: A versatile data framework for integrating spectral, environmental, and ecophysiological trait data
studi.s: With the increasing availability of large datasets and the growing importance of artificial intelligence (AI), robust and sustainable data management systems have become essential for plant and ecosystem research. In particular, the integration of heterogeneous spectral data with plant functional traits and environmental measurements from multiple sensors poses a major challenge, requiring significant time investment and long-term planning.

studi.t: Random-walk-based Probabilistic Microglia Morphology Reconstruction in 2D and 3D from Confocal Microscopy Images
studi.s: Reconstructing individual microglia from confocal images is challenging when fine processes have weak fluorescence or neighboring cells form connected structures. Inspired by Grady's random-walker framework, we propose a soma-guided probabilistic method for three-dimensional microglial reconstruction and cell-of-origin assignment. Signal-weighted random walks quantify voxel connectivity to each soma by the probability of reaching that soma before background or another soma. A path-length adjustment reduces the penalty on distal processes.

studi.t: RNAhub2: prefiltering and compression enable scalable structure-based RNA discovery
studi.s: RNAhub is an established web server for structure-agnostic RNA homology search that builds multiple sequence alignments with nhmmer and performs downstream structural covariation analysis with R-scape and CaCoFold. RNAhub is efficiently applied to smaller genomes, including viruses, bacteria, and fungi. However, searches against large eukaryotic genomes remain computationally expensive, and genome storage requirements currently limit its taxonomic coverage, thereby reducing the opportunities to identify novel structural RNAs.

studi.t: Functional cooperation, adaptation and synchronization of subcellular processes in cellular neighborhoods as inferred from spatial transcriptomics
studi.s: Tissue-level functions emerge from pathway activities distributed across neighboring cells. Yet analyses of spatial transcriptomics mostly focus on cell type composition or signaling through ligand-receptor pairs, leaving spatial relationships between effector processes undescribed. We inferred networks of functionally interacting subcellular processes (SCPs) that are independent of shared gene products and lie beyond sibling relationships defined in parent-child hierarchies.

studi.t: Niche-FATE: niche-aware inference of cell-state transitions from spatiotemporal data
studi.s: Cell-state transitions depend on intrinsic transcriptional programmes and local signals. Existing spatiotemporal mapping methods largely match cells by expression or position, not by received signals. Here we introduce Niche-FATE, an optimal transport framework integrating gene expression, spatial neighbourhoods and inferred ligand-receptor signalling to estimate transition probabilities and prioritise fate-associated signals.

studi.t: An interpretable framework for decoding transcriptomic foundation models
studi.s: Background: What transcriptomic foundation models encode, and how well they describe cells and tissue on targeted spatial panels, is under-explored. It is unclear whether a concept-labeled sparse autoencoder (SAE) feature represents its concept or only the genes it detects. Results: Here, we propose interpreTFM, which decomposes frozen transcriptomic foundation model activations with SAEs. We applied it to a CosMx lung-cancer section, four further CosMx donors, and a Xenium renal-cell-carcinoma section.

studi.t: Zero-Shot Generation of Protein Conformational Ensembles Through AlphaFold Latent Flooding
studi.s: Despite transformative advances in protein structure prediction, generating conformational ensembles directly from sequence in an efficient and accessible manner remains a central challenge. We introduce a heuristic importance sampling framework for the zero-shot prediction of functionally relevant, conformationally diverse structures, bypassing the need for extensive physics-based modeling or prior domain knowledge.

studi.t: VMDance: An Efficient and Interactive Molecular Dynamics Clustering Plugin for VMD
studi.s: Clustering is the standard route from a molecular dynamics trajectory to a small set of interpretable conformational states, yet it is usually performed outside the molecular viewer, leaving cluster assignments to be exported, tracked, and mapped back onto the structures by hand. We present VMDance, an open-source plugin that brings the MDANCE family of $n$-ary similarity clustering methods into VMD. Through a graphical interface backed by a C++ implementation, it provides \kmeans{} NANI, HELM, eQual, and DIVINE clustering, together with PRIME representative-structure selection.

studi.t: L-Cystine Is a Conserved Host-Entry Signal That Activates Development in Diverse Parasitic Nematodes Through an Olfactory Receptor
studi.s: Soil-transmitted helminths infect over 1 billion people worldwide, yet how dormant infective larvae sense entry into a host and exit developmental arrest to establish infection remains largely unknown. Here, in the human parasite Strongyloides stercoralis, we identify L-cystine as a host signal that stimulates larval feeding and synthesis of dafachronic acid, a steroid hormone that activates DAF-12 and promotes post-infection development.

studi.t: Isolating soluble, near-native, misfolded states and their functional characterization: A step towards high-resolution protein misfolding structures
studi.s: Proteins can misfold into soluble, near-native states that act as long-lived kinetic traps with aggregation independent biological consequences. A key step toward obtaining high-resolution structures of these states is the ability to isolate/purify them. Here, we show this is possible for the Escherichia coli protein pyruvate kinase (pykF) following refolding from chemical denaturant. After controlling for aggregates the refolded (treatment) ensemble exhibits a decrease in average specific activity relative to the untreated (natively folded) sample.

studi.t: Insights into Ice-Growth Inhibition and Hydration Ordering by the Ca2+-Dependent Antifreeze Protein MaIBP_RIV
studi.s: Antifreeze proteins (AFPs) inhibit ice growth by binding to specific ice surfaces, although the molecular basis of this activity remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigate the ice-growth inhibition mechanism of the calcium-dependent antifreeze protein MaIBP_RIV from Marinomonas arctica using all-atom molecular dynamics simulations. MaIBP_RIV exhibits stable binding to the primary prism and basal ice planes through its ice-binding surface (IBS), effectively suppressing ice growth. IBS binding to the secondary prism plane is weaker and only temporarily inhibits growth.

studi.t: High-fat feeding increases graft-derived glucagon output and impairs beta-cell secretion in transplanted human islets
studi.s: Dysregulated glucagon secretion is central to the bihormonal disturbance that drives hyperglycemia in T2D, yet how a chronic obesogenic environment alters human alpha-cell function over time has not been directly examined. Models to specifically assess in vivo human alpha-cell function have not been possible because mouse and human glucagon are sequence-identical. We transplanted human islets (+I) into glucagon-knockout immunocompromised (GKO-NSG) mice, in which all circulating glucagon is graft-derived, and fed recipients a regular diet (RD+I) or a 60% high-fat diet (HFD+I) for 12 weeks.

studi.t: Near-surface flight enhances thrust in an insect-inspired flapping-wing robot
studi.s: A number of semi-aquatic insects rapidly move across the water surface using interfacial flight. In this locomotion strategy, flapping wings generate thrust above the air-water interface while surface tension supports their weight. This close proximity to the air-water interface alters aerodynamic force generation through ground effect, potentially enhancing horizontal propulsion. Here, we demonstrate that near-surface flapping enhances horizontal thrust by up to 17% at shallow stroke-plane inclinations.

studi.t: Sublethal chemical exposure predominantly reduces heat tolerance while increasing its variability in freshwater invertebrates and fish
studi.s: Increasing temperatures, in conjunction with widespread chemical pollution, threaten freshwater biodiversity worldwide. General patterns describing how chemical exposure affects heat tolerance have yet to be quantified beyond individual studies. Therefore we quantitatively synthesized the literature on chemical effects on the heat tolerance of freshwater fauna.

studi.t: Structural deformations of lipid bilayers around membrane proteins inform oligomerization type
studi.s: A functional definition of a membrane protein's structure is the three-dimensional arrangement of the polypeptide and the structure of the membrane around it. Biological membranes are composed of self-assembled lipid bilayers, with membrane proteins acting as inclusions that perturb this phase. These inclusions induce long-range changes in membrane structure and create an intrinsic, lipid-mediated driving force for membrane protein association. The question is how much different membrane protein folds shape their surrounding membrane to tune the affinity and specificity of this driving force.

studi.t: Transcriptional activation forms insulation boundaries through cohesin-independent decompaction and cohesin-dependent barrier formation
studi.s: How 3D genome structure regulates transcription has been intensely studied, but how transcription regulates 3D genome structure remains poorly understood. To elucidate this relationship, we integrate Region Capture Micro-C and simultaneous live-cell imaging of CTCF chromatin looping and inducible nascent transcription at the Fbn2 locus with 3D polymer modeling and perturbation experiments. We find that transcription activation induces cohesin-independent insulation boundary formation at the Fbn2 promoter, locus decompaction, and faster chromatin dynamics.

studi.t: The pecten oculi regulates pH in the bird eye
studi.s: The bird retina generates a dual acid load: aerobic metabolism in the outer retina produces CO2, while chronic anoxia in the inner retina yields lactic acid, raising the question of how intraocular pH homeostasis is maintained in birds. We show that chicken (Gallus gallus) vitreous pH remains close to blood pH despite these respiratory and metabolic acid-base challenges and a low non-bicarbonate buffering capacity, which is compensated by high vitreous bicarbonate.

studi.t: Molpylot: a shared workspace for human-AI collaboration in molecular simulation
studi.s: Rigorous biomolecular simulation requires a long chain of physical decisions across fragmented tools. Language-model agents offer to automate this work, yet current agents operate outside the scientist's environment, generating ad hoc scripts or files that are effortless to launch but laborious to inspect and verify.

studi.t: The Tomato Isochorismate Synthase Coordinates both Salicylic Acid-Mediated Immunity and Phylloquinone-Dependent Chloroplast Function
studi.s: Isochorismate synthase (ICS) provides isochorismate for salicylic acid (SA) and phylloquinone biosynthesis, yet how these functions are integrated in crop species remains poorly understood. We investigated the biological role of the single ICS gene in tomato. CRISPR/Cas9-generated ics mutants were analysed using pathogen assays, targeted and untargeted metabolomics, transcriptomics, chloroplast imaging, photosynthetic measurements and polysome profiling. Loss of ICS strongly reduced pathogen-induced SA accumulation and compromised Pto-mediated resistance to Pseudomonas syringae.

studi.t: Functional divergence of D-, A-, and B-type cyclins in the moss Physcomitrium patens
studi.s: Cyclins and cyclin-dependent kinases (CDKs) are central cell-cycle regulators that have undergone diversification in land plants; however, the functional implications of this divergence remain incompletely understood, particularly in non-vascular lineages. Here, we systematically dissected the roles of the three principal cyclin classes--D, A, and B--in the model moss Physcomitrium patens.

studi.t: Beyond IgG: Oral Secretory IgA as a new efficient modality for cancer immunotherapy
studi.s: Monoclonal antibody therapies have revolutionized cancer treatment but are almost exclusively based on intravenously administered IgG antibodies. Here, we developed and evaluated the first orally delivered anti-CEACAM5 secretory IgA (SIgA) for colorectal cancer. The pharmacokinetics, biodistribution, antitumor efficacy and immune effects of oral anti-CEACAM5 SIgA (ABC-101) were evaluated in an orthotopic metastatic human colorectal cancer model.

studi.t: O2 exchange profiling reveals physiological diversity among taxonomically characterized green microalgal strains
studi.s: Taxonomic identification provides essential information about microalgae, but a shared species assignment does not necessarily imply similar physiological behavior. This study combined microscopy, ribosomal DNA sequencing, and O2 exchange measurements to characterize 20 green microalgal strains, comprising 18 environment-derived and two previously identified model strains. Net O2 evolution and post illumination consumption were measured across 17 increasing irradiances in three independently grown cultures per strain.

studi.t: Ecological Feedback Dimensionality and Trade-Off Shape Govern Cancer Phenotypic Diversification
studi.s: Cancer cells face a variety of trade-offs in their microenvironment, from competition vs. colonization to immune evasion vs. rapid proliferation. Whether such trade-offs drive cancer cell populations to a single optimal phenotype or to a stable coexistence of phenotypes depends on the trade-off's shape and the number of independent ecological feedbacks that cells impose on each other and on their environment.

studi.t: GnotoBag: A versatile peat-based gnotobiotic system for plant microbiome research beyond model species
studi.s: Plants and their microbial communities form a symbiotic system, where microbial communities play a key role in plant growth, development and stress resilience. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying plant-microbiota interactions remain poorly understood. A practical challenge is maintaining axenic conditions during prolonged plant growth while providing adequate space, ventilation, water, and nutrients. To advance research on plant-microbiome interactions, we developed the "GnotoBag" system, a bag-based extension of a previously established peat-based gnotobiotic plant growth platform.

studi.t: Canine rabies detection at the livestock carcass interface: a modelling study of an integrated surveillance approach in rural India
studi.s: Introduction: Rabies is a deadly disease that remains endemic in many countries, particularly in rural areas. In parts of India, livestock carcass disposal sites are used by villages and visited by free-roaming dogs, providing a potential opportunity for active rabies surveillance. Methods: We evaluated the potential for rabies detection at carcass disposal sites using a stochastic scenario-tree modelling framework.

studi.t: Discovery of latent clinical phenotypes through optimal transport of brain dynamics
studi.s: The increasing availability of large clinical neuroimaging datasets has enabled the discovery of objective, data-driven clinical phenotypes. However, current approaches typically rely on structural or static functional metrics, thereby overlooking the rich information embedded in brain dynamics. To address this limitation, we developed a computational framework combining a Gaussian Hidden Markov Model (HMM) with Optimal Transport (OT) theory.

studi.t: Latent state selection, not outcome integration, resolves approach-avoidance conflict
studi.s: Appropriate action selection under approach-avoidance is crucial for survival and emotional resilience. Tasks designed to measure this conflict typically observe response rates at an intermediate rate. However, whether this reflects a single compromised policy or alternation between opposing strategies is unresolved. We trained rats on a novel three trial operant conflict task and recorded anterior insular cortex (aIC) activity with fiber photometry.

studi.t: Influence of Memory Modulation on Affective States in Methamphetamine Use Disorder
studi.s: Background: Negative affect and low positive affect are linked to craving and relapse in methamphetamine use disorder (MUD). Brief positive autobiographical memory recall improves mood in non-clinical samples, but it has not been tested in people in treatment for MUD. We tested whether positive memory recall improves affective state, withdrawal and craving compared with a neutral recall condition. Methods: Adults with past-year MUD in their first year of abstinence were recruited from two residential treatment programs in Tulsa, Oklahoma.

studi.t: Sleep EEG distinguishes learned from novel auditory cues without predicting memory retention in a targeted memory reactivation study
studi.s: Memory consolidation during sleep is thought to build on processes initiated during encoding, but how encoding-related brain activity affects individual memories during sleep is unknown. Using targeted memory reactivation (TMR), we tested whether auditory cues elicit memory-related responses during sleep, whether encoding theta and delta power predict these responses, and whether encoding- and sleep-related measures predict long-term retention. Eighty-one healthy young adults learned sound-associated item-face/place pairs during electroencephalography (EEG).

studi.t: Connectomic Flow Across Cortical Sensory Systems in Juvenile Fibromyalgia
studi.s: Adult fibromyalgia (FM) is characterized by altered functional connectivity between sensory, salience, and default mode networks (DMN), yet its early emergence and hierarchical organization remain unclear in Juvenile Fibromyalgia (JFM). We used stepwise functional connectivity (SFC) to detect early changes in the hierarchical integration of sensory signals toward salience and heteromodal networks in adolescents with JFM. Additionally, we assessed whether these alterations overlap with FM-associated gene expression from the Allen Human Brain Atlas (AHBA).

studi.t: Oxidative stress and lipidocentric mechanism of hyperglycemic glycolaldehyde damage to skeletal muscle cells
studi.s: Currently, diabetes-induced skeletal muscle complications affect over half of diabetic patients yet the pathway by which this hyperglycemic damage occurs has yet to be fully elucidated. As such, the goal of this study is to investigate the hypothesis: Glucose-derived glycolaldehydes, glyoxal and methylglyoxal, formed in hyperglycemia cause damage to the skeletal muscle myoblasts through oxidative stress and formation of pro-inflammatory eicosanoids upon activation of phospholipase A2 (PLA2) and cyclooxygenase (COX).

studi.t: BMP-2 Release from Biomaterial Carriers: Reporting Heterogeneity and the Limits of Cross-Study Prediction
studi.s: Published release profiles offer a potential basis for predicting bone morphogenetic protein-2 (BMP-2) delivery from biomaterial carriers, but heterogeneous reporting and study-specific effects complicate their reuse in machine learning (ML) models. As a preliminary exploration, we compiled 79 release experiments and 487 time points from 21 publications with a workflow that combined a large language model assistant and human verification, and we examined data comparability and cross-study prediction with ML models.

studi.t: Dietary betaine-based supplementation improves laying performance and modifies intestinal morphology and microbial profile in hens exposed to a tropical environment
studi.s: This study evaluated dietary betaine, alone or combined with vitamin C and/or sodium bicarbonate, in laying hens under chronic tropical heat stress, and characterized the intestinal morphological and microbial responses to the best-performing treatment. Two hundred forty 65-week-old Lohmann Brown hens were allotted to five diets (eight replicates of six birds) for seven weeks: basal diet (T0), betaine (T1), betaine + vitamin C (T2), betaine + sodium bicarbonate (T3), and betaine + sodium bicarbonate + vitamin C (T4).

studi.t: The selective autophagy receptor AtNBR1 associates with lipid droplets during seed germination and contributes to seed longevity
studi.s: Lipid droplets, once viewed primarily as lipid storage organelles, are increasingly recognized as key regulators of cellular homeostasis, which is particularly critical during seed imbibition and germination. Here, we investigated the role of the selective autophagy receptor AtNBR1 in lipid droplet-associated processes during Arabidopsis seed germination. AtNBR1 and ATG8 proteins were specifically and transiently recruited to lipid droplets during germination.

studi.t: Mechanical Induced Stress Enhances Arabidopsis Susceptibility to Fusarium oxysporum in a Jasmonic Acid-Dependent Manner
studi.s: Prolonged mechanical-induced stress (MIS) primes juvenile Arabidopsis plants for enhanced resistance against necrotrophic pathogens through the activation of jasmonate-mediated defense pathways. We hypothesised that MIS would weaken defense against hemibiotrophic pathogens that exploit jasmonate pathways to promote infection. We show that touch-acclimated wild-type plants were more susceptible to Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. conglutinans (Foc) infection than un-touched control plants.

studi.t: Designing a Saccharomyces cerevisiae Cell Factory for the Overaccumulation of Tyrosol using Rational Design and Genome-Scale Metabolic Modeling Approaches
studi.s: Tyrosol (TyOH) is a phenolic compound with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, naturally present in two Mediterranean products, wine and virgin olive oil, and is the key precursor of Hydroxytyrosol or Salidroside. Its industrial production still relies on chemical synthesis, which conflicts with the EU Green Deal roadmap to transition to a clean, circular, resource-efficient economy by 2050. Thus, moving to a sustainable economy is a priority. Here, we engineered Saccharomyces cerevisiae as a cell factory to produce TyOH.

studi.t: Ancient DNA resolves the taxonomic status and functional characteristics of the Pleistocene lowland yak (Bos baikalensis)
studi.s: Species delineation and taxonomy are notoriously complicated, especially for fossils where available information is often limited to morphology. However, palaeogenomics can add a genetic dimension to fossils, which allows for both robust resolution of taxonomy and trait functional characterization. In this study, we present the two first ancient genomes from voucher specimens morphologically attributed to the extinct yak Bos mutus baikalensis.

studi.t: Validation of the host fish relationship between Hickorynut (Obovaria olivaria) and Lake Sturgeon (Acipenser fulvescens from wild-caught and archival museum fishes
studi.s: Understanding the obligate relationship between freshwater unionid mussels and the host fish(es) of their larvae (glochidia) is key to the conservation of this generally threatened fauna. A host relationship between at-risk species Hickorynut (Obovaria olivaria) and Lake Sturgeon (Acipenser fulvescens) in Canada has long been presumed based on evidence from laboratory experiments in the United States. This study aimed to make a definitive link in the wild between these two species, while also examining other potential fish-mussel connections in the Ottawa and St. Lawrence Rivers.

studi.t: Neural mechanisms by which spaced learning promotes understanding
studi.s: Spaced learning reliably improves memory. A few studies suggest it also benefits understanding and problem solving, but none has examined the neural mechanism. We hypothesised that this benefit arises because spacing changes the memory trace rather than merely strengthening it. To test this, we taught participants how unfamiliar words meanings could be derived from familiar parts: meaningful rather than rote learning. Each participant learned words in one session, or in two sessions about 2 h (massed) or 48 h (spaced) apart, to the same criterion; one-session words served as the reference.

studi.t: Active exploration generates observer-specific image cues for material identity
studi.s: When observers interact with an object, each observer generates a different sequence of images. However, which image statistics underlie their perceptual judgments, and whether this self-generated visual input explains what they perceive, remain unclear. We analyzed the first-person recordings of a virtual-reality experiment in which 19 observers judged whether an object was metal or glass while exploring the object with the hand, with the head, with both, and without moving.

studi.t: Genome-Wide Association Study Identifies Novel Genetic Variants Linked to Meropenem Resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae
studi.s: Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae have emerged as an urgent public health threat in recent years. Infections caused by carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae in particular are associated with high rates of mortality, especially in immunocompromised patients. Substantial carbapenem resistance remains unexplained in K. pneumoniae even after accounting for known resistance genes. To uncover unknown mechanisms associated with meropenem resistance, we performed a genome-wide association study (GWAS) in 1,705 K.

studi.t: Comparative transcriptomic validation of candidate geroprotectors in human iPSC-derived neurons
studi.s: The discovery of geroprotectors, defined as interventions that slow aging-related deterioration and preserve function, remains constrained by reliance on lifespan studies. Lifespan studies take years, are costly and resource intensive, and return a whole-organism endpoint dominated in mice by neoplastic death. These studies cannot be readily scaled and do not specify which tissue(s) are protected by geroprotectors. Human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived cells provide a scalable alternative that enables defined lineages and genetically diverse donors to be studied in parallel.

studi.t: Allele-specific open chromatin analysis revealed allelic bias of alcohol-induced gene expression in human microglia
studi.s: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a polygenic disorder. Most AUD-associated variants identified by genome-wide association studies (GWAS) are located in non-coding regions, making it challenging to determine which variants are functional and how they contribute to disease-relevant cellular phenotypes. Here, we integrated microglia-specific allele-specific open chromatin (ASoC) mapping, GWAS, eQTLs, differentially expressed genes identified from postmortem human microglia and iPSC-derived microglial-like cells, and chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq) data from postmortem microglia to prioritize…

studi.t: Single-cell transcriptomics atlas of Echinococcus granulosusreveals germinative cell heterogeneity and candidate developmental key genes
studi.s: Cystic echinococcosis is a zoonotic parasitic disease caused by infection with Echinococcus granulosus. Progressive cyst growth can compress host tissues and elicit immune responses. Characterizing the cellular composition and lineage differentiation of E. granulosus protoscoleces may provide insight into the regulation of parasite proliferation and development and facilitate the identification of potential intervention targets. We generated a single-cell transcriptomic atlas of E.

studi.t: Morphological and transcriptomic renal characteristics of dioxin-induced fetal obstructive uropathy
studi.s: Congenital obstructive uropathy (COU) is an important cause of childhood kidney failure, yet understanding its variable renal outcomes and genetic modifiers is limited by the lack of genotype-independent models of in utero obstruction. Here, we characterized renal morphology and gene expression at embryonic day (E)18.5 in a mouse model of COU induced by exposure to 2,3,7,8-tetrachlorodibenzo-p-dioxin (dioxin) at E10.5. Dioxin exposure reproducibly induced bilateral hydroureteronephrosis with selective medullary flattening with relatively preserved renal architecture.

studi.t: Lactation is an Exercise-Responsive Window for Intergenerational Metabolic Programming
studi.s: Maternal exercise during pregnancy can influence offspring metabolic health, but whether exercise initiated exclusively during lactation has lasting effects is less clear. We investigated the effects of postpartum exercise in chow-fed and high-fat diet (HFD)-fed dams and followed their offspring after weaning. Female C57BL/6J mice consumed chow or a 60% HFD before mating and throughout lactation. Beginning on postpartum day 1, dams were assigned to sedentary or treadmill-exercise conditions until weaning on day 25.

studi.t: Stomatal conductance and net photosynthesis depend on nitrogen supply in drought-limited boreal forest
studi.s: Transition from cold limitation to drought limitation due to climate change is widespread in boreal forests. We explored in the scope of the Dry Boreal Forest Long-Term Nitrogen Fertilization Experiment (DryBoreal-LTNE) in southern boreal forests of Mongolia how N supply interacts with tree water and C relations in forests of Larix sibirica, which are naturally drought-limited. Using branches of mature L.

studi.t: Resolving Hepatic Metabolic Flux During Ex Vivo Liver Perfusion Reveals Compartment-Specific Constraints
studi.s: Normothermic machine perfusion (NMP) is used to preserve and assess donor livers, but current viability criteria rely on global measures that do not resolve intracellular metabolism, which would provide a more mechanistic measure of donor liver function. We combined staged ex vivo perfusion of mouse livers, serial lobectomy and 13C tracers ([U-13C3]lactate, [U-13C3]pyruvate and [U-13C6]glucose) to test whether glucose fragment-based flux models used in vivo describe intact hepatic metabolism.

studi.t: Optimisation of GMP-compliant hollow-fiber culturing and scaled-up separation of mesenchymal stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles to overcome unexpected impact of bovine serum contaminants' transfer to end products
studi.s: The clinical translation of mesenchymal stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles (MSC-EVs) requires scalable manufacturing strategies ensuring product purity, reproducibility, and compliance with Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) standards. However, fetal bovine serum (FBS)-derived contaminants may persist in EV preparations, compromising their characterization and clinical applicability. This study aimed to optimize MSC-EV production using hollow-fiber bioreactors while minimizing bovine protein contamination through improved culture and purification strategies.

studi.t: TEMPLE-MEASURED POSTPRANDIAL CARDIOVASCULAR RESPONSES UNDER FREE-LIVING CONDITIONS
studi.s: Eating perturbs cardiovascular homeostasis: splanchnic vasodilation after a meal is offset by autonomic adjustments that raise heart rate, and both the magnitude and duration of this response can depend on meal size and composition. Measuring these responses in daily life requires knowing when each meal begins and ends, which self-report captures poorly.

studi.t: mRNAspect: Real-Time Quality Control of Therapeutic mRNA with N1-Methylpseudouridine Bias Correction Using Nanopore Direct RNA Sequencing
studi.s: Quality attributes of therapeutic mRNA include sequence identity, transcript completeness, and poly(A) tail length. While these attributes require monitoring from development through manufacturing, each needs a separate assay. Nanopore direct RNA sequencing enables rapid quality control because it measures all three on the same molecules within a single run, and the resulting data are available during sequencing. However, N1-methylpseudouridine (m1{Psi}), which often replaces uridine in therapeutic mRNAs, alters the nanopore signal, biasing basecalling and poly(A) estimation.

studi.t: Fishing for new immunotherapy compounds to boost innate tumor rejection
studi.s: Despite significant advances in cancer immunotherapy, tackling immunosuppression remains critical to achieve more effective responses. While developing the zebrafish xenograft model, we found that some human tumors engraft very efficiently ("progressors"), while others are cleared by the host ("regressors"). We showed that this was dependent on innate immunity, which recognizes and eliminates some cancer cells, while others are able to evade and suppress it.

studi.t: Targeting ATR-CHK1-WEE1 signaling enhances IMPDH inhibitor efficacy in mTORC1-driven tumor cells
studi.s: Uncontrolled activation of the master metabolic regulator Mechanistic Target of Rapamycin Complex 1 (mTORC1) in tumors confers strong dependence on the guanylate nucleotide synthesis enzyme inosine-5'-monophosphate dehydrogenase (IMPDH) for tumor cell growth and viability. Clinically approved IMPDH inhibitors reduce the guanylate nucleotide pool available for DNA synthesis in mTORC1-driven tumor cells, resulting in prolonged DNA replication stress and accumulation of DNA damage that culminates in apoptosis.

studi.t: Autumn warming decouples the molecular control of photosynthesis and cold acclimation from growth cessation in white spruce
studi.s: {middle dot} In evergreen conifers, late-season photosynthetic downregulation is typically coordinated with growth cessation and the induction of cold acclimation, a key component of winter adaptation. However, the transcriptional basis of this coordination and its sensitivity to warming and drought remain poorly understood.

studi.t: Interpreting citizen science data for larval surveillance: lessons from storm drain reports in Mosquito Alert
studi.s: Mosquito-borne diseases are an increasing public health concern, and urban drainage infrastructure such as storm drains and catch basins can provide breeding habitat for Aedes vectors, including Aedes albopictus. Detecting these sites over large areas is costly with traditional surveillance alone, and citizen science offers a complementary, lower-cost source of geolocated observations. Mosquito Alert is a citizen science platform, active since 2014, through which participants report adult mosquitoes, bites, and potential breeding sites.

studi.t: Constraint-Based Pan-Cancer Metabolic Modeling Identifies Medium-Robust Biomarkers and Broad-Spectrum Anticancer Targets
studi.s: Background: Cancer metabolic reprogramming varies across tumour types and nutrient environments, complicating the identification of robust metabolic biomarkers and therapeutic targets. We developed a constraint based pancancer framework to identify medium robust metabolic alterations and broadly effective candidate enzyme targets. Methods: Transcriptomic profiles from 33 TCGA cancer types were integrated with Recon3D to reconstruct cancer and healthy tissue specific genome scale metabolic models.

studi.t: Fixed-parameter feedback can hold the hand near a target under gravity in two musculoskeletal arm models
studi.s: Can fixed-parameter feedback hold the hand near a target under gravity? Using muscle-length reflex and endpoint feedback in two MyoSuite arm models, we asked whether settings selected with a rigid index finger could still keep its tip near the target when the finger could bend. In the 34-muscle model, we screened 5640 combinations of controller type and parameters across three target arm postures and two update periods.

studi.t: A tuned topographic map hierarchy formats visual working memory load
studi.s: Visual working memory tasks rely on neural systems that scale activity with task load. Traditional models assume higher demands are met by monotonically increasing activity within a single process, implying high informational redundancy across responses. However, theories of cognitive control suggest processing strategies change with task demands, flexibly linking sensory inputs to behavior. Using 7T fMRI and neural encoding models, we hypothesized and confirmed that association cortices format task load-dependent responses using sensory-like neural tuning.
