studi.t: GESTATIONAL PROTEIN RESTRICTION PROGRAMS SEXUALLY DIVERGENT BEHAVIORAL AGING IN MICE: EARLY AFFECTIVE VULNERABILITY IN MALES AND LATE-LIFE MNEMONIC PRESERVATION AT A HEDONIC COST IN FEMALES
studi.s: Maternal protein restriction is a well-established model of developmental programming, yet its consequences for behavior and cognition across the second half of life, and how these differ between sexes, remain poorly characterized. We fed C57BL/6J dams a normal-protein (NP, 17%) or low-protein (LP, 6%) diet throughout gestation and followed male and female offspring with an integrated battery assessing reward sensitivity, locomotion, anxiety-like behavior, social behavior, recognition memory, spatial learning and cognitive flexibility at 12 (middle age) and 18 months (old age).

studi.t: Prioritization over certainty: Action planning in visual working memory iscoupled with selective attention, rather than action predictability
studi.s: When visual information is no longer perceptually available, working memory (WM) allows us to act on sensory representations. But does this guidance require attentional prioritization? We addressed this question by asking participants to remember two oriented bars that were later tested with one predictable and one random probe. This design allowed us to track when a remembered orientation became linked to a specific response hand and whether that link depended on which item was currently prioritized in WM.

studi.t: mRNA-1273.262 and mRNA-1283.262 Vaccines Expressing XFG Antigens Neutralize Relevant Circulating Variants
studi.s: SARS-CoV-2 continues to circulate and causes substantial disease burden as an endemic respiratory pathogen. Vaccination is a key public health measure to ameliorate the effects of COVID-19 disease but requires annual update to match strains that are circulating. Monitoring of circulating virus and characterization of matched candidate vaccines helps to inform which antigens will provide the greatest benefit to public well-being.

studi.t: Nerve and vascular abnormalities precede loss of corneal transparency in Pax6-haploinsufficient mice
studi.s: Aniridia-associated keratopathy (AAK), caused by PAX6 haploinsufficiency, progresses from a clinically clear cornea to opacity, neovascularization, and abnormal innervation, but when disease-associated changes first emerge remains unclear. We combined corneal nerve imaging, CD31 immunolabeling, transmission electron microscopy, and RNA sequencing of whole cornea from Pax6Sey-Neu/+mice at postnatal day 3-4, day 15, and adulthood. Corneal transcripts were analyzed using curated axon-guidance, myelination, and vascular/lymphatic gene panels.

studi.t: A conserved ubiquitin signalling module controls membrane raft integrity at the neuronal synapse
studi.s: Activity-dependent ubiquitination of synaptic proteins is one of the key contributors of synaptic plasticity, along with localized protein synthesis and ubiquitin-dependent protein turnover. Substantial changes in the protein composition occur in the postsynaptic density upon chronic activation or inhibition of primary neurons. Precisely how a large-scale regulation of ensembles of synaptic proteins occurs through the ubiquitin proteasome system remains unknown.

studi.t: DDB2 localizes to the nucleolus to mediate oxaliplatin resistance in colorectal cancer
studi.s: Despite the widespread use of platinum drugs in cancer therapy, defining their mechanisms of action and predicting clinical outcomes remain challenging. Unlike cisplatin, which kills cells mainly through the DNA damage response, oxaliplatin toxicity is driven largely by nucleolar stress, yet how cells cope with this stress remains poorly understood. A nucleotide excision repair protein, damage-specific DNA binding protein 2 (DDB2), protects cells from oxaliplatin but not cisplatin, suggesting that it may preferentially engage oxaliplatin adducts.

studi.t: Spatiotemporal Dynamics of Vascular Wall Cells during Ductus Arteriosus Development and Closure
studi.s: Background: The transition from fetal to postnatal circulation requires closure of the ductus arteriosus (DA), involving smooth muscle cell contraction followed by anatomical remodeling. However, the spatial organization and developmental transcriptional dynamics of vascular wall cells during this transition remain poorly understood. Methods: We analyzed vascular morphology and spatial transcript profiles of the mouse DA and aorta at five stages from embryonic day 14.5 (E14.5) to postnatal day 2.5 (P2.5), enabling paired comparisons within tissue sections.

studi.t: Single-cell Morphological Mechanisms-of-Action Profiling using Nanowell Imaging Plates
studi.s: Mechanism-of-action (MoA) analysis is used in drug discovery to prioritize compounds that act through desired pathways while eliminating compounds associated with nonspecific or undesirable activity. Image cytometry provides a promising route for MoA inference by capturing high-dimensional cellular phenotypes at single-cell resolution, but conventional workflows remain limited by unreliable cell segmentation and dependence on human-engineered feature extraction.

studi.t: CSF Boundary Disruption and Tumor-Dependent Patterns of Medulloblastoma Metastasis
studi.s: Background: Leptomeningeal metastasis is the major cause of mortality in medulloblastoma, yet the mechanisms that facilitate dissemination are poorly resolved. Here, we leveraged preclinical models to define metastatic topology, the anatomical distribution and organization of disseminated disease across craniospinal compartments and ask how topology is influenced by cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) access, primary tumor anatomy, and tumor biology.

studi.t: Actionable, Motivating, and Not Beyond Question: Student Insights On AI-Enabled Feedback and Instructor AI Use
studi.s: Scientific writing helps students develop and communicate their understanding through practices such as constructing explanations and arguing from evidence, but its complexity often requires individualized feedback and guidance. This makes scientific writing a worthwhile context in which to study the effects of feedback augmentation with generative AI (genAI). Although emerging work demonstrates that genAI can support feedback generation, considerably less is known about how students experience and respond to AI-enabled feedback.

studi.t: Archetypal analysis provides interpretable mixture representations of microbiome community structure
studi.s: Microbiome studies routinely reduce high-dimensional community profiles to a small number of coordinates for visualization and comparison. Ordination methods are powerful for detecting compositional differences, but their axes are often difficult to translate into explicit microbial community configurations; conversely, hard clustering can impose discrete states on variation that is frequently continuous.

studi.t: The emergence and neural organisation of facial-expression information during ultra-brief vision
studi.s: A glimpse lasting only a few milliseconds can convey meaningful information about a face, but how the brain transforms such minimal input into stable representations of facial expression and conscious experience remains unclear. Across two experiments using ultra-brief face presentations, we combined hierarchical psychophysical modelling, multivariate EEG decoding, and information-theoretic measures to characterise this transformation.

studi.t: Continuous ex utero development of mouse zygotes to early organogenesis
studi.s: In mammals, embryogenesis normally unfolds within the uterus, limiting direct access to the developmental processes that transform a zygote into an embryo with forming organs. Although mouse embryos can be cultured ex utero from early post-implantation stages to mid-gestation, continuous culture from the zygote into organogenesis has not been achieved. Through comparative single-cell transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses, here we discover aberrant BMP signaling and suboptimal metabolic support as barriers to continuous ex utero development.

studi.t: PMRIPrep: automated preprocessing and quantification of DSC and DCE MRI
studi.s: While dynamic susceptibility contrast (DSC) MRI measures hemodynamics and dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) MRI characterizes vascular permeability, quantitative values from both modalities remain processing-dependent. We present PMRIPrep, a Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) App for automated DSC and DCE preprocessing and quantification. PMRIPrep adapts to available acquisitions and metadata, integrates both modalities within a session, and supports four DSC deconvolution methods and four DCE pharmacokinetic models.

studi.t: Roe deer embryonic diapause is associated with reduced oxidative phosphorylation and altered lipid metabolism
studi.s: Conceptus elongation is a shared feature of preimplantation development in roe deer and cattle. However, unlike cattle embryos, roe deer embryos undergo embryonic diapause prior to elongation, during which blastocyst growth remains markedly reduced for 4-5 months before development rapidly resumes. To investigate the molecular basis of these developmental differences, we assembled a novel roe deer reference genome and analyzed single-embryo transcriptomes from diapausing and elongated roe deer conceptuses, comparing their transcriptomes with those of cattle embryos from day 6 morulae to day…

studi.t: FGF activates Wnt signaling during newt lens regeneration
studi.s: Newts regenerate their eye lens following its complete removal. To accomplish this, pigmented epithelial cells located in the dorsal iris transdifferentiate to lens epithelial cells. FGF and Wnt signaling pathways have been implicated during this process, but their association remained unclear. Here, we used FGF signaling inhibitors to stall lens regeneration and studied the affected downstream mechanisms using immunofluorescence, western blotting, and RNAseq.

studi.t: Self-generated action shapes theta phase alignment at encoding and later recollection
studi.s: Across species, self-directed action is linked to theta rhythms and better memory, but such action combines choosing, moving, and controlling the outcome. Whether choosing and control over the outcome shape recollection, and the encoding dynamics that support it, remains unclear. Three preregistered experiments in human participants separated these components while holding movement constant. Participants encoded scene pairs by dragging either a freely chosen scene or one indicated by the program, with fluent or disrupted feedback.

studi.t: Genetically Encoded Photodecaging of Asparagine Enables Protein Function Control and Time-Resolved N-Glycosylation
studi.s: Asparagine contributes to protein function through its polar carboxamide side chain and serves as the acceptor residue for N-linked glycosylation, yet temporally controlling these roles directly through the side-chain carboxamide remains challenging. Here, we report the genetic encoding of N4-(2-nitrobenzyl)-L-asparagine (ONBN), a photocaged asparagine that regenerates the native side-chain carboxamide upon 365 nm irradiation. Engineered aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs enabled site-specific ONBN incorporation into proteins in Escherichia coli and mammalian cells.

studi.t: An isogenic platform to model the impact of sex chromosome and donor genotype in hiPSC-derived vascular smooth muscle cells
studi.s: Monosomy-X results in Turner Syndrome (TS), which beyond its cardinal height and reproductive phenotypes, spans incompletely penetrant cardiovascular phenotypes, including bicuspid valve, hypoplastic left-sided heart syndrome and aortic coarctation. These congenital heart defects (CHD) conspire with hypertension to dilate the ascending aorta, which can progress to rupture and drive early mortality in TS. Genetic contributors to incompletely penetrant phenotypes in TS remain only partially explored, thus complicating risk stratification.

studi.t: A comprehensive Drosophila toolkit reveals context-dependent functional hierarchies across RasG12X variants in vivo
studi.s: KRAS is a GTPase regulating key signalling processes involved in cell proliferation, differentiation, growth and survival. KRAS is the most prevalent oncogene in human cancers, often acquiring a point mutation at Glycine 12 (G12). Although several possible amino acid substitutions occur at this hotspot in humans, most animal cancer models often examine only a single or limited subset of G12X variants, restricting our understanding of their distinct biological effects.

studi.t: ceTDP: A Practical Tutorial on Valid and Quantitative Cluster-Extent Inference in Neuroimaging
studi.s: We introduce ceTDP, a two-stage framework for cluster-extent inference in neuroimaging that extends conventional random field theory-based and permutation-based methods. In contrast to standard cluster inference, which yields binary significance, ceTDP additionally quantifies the proportion of truly active voxels within clusters using the true discovery proportion (TDP). The method is built on closed testing and provides strong family-wise error rate control while remaining consistent with standard cluster inference.

studi.t: Bacteria hyperpolarize in response to oxygen drop
studi.s: Aerobic microbes use oxygen as a terminal electron acceptor to establish an electrochemical gradient across their cell membranes. While this membrane potential ({triangleup}{Psi}) is essential for multiple cellular processes, it is unknown how it is maintained in bacteria during shifts in oxygen availability. We find that bacteria hyperpolarize in response to oxygen drop. Focusing on Bacillus subtilis and guided by modeling, we report that hyperpolarization magnitude scales with electron acceptor deprivation. We find that potassium efflux contributes to the response.

studi.t: NETWORKED proteins link actin-dependent vacuolar organization to the endoplasmic reticulum
studi.s: The organization of plant endomembrane compartments depends on coordinated interactions between membranes and the actin cytoskeleton. NETWORKED (NET) proteins are plant-specific, membrane-associated actin-binding proteins whose cellular functions remain incompletely understood. Here, we show that NET3 and NET4 have overlapping functions in maintaining vacuolar architecture and that NET4 connects actin organization with vacuolar remodeling.

studi.t: An ancient Hippo-dystrophin axis controls cortical stability and multicellular interactions in a close unicellular relative of animals
studi.s: How the protein complexes and signal transduction pathways that regulate animal physiology and human disease emerged over evolutionary time remains poorly understood. The dystrophin-dystroglycan complex (DGC), whose disruption causes muscular dystrophy in humans, is best known for its role in maintaining muscle integrity and was previously thought to have originated in animals. Here we show that Capsaspora owczarzaki, a close unicellular relative of animals, encodes core DGC components- including a bona fide dystroglycan ortholog- as critical downstream targets of the Hippo pathway.

studi.t: Asymmetric dispersal alters extinction dynamics in a two-patch metapopulation under an Allee effect
studi.s: This paper investigates a two-patch metapopulation model with asymmetric dispersal, motivated by the directional transport of organisms between populations by aquatic currents. We consider a system of ordinary differential equations in which dispersal is population-conserving but directionally asymmetric, and each patch is subject to a strong Allee effect: Populations below a critical threshold decline toward extinction, whereas those above the threshold persist and approach their carrying capacities.

studi.t: Domain Architecture Analysis Guides the Discovery of Unusual Glycyl Radical Enzyme Fusion Proteins
studi.s: Glycyl radical enzymes (GREs) use a post-translationally installed glycyl radical cofactor to catalyze chemically challenging reactions that are critical for anaerobic metabolism in microorganisms. Despite its importance, the GRE superfamily remains undercharacterized in part due to the vastness of its sequence space. Herein, we use sequence similarity network (SSN) analysis to survey the sequence diversity of the GRE superfamily and identify previously uncharacterized subfamilies.

studi.t: A Full-Thickness 3D Bioprinted Melanoma-on-Chip Platform for Preclinical Therapeutic Testing
studi.s: Malignant melanoma remains a major clinical challenge due to its high metastatic potential and frequent therapy resistance. Although recent therapeutic advances have improved patient survival, predictive preclinical models that recapitulate the human tumor microenvironment (TME) remain limited. We developed a human 3D bioprinted melanoma-on-chip platform that combines a fully differentiated, barrier-forming human skin model with microfluidic perfusion and spatially controlled integration of melanoma spheroids at the epidermal-dermal junction.

studi.t: Deep Learning Prediction of DNA Damage Response Protein Signaling from H&E Histopathology and Reverse-Phase Protein Arrays in Pan-Gynecologic and Breast Cancers
studi.s: Defects in homologous recombination and the DNA damage response (DDR) make gynecologic and breast tumors sensitive to platinum chemotherapy and PARP inhibitors, but identifying them requires costly genomic testing that reads permanent genomic scars rather than current pathway activity. Routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) slides are available for nearly every patient. This project asked whether H&E morphology carries information about functional DDR protein signaling across five cancer types in a single model.

studi.t: Ruthenium Coordination Architecture Redirects Imiquimod Antiviral Activity
studi.s: Immune agonists can reinforce antiviral defence, but therapeutic efficacy requires control over the magnitude and quality of the host response. Here we show that metal coordination can reprogramme the pharmacology of imiquimod, a clinically used TLR7 agonist. A series of Ru(II)-arene-imiquimod complexes identified the trinuclear compound 7 as a lead with activity against Herpes simplex virus types 1 and 2 (HSV-1 and HSV-2), including clinical isolates and antiviral-resistant strains.

studi.t: Ubiquitin recognition integrates plant cell-surface and intracellular receptor immunity
studi.s: Plant immunity is activated by cell-surface and intracellular receptors that detect pathogen-derived molecules. Mutual potentiation between these two receptor types is essential for robust disease resistance, but the mechanisms underpinning integrated dual receptor immunity remain unknown. Here, we found that activation of the intracellular receptor, ZAR1, induces its site-specific modification by non-proteolytic ubiquitin chains.

studi.t: FBH1 restrains replication progression independently of promoting double strand breaks at hydroxyurea-stalled replication forks
studi.s: In response to stress, stalled replication forks undergo fork reversal converting replication forks into a 4-way junction. FBH1 is a DNA helicase that promotes replication fork reversal. After prolonged replication stress, FBH1 promotes double strand break accumulation and cell death. One of the hallmarks of loss of fork reversal is unrestrained replication in the presence of DNA damage, but how FBH1 restrains replication at stalled forks is not known. Here, we show that FBH1 limits replication fork progression by PRIMPOL and REV1 in response to hydroxyurea.

studi.t: Mechanical Tension Actively Triggers RhoA-Mediated Cell Extrusion
studi.s: Cell extrusion is a fundamental process in tissue homeostasis, morphogenesis, and cancer progression, facilitating the removal of cells either alive or through apoptosis. While biochemical signaling pathways are known to regulate extrusion, recent advances have underscored the importance of mechanical forces in this process.

studi.t: WS6 enhances expansion of primary human airway basal cells and supports clonal genome editing
studi.s: Fundamental airway epithelial biology, disease modeling and regenerative medicine research rely on the ability to expand and manipulate primary human airway basal cells, often from small clinical samples. Basal stem/progenitor cells from (pseudo)stratified epithelia can be expanded in 3T3-J2 fibroblast feeder cell co-culture systems, and the addition of the ROCK inhibitor Y-27632 enhances proliferation and culture longevity, a phenomenon that has been described as 'conditional reprogramming'. Here, we developed 'EpMED', a feeder-based FAD medium supplemented with Y-27632 and WS6.

studi.t: Sustained LDL-C Lowering Reveals Selective Expansion of Fibroblast Subpopulations with Distinct Regulatory and Matrix Programs During Atherosclerosis Remodeling
studi.s: Background: Smooth muscle cells (SMCs) and SMC-derived cells contribute to atherosclerotic plaque stability through matrix production and fibrous cap formation. Recent studies have also identified distinct fibroblast populations in atherosclerotic lesions, but how these populations respond to sustained LDL-C lowering and contribute to plaque remodeling remains poorly understood.

studi.t: NFYA regulates two genome-wide transcriptional activation events during oocyte-to-embryo transition
studi.s: Primordial follicle oocyte activation (PFA) and zygotic genome activation (ZGA) represent two major waves of transcription activation respectively required for oocyte growth and embryo development. Although many shared molecular hallmarks between PFA and ZGA suggest potential common mechanisms driving both waves of transcriptional activation, such regulators are yet to be identified. Here we demonstrate that the pioneer factor NFYA belongs to such regulators.

studi.t: Integrin-Linked Kinase Controls Tissue Integrity in Embryonic Renal Stroma Via Expression of Fibronectin During a Critical Developmental Time Window
studi.s: The stroma is a heterogenous framework that plays a critical role to mechanically and biologically support contiguous parenchymal elements in any organ. Studies on kidney development have historically focused largely on the epithelial and vascular tissue elements. Recent progress demonstrating stromal cell heterogeneity provided a basis to further investigate stromal functions at the crossroads of mechanical and chemical signaling in genetic mutants with stromal cell deficiency of Integrin-Linked Kinase, a Focal Adhesion (FA) adaptor, and a key regulator of the embryonic kidney.

studi.t: Mitochondrial dysfunction plays a key role in premature musculoskeletal aging in hypochondroplasia mouse model
studi.s: Hypochondroplasia (HCH) is a developmental disorder characterized by short stature and caused by gain-of-function mutations in fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 (FGFR3). These mutations result in impaired bone and cartilage growth, tissues which are significantly affected in aging. We show that Hch mice exhibit hallmarks of accelerated aging: bone fragility, articular cartilage and subchondral bone changes, decreased muscle strength and reduction in muscle fibers size. Proteomic analyses of the cortical bone revealed that Hch mice follow a different aging trajectory than controls.

studi.t: A mechanistic framework for nascent RNA-seq simulations
studi.s: Recent advances in nascent RNA sequencing promise profound insights into transcriptional dynamics. Analyzing the complex datasets generated from nascent RNA genomic approaches require robust computational pipelines and methods to harmonize across experimental workflows. Current solutions include simulation of read counts from individual protocols, but these methods fail to properly replicate biological and technical artifacts or allow for the comparison between nascent RNA approaches.

studi.t: PP2A-B55α Terminates Mitophagy by Selectively Dephosphorylating Parkin via a Non-Canonical Interface
studi.s: Mitophagy, the selective autophagic clearance of damaged mitochondria, is tightly governed by the PINK1-Parkin signaling axis. Although the activation of Parkin, driven by phosphorylation of ubiquitin (Ub) and Parkin, has been well characterized, the mechanisms that terminate mitophagy remain poorly understood. Here, we identify the heterotrimeric protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A) holoenzyme assembled with the B55 regulatory subunit (PP2A-B55 as the terminator of mitophagy.

studi.t: Internet of Genetic Things (IoGT): Programmable Long-Distance Cybergenetic Logic Circuits Integrating IoT, Optogenetics, and Bacterial Gene Expression
studi.s: The Internet of Things (IoT) exchanges information and coordinates functions among geographically separated electronic devices. However, establishing analogous long-distance networks between genetically engineered living systems remains a challenge because synthetic genetic intercellular communication largely relies on local molecular signal transport.

studi.t: CICADA: A unified framework for NWB-based neurophysiological data analysis
studi.s: Neurophysiology datasets are becoming increasingly complex, combining behavioral measurements with high-dimensional neuronal activity recordings coming from optical and/or electrophysiological measurements. The Neurodata Without Borders (NWB) standard has emerged in the community as the format of record. While standardized and widely used preprocessing tools generating NWB files have been developed, extensible frameworks for scientific analysis downstream of the NWB ecosystem are still under-represented.

studi.t: Copper sensing by OXA1L triggers a mitochondria-to-nucleus stress response to restrain cuproptosis
studi.s: Copper overload triggers cuproptosis, a regulated cell death driven by aggregation of lipoylated DLAT and collapse of mitochondrial proteostasis. How cells sense this stress and mount an adaptive response is unknown. Here, combining time-resolved proximity-labeling proteomics across five subcellular compartments with genetic and biochemical dissection, we define a mitochondria-to-nucleus retrograde surveillance pathway.

studi.t: NPEPPS segmental duplication drives position effect expression of TBC1D3 in the human brain
studi.s: In humans, the TBC1D3 gene family has been implicated in cortical expansion by promoting neuronal proliferation, yet the gene family exhibits extreme copy number variation (3-39 copies) and structural heterozygosity (97%). We investigate how a gene linked to development can remain so variable. We show that 45-96% of TBC1D3 expression derives from a single paralog. The paralog's >3-fold higher expression is driven by a ~8.9 MYA segmental duplication that relocated a partial duplication of puromycin-sensitive aminopeptidase (NPEPPS), including its promoter, adjacent to TBC1D3.

studi.t: Fighting Sleep: Minute-by-Minute Driver Fatigue from a Dry-Electrode EEG Headband
studi.s: Driver-facing cameras often catch fatigue too late. We asked whether a four-electrode dry headband, which picks up eye movements electrically and head tilt with a motion sensor, can follow fatigue minute by minute. Nine participants wore the headband for twelve sessions of a 50-minute monotonous task at a driving simulator station, without driving, answering one cue a minute and rating their sleepiness every five minutes, with a webcam on the face for comparison.

studi.t: PFLISA: A New Ultrasensitive, Multiplex Immunoassay Platform Enables Cytokine Network Profiling in Sepsis
studi.s: Immune responses emerge from coordinated cytokine networks, but quantitative profiling remains constrained by limited clinical sample volumes and the very low circulating concentrations of many biologically important mediators. We introduce the Plasmonic Fluor-Linked ImmunoSorbent Assay (PFLISA), that combines plasmonic-enhanced fluorescence with spatially encoded antibody arrays in a standard 96-well format.

studi.t: PTP1B supports survival and regulates CFL1 and HSP90a abundance in trastuzumab-resistant HER2-positive breast cancer.
studi.s: Trastuzumab resistance limits the treatment of HER2-positive breast cancer. Here, we identify protein tyrosine phosphatase 1B (PTP1B) as a survival dependency in models of intrinsic and acquired trastuzumab resistance, including cells with endogenous ERBB2 kinase domain mutations (L755S and V777L), a patient-derived tumor organoid model, and orthotopic xenografts. PTP1B expression was elevated in multiple trastuzumab-resistant models, accompanied by increased PI3K-AKT and ERK signaling in several of these.

studi.t: DECODING SHAPE ICONICITY OF WORDS AND PSEUDOWORDS: AN fMRI STUDY
studi.s: Iconicity refers to systematic links between word form and meaning. Although evidence for iconicity in natural language continues to grow, its neural basis remains unclear. Using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and multivariate pattern analysis (MVPA), we examined iconic shape associations of auditory real words and pseudowords. The pseudowords were matched to the real words in phonemic and phonotactic properties, differing primarily in the absence of learned semantic representations. Participants listened to each item and judged whether it sounded rounded or pointed.

studi.t: Memory network activity flow failures in temporal and frontal lobe epilepsy
studi.s: Declarative memory emerges from distributed brain networks, yet how large-scale network organization constrains memory function remains unclear. Intrinsic connectivity mirrors task activity, suggesting intrinsic architecture governs memory states. Temporal and frontal lobe epilepsy (TLE, FLE), differentially affecting episodic and semantic systems, provide complementary models of network disruption.

studi.t: Neural representations of visual memory in inferotemporal cortex reveal a generalizable framework for translating between spikes and field potentials
studi.s: Translating neurophysiological findings requires understanding the relationship between common measures of brain activity in animals (spiking activity) and humans (local field potentials, LFP). Prior work suggests alignment between population spiking and high-gamma activity (HGA, 50-150 Hz) of the LFP; however, this is not always observed and is consequently debated. Here, we show that this alignment and prior failures depend on the underlying coding scheme. First, we examined neural representations of variables related to visual memory in macaque inferotemporal cortex.

studi.t: Competition Between Task Accuracy and Habitual Locomotor Behavior Underlies the Speed-Accuracy Trade-Off in Walking
studi.s: The speed-accuracy trade-off is a hallmark feature of motor behavior, yet its underlying causes in cyclic, whole-body movements such as walking remain to be understood. In discrete, point-to-point movements, reduced accuracy at higher speeds is typically attributed to signal-dependent motor noise and an inability to use online error correction. Walking, however, may be governed by additional objectives, such as minimizing metabolic energy expenditure.

studi.t: Loss of the s2U tRNA modification induces antibiotic tolerance and is linked to changes in ribosomal protein expression
studi.s: Stress promotes phenotypic changes in bacteria that allow them to survive antibiotic treatment. This phenomenon, termed antibiotic tolerance, can cause antibiotic treatment failure, highlighting a need to define bacterial pathways that promote survival. Previously, we found Yersinia pseudotuberculosis downregulates the gene tusB in response to doxycycline. tusB is involved in generating a sulfur tRNA modification, 2-thiouridine or s2U, that increases translation fidelity and efficiency. Here, we find that deletion of tusB results in loss of s2U and induces antibiotic tolerance.

studi.t: RasGRP1 agonism stimulates P-TEFb biogenesis via MEK-ERK-mTORC1 signaling to reverse HIV latency with minimal CD4 downregulation
studi.s: Reactivating latent HIV to eliminate persisting infected cells requires non-toxic latency-reversing agents (LRAs) that activate P-TEFb, a cellular transcription factor essential for efficient HIV RNA synthesis. Diacylglycerol (DAG)-mimicking PKC agonists induce P-TEFb to reverse HIV latency mainly through a PKC-independent RasGRP1-Ras-Raf-MEK-ERK1/2 pathway, but also elicit global T-cell activation and a drastic downregulation of CD4 receptors.

studi.t: Isolation by distance and metapopulation structure in Mozambican populations of the soft tick Ornithodoros phacochoerus, a vector of African swine fever virus.
studi.s: Ticks of the species Ornithodoros phacochoerus are endophilic soft ticks which infest warthog burrows. Like other Ornithodoros of the O. moubata species complex, O. phacochoerus is a vector of the African swine fever virus and participates in the maintenance of the virus among warthogs in the sylvatic cycle in Southern and Eastern African countries. In this study, the population genetic structure of O. phacochoerus was investigated using fifteen microsatellite markers.

studi.t: Rapid, accurate, and memory-frugal sub-gene-level quantification of probe-based, multiplexed single-cell data
studi.s: Probe-based, multiplexed single-cell assays profile multiple samples in parallel by sequencing known DNA probes tagged with both sample and cell barcodes. Most existing single-cell quantification tools were built for poly(A)-based assays and are not tailored to compact probe references or nested sample-cell barcodes. We extend simpleaf to demultiplex and quantify probe-based single-cell libraries rapidly with a low memory footprint.

studi.t: Comprehensive analysis of TEAD inhibition in meningioma identifies MEK and mTOR inhibition as effective combination therapies against resistant lines.
studi.s: Meningiomas are the most common primary central nervous system tumors in adults, posing a significant burden to society. Although a large percentage of lower-grade meningiomas are curable by surgery or radiation alone, high-grade and a subset of low-grade meningiomas demonstrate recurrences and complications from treatment. Systemic therapies for meningioma remain ineffective, and no targeted treatments are approved. We have recently shown that YAP1/TAZ-TEAD signaling is an oncogenic driver of meningioma.

studi.t: Beyond canonical: Hidden phosphoregulatory control in RAS signaling reveals context-dependent rewiring in Y1 tumor cells
studi.s: Cell signaling pathways are not static. Regulatory mechanisms finely control the signal across complex networks to promote signal propagation. Among them, phosphorylation is one of the most important regulatory mechanisms, in which signal cascades propagate signals to the nucleus, enabling responses. Phosphorylation events can be regulated by guanine nucleotide exchange factors (GEFs) and GTPase-activating proteins (GAPs) to coordinate the activation state of small G-proteins.

studi.t: Ontogenetic and time-course transcriptomic analyses of maize leaf primordia reveal regulators of transverse vein development
studi.s: Leaf vein patterning varies greatly among land plants and is linked to leaf structure and function. C4 plants, such as maize, have a denser arrangement of veins than C3 plants, which is hypothesized to be a pre-adaptive trait for C4 photosynthesis. Therefore, understanding how leaf veins are patterned has implications for maximizing photosynthetic efficiency. Major maize leaf veins, called longitudinal veins, are arranged in parallel and are interconnected by transverse veins.

studi.t: Managing the genetic diversity of Dioscorea yams for adaptation to climate change
studi.s: Understanding adaptation to the environment is fundamental to agriculture. We analyzed a georeferenced collection of 167 accessions of three Dioscorea species (cultivated D. rotundata and its wild relatives D. praehensilis and D. abyssinica) spanning a wide range of environments, from dry Sahelian to rainforest. After accounting for species identity, population structure and geography, environment explained 1.8% of genetic variation, and genome-environment association analyses identified few loci (16 in the full panel and three within cultivated D.

studi.t: Genetically encoded RNA strand exchange circuits for programmable protein expression and information processing in cells
studi.s: Nucleic acid circuits based on toehold-mediated strand exchange (TMSE) have enabled sophisticated in vitro molecular computers, biosensors, and diagnostics, but translating these successes to living cells for continuous operation has been challenging. Primary hurdles include difficulty producing the multi-stranded circuit components in situ and poor understanding of design principles in complex cellular environments.

studi.t: Stress-Induced Early Hatching Alters Growth Trajectory and Experience-Dependent Transcriptome in Red-Eyed Treefrog (Agalychnis callidryas) Tadpoles
studi.s: The ability to grow fast and develop frugally in the face of hazards is a common feature of plants and animals. Life History Theory predicts that trade-offs between immediate survival or reproduction and future longevity may occur under threatening conditions. Embryos of the Neotropical red-eyed treefrog (Agalychnis callidryas) hatch prematurely (escape hatching) in response to ecological stressors such as flooding-induced hypoxia, desiccation, and egg-predator attack, making this species an ecologically grounded model for the evolutionary-developmental biology of early life stress (ELS).

studi.t: Fluorescence Lifetime Imaging Microscopy (FLIM) reveals the diversity and complexities of an open ocean photosymbiosis
studi.s: The Retaria are a marine protist lineage that host photosynthetic endosymbionts, where these symbioses play an important role in open ocean food web dynamics. Despite the importance of these relationships, our knowledge about planktonic Retaria photosymbiont diversity remains limited due to the present inability to cultivate these lineages, requiring direct, culture-free observations.

studi.t: Environmental and anthropogenic drivers of Culex pipiens biotype pipiens overwintering phenology
studi.s: Background: Culex pipiens biotype pipiens (Cx. p. pipiens) is the primary vector of West Nile and Usutu viruses in Europe and overwinters as adult females in shelters, such as cellars. However, the localised environmental and anthropogenic drivers regulating adult behavioural plasticity and the timing of entry into and exit from these overwintering sites remain poorly understood. Methods: Over two consecutive winters (2023-2025) in Northwestern Germany, we monitored the overwintering period of Cx. p.

studi.t: Selection for extreme neck elongation in crown birds
studi.s: Variation in segment number, length, and identity is a major axis of diversification in bilaterians, shaped by developmental novelty and constraint. The near-invariant neck vertebral (cervical) count of mammals is a classic example of such constraint, yet we find that mammals occupy an unexceptional region of amniote cervical morphospace. In contrast, crown birds evolved extraordinarily long-neck proportions through increases in both cervical number and length, a combination only approached by ecologically-distinct sauropods among other archosaurs.

studi.t: Auditing Confidence-Calibrated Benchmarking of Single-Cell Perturbation Models
studi.s: Single-cell perturbation models are increasingly assessed for both predictive performance and calibrated uncertainty under distribution shift. We constructed such an evaluation harness (two datasets, Norman 2019 and Replogle 2022; four split types over six dataset-split combinations; three models, scVI, CPA and a linear Ridge baseline; three uncertainty quantification methods, MC dropout, quantile regression and split conformal prediction) and then audited it against null baselines it had never included. Most of its headline results measure something other than what their metric names claim.

studi.t: Very Early Cortical Auditory Responses to Speech in Humans
studi.s: A foundational measure of the auditory system's ability to process sound correctly is the auditory brainstem response (ABR) and middle latency response (MLR) complex, but their dependence on stimulus complexity and behavioral relevance is poorly understood. Here we recorded noninvasive, simultaneous electroencephalography (EEG) and magnetoencephalography (MEG) in adults listening to both naturalistic speech and clicks, and computed the resulting temporal response functions (TRFs).

studi.t: HERO: A hierarchy-aware analysis pipeline for reducing and refining whole-brain atlas-mapped cellular datasets
studi.s: Advances in high-throughput mesoscale microscopy and machine learning-based image analysis pipelines have made unbiased whole-brain imaging widely accessible. However, translating the resulting atlas-mapped datasets into biologically meaningful results remains a substantial barrier owing to their sheer magnitude and complex hierarchical organization. Consequently, reporting structure and analysis methods vary widely across studies, undermining rigor and reproducibility.

studi.t: Neural networks as decision trees: an analytical solution for learning and neural selectivity
studi.s: Nonlinear neural networks develop structured internal representations, yet how their geometry is determined by the tasks being learned remains poorly understood. Here, we develop an analytical framework for piecewise-linear feedforward and recurrent networks that links learning, activation-region structure, and neural selectivity. We show that, at any stationary point of gradient-aligned learning, a nonlinear network decomposes into local linear regressions over its activation regions.

studi.t: Seeing new 'stuff' for the very first time
studi.s: Humans are excellent at recognizing materials like food, soil or paper, which is crucial for many everyday tasks. We generally enjoy vivid intuitions about what surfaces would feel like, without reaching out and touching them. While this capability is understandable for familiar materials, how does the brain interpret stuff we have never encountered before? We hypothesized that the need to distinguish useful or hazardous substances by sight led to the ability to infer material properties from the very first encounter.

studi.t: Estimating Divergence Times and Diversification Rates with the Unresolved Fossilized Birth-Death Process
studi.s: Tip-dating using Fossilized Birth-Death (FBD) models offers a favorable alternative to conventional node-dating analyses of the evolutionary timescale, bypassing various conceptual and technical difficulties. However, despite their increasing popularity in phylogenetic studies, their use has remained rather limited in taxonomic scope because of the difficulty in collecting morphological data, which is often required for tip-dating analyses, and computational intractability when a large number of fossils are present.

studi.t: Octopamine instructs head direction plasticity
studi.s: Many plasticity rules rely on adjusting the strength of synapses between pairs of cells based on their coincident activity. We uncovered a new mechanism for coincidence detection in the Drosophila head direction network. To maintain an accurate sense of direction, head direction neurons that signal orientation during navigation must learn to anchor to relevant external sensory cues in novel environments. Yet the synaptic mechanism for this form of unsupervised learning is unknown in any organism.

studi.t: Sall1a, a transcription factor responsible for the Townes-Brocks syndrome, is involved in hair cell maturation
studi.s: Hair cells of the inner ear are highly specialized mechanosensory cells that convert auditory and vestibular stimuli into electrical signals essential for hearing and balance. While early hair cells fate commitment is well defined, the transcriptional regulators acting at later stages of hair cell maturation remain poorly understood. Spal-like (SALL) family transcription factors are evolutionarily conserved and implicated in multiple developmental processes, and mutation in humans causes Townes-Brocks syndrome, associated with hearing impairment.

studi.t: AI, Automation, and Fiscal Pressure
studi.s: We study how automation affects public finances in countries that (i) tax labor at a higher rate than capital and (ii) fund services such as health care and education from tax revenues rather than user fees. We embed task-level automation within a two-sector general equilibrium model, which we calibrate to match data from EU countries. Automation shifts income toward more lightly taxed capital. If public services follow consumer demand, the budget deficit worsens at unchanged tax rates, even if automation is as fast in the public-service sector as in the private sector.

studi.t: The Socratic PAUSE: safeguarding scientific judgement at AI speed
studi.s: Generative AI can turn a tentative scientific question into hypotheses, methods, code and interpretations within minutes. Yet generating a contribution does not establish that it deserves scientific reliance: researchers must still examine its evidence, assumptions and implications, and remain accountable for the decision to rely on it. Using Einstein's sketch of scientific discovery as a lens, we argue that AI has accelerated discovery far more than justification.

studi.t: Interacting with Alexa: A Longitudinal Case Study of Voice Assistant Use in Down Syndrome
studi.s: As life expectancy for individuals with Down syndrome (DS) continues to increase, supporting cog- nitive engagement, everyday autonomy, and participation throughout adulthood has become an important research priority. Conversational voice assistants have emerged as promising assistive tech- nologies for these purposes, yet evidence regarding their long-term use in naturalistic settings remains limited. This paper presents a longitudinal case study of the everyday use of Amazon Alexa by an adult with Down syndrome over nine months in a real domestic environment.

studi.t: Somatic Alignment: Scaffolding Non-Visible Inner Body Sensations in and beyond Vocal Pedagogy
studi.s: Inner bodily sensations inform expressive musical performance but can be difficult to interpret and communicate. Through two separate workshops with five singing learners and four senior voice teachers, we investigate breath control in vocal pedagogy. Participants reported difficulty interpreting bodily sensations (Opacity of Inner Sensations) and translating awareness into intended adjustments (Disconnected Regulation of Inner Sensations), alongside strategies involving touch, demonstration, and imagery.

studi.t: Is Sara Omar the true author of Dødevaskeren (The Dead Washer)? Authorship attribution in Danish literature
studi.s: The bestseller Dødevaskeren (The Dead Washer) was published in 2017 under the name Sara Omar. A Danish colleague has suggested that the novel may have been written by another author, possibly Mads Peder Nordbo. To investigate this authorship question, four authorship attribution methods were applied, namely Delta, intertextual distance, Nearest Shrunken Centroids (NSC), and naïve Bayes.

studi.t: Will AI Replace Juniors? How Task Complexity Reduces Automation Risk
studi.s: How does task complexity shape firms' willingness to substitute entry-level labour with artificial intelligence (AI) tools? We study this question using a pre-registered survey experiment with managers from 1,435 German firms in the information economy and manufacturing industry. Managers are randomly assigned to consider a long lasting need for additional capacity involving either well-structured and standardised tasks, or more complex tasks that require professional judgement, contextual knowledge and independent problem-solving.

studi.t: Silent on Code? A Computing Lens on Generative AI Guidance at Canadian Polytechnics and Research Universities
studi.s: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools now write, explain, and debug code, which changes how computing students learn and how their work is assessed. Instructors, however, act within institutional guidance written largely with essays in mind. We report a document analysis of the public, institution-level GenAI guidance of the 13 members of Polytechnics Canada and the 15 members of the U15 Group of Canadian Research Universities, retrieved in October 2026.

studi.t: A new method of Ecological Inference based on the Cressie--Read power divergence
studi.s: Ecological inference aims to estimate the bivariate association structure between a pair of variables from the row and column totals of a set of contingency tables. The paper introduces a new approach based on minimizing the Cressie--Read power divergence, applied to the estimation of vote transitions between two elections. It also outlines a Fisher scoring algorithm and derives the asymptotic distribution of the estimator.

studi.t: Budget, Readout or Reasoning? Where Small Reasoning Models Lose Value in Auction Bidding
studi.s: Ad platforms and marketplaces show bidders a bid landscape, the estimated chance of winning at each candidate bid, and increasingly let agents built on reasoning language models choose the bid. We give six open reasoning models of 4B to 14B parameters such landscapes, with win curves from eBay closing prices and from a simulated advertising market (AuctionNet), and score their bids on held-out auctions against an exact calculator. Because the agent is handed the estimates, the lost value can be split by cause. Two failures belong to the models.

studi.t: How AI Is Reconfiguring Work in India: A Task-Based Framework for Understanding Augmentation, Displacement, New Roles and the Changing Structure of Jobs
studi.s: Public debate on AI and Indian employment tends to compress a complicated phenomenon into a single binary: will AI take a given job, or not. This paper argues that the accurate picture is a taxonomy rather than a binary. AI rarely replaces a job wholesale; more often it automates a bundle of tasks within a job, and the size of that bundle varies with task structure, sector, regulatory setting, and, distinctively in India's case, the economics of AI access itself.

studi.t: The Illusion of an Automated German Census: Assessing the Feasibility of the 2031 Register-Based Census via Simulation
studi.s: The next German Census (2031) is planned to be the country's first fully register-based census, relying exclusively on administrative data sources. In addition to the population registers, ten further administrative registers are envisaged, covering a wide range of information, from driving licences to agricultural social insurance. This study simulates potential data-quality challenges in linking these registers using quasi-identifiers (QIDs), such as names and dates of birth.

studi.t: Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao Reconstruction of Discrete space Population Dynamics
studi.s: Reconstructing the continuous time dynamics of cell state evolution from sparse snapshot observations can be formulated as an unbalanced optimal transport problem. To study such dynamics at a coarse grained cell type level, unbalanced optimal transport must be extended to discrete state spaces. Inspired by discrete flow matching, we extended the dynamic Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao (WFR) problem to discrete spaces, and derived a closed form for its solution.

studi.t: Language models call themselves AI but do not favor AI over people
studi.s: Many fear that AI systems will side with one another against people. Social identity theory, which explains why people favor their own group, offers one way to examine this fear. Seen through this theory, AI would side with AI only if it treated AI as its group and favored AI over people. In three experiments, 24 language models favored a group they were assigned to, even a team of AI agents. With no group assigned, they gave a person more money and credit than an AI agent. Prompts that made them say they belong with AI changed their behavior much less than an assigned team did.

studi.t: Beyond Disclosure: Compositional Privacy Harm in AI Systems
studi.s: Privacy law attaches obligations to each stage of information processing, whether it be collection, use, storage, or disclosure. We examine how legally cognisable privacy harm emerges across this full lifecycle rather than at any single one of these points. We argue that privacy risk in AI systems is compositional, arising from the interaction of memorisation, extraction, inference and contextual transfer. Disclosure is therefore not the sole threshold of privacy harm: legally significant consequences may emerge even where no underlying record is reproduced verbatim.

studi.t: Simple, general strategies for correcting the upward bias of calibration summaries of prediction models
studi.s: For clinical prediction models, calibration across the spectrum of predicted values is often assessed via flexible calibration curves and associated scalar summaries such as the integrated calibration index (ICI). However, these scalar summaries tend to have a finite-sample upward bias, as they are based on the absolute value of an estimate whose sampling distribution can cross zero. We show the mechanism underlying this bias and quantify its magnitude as a function of the true calibration error and its variance.

studi.t: Shooting for Fit: Risk-Averse Stochastic Roster Construction from Bayesian Shot-Pattern Models
studi.s: Roster construction is a critical decision problem in professional basketball, requiring teams to balance player quality, player complementarity, and financial constraints under uncertainty. Existing roster optimization models primarily rely on individual player ratings and aggregate performance statistics, which provide limited information about how players' offensive contributions vary with their teammates. Recent advances in player-tracking technology have enabled statistical analyses of spatial shooting patterns, but these insights have rarely informed roster construction.

studi.t: GlassGround: GUI Grounding Beyond Native Screenshots with Egocentric Wearable Vision
studi.s: Wearable assistants must localize interface elements from camera observations when direct screenshot access is unavailable, yet existing GUI grounding benchmarks primarily evaluate native screenshots. We introduce GlassGround, a new benchmark that pairs native screenshots with wearable camera observations while holding GUI states, instructions, and targets fixed. GlassGround contains 3,250 tasks across Android and iOS, captured using four wearable devices under four viewing conditions.

studi.t: AI Persona Dialogue Pipeline; From Survey Report to Conversational Personas, Evaluated by LLMs and Experts
studi.s: Simulating dialogue of a population with LLM-enacted personas is increasingly common, yet each pipeline is generally built for one task, so a new task usually means reworking how the persona is authored, enacted and evaluated. We present an end-to-end persona dialogue pipeline meant to carry over to other populations as a whole; a background is written by an LLM from a national survey report, an off-the-shelf LLM enacts it without fine-tuning, and both are rated for perceived plausibility.

studi.t: RoboJackVR: Turning Robot Tasks into VR Games for Scalable Demonstration Collection
studi.s: Scaling robot demonstration datasets requires collection systems that accommodate more participants and diverse tasks, yet teleoperation barriers and task-adaptation effort limit this expansion. We present RoboJackVR, a standalone virtual reality (VR) game in which players manipulate simulated robots to execute combat skills and contribute demonstrations. MuJoCo simulation and demonstration recording run locally on the headset, removing the need for an external PC or simulation server during collection.

studi.t: Knocking on Minds Door; A Mixed-Methods Field Study of a Voice LLM Companion in Older Adults Daily Lives
studi.s: Global aging makes digital technology important for older adults healthy aging, yet graphical user interfaces remain inaccessible to many. Voice agents based on large language models may help, but users needs and reasons for sustained use remain unclear. We developed a phone-call-style companion that initiates conversations proactively and structures calls using a persona, conversation rules, and prior-call memory (facts, insights, relationship background).

studi.t: Refusal Is Not Scored: A Coverage Limit in Content-Based Bias Evaluation
studi.s: Bias audits of conversational models often discard refusals (responses such as "I can't assist with that request") before scoring, a filtering step which is rarely examined as a measurement decision even though it determines which responses an audit is capable of evaluating. This work examines what the step removes, applying seven bias-evaluation instruments spanning both deployed paradigms, three dictionary-based and four LLM-as-judge, to two intersectional datasets of 360 generated responses each.

studi.t: Cutting Bus Service Without Cutting Access: Persistent Homology of Service Deserts and Timetable Reductions
studi.s: Japanese bus operators are withdrawing service for lack of drivers, and the choice of which trips to withdraw determines who keeps a bus. We measure service at each stop from vehicle GPS and smart-card records, without timetables, and use persistent homology of walking and walking-plus-waiting time to find enclosed service deserts: pockets surrounded by service but beyond walking distance from it. Around Tsukuba, 35 such pockets lie more than 800m from any station or hourly stop. The 17 that are fully ringed by walkable service hold 18,446 residents.

studi.t: The evolution of extreme spatial heterochiasmy in amphibians: interactions between sex-specific meiotic program and chromosome architecture
studi.s: Heterochiasmy, sex differences in meiotic recombination, is usually described in terms of genetic-map length, potentially obscuring more consequential differences in crossover location. Amphibians provide striking examples of extreme spatial heterochiasmy, with male recombination concentrated near chromosome ends and female recombination broadly distributed, yet the evolution and genetic basis of this pattern remains poorly understood. Here, we combine a review with a phylogenetic comparative synthesis of male chiasma location across 97 amphibian species.

studi.t: Before They Were Cool: Do Early Fans Abandon Artists Who Suddenly Become Popular? Evidence from Online Music Listening
studi.s: Identity-signalling theory, echoed in the hipster's "I liked them before they were cool", expects an artist's first fans to pull away once the artist becomes popular, by leaving or by avoiding what the newcomers play. A rival account expects the event that brings the crowd to renew existing listeners' attention to the artist. We test both in the Last.fm listening histories of 594,415 users (21.1 billion plays, 2005-2013), where every play appears on the user's profile.

studi.t: Refinements to precision-information imputation in meta-analysis of survival rates: Boundary correction and cross-study borrowing
studi.s: Meta-analyses of survival rates require precision information, such as standard errors (SEs), which is often unreported. We previously proposed imputing missing SEs from reported survival rates, sample sizes, and risk-set sizes. The original method has two limitations. First, it replaces Kaplan--Meier estimates of 1 with 0.99 regardless of sample size. Second, when the risk-set size is unavailable, it uses the total event count as a fallback. The count is often unreported, and the fallback can also substantially overestimate SEs.

studi.t: Optimization of a Hybrid Solar-Biogas-Battery Energy Storage Microgrid: A Case Study
studi.s: Low-income regions like eastern Uganda often lack reliable grid power. This paper presents the techno-economic optimization of the Soroti Integrated Renewable Energy Microgrid (SIREM), a hybrid renewable system for grid-access expansion where Soroti District household grid access stands at 16.7\%. The microgrid integrates concentrating solar power (CSP) with thermal storage, biogas combined cycle generation, and lithium iron phosphate battery storage.

studi.t: Evaluating Strategies for Multimodal Bidirectional Interactions between Pedestrians and AVs
studi.s: Autonomous Vehicles (AVs) share spaces with Vulnerable Road Users (VRUs) in encounters where driver cues are absent. This can leave people uncertain whether the vehicle has noticed them and understood their request. Existing research has studied how AVs communicate with pedestrians through external human-machine interfaces. This work investigates bidirectional multimodal VRU-AV interactions combining Augmented Reality (AR), speech, and gestures.

studi.t: Noise-induced Extinction in Hierarchical Food Webs
studi.s: Every finite population is eventually driven to extinction by demographic noise, even when the deterministic dynamics have a stable coexistence state. We develop a large-deviation theory of this process for hierarchical food webs of arbitrary size. In a community of $N$ species, the basal species $X_1$ reproduces intrinsically and every consumer may prey on all species below it, so that omnivory is built into the interaction graph. For unit conversion efficiency and self-limitation confined to the basal species, the mean-field dynamics have at most $2^{N-1}+1$ feasible fixed points.

studi.t: EgoCARBS: Egocentric Video Meets Active Acoustics for Kitchen Action Understanding
studi.s: Egocentric video records what a person looks at, but often misses what their body does: the hands leave the frame, and arm motion goes unseen. An exocentric camera recovers this context, but it must be installed wherever the activity happens. Active acoustic sensing can recover it from the wearables themselves: a device's speaker emits inaudible chirps, and its microphone senses the motion of the hands, arms, and nearby objects from their echoes. Yet no public dataset pairs it with egocentric video. We present EgoCARBS, with two deliverables.

studi.t: Temporal Conditioning for Human Behavioral Cloning in Chess
studi.s: Behavioral cloning models in chess typically predict human moves from board states while ignoring temporal inputs such as the remaining clock. However, time pressure is a major determinant of human decision-making quality, and temporal state is a missing dimension of human behavioral modeling. This paper introduces a time-aware transformer that extends a Chessformer-style architecture with learned temporal conditioning tokens encoding player clock state, time control, and recent tempo, together with behavioral heads for thinking time and resignation.

studi.t: Evolutionary constraints on protein fold diversity
studi.s: Arrangements of secondary structures in proteins yield a wide variety of possible topologies, yet the protein folds observed in nature are limited in their diversity. Is the number of protein folds limited by biophysical constraints or by evolutionary contingency? In recent years, the development of new methods for protein structure prediction and comparison, molecular design, and the rapid progress of cryo-electron microscopy revealed new insights into the protein fold space.

studi.t: Bayesian Learning of Spatially Heterogeneous Causal Structure in Spatial Transcriptomics
studi.s: Spatial transcriptomics preserves the location of each expression profile, making it possible to study how gene regulatory networks differ within a tissue. Across regions of a tissue, regulatory relationships may vary and even reverse direction, so identifying the causal relationships in a specific pathological region can provide insight into therapeutic targets. We propose SpaDAG, a Bayesian method for learning spatially varying causal directed acyclic graphs.

studi.t: The Radar-based Activities of Daily Living (R-ADL) Dataset
studi.s: Monitoring Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) supports safety and well-being for people living at home, especially older adults, and radar sensing is gaining increasing attention in the field of activity recognition for its ability to ensure privacy in the home while also surpassing technical limitations of other sensing modalities. However, radar-based activity recognition remains constrained by the limited availability of large-scale datasets.

studi.t: Who decides the norms in TCS? Analysing the composition of the STOC 2027 committees and of the Simons Institute "AI+TCS" working group
studi.s: A working group organised by the Simons Institute released a report last September containing recommendations aiming to increase the usage of LLMs in theoretical computer science (TCS), including introducing them for communication and evaluation. Most of these recommendations were enacted by the STOC 2027 programme committee and the ACM SIGACT executive committee (as the steering committee of STOC). The composition of the Simons Institute working group is analysed along two axes: country of affiliation, and ties with industry (i.e. affiliated with or funded by).

studi.t: Worth the Wait? How Response Time and Streaming Shape Judgments of Generative AI Answers and Chatbot Engagement
studi.s: Answers from generative AI chatbots built on large language models (LLMs) now arrive at very different speeds: reasoning models deliberate before replying, while response caches can return a stored answer at once. Blind preference votes, which rank these models, are read as judgments of their text, and if delivery matters, faster answers are expected to gain. Research on the labor illusion and on how text appears on screen suggests instead that an answer which unfolds as it is written is credited over the same answer shown at once.

studi.t: Online V-Learning with Adaptive Longitudinal Data
studi.s: Reinforcement learning methods for estimating optimal dynamic treatment regimes are increasingly applied in mobile health (mHealth), where treatment decisions are made continually. Luckett et al. (2020) proposed V-learning, which estimates an optimal policy from offline trajectories. In practice, mHealth policies are updated online. Batch updating, in which the policy is re-estimated after each block of new data, is a tractable middle ground between offline learning and updating after every observation.

studi.t: One Style Fits All? Cultural Values Embedded in Conversational AI via a People-Pleasing Lens
studi.s: Conversational AI systems trained on large-scale web corpora inevitably encode the cultural values and interactional norms embedded in their training data, yet our understanding of how deployed LLMs reflect or reinforce culture-specific social expectations remains limited. This study examined how supportive versus challenging chatbot interaction styles shape user experience and continuance intention, and whether people-pleasing tendency (PPT) moderates these effects across cultures. Taiwanese (N = 49) and Korean (N = 52) participants completed a collaborative tourism-planning task.

studi.t: Generalizing Couple-Randomized Trials Under Limited Overlap and Missing Partner Linkage
studi.s: We study how to generalize couple-randomized trials when some couple types are absent from the trial and the target survey reports partner characteristics without linking spouses. Under an additive effect model with unrestricted partner-profile terms, the target average effect is identified exactly when the wife and husband margins assign equal mass to each connected component of the trial support graph. A specified interaction is identified when its alternating contrast around at least one cycle is nonzero.

studi.t: AI, Bias, and Inclusion: A Two-Phase Mixed-Methods Study of Gender Bias, Awareness, and Trust in Artificial Intelligence
studi.s: Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems are widespread across fields such as healthcare, finance, employment, and criminal justice, with a substantial impact on the lives of individuals and society. However, it has been established that AI systems perpetuate existing social inequalities, particularly through biases that are not easily discernible. Such biases are embedded in the technical and social structures of artificial intelligence systems, making them difficult to detect.

studi.t: Emerging International Best Practices for AI Model Specs
studi.s: Frontier AI developers from around the world have begun to publish documents that describe how their AI models are intended to behave. Although these 'model specifications'-or 'model specs', for short-are increasingly important in AI development and governance, little independent guidance exists for writing them. This paper addresses this gap in five main sections. First, we outline the advantages of writing a model spec for AI developers and society at large. Second, we introduce a taxonomy for model specs that developers can take inspiration from.

studi.t: Red-Teaming a Sovereign LLM, Its Reasoning and Its Training Stages
studi.s: Open-weight large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed for applications with sensitive information. We investigate whether confidentiality instructions in system prompt can protect such information. We red-team Apertus v1.5, an open sovereign LLM, and five other model families across six languages and reasoning modes. We use synthetic personal records to evaluate direct disclosure, correction baits, yes/no verification, derived-value queries, reasoning leakage and authorisation checks. We also explore copyright attribution, historical misrepresentation and stereotyping.

studi.t: Adaptive Multi-kernel Correntropy Kalman Filter: A Variational Bayesian Approach
studi.s: This paper proposes an adaptive multi-kernel correntropy Kalman filter (AMCKF) for robust state estimation in the presence of heavy-tailed measurement noises and outliers. The multi-kernel correntropy loss is reformulated via half-quadratic (HQ) duality into a quadratic form with auxiliary weights, enabling efficient Kalman-like recursions. We establish a rigorous variational Bayesian framework under the mean-field assumption, deriving closed-form coordinate ascent variational inference updates for joint state and kernel width estimation.

studi.t: Simultaneous Inference for Watermark Proportions in LLM-Generated Text
studi.s: Watermarking enables detection of text generated by large language models, but practical review also requires quantifying retained signals within content of interest. Readers may choose passages based on their content and refine their selections after examining the watermark evidence. We develop simultaneous lower confidence bounds on the fraction of selected tokens that retain a watermark signal. The bounds hold jointly for the full document and any passages selected during review.

studi.t: FoXSight: Facilitating Computational Hit Identification in Crystallographic Fragment Screening Experiments
studi.s: X-ray crystallographic fragment screening reveals how small molecules bind to proteins, providing important starting points for drug design. Identifying these weak binding events remains difficult when electron density signals are noisy, partially occupied or obscured by solvent, and campaigns may comprise thousands of datasets. Here, we present FoXSight, a computational method for hit identification in crystallographic compound screening.

studi.t: Structural basis for alpha-actinin inhibition of cofilin binding to actin filaments
studi.s: Actin is a conserved cytoskeletal protein essential for morphogenesis, motility, and division. Its versatility arises from filament assembly and regulation by actin binding proteins. Among these, alpha-actinin organizes filaments into bipolar or unipolar networks, whereas cofilin binds preferentially to ADP-actin regions and forms clusters to shorten the half helical pitch (HHP). Here, we investigated the molecular mechanism of how alpha-actinin alters filament and protomer conformations and influences cofilin binding.

studi.t: Spatial geometry of the Hypoxic niche predicts Radiotherapy failure in Colorectal Cancer: A Spatially Explicit Agent-Based Model
studi.s: Radiotherapy failure in locally advanced colorectal cancer is mechanistically linked to tumour microenvironmental heterogeneity, yet the spatial determinants of immune clearance following fractionated irradiation remain poorly understood. Here we present a spatially explicit hybrid agent-based model of colorectal cancer response to short-course radiotherapy in which cellular fate - proliferation, dormancy, or necrosis - is governed by local oxygen tension and ATP availability computed via Michaelis - Menten kinetics.

studi.t: Structure determination and dual targeting of a plant TACO1 identifies its ancient role as an organelle translation regulator
studi.s: Ribosome stalling caused by polyproline (PPs) motifs is common. Their translation is enhanced by accessory proteins such as YebC in bacteria, whose homolog, TRANSLATIONAL ACTIVATOR OF CYTOCHROME C OXIDASE 1 (TACO1), aids the translation of mitochondria-encoded proteins. The prevalence of PP motifs across plastid-encoded genes and their impact on the translation of photosynthesis-relevant proteins remains unexplored. Equally, a translation-enhancer of PP motifs equivalent to TACO1 for plastid ribosomes has not been reported.

studi.t: Differential DNA methylation and transcriptome revealed enhanced photosynthetic recovery and ROS modulation to promote cold tolerance in Oryza sativa L. ssp. indica.
studi.s: Indica rice, being a tropical crop, is highly sensitive to cold temperatures. Cold stress affects vegetative growth, photosynthetic efficiency and reproductive features. Screening diverse landraces to identify novel alleles associated with cold tolerance can be an approach to develop cold resilient indica rice. We have characterized a boro germplasm, CB1, with an efficient germination rate and growth vigor when treated with chilling temperatures. CB1 seedlings show a higher survival rate compared to IR36 when subjected to prolonged chilling stress.

studi.t: Two copy-number forms of the Kala4/OsB2 upstream duplication in purple rice revealed by a telomere-to-telomere genome of landrace ZN65
studi.s: Background: Black and purple pericarp in rice requires activation of the regulator Kala4/OsB2. The canonical black-rice allele is a promoter rearrangement that was described from DNA gel blots and amplified fragments, and its sequence is unavailable. Whether pigmented landraces carry one upstream structure or several is therefore unknown. We examined this region in the purple-pericarp landrace Mojiang ZN65 and its distribution in sequenced rice germplasm. Results: We assembled a gap-free telomere-to-telomere genome of ZN65 (395.1 Mb; all 24 telomeres).

studi.t: A sunflower FLS2 guides reconstruction of immune-evasive Xanthomonas flg22 recognition across divergent FLS2 backgrounds
studi.s: Immune-evasive Xanthomonas flg22 epitopes pose a challenge to FLS2-mediated immune surveillance. A further challenge is to reconstruct their recognition across divergent FLS2 backgrounds with a limited number of amino-acid substitutions. AlphaFold 3 (AF3) screening of 256 natural FLS2 homologues identified sunflower HaFLS2-1, responsive to flg22Xcc and flg22Xoo in transient ROS assays. We validated flg22Xcc recognition by in planta ligand-association assays and immune responses in stable Arabidopsis lines.

studi.t: Acetate promotes nutritional adaptation in Escherichia coli
studi.s: Escherichia coli often releases acetate in its environment where it can accumulate to concentrations high enough to inhibit the bacterium's own growth. Here, we demonstrate that acetate promotes E. coli adaptation to nutrient changes by accelerating growth resumption, with as little as 250 M acetate being sufficient to shorten the lag phase by several hours. Acetate was found to be consumed via acetyl-CoA synthetase very early after the nutrient change.

studi.t: Laterality of subcortical structures predicts spontaneous brain dynamics
studi.s: Subcortical structures contribute to neocortical activity through extensive circuits supporting cognition and behaviour. Although these anatomical connections are well established, how subcortical structure relates to neocortical oscillations remains poorly understood. Previous studies have linked subcortical volume asymmetries to cortical alpha modulation during attention tasks, but whether these relationships extend to spontaneous brain activity remains unclear.

studi.t: Individual neurons in monkey sensory and prefrontal cortices contribute to both working memory maintenance and readout
studi.s: Despite extensive research, the neural implementation of working memory, from information maintenance to readout that guides behavior, remains elusive. We provide direct evidence that neurons in auditory and prefrontal cortices of monkeys maintain tone-specific information via persistent changes in spiking during the memory delay. Crucially, during the subsequent readout phase, these same memory neurons transition to reflect behavioral decisions of the monkeys, demonstrating a direct role in translating maintained information into action.

studi.t: MicroRNA spatial profiling for assessing drug efficacy in BRCA1-related triple-negative breast tumors
studi.s: BRCA1/2-mutated breast cancers exhibit homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) and are initially sensitive to poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitors, but 40-70% of patients develop resistance, creating a need for predictive biomarkers that capture treatment-associated spatial heterogeneity. Using the K14-Cre Brca1f/fTrp53f/f model with tumors that acquired PARP inhibitor resistance, we evaluated PARP inhibitor combinations with either PI3K inhibition or Poly(I:C) in vivo.

studi.t: XSSDense: X-ray Solution Scattering Density Reconstruction Using a Variational Autoencoder
studi.s: Solution X-ray scattering reveals the structure of biomolecules in solution. Scattering profiles also encode information on conformational heterogeneity and, when measured with time resolution, transient structural intermediates. However, this information is difficult to access because scattering profiles contain limited information, and their interpretation largely relies on fitting candidate structures guided by prior knowledge. Direct reconstruction of electron densities has remained challenging because of the difficulty of incorporating such priors.

studi.t: A Minimally Perturbative DARPin Probe for Quantitative Fluorescence Imaging of the Human TCR-CD3 Complex
studi.s: Fluorescence microscopy is a powerful tool for dissecting the molecular mechanisms of T-cell antigen recognition in living cells, but its quantitative insight critically depends on non-perturbative, high-quality probes. Here, we repurpose a small (~15 kDa) CD3epsilon-binding DARPin (designed ankyrin repeat proteins) to a fluorescent label for T-cell receptor (TCR)/CD3 complexes on primary human CD8+ T-cells, with the aim of generating a powerful tool for quantitative analysis, single-molecule tracking, and advanced imaging of TCR dynamics.

studi.t: Population-scale immunoglobulin genomics links inherited variation to antibody repertoire organization
studi.s: Human antibody repertoires emerge from inherited immunoglobulin variation interacting with V(D)J recombination and selection, yet how population-level germline diversity contributes to repertoire organization remains incompletely understood.
