We integrated long-read genomic data across the IGH, IGK, and IGL loci from 871 individuals, including 172 individuals with matched antibody repertoire sequencing. We identify extensive previously unrepresented genetic diversity and show that coding variation is embedded within a smaller set of recurrent RSS and leader sequence architectures.

studi.t: Identifying a cooperative catalytic network for efficient esterase catalysis
studi.s: Efficient catalysis is hard to engineer because sequence comparisons reveal only a handful of conserved catalytic residues, and single substitutions rarely speed up catalysis. We hypothesize that efficient catalysis requires a cooperative catalytic network of residues enabling the physical and chemical steps that together determine kcat. In ancestral hydroxynitrile lyase HNL1, an /{beta}-hydrolase with poor esterase activity, we identified such a network.

studi.t: Delta rhythm and voice familiarity organize neural entrainment in the infant brain
studi.s: Delta-range rhythms (~0.5-3.5 Hz) are a phylogenetically conserved tempo of biological communication, yet how the infant brain tracks them remains poorly understood. Thirty 6-month-olds heard syllable sequences produced by their mother or a stranger at a delta (2 Hz) or theta (4 Hz) rate, or at irregular intervals, while high-density EEG was recorded. Rhythmic sequences, at both rates, increased low-frequency power over frontotemporal sites.

studi.t: CA19-9-associated transcriptional programs in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma are linked to survival and drug sensitivity
studi.s: Pancreatic cancer contains diverse cancer-cell states that complicate treatment selection. We asked whether targeted transcriptomics of glycan-defined PDAC cells would reveal novel and clinically informative subtypes. Spatial profiling of CA19-9-positive regions from 3 tumors with divergent clinical outcomes identified four transcriptional programs: inflammation and tissue remodeling (Cluster 1), proliferation (Cluster 2), antigen presentation and differentiation (Cluster 3), and protein synthesis (Cluster 4).

studi.t: The use of cultured symbionts enhances the survival of reef-deployed coral recruits
studi.s: Introduction: Symbiodiniaceae dinoflagellates are essential for coral juvenile development and survival, yet early-life symbiont provisioning remains underused in coral restoration. Objectives: We tested whether inoculating sexually propagated Acropora spathulata recruits with cultured symbionts before reef deployment improves survival and shapes symbiont community composition. Methods: Recruits inoculated with cultured Cladocopium sp. (C1) or Durusdinium trenchii (D1), and uninoculated recruits (Control) were deployed on the central Great Barrier Reef.

studi.t: Apple floral attractants function across the 24-hour cycle to support potential diurnal and nocturnal pollinators
studi.s: Pollination in apple (Malus domestica Borkh.) is typically attributed to diurnal bees, yet nocturnal insects also contribute to fruit set. To assess whether apple flowers recruit potential pollinators throughout the 24-hour cycle, we quantified diel patterns in floral attractants and insect visitation in an orchard in Northwest Arkansas, United States. We measured nectar and volatiles and used a combination of visual surveys, light traps, and video recordings to assess insect abundance and floral visitation while controlling for weather conditions.

studi.t: Historical overestimated abundance of a Critically Endangered species: the case of the tamaraw (Bubalus mindorensis) of Mindoro Island
studi.s: Population abundance is a central parameter in conservation, for which biased estimates can seriously undermine management strategies for threatened species. The tamaraw (Bubalus mindorensis) is a Critically Endangered large herbivore endemic to Mindoro Island, Philippines. The species has been monitored annually at Mounts Iglit-Baco Natural Park (MIBNP) since 2000 using a multi-vantage-point count method that is prone to both imperfect detection and repeated counting of the same individuals across sessions.

studi.t: No evidence of evolution of male fitness components in response to yeast deprivation: Putative female specific nutrient dependent reproductive adaptation
studi.s: Intersexual genetic correlation (IGC) is pervasive in sexually reproducing organisms and can constrain sex-specific adaptive evolution. Nevertheless, sexes frequently undergo adaptive divergence in response to novel ecological challenges. Here, we investigated whether adaptation to nutritional stress is sex-limited or constrained by shared genetic architecture.

studi.t: Diversity of Environmental and Genome-Associated Eukaryotic Circular Rep-Encoding Single-Stranded DNA Viruses
studi.s: Circular Rep-encoding single-stranded (CRESS) DNA viruses are widespread across diverse environments, yet their genomic diversity, evolutionary relationships, and associations with eukaryotic hosts remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the evolutionary diversity of CRESS DNA viruses by integrating replication-associated protein (Rep) sequences from environmental viral metagenomes, publicly available viral references, and endogenous viral elements (EVEs) identified in fungal and algal genomes.

studi.t: Pharmacogenomic diversity at tuberculosis-treatment loci across African populations: phased haplotypes, regulatory architecture and NAT2 acetylator inference
studi.s: Background: Tuberculosis imposes a major public-health burden in Africa, while variation in isoniazid and rifampicin disposition creates opportunities for improved pharmacotherapy. The population architecture of extended, phased pharmacogenomic backgrounds remains less well characterized than individual marker frequencies. Methods: We analyzed high-coverage, phased GRCh38 genomes from 661 unrelated individuals sampled from five continental-African and two African-diaspora populations at NAT2, SLCO1B1, CES2, HLA-B, NR1I2 and UGT1A1.

studi.t: Divergent immune trajectories distinguish resistance and susceptibility to bacterial leaf streak in wheat
studi.s: Bacterial leaf streak (BLS) is an increasingly important disease affecting several cereal crops. The mechanisms linking quantitative trait loci for resistance to downstream immune response against BLS in wheat remain poorly understood. Here, we developed a chromosome-scale genome assembly of the BLS resistant cultivar Boost. With de novo annotation of Boost and Timstein (susceptible cultivar) assemblies, we established a cultivar-resolved framework for dissecting BLS resistance.

studi.t: FiberTron enables regulatory variant effect prediction and testing from multi-omic long reads of a single sample
studi.s: State-of-the-art sequence-to-function models are trained on large compendia of public data to predict regulatory activity across hundreds of cell types. However, they are not designed to interpret individual genomes, effects in under-sampled cell types, or provide a comprehensive view of how genetic variation influences complex diseases. Here we show that a single sample profiled with Fiber-seq and Nanopore direct RNA-seq contains enough information to train such a model from scratch.

studi.t: Effective control of treadmilling filaments by plus-end capping
studi.s: Bacterial cell division depends on the tubulin homolog FtsZ, which assembles into a membrane-bound cytokinetic Z-ring. FtsZ filaments treadmill, growing at one end and shrinking at the other, and many regulatory proteins control where and when the Z-ring forms. Whether treadmilling itself confers a regulatory advantage, and how inhibitors exploit it, has remained unclear. Here we show that the Escherichia coli nucleoid occlusion factor SlmA caps the growing ends of treadmilling FtsZ filaments, converting steady-state subunit turnover into net filament shrinkage.

studi.t: Albumin alleviates pressure overload-induced heart failure by improving mitochondrial homeostasis via PKA-LKB1-AMPK axis
studi.s: Aims Heart failure (HF) is a global health challenge due to its high incidence, mortality, and socioeconomic burden. Despite medical advancements, HF prognosis remains poor, highlighting the need for enhanced understanding and treatment strategies. Serum albumin, a key circulatory protein, has gained attention as a biomarker in cardiovascular diseases. Low serum albumin levels are linked to HF incidence, progression, and prognosis, suggesting its regulatory role, though mechanisms remain unclear.

studi.t: Rigid granular scaffolds reveal transcriptional responses to cellular confinement
studi.s: A large variety of cells migrate through confined spaces in vivo, where mechanical confinement influences their fate and function. However, existing in vitro confinement models are low-throughput, limiting discovery of confinement-responsive genes and recovery of confined cells. Here, we present non-annealed glass microparticle scaffolds (GlaMS) as a scalable, high-throughput 3D confinement system with interconnected voids that mimic physiological confinement while enabling efficient cell retrieval.

studi.t: Engineering Bacteriophages to Overcome Complement-Mediated Neutralization
studi.s: Bacteriophages (phages) are promising alternatives to antibiotics for treating antibiotic-resistant infections, but their clinical durability is limited by the host immune response against phages. Using phage T4 as a model and both C1q-KO and C3-deficient mice, we show that antibody recognition of phages triggers complement-dependent neutralization and clearance of phage particles in vivo. To mitigate this complement-mediated clearance, we engineer phages to display the complement-modulating Factor H binding peptide, a phage we call T4-FactorH.BP.

studi.t: Biophysics-informed generative models improve activity and thermostability of designed ribozymes
studi.s: Generative models of biological sequences can produce molecules that fold and function similarly to natural ones. A further challenge is to steer generation toward a desired property, such as resistance to high temperature. This is particularly difficult when available sequence data are limited, and typically requires probing thousands of variants experimentally, either through directed evolution or to retrain a model specialized to the targeted property. Ideally, however, one would avoid such an expensive experimental step.

studi.t: Beyond screens: a gaze-driven auditory human-computer interface
studi.s: Brain-computer interfaces enable humans to communicate and manipulate external devices by converting physiological signals into actions. These signals often have a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) too low to enable their use in real-world Human-Computer Interaction (HCI). Notably, electrooculography (EOG) measurements of gaze direction exhibit a higher SNR, making them widely employed in HCI applications with displays. Nevertheless, display-free paradigms can also leverage the high SNR of EOG measurements of eye gaze.

studi.t: A Two-Stage YOLO-Swin Transformer Pipeline for Cross-Dataset White Blood Cell Classification
studi.s: Background: White blood cell (WBC) classification across datasets is challenged by differences in staining, image context, and class distributions. Methods: We developed a two-stage YOLO11-Swin Transformer pipeline. In the first stage, WBC detection and context-preserving cropping, a YOLO11 detector finds the leukocyte in each uncropped image and produces a cell-focused crop that retains the surrounding background. In the second stage, WBC classification, a Swin Transformer (Swin-B) assigns the crop to one of nine cell types.

studi.t: WildTrust-UAV: uncertainty-aware wildlife detection with privacy-preserving spatial disclosure and verifiable inference provenance
studi.s: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery has made wildlife surveys faster and safer, but a detected animal is not yet a conservation record. Detector confidence scores are often poorly calibrated, exact coordinates of threatened species can expose them to harm, and an observation is rarely tied back to the image, model, and settings that produced it. WildTrust-UAV addresses these three problems in one framework.

studi.t: CheekAI: An explainable, deep learning epigenetic aging clock based on lifestyle and health epigenetic biomarker proxies
studi.s: The human methylome is poorly understood and, as such, the vast majority of epigenetic aging clocks are unexplainable black boxes. To address this, we created CheekAI, a robust deep learning model that uses lifestyle and health epigenetic biomarker proxies (EBPs) to predict age. Trained using a longitudinal dataset of 25,400 adult buccal DNA methylation samples derived from 14,716 distinct adults, we used principal components and multi-objective optimization to produce a clock that is explainable, reproducible, responsive, and accurate.

studi.t: Local wavefront alignment with corrected free-end penalty
studi.s: Background: Pairwise alignment of nucleotide and protein sequences is a fundamental problem in bioinformatics. Wavefront alignment (WFA) is a groundbreaking algorithmic advance that reduces the time complexity of exact (semi-)global pairwise alignment with affine gap penalties from O(N2) to O(sN). Despite its success, WFA has yet to be extended to the local sequence alignment scope. Results: In this work, we propose a local wavefront alignment (lWFA) which generalizes WFA to the local alignment scope and preserves both the O(sN) time and the O(sN) to O(s2) space complexity.

studi.t: BiocPy: A Framework for Cross-Platform Genomic Data andMethods Interoperability
studi.s: Bioconductor provides standardized data structures and statistical methods for high-throughput genomic analysis in R, whereas Python has become a primary environment for machine learning, image analysis, and general-purpose data science. Combining tools across both ecosystems often requires ad-hoc file conversions or embedded language runtimes that can lose metadata, introduce maintenance overhead, or lead to subtle differences in downstream results.

studi.t: An AI agent guides a pipeline for selective protein interaction inhibitors from discovery across targets to preclinical evaluation
studi.s: A protein can engage multiple partners, making it challenging to disrupt disease-associated interactions while preserving others. We developed Bivexia, an AI agent that guides a multistage pipeline from discovery and de novo design through preclinical evaluation. Its decision rules are fixed in advance, and each prospective selection by the agent is cryptographically committed before testing. The objective is to discover small molecules that disrupt specified interactions of a target protein while preserving others.

studi.t: Convergence of Independently Established Oncogenes in a Combined Breast and Ovarian Cancer Model: Hub Gene Validation and identification of potential Food-Derived therapeutics.
studi.s: Breast and ovarian cancers share molecular alterations that may reveal common therapeutic targets. Here, we integrated six Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) datasets to identify shared transcriptional changes across the two cancers. Independent differential expression analysis followed by direction-specific intersection identified 396 shared differentially expressed genes (DEGs), comprising 192 upregulated and 204 downregulated genes. Protein-protein interaction analysis prioritized ten hub genes: AURKA, AURKB, BCL2, BIRC5, CCNA2, CDK1, FOXO1, KIF11, PTEN, and TOP2A.

studi.t: GlycanPUG: WURCS-Based Heterogeneous Graph Pretraining for Structurally Ambiguous Glycans
studi.s: Background: Glycans orchestrate diverse biological processes, yet they remain underrepresented in computational biology compared to proteins and nucleic acids. Although WURCS 2.0 provides a machine-readable structural representation that preserves uncertainty, the evaluated IUPAC-based deterministic workflow processes 43.1% of the GlyCosmos-derived cohort examined here, motivating approaches that retain structural ambiguity. Methods: To overcome this limitation, GlycanPUG (Probabilistic Uncertainty-aware Graph) was introduced as a pretrained graph model for glycan representation learning.

studi.t: Structural clustering of paired αβ T-cell receptor repertoires recovers antigen-specific convergence beyond sequence similarity
studi.s: T-cell receptor (TCR) antigen recognition depends on the three-dimensional geometry of the paired {beta} complementarity-determining regions (CDRs), which primary sequence does not fully capture. Most repertoire-clustering methods group receptors by CDR3 motifs, sequence distance or V-J gene usage, and may miss receptors that differ in sequence but adopt similar loop conformations.

studi.t: Confidence-guided spatial gene expression inference for reliability-aware prognostic analysis from histology
studi.s: Inferring spatial gene expression from histology images offers a promising strategy for extending spatial molecular profiling to large-scale clinical tissue archives. However, existing approaches face two major challenges: limited generalizability of single-cell expression inference across datasets and platforms, and the lack of reliable estimates of prediction uncertainty, which compromise downstream biological and clinical analyses. Here, we present REGAIN, a framework for spatial gene expression inference at both single-cell and spot resolutions with prediction confidence.

studi.t: Evaluating the Nanopore Inosine Model for ADAR-Dependent A-to-I RNA Editing Detection
studi.s: Oxford Nanopore direct RNA sequencing (dRNA-seq) reads native RNA molecules, and its basecaller now includes models that detect RNA modifications directly, among them inosine, the product of adenosine-to-inosine (A-to-I) editing by ADAR enzymes. These models are increasingly used, but how reliably they detect modifications in biological samples has rarely been tested. We evaluated the Dorado inosine model in a mouse macrophage cell line, comparing wild-type cells with ADAR1-knockout cells and in vitro transcribed RNA, before and after an inflammatory stimulus that increases editing.

studi.t: To sort or to hash? Revisiting k-mer counting
studi.s: Motivation: Counting k-mers in large genomic datasets is a foundational primitive in bioinformatics, supporting applications such as genome assembly, variant discovery, metagenomic profiling, and sequence database indexing. As sequencing throughput grows, k-mer counting is routinely applied to collections of hundreds to thousands of files. Even a modest per-file speedup compounds into hours of saved computation across such collections.

studi.t: Disentangling within-cell-type heterogeneity from transcript contamination in imaging-based spatial transcriptomics
studi.s: Recent advances in imaging-based spatial transcriptomics have enabled high-resolution characterization of gene expression and cellular organization in situ. Resolving within-cell-type heterogeneity is essential for understanding how cellular states relate to tissue function and disease. However, imperfect cell segmentation and RNA spillover can contaminate cell-level expression profiles, obscuring intrinsic expression patterns and generating spurious variation.

studi.t: Multi-omics causal deep learning reveals regulatory structure while interventions refine perturbation predictions
studi.s: Inferring gene regulation from single-cell data is difficult because observational measurements cannot distinguish correlation from causation and access to perturbational data, especially with multiple modalities, remains limited. Here we present the Cross-Modal Causal Variational Autoencoder (CMC-VAE), which learns a network linking genes and proteins (gene-gene, protein-protein and gene-protein) in the latent space and maps each connection back onto measured features.

studi.t: PathwayTheme: identifying and attributing pathway-level axes of variation in omics data
studi.s: Exploring gene expression datasets often involves delineating principal axes of variation corresponding to either biological or technical variables. Principal component analysis (PCA) is typically employed as it uses all genes, reflecting global relationships between samples. Existing tools decompose gene expression first and interpret components afterwards.

studi.t: Deciphering Molecular Language for Spectral Interpretation with a Foundation Model Pretrained on Repository-Wide Metabolomics Data
studi.s: In-depth, scalable structural interpretation of tandem mass spectra from diverse biological tissues and environmental samples is essential for understanding the molecular diversity of cellular environments and the metabolic architecture of living systems. Although community-driven resources such as GNPS and MassIVE have aggregated massive volumes of tandem mass spectra spanning a wide range of organisms, clinical cohorts and environmental surveys, modeling and interpreting this exponentially expanding spectral corpus to distill molecular information and derive meaningful biological insights…

studi.t: Measuring Cell Type Resolved Aging Through Long-Read Sequencing
studi.s: Epigenetic clocks based on bulk blood DNA methylation are powerful tools for quantifying biological aging, but bulk measurements conflate cell-autonomous epigenetic changes with age-related shifts in blood cell composition. Here, we develop LongReadClock, a set of cell-type-resolved epigenetic aging clocks constructed from cohort-scale long-read whole-genome sequencing of bulk blood without physical cell sorting. Individual sequencing reads were classified using seven target-specific blood-cell models using methylation-based log-likelihood-ratio scoring against a purified-cell atlas.

studi.t: Red-light-catalyzed photolipid switching enables leaflet-selective control of membrane mechanics
studi.s: Azobenzene photolipids are versatile actuators of membrane mechanics and protein function, yet long-wavelength control and leaflet-selective perturbations remain difficult to impose. Here, we address both limitations. First, we confirm that red-light excitation of a lipidated Nile Blue derivative (NB-lipid) catalyzes rapid cis[->]trans photoisomerization of co-localized azobenzene photolipids in planar bilayers without requiring covalent conjugation.

studi.t: EM-Claw: An Experience-Grounded Language-Model Agent for Auto Cryo-EM Single-Particle Analysis
studi.s: Single-particle cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) processing remains strongly dependent on expert judgement because difficult specimens often require dataset-specific strategies that cannot be captured by a fixed pipeline. Here we present EM-Claw, an experience-grounded multi-agent system for adaptive cryo-EM single-particle analysis.

studi.t: Determination of both global and local protein stability in complex environments with X-ray hydroxyl radical footprinting
studi.s: Protein thermodynamic stability is a major determinant of cellular function, yet traditional methods for determining protein stability require large quantities of pure protein under idealized conditions. Here, we overcome this challenge by combining X-ray hydroxyl radical footprinting monitored by mass spectrometry (XF-MS) with chemical denaturation, to accurately measure protein thermodynamic stability. We demonstrate that XF-MS quantitatively reproduces known stability values using ~500-fold less protein than traditional spectroscopic approaches such as circular dichroism.

studi.t: Hour-long live-cell TIRF imaging of GFP-talin at ensemble and single-molecule level with low-duty-cycle picosecond supercontinuum excitation
studi.s: Photobleaching and phototoxicity limit how long living cells can be followed by total internal reflection fluorescence (TIRF) microscopy. We describe an objective-type TIRF microscope illuminated by a picosecond supercontinuum laser spectrally windowed to 20-nm bands, pulse-picked to 1 MHz and delivered through two TIRF illuminators, one per polarisation direction.

studi.t: Automated Transcription Factor Cluster Analysis Toolkit (ATAT)
studi.s: Many nuclear regulatory proteins, including transcription factors (TFs) form clusters often referred to as hubs or condensates. These clusters vary widely in their enrichment, size, and persistence, yet tools for quantifying these properties are typically developed for individual datasets. Here, we present the Automated TF Cluster Analysis Toolkit (ATAT), a Python-based toolkit for quantifying TF clustering in four-dimensional fluorescence microscopy data.

studi.t: CIP2A is a biomarker for progression and poor prognosis in cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma
studi.s: The incidence of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) is rising worldwide, highlighting the need for novel therapeutic options for recurrent and metastatic disease. Protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A) is a keyt tumor suppressor, and its inhibition promotes malignant progression. Here, we investigated the role of the cancerous inhibitor of PP2A (CIP2A) in cSCC progression. RNA-sequencing, oligonucleotide array-based expression, and qRT-PCR analysis demonstrated elevated CIP2A mRNA levels in cSCC cells compared with normal human epidermal keratinocytes (NHEKs).

studi.t: A hidden mitotic vulnerability emerges from BCAT1 redox-motif disruption in Ewing sarcoma
studi.s: Cancer cells must keep oxidative stress and chromosome-segregation errors within tolerable limits to sustain rapid proliferation. Because redox homeostasis supports faithful chromosome segregation, disrupting redox-dependent mitotic safeguards could drive chromosomal instability (CIN) beyond cell tolerance and suppress tumor growth. Here, we investigated whether selectively disrupting redox-dependent safeguards could uncouple oxidative-stress adaptation from faithful chromosome segregation, exposing a therapeutic vulnerability at the interface of metabolic regulation and genome maintenance.

studi.t: Androgen Receptor and ACSL4 Interplay as Therapeutic Targets in Breast Cancer
studi.s: High Acyl-CoA synthetase 4 (ACSL4) expression is implicated in the development and progression of aggressive tumors, poor prognosis, and unfavorable clinical outcomes, as observed in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). The androgen receptor (AR) has emerged as a therapeutic target in AR-positive TNBCs, while treatment options are even more limited for quadruple-negative breast cancer (QNBC), the AR-negative TNBC subtype. This study investigates the reciprocal regulation between AR and ACSL4 and evaluates their potential as therapeutic targets in breast cancer.

studi.t: Glycogen fuels and spatially regulates nucleotide biosynthesis in cancer
studi.s: Cancer cells must coordinate metabolic substrate availability with the organization of biosynthetic pathways to sustain proliferation. Glycogen accumulates in many cancers, but its function extends beyond glucose storage. Here, we show that glycogen regulates nucleotide biosynthesis through distinct metabolic and spatial mechanisms. Disrupting glycogenolysis impairs tumor growth and mitochondrial pyruvate oxidation, compromises NADPH homeostasis, and selectively reduces glutamine utilization for reductive biosynthesis.

studi.t: DYRK1A inhibition by the postbiotic metabolite Urolithin A contributes to enhanced β-cell function: Structural, Biochemical and Cellular Evidence
studi.s: Urolithin A (UA), a postbiotic metabolite of ellagitannins (ETs), has shown potential in modulating metabolic disorders but the mechanisms underlying these activities remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigate the influence of UA on {beta}-cell function and assess the role of dual-specificity tyrosine-regulated kinase 1A (DYRK1A) inhibition in mediating these effects. We develop a novel transition-metal-free synthesis of UA employing a one-pot triple Baeyer-Villiger oxidation.

studi.t: Oral Silver Nanoparticle Exposure Increases Phosphorylated Tau Protein and Antioxidant Expression in Dentate Gyrus of Rat Brain
studi.s: Silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) are incorporated into products including toys, cosmetics, and surgical tools due to their antimicrobial properties. AgNPs can cross the blood-brain barrier and bioaccumulate in the brain, persisting for months with no clearance. We previously found that AgNPs disrupt the f-actin cytoskeleton, induce neurite collapse, and disrupt cytoskeletal regulatory pathways in cultured neural cells.

studi.t: CLOVER: Chemical-gene LLM benchmark for obtaining valid entity relationships for the Comparative Toxicogenomics Database (CTD)
studi.s: Objective: The Comparative Toxicogenomics Database (CTD) provides expert-curated chemical-gene interactions about environmental exposure effects on human diseases. Existing automated relation extraction systems are typically restricted to 3-10 interaction types and operate on abstracts only. We introduce CLOVER, a systematic benchmark for evaluating large language models (LLMs) on full-text chemical-gene interaction extraction using CTD-defined chemical-gene interaction terminology.

studi.t: A scalable method for preparation and long-term preservation of tea leaf plant-derived vesicles in tissue regeneration and drug encapsulation
studi.s: Plant-derived vesicles (PDVs) are emerging as sustainable nanotherapeutic platforms, although challenges regarding isolation, scalability, biological activity, drug loading, and storage stability hinder their biomedical translation. This study aimed to optimize PDV production, exploring different sources to assess the one with greater translation potential, in terms of for yield and purity.

studi.t: Photorespiration mediates plant carbon-nitrogen coordination
studi.s: Plant species differ widely in their sensitivity to ammonium, and legumes are generally more sensitive than cereals, yet the mechanisms behind this difference remain unclear. Photorespiration links photosynthetic carbon assimilation with nitrogen metabolism, but its response to nitrogen form has rarely been compared between species.

studi.t: Comparative Metabolomics and Lipidomics Reveal Selective Fatty Acyl Partitioning and Metabolic Reorganization Associated with Long-Term Cold Adaptation in Euphausia superba
studi.s: Antarctic krill (Euphausia superba) inhabits the persistently cold waters of the Southern Ocean, where lipid metabolism supports membrane function and energy storage. Despite extensive characterization of euphausiid lipid classes and bulk fatty acids, fatty acyl organization across lipid pools remains poorly understood. We integrated untargeted metabolomics and lipidomics to compare whole-body biochemical profiles of E. superba and its congener E. triacantha.

studi.t: Zeaxanthin-dependent rapid energy quenching uncovers complexity of PsbS protonation
studi.s: Rapid responses to changes in light intensity are crucial for photosynthetic organisms to regulate their light-harvesting capacity and optimize growth. PsbS, the S subunit of photosystem II (PSII) located in the thylakoid membrane, senses lumenal pH changes that reflect the balance between the light and carbon reactions of photosynthesis. Upon lumenal acidification caused by absorption of excess light energy, PsbS undergoes protonation of its lumen-exposed domain, triggering energy-dependent quenching (qE), which dissipates excess energy as heat.

studi.t: Imaging photosynthetic pH dynamics in living plants and algae
studi.s: Photosynthetic light reactions generate a proton motive force across the thylakoid membrane, composed of a pH gradient ({Delta}pH) and an electric potential ({Delta}{psi}). However, non-invasive dynamic tracking of the pH gradient across chloroplast sub-compartments has remained technically challenging in vivo. Here, we systematically evaluated four genetically encoded pH biosensors, cpYFP, pHGFP, Lime and pHluorin2, in vitro and in planta to provide a versatile pH-sensing toolbox.

studi.t: The NAC38-NAC58-FUSCA3 module regulates outer integument differentiation in the seed coat of Arabidopsis thaliana
studi.s: The seed coat protects the embryo from environmental stresses while controlling important agricultural traits, such as seed dormancy, germination, and longevity. The Arabidopsis seed coat epidermal layer secretes a pectin-rich cell wall, the mucilage, which regulates seed hydration and germination. In the subepidermal layer, the lipid polyester suberin is deposited in the cell wall, where it forms a protective barrier against solutes and gases. Currently, the mechanisms coordinating the development of these important cell layers of the outer integument are poorly understood.

studi.t: Ardisia tchimbele sp. nov. (Primulaceae) - A Critically Endangered forest shrub, and notes on the Crystal Mountains of Gabon
studi.s: Ardisia tchimbele sp. nov. (Primulaceae) an erect, branching shrub, is described from the forests downstream of Tchimbele, a hydroelectric installation in the Crystal Mountains, Gabon that supplies Libreville, the capital with energy. The new species is based on three specimens collected in the 1980s and 1990s. It keys out and has similarities with a taxon informally described in 1979 by Taton as Ardisia sp. 1, also from the Crystal Mts and which is slightly discordant morphologically.

studi.t: Real-world longitudinal multi-omics separates weight-loss-associated responses to incretin agonists from a broader response not dependent on weight loss
studi.s: The benefits of incretin agonists, including glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonists, are largely attributed to glycemic control and weight loss, as these therapies enhance insulin secretion, suppress glucagon release and delay gastric emptying to produce satiety. Yet treatment is also associated with lower risk of cardiometabolic, renal and other chronic diseases.

studi.t: An information theoretic approach to evaluating social behaviour in mice using automated home-cage monitoring
studi.s: Background: Social behaviour in mice is commonly assessed using standardized assays such as the three-chambered task, which provide controlled measures of sociability but often capture behaviour over short timeframes that may not capture the complex behavioural repertoire exhibited in the home environment. Although automated home-cage monitoring enables continuous, longitudinal assessment of group-housed mice with minimal human interference, methods for quantifying social behaviour in this complex setting remain limited.

studi.t: Correction for age-appropriate relaxation reference values alters estimates of neurometabolite concentration, but not age relationships
studi.s: MRS-measured metabolite concentration estimates in the brain show significant changes over the lifespan. An important step in accurately quantifying metabolite levels using in vivo MRS is correction for T1- and T2- weighting of water and metabolite signals. Despite substantial literature indicating that both T1 and T2 of water and metabolites change across the lifespan, most aging studies use age-invariant reference values in quantification equations. It is important to establish whether observed changes in metabolite levels are driven by relaxation effects or actual concentration changes.

studi.t: Sex differences in the effects of enhanced adult hippocampal neurogenesis on pattern discrimination and Intellicage spatial learning in Bax-knockout mice
studi.s: Adult hippocampal neurogenesis has been implicated in learning and memory. Although increasing neurogenesis has been associated with improved spatial learning and pattern discrimination, whether these benefits differ between male and female mice remains unclear. The goal of this study was to see if increasing adult hippocampal neurogenesis improves learning in male and female mice, and whether the benefit is the same in both sexes. We used conditional deletion of the pro-apoptotic gene Bax to increase the survival of newborn dentate granule cells.

studi.t: Sympathetic-to-microglia readouts in human brain single-nucleus data: sparse adrenergic receptor detection and age-associated homeostatic-to-inflammatory shifts in hippocampal microglia
studi.s: Stellate ganglion block (SGB) improves sleep in clinical populations, yet the mechanisms linking sympathetic activity to human microglial states remain untested. A prerequisite is to establish what sympathetic signaling readouts exist in human microglia and whether state composition changes in a disease-relevant physiological dimension.

studi.t: Target- and network-specific downstream effects of personalized precision transcranial magnetic stimulation: Evidence from concurrent functional neuroimaging
studi.s: Background: Personalized targeting of transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) based on functional connectivity (FC) to the subgenual anterior cingulate cortex (sgACC) is promising for depression treatment, but direct evidence that precisely engaging an individually defined FC target produces specific downstream modulation is lacking. Objective: To test whether stimulating individually defined cortical targets with strong negative or positive FC to sgACC/ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC) produces target- and network-specific downstream BOLD effects compared to nearby control targets.

studi.t: Hierarchical control of visual perceptual learning with model-synthesized stimuli
studi.s: Visual perceptual decisions depend on both how the visual system represents the stimuli and how those representations are read out to guide perception and behavior. Improved visual perception through training, a phenomenon known as Visual Perceptual Learning (VPL), has been partly attributed to adjustments of the readout weights across visual areas to reach better decisions.

studi.t: Novel Stable 5-OP-RU Analogs Activate Human MAIT Cells and Promote Cytotoxic Antitumor Function
studi.s: Mucosal-associated invariant T (MAIT) cells are abundant innate-like T lymphocytes that recognize microbial vitamin B2-derived metabolites presented by MR1 and play pivotal roles in infection, autoimmunity, and cancer. Pharmacologic activation with 5-OP-RU, 5-(2 oxopropylideneamino)-D-ribityl-aminouracil potently stimulates MAIT cells and elicits antitumor immune responses, but its intrinsic chemical instability limits therapeutic development. Here, we designed and evaluated novel synthetic 5-OP-RU analogs to improve stability and assess their potential for MAIT directed anti-tumor immunity.

studi.t: DNA Methyltransferase Inhibition During CAR T-cell Manufacturing Enhances Antitumor Activity in Immunocompetent Brain and Ovarian Cancer Models
studi.s: Limited persistence and progressive dysfunction remain major barriers to effective CAR T-cell therapy for solid tumors. Epigenetic regulation, particularly DNA methylation, can reinforce dysfunctional T-cell programs by restricting expression of genes required for sustained effector function. CAR T-cell manufacturing provides an opportunity to pharmacologically prime CAR T-cells prior to infusion without additional treatment burden.

studi.t: Distinct monocyte replenishment kinetics of macrophages at the oral barrier restrict early-life bacterial colonisation
studi.s: Resident tissue macrophages (RTMs) support tissue integrity and homeostasis. However, RTM in the gingiva, the mucosal barrier surrounding the teeth and the site of the prevalent inflammatory disease periodontitis, remain minimally explored. The gingiva experiences a unique combination of challenges, it is continuously exposed to both microbial stimuli and mastication-induced tissue damage; RTM could provide barrier reinforcement against both these challenges. Here we outline that no long-lived macrophage population could be identified within the gingiva.

studi.t: A B-cell-cardiac autoantibody-complement axis contributes to myocarditis induced by checkpoint blockade and cardiac irradiation
studi.s: Thoracic radiotherapy and immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) improve outcomes in locally advanced lung cancer but can cause cardiac toxicity. The mechanisms by which radiation-associated cardiac injury develops into autoimmune myocarditis during ICI therapy remain incompletely defined. Using autoimmune-prone A/J mice, we investigated whether cardiac irradiation (CIR) promotes a B-cell-cardiac autoantibody-complement axis during dual PD-1 and CTLA-4 blockade. Dual ICIs plus CIR increased the incidence of myocarditis to 76.2% and cardiac fibrosis to 69.0%.

studi.t: Intradermal and intranasal vaccination with microparticulated ASFV proteins induces distinct immune profiles in pigs
studi.s: African Swine Fever (ASF) is a major threat to the swine industry due to its severe socioeconomic impact and the lack of safe and effective vaccines. Although live attenuated vaccines (LAVs) can induce robust immunity, biosafety concerns restrict their use, making subunit vaccines the preferred alternative. In this context, understanding how vaccination routes modulate immunity is critical. A previous study using a viral vector-based vaccine, encoding for the ASFV antigens p30, p54, p72, p72c and CD2v, induced protection when combining intranasal (IN) and parenteral administrations.

studi.t: Characterizing the Effects of Filtration on Microbial Diversity, Reproducibility, and Genome Recovery from Wastewater
studi.s: Filtration is widely used in wastewater microbiome workflows, but how pore size, filtration tactics, and sampled fraction shape microbial profiles across sequencing approaches remains unclear. We compared direct and sequential filtration of wastewater through 3-, 0.45-, and 0.22- micro meter filters and analyzed filter-retained and corresponding filtrates using 16S rRNA gene and ITS amplicon sequencing, shotgun metagenomics, and metatranscriptomics.

studi.t: Rapid development of E. coli resistance to Bdellovibrio predation during short-term co-culture
studi.s: When E. coli ML35 is co-cultured with Bdellovibrio sp. NC01 over 72 hours, prey populations initially experience a 3-log reduction, but then partially recover to ~20% of starting density. Population recovery is correlated with emergence of irregular colonies, which are distinct from typical circular ML35 morphotype. ML35 populations do not recover when co-cultured with Bdellovibrio bacteriovorus HD100, and irregular colonies are not observed in HD100 co-cultures or in prey-only controls.

studi.t: A 6-week all-liquid caloric restriction diet reduced abundance of some butyrate-producing bacteria while increasing abundance of mucin-degrading bacteria
studi.s: Caloric restriction diets are a common diet strategy to reduce excess weight and obesity. The diets work by lowering the number of calories or energy input below a human's normal energy expenditure creating an energy deficit. Caloric restriction diet meals can be composed of whole foods, meal replacement shakes, or a combination of the two. While the effects of these diets on human metabolism are well-known, the effects of these diets and the durability of these effects on the human gut microbiome are less well-known.

studi.t: Understanding the dynamics of Telomerase-RNP complex in the human malaria parasite
studi.s: Amongst the human malaria causing species, P. falciparum exhibits an interesting telomere-telomerase (TERT) dynamics. In a striking contrast to humans, which have 10-15 kb long telomeres, parasite telomeres are shorter (1-2 kb) and are maintained by a very large Pf TERT (2.5 times bigger than hTERT) and its structural RNA (Pf TR is 5 times bigger than hTR). Till date, there are no studies on Telomerase-RNP complex in the malaria parasite. The RNP complex comprises of diverged TERT and RNA-interacting proteins (Dyskerin, GAR1, NHP2, NOP10, TCAB1) and structural TR.

studi.t: A simplified protocol for the generation of apical-out human bladder organoids in suspension using a rotating bioreactor
studi.s: Bladder organoids are commonly generated in extracellular matrix domes, where apical surfaces line an enclosed central lumen, limiting experimental accessibility. Suspension-based systems have been explored to generate polarity-reversed organoids, but current models are often derived from cancer cells, remain incompletely characterized or rely on highly specialized scaffolds.

studi.t: Cryo-EM-based examinations of honey bee colony losses reveal structural insights into acute bee paralysis virus maturation and mechanical carriage
studi.s: Honey bee colony losses pose a complex and significant agricultural problem in the United States and Europe, which has also been linked to viruses. As opposed to a purely sequence-based approach, we used cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) as an alternative sequencing- and culture-independent diagnostic tool to investigate viral pathogens associated with colony losses in the state of Texas.

studi.t: Legionella pneumophila DenR is a bacterial S-acyltransferase for the human GTPase NRAS
studi.s: In eukaryotic cells, the covalent attachment of palmitic acid to cysteine residues is catalyzed by the DHHC superfamily of membrane-embedded protein acyltransferases (DHHC-PAT). Here, we discovered that the bacterial pathogen Legionella pneumophila codes for its own protein acyltransferase, DenR, which hijacks host palmitoylation. Unlike the DHHC-PATs, DenR is a cytosolic protein that peripherally associates with membranes via binding of PI3P lipids through its carboxy-terminal domain.

studi.t: Two CntT methyltransferases from Actinosynnema mirum and Pseudomonas aeruginosa reveal conserved opine-type metallophore methylation but divergent biological roles
studi.s: Opine-type metallophores have been discovered in mono- and diderm bacteria, where they allow zinc import under conditions of severe deficiency, a situation often found in natural environments. Whilst this family of metallophores is relatively well characterised, their modes of action in the organisms in which they are found remain poorly documented. In the present study, we identified and characterized two homologous SAM-dependent methyltransferases from the monoderm Actinosynnema mirum and the diderm Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteria.

studi.t: Poxvirus-induced concurrent activation of SAMD9 and ERK establishes a unique immune state with heightened IFN-I responses to danger signals
studi.s: Mammalian poxviruses must overcome the cellular restriction factor SAMD9 to establish productive infection. SAMD9 is a widely expressed cytoplasmic sensor of double-stranded nucleic acids (dsNA) that induces type-1 interferon (IFN-I) responses and possesses anticodon-nuclease activity targeting tRNAphe specifically. To counteract SAMD9, poxviruses have evolved dedicated antagonists, including myxoma virus (MYXV) M062, which blocks both dsNA sensing and tRNAphe-nuclease activity. However, the significance of tRNAphe depletion during poxvirus infection has remained unclear.

studi.t: Human eIF3 and eIF5 coordinate AUG recognition to sustain energy homeostasis
studi.s: Precise translation initiation is essential for efficient production of proteins; missing or mis-selecting the canonical start site can have detrimental consequences. Past research identified several initiation factors governing start codon selection accuracy in yeast, but the increasing complexity of higher eukaryotes have limited similar research in mammalian cells. We present an in cellulo study of knock-in mutants of the eIF3c subunit of the multitasking eIF3 complex that disrupt eIF3's interaction with eIF5, thereby preventing functional binding of eIF5 to pre-initiation complexes.

studi.t: LUBAC ubiquitinates FADD and Caspase-8 through distinct catalytic mechanisms and limits TNF-induced apoptosis
studi.s: The linear ubiquitin chain assembly complex (LUBAC) is a critical regulator of tumor necrosis factor (TNF) signaling that promotes pro-survival responses and suppresses apoptosis. Linear ubiquitination of the TNFR1-associated complex II components FADD and Caspase-8 has been reported, but whether they are direct LUBAC substrates, how they are modified, and what the modification does remain poorly understood.

studi.t: Protease shaving resolves the surface proteome of infection-derived extracellular vesicles and unmasks their inflammatory activity
studi.s: Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) produced and released by infected macrophages carry both host proteins and bacterial antigens, but whether these components face outward, are enclosed within vesicles, or are associated with co-isolated material remains unclear, limiting our understanding of their accessibility to recipient cells. We combined proteinase K shaving with quantitative proteomics to characterize the protease-accessible proteome of sEVs released by Salmonella-infected RAW264.7 macrophages. Host and bacterial proteins exhibited distinct responses to proteolysis.

studi.t: Electrophysiological Comparison of Mechanosensitive PIEZO1 Channel Currents across Different Human Cell Types
studi.s: The detection of mechanical stress is essential for a wide range of physiological functions in humans, including touch sensation, hearing, and the maintenance of vascular myogenic tone. PIEZO1 is a mechanosensitive cation channel that is widely expressed in both neuronal and non-neuronal cells and plays critical physiological roles in multiple organs. However, the electrophysiological comparisons of endogenous PIEZO1-mediated mechanosensitive currents have remained limited across different human cell types under identical experimental conditions.

studi.t: ATAD1 at Mitochondria-ER Contact Sites FacilitatesMislocalized Protein Transfer to the ER
studi.s: Mitochondria-ER contact sites (MERCs) play important roles in cellular functions such as lipid and Ca2+ transport and the regulation of mitochondrial dynamics. To better understand the functional diversity of MERCs, it is critical to identify proteins localized at these sites. Here, we employed CsFiND (Complementation assay using fusion of Split-GFP and TurboID) to identify MERC-associated proteins in HeLa cells. Proteomic and cell biological analyses identified ATAD1, a mitochondrial AAA-ATPase, as a MERC-associated protein.

studi.t: Targeted protein depletion in quiescent fission yeast cells using an auxin-degron system
studi.s: Quiescence is a reversible, non-proliferative cellular state in which cells can remain for extended periods of time while retaining the ability to re-enter the cell cycle upon exposure to favorable conditions. This physiological state is critical for a broad range of biological processes, from stress response in unicellular systems to differentiation and development in multicellular organisms. Surprisingly, despite its recognized roles in cell biology in diverse species, key aspects of the regulation of quiescence remain poorly understood.

studi.t: Phosphorylation of the ER-plasma membrane tether E-Syt2 facilitates the loss of contact sites in mitosis
studi.s: Mitosis is associated with dramatic remodeling of intracellular organelles that supports their equal distribution between daughter cells. Recent investigations into membrane contact sites (MCS) show that they also remodel in mitosis with a significant loss of ER-plasma membrane CS (ERPMCS). However, the mechanisms governing this loss are unknown. Here we show that phosphorylation of the ERPMCS tether extended synaptotagmin 2 (E-Syt2) facilitates the loss of ERPMCS in mitosis. Preventing E-Syt2 phosphorylation in mitosis rescues the loss of ERPMCS.

studi.t: Hemodynamic and Yap1/Wwtr1-dependent epithelial-endothelial signaling establish fenestrated endothelial identity and permeability in the choroid plexus
studi.s: The choroid plexuses (CPs) constitute the interface between cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and circulating blood, mediating their molecular exchange. How the CPs establish permeable endothelial identities and properties distinct from neighboring barrier-forming endothelium remains unknown. By developing new genetic and functional screening platforms in zebrafish, we identified blood flow-responsive KLF2 orthologues, klf2a and klf2b, as critical regulators of CP endothelial identity and permeability.

studi.t: Spatial and temporal drivers of genomic inbreeding in a declining population of yellow-bellied marmots
studi.s: Estimates of genetic diversity and effective population size are critical for predicting the resilience of natural populations to environmental change. We generated the first estimates of genetic diversity, effective population size and genomic inbreeding in a wild population of yellow-bellied marmots (Marmota flaviventer) studied continuously in western Colorado since 1962.

studi.t: Power analysis for selection in allele-frequency time series.
studi.s: Allele frequencies tracked through time, from ancient DNA, museum collections or monitoring, offer a direct view of selection. Their value depends on whether the sampling design can distinguish change caused by selection from genetic drift and from the noise of sampling few individuals, often sequenced at low coverage. Researchers need to know how much power a design has before committing specimens and sequencing effort, which usually requires study-specific simulations.

studi.t: A naïve genome reveals the evolutionary dependence of CTCF functions
studi.s: The functions of genome regulatory proteins often emerge through long-term coevolution with their genomic and nuclear environments, complicating the distinction between intrinsic protein properties and context-dependent activities. The DNA-binding protein CTCF is a multifunctional regulator that plays central roles in genome organization and gene regulation across animals. Here, we investigated the behaviour of human CTCF in a deeply heterologous system by expressing it in the budding yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae, a lineage that diverged before the evolution of CTCF itself.

studi.t: Models show altered outcomes from evolution of standing genetic variation in response to a suppression gene drive
studi.s: Gene drives are commonly modelled as engineered inheritance-biasing systems with fixed performance, showing great potential for controlling disease vectors and other pests. Yet, natural populations contain standing genetic variation potentially capable of modifying drive transmission, resistance allele formation, and drive-associated fitness. This could lead to evolution in the population after the release of a drive system, potentially affecting the outcome.

studi.t: Genomic trinucleotide composition reflects context-dependent mutation spectra in plants and mammals
studi.s: Mutation rates vary substantially across mutation types and sequence contexts, yet it remains unclear how variation in the mutation spectrum shapes genome composition across species. Motivated by the strong cross-species relationship between CpG mutation rate and CpG content, we hypothesize that multi-nucleotide genome composition reflects the context-dependent mutation spectrum, with additional effects of GC-biased gene conversion (gBGC).

studi.t: The effects of selfing, limited seed dispersal and environmental persistence on the evolution of size-dependent sex allocation
studi.s: Sex allocation, the division of resources between male and female function, often varies as a function of size in cosexual plants. This variation is thought to evolve because fitness returns gained from allocating to each function are influenced by plant size, and many mechanisms have been proposed for why it should be so. Here, we explore how competing selfing and limited seed dispersal jointly shape the evolution of size-dependent sex allocation in an annual plant population where size is environmentally determined.

studi.t: From ancestral patterns of variation to the human condition: Leveraging disease phenotype associations and gene expression changes
studi.s: The shift in perspective to characterize the genetic basis of the human condition beyond fully fixed mutations opens many possibilities to scrutinize the nature of high-frequency derived variants in modern human genomes through the effect of the minor alleles, either already present in extant Pan relatives ("basal"), or found across most genomes of extinct hominins and likely introgressed into sapiens genomes.

studi.t: Beyond Abundance: Integrated Splicing and Expression Quantitative Trait Loci Refine Causal Gene Mapping in IBD
studi.s: Molecular quantitative trait loci for expression (eQTL) and splicing (sQTL) connect inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) risk loci to potential molecular mechanisms. We mapped cis-eQTL and cis-sQTL in 1,149 colon samples from SPARC IBD participants in IBD Plexus, identifying 20,566 genes with eQTL (eGenes) and 9,906 with sQTL (sGenes). Colocalization prioritized 239 eGenes and 164 sGenes across 147 IBD risk loci, including 58 genes supported by both traits.

studi.t: Multi-resolution QTL mapping in four interconnected rice RIL populations reveals recurrent, background-specific, and environment-dependent loci
studi.s: We aimed to determine how marker density influences the detection and localization of quantitative trait loci (QTLs) in rice and to identify parental alleles with consistent effects across genetic backgrounds and environments. We evaluated grain yield, plant height, and flowering time in four interconnected recombinant inbred line populations at two Brazilian sites, Goianira and Boa Vista. Each parent contributed to two crosses, allowing us to compare the direction of its allelic effects in different genetic backgrounds.

studi.t: A refined InDel taxonomy broadens the repertoire of mutational processes shaping multiple myeloma
studi.s: Somatic aberrations have been extensively characterized in multiple myeloma (MM). However, the mutational processes underlying small insertions and deletions (InDels) remain poorly understood. Here, we used a recently developed 89-channel InDel classification schema which allows differentiating mutational processes. We analyzed whole-genome sequencing data from 887 MM samples, spanning both newly diagnosed (NDMM) and relapsed/refractory disease (RRMM).

studi.t: High prevalence and diversity of nematodes associated with Europe's most destructive forest pest, revealed by off-target genomic data
studi.s: We know very little about the biotic interactions of most species on our planet, including many organisms that play a crucial role in ecosystem networks. One highly cost-effective way of reconstructing these networks is to analyse the rapidly growing collections of high-throughput sequencing datasets. In this study, we examine a large whole-genome resequencing dataset for the spruce bark beetle (Ips typographus), one of Europe's most destructive forest pests, to determine the diversity and distribution of associated organisms that such datasets can reveal.

studi.t: Distinctive fragmentation of circulating DNA from chromosome Y and its alteration in cancer
studi.s: Circulating cell-free DNA (cirDNA) fragmentation reflects chromatin organization and represents a promising source of cancer biomarkers. Here, we characterized the fragmentation patterns and nucleosome occupancy of Y chromosome (chrY) cirDNA in healthy individuals and cancer patients. In healthy males, we found that the shorter chrY-derived cirDNA fragments predominantly originate from heterochromatic regions. We also observed substantially lower nucleosome occupancy on chrY than on all other chromosomes, a finding independently supported by micrococcal nuclease digestion data.

studi.t: Somatic mutation detection from non-malignant liver tissues using cell-free DNA
studi.s: Somatic mutations accumulate in the liver during aging, yet their role in chronic liver disease (CLD) remains unclear due to the difficulty of obtaining liver tissue for analysis. Here, we demonstrate that circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) can be used as a minimally invasive tool to detect liver-derived somatic mutations in patients with CLD. Using ultra-deep targeted duplex sequencing, we show that CLD patients have a higher mutation burden in CLD-associated somatic mutation (CASM) genes compared to healthy individuals.

studi.t: Large-scale analyses of short open reading frames yield few if any novel human genes
studi.s: Recent efforts to discover new protein-coding genes in the human genome have yielded a large number of short open reading frames supported by limited experimental evidence supporting translational activity in fragmented parts of those sequences. We examined the 19 highest-confidence predictions made by the TransCODE Consortium, and found that three of them were previously known and thus not novel, while the other 16 could be explained by mechanisms that do not require the assertion of a novel human protein.

studi.t: The 'near T2T' Canton-S assembly is inconsistent with other Canton-S genomes
studi.s: Canton-S is among the most widely used Drosophila melanogaster strains, underlying substantial community infrastructure, including serving as a wild-type strain for: genetics studies; studying phenotypes, especially in behavioral studies; and complex trait mapping studies among many others. The recent 'near T2T' assembly of Canton-S (LIU et al.) is presented as delivering modern sequencing and assembly quality to the Drosophila community via this important strain.

studi.t: Full-length transcript architecture reveals RNA fate and regulatory state
studi.s: Pervasive transcription generates diverse RNAs, including promoter-upstream transcripts (PROMPTs), coding and non-coding transcripts from protein-coding loci, and enhancer RNAs. How their full-length architectures relate to RNA fate remains poorly understood. Using ultra-deep sequencing of polyadenylated and non-polyadenylated capped RNAs from mouse embryonic stem cells, we show that nuclear exosome surveillance of PROMPTs is associated with transcript length and sequence composition.

studi.t: Annotated reference genome for the Critically Endangered, paleoendemic Bermuda skink (Plestiodon longirostris)
studi.s: Skinks, one of the largest vertebrate families with over 1,500 described species, are represented by only 19 publicly available chromosome-level genome assemblies. Here, we present the first whole-genome assembly of the Bermuda skink, Plestiodon longirostris, a Critically Endangered, evolutionarily distinct, and endemic species. We conducted a de novo genome assembly using Oxford Nanopore Technology long reads, followed by reference-guided scaffolding against the five-lined skink Plestiodon fasciatus and Gilberts skink Plestiodon gilberti genomes.

studi.t: Relying on a declarative as opposed to a procedural learning strategy predisposes to the development of instrumental habits in female but not in male rats
studi.s: Across species, individuals differ in their reliance on declarative versus procedural long-term memory systems for exploring and controlling the environment, mapping respectively onto allocentric place versus egocentric response learning strategies in a spatial navigation task. Several factors motivate the widely held consideration that procedural spatial learning strategies are generalisable to stimulus-response habits in the domain of instrumental conditioning, and vice versa; however, this hypothesis has received little empirical testing.

studi.t: Sucker recruitment patterns on the octopus arm during chemotactile exploration
studi.s: Octopuses possess highly flexible arms lined with chemo- and mechanosensory suckers that mediate exploration, prey capture, and object manipulation. How individual suckers communicate with adjacent and distant suckers to accomplish such tasks is poorly understood. We developed a behavioral protocol with Octopus bimaculoides to investigate inter-sucker recruitment once an individual sucker encountered an object of interest.

studi.t: Discovery and Optimization of Indoline-2-Carboxamide-Based FBXO31 Recruiters for Targeted Protein Degradation
studi.s: Expanding the repertoire of chemically recruitable E3 ligases is critical for advancing targeted protein degradation (TPD). FBXO31 has recently emerged as a promising E3 ligase for TPD, but existing peptide-derived recruiters exhibit limited degradation potency and efficacy at endogenous FBXO31 expression levels. Here, we report the discovery and optimization of indoline-2-carboxamide-based FBXO31 recruiters through structure-activity relationship studies.

studi.t: A Shifting Landscape: Deconvoluting the Effect of Mg2+ and pH on Base Triple Formation in 7SK SL-1
studi.s: The small-nuclear RNA (snRNA) 7SK is essential for regulating the transcription of genes by RNA polymerase II through its interactions with Hexamethylene Bisacetamide Inducible Protein (HEXIM) and positive transcription elongation factor b (P-TEFb). High-resolution structures of 7SK stem-loop 1 (SL-1) reveal the presence of several base triples that coordinate the interaction with HEXIM. However, different high-resolution structures of 7SK SL-1 exhibit different conformations, each with unique base triple configurations.

studi.t: Correlative mapping links extracellular matrix architecture to local mechanics in cardiac aging
studi.s: Cardiac aging is accompanied by extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling, but how changes in matrix architecture relate to local tissue mechanics remains poorly understood. Here, we quantified six image-derived architectural descriptors across selected ECM components in young and aged murine myocardium and integrated them into an architectural index that we term 'ArchI'. Age-associated architectural changes differed among ECM components, with higher ArchI values observed for fibrillar collagen, fibronectin, and laminin-associated networks.

studi.t: BioSensor-X: A Coverage-Aware Evidence-Integration and Benchmarking Framework for Transcription-Factor Prioritization in Microbial Biosensor Engineering
studi.s: Transcription-factor (TF) prioritization in microbial biosensor engineering requires integration of heterogeneous molecular and regulatory evidence, yet benchmark-associated performance may be influenced by candidate coverage, annotation density, and information-flow structure. BioSensor-X was developed as a leakage-controlled, coverage-aware framework for evaluating heterogeneous transcriptomic and regulatory evidence for Escherichia coli TF prioritization.

studi.t: Benchmarking sample mispairing detection tools in complex cancer datasets
studi.s: Sample mispairs are common and potentially costly mistakes, and therefore checking for sample mispairing is a crucial quality-control step in multimodal genomic studies. This study presents an independent benchmark of sample mispairing detection tools in multimodal transcriptomic cancer datasets. In pseudobulk experiments with known sample pairings, four tools achieved near-perfect F1 scores across datasets. In real-data experiments, three tools performed particularly well, and sample mispairs were identified in three of five datasets.

studi.t: Biomedical Text Embeddings Weakly Capture Chromatin Accessibility Similarity: A Large-Scale Measurement Study
studi.s: Text metadata provides the most readily available description of public chromatin accessibility data, but it remains unclear how well it reflects similarity between the underlying chromatin profiles. We systematically compared pairwise cosine similarity matrices derived from 12 embedding types across 32,245 human assay for transposase-accessible chromatin with sequencing (ATAC-seq) experiments obtained from ChIP-Atlas.

studi.t: Fast draft assemblies using locally consistent parsing
studi.s: Recent improvements in long-read sequencing accuracy, particularly the introduction of PacBio HiFi reads, have created new opportunities for more efficient sequence representations in genome assembly. In particular, variations of de Bruijn graphs (dBG), such as sparse dBG and minimizer-space dBG, provide efficient representations of sequences and have enabled genome assemblers to leverage the high accuracy of long-read data while maintaining low memory usage and fast analysis times.

studi.t: In silico pipeline for identification of targets of plastic-derived chemicals
studi.s: Plastic pollution is a growing global health concern, yet the specific human protein targets mediating the toxic effects of plastic-derived chemicals (PDCs) remain largely unknown. Here, we present an integrative in silico pipeline that combines transcriptomic data with structural bioinformatics to identify putative human plastic-derived targets.

studi.t: APEs: Agentic Prediction of Epitopes to Guide Antibody-Antigen Structure Prediction
studi.s: Antibody-antigen complex prediction remains difficult because the surface recognized by a specific antibody is often uncertain, and model confidence may not distinguish alternative poses. We developed APEs (Agentic Prediction of Epitopes for Structure Prediction), an agentic system that retrieves public evidence, interprets predicted antibody and antigen structures, and produces ranked residue-level epitope hypotheses. For retrospective evaluation, web retrieval was restricted to sources released before each CASP target entry date.

studi.t: Unipept in 2026: A Unified Web Platform for Comparative Metaproteomics Analysis
studi.s: Metaproteomics studies the collective proteome of microbial communities to characterize their taxonomic composition and functional activity. Unipept has long supported such analyses, but organizing samples into projects, building targeted reference databases, and comparing samples across a study were only possible in a standalone desktop application. Here we present a major update that moves these workflows into the web application, so a complete multi-sample study can be assembled, analyzed, and shared without local installation.

studi.t: From Growth Inhibition to Fluctuations: Testing an Ising Model of Bacterial Responses to Antibiotics
studi.s: Complex networks of biochemical reactions have been proposed to exhibit emergent cooperativity that can be described by an effective Ising model, with a small number of parameters encoding collective interactions. Here this mapping is experimentally tested using the response of three bacterial species to a range of antibiotics acting on different cellular targets. The Ising description is compared to the conventional Hill model, examining both the mean growth-rate response and, importantly, its population growth-rate heterogeneity (PGRH).

studi.t: Integrating hydrogen-exchange experiments with conformational ensembles
studi.s: Protein conformational dynamics are central to biological function but remain difficult to characterise at scale. Amide hydrogen exchange (HX), measured by NMR or mass spectrometry, probes these dynamics but requires computational models for integration with structural ensembles. We benchmark models for calculating HX from ensembles using a large literature-derived dataset spanning folded and intrinsically disordered proteins. We then develop a model that identifies exchange-competent amides from local structural descriptors while accounting for electrostatic effects.

studi.t: AVF creation in mice disrupts blood flow patterns to impact vasoreactivity
studi.s: Maladaptive venous remodeling contributes to the high rate of arteriovenous fistula (AVF) maturation failure. Impaired vasoreactivity might impact this pathology. We created a murine AVF by anastomosing the external jugular vein to the carotid artery, establishing the AVF vein (AVF-V) and proximal (PA) and distal (DA) carotid artery. We hypothesized that endothelium-dependent vasorelaxation is impaired in the AVF-V vs.

studi.t: The neural basis of unfamiliar face recognition in humans with fMRI frequency-tagging
studi.s: Faces provide the most diagnostic information for identifying individuals in humans. Understanding the neural mechanisms involved in face identity recognition (FIR) is particularly important for unfamiliar faces, for which identity cannot rely on encoded multimodal semantic associations. Here, we investigated the neural basis of FIR using an original frequency-tagging fMRI approach providing objective, sensitive, and reliable measures of face recognition.

studi.t: ELLA-mix: Detecting Cell-to-Cell Heterogeneity in Subcellular RNA Localization
studi.s: Subcellular RNA localization can differ between cells expressing the same gene, yet most analyses summarize transcript positions with a single gene-level pattern. We propose ELLA-mix, a finite mixture model for identifying cell subpopulations with distinct radial localization patterns from imaging-based spatial transcriptomics data. Transcript positions are normalized relative to the cell boundary and modeled using flexible spline densities within a count-conditioned nonhomogeneous Poisson process framework.

studi.t: Rapamycin Mitigates Branched-Chain Amino Acid Accumulation in Maple Syrup Urine Disease Mice
studi.s: Maple syrup urine disease (MSUD) is an inborn error of metabolism caused by mutations in the mitochondrial branched-chain -keto acid dehydrogenase (BCKDH) complex, resulting in toxic accumulation of branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs) and their corresponding branched-chain keto acids (BCKAs). This leads to poorly understood clinical features in both brain and muscle. Due to a limited understanding of MSUD pathophysiology, there is a marked paucity of effective pharmacological interventions.

studi.t: The Dark Side of Light: Adolescent Light Exposure at Night Disrupts Hippocampal Clocks and Plasticity-Related Signaling in a Sex-Dependent Manner.
studi.s: In today's society, adolescents are being increasingly exposed to artificial blue light at night from electronic devices, raising concerns about its effects on brain development and mental health. The hippocampus, and specifically the dentate gyrus (DG) regulates memory formation and itself operates as a subordinate circadian oscillator detecting changes in the light environment. However, whether light at night during adolescence can impair hippocampal clock and function remains unknown.

studi.t: Evaluating WGS-based methods as an in silico replacement of phage typing for historical continuity and host association in Salmonella Typhimurium
studi.s: Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium (STm) poses a significant burden on public health worldwide. The Anderson phage typing scheme has historically supported surveillance, outbreak investigations and source attribution through associations between phage types and animal hosts. However, limitations inherent to the scheme have led to the gradual replacement of phage typing by whole-genome sequencing (WGS)-based methods.

studi.t: WITHDRAWN: Metabolic Intervention with Dimethyl Malonate Impairs Phagocytic Clearance but Fails to Protect Neurons
studi.s: The authors have withdrawn this manuscript because exposure to 4{degrees}C, similar to dimethyl malonate treatment, inhibits microglial phagocytosis, resulting in the persistence of retinal ganglion cell (RGC) somas after injury challenging the proposed interpretation of RGC soma persistence as evidence of neuroprotection. Therefore, the authors do not wish this work to be cited as reference for the project. If you have any questions, please contact the corresponding author.

studi.t: WITHDRAWN: Increasing spatial approximation complexity can degrade prediction quality in distribution models
studi.s: The authors have withdrawn this manuscript because we had substantial errors in how we were calculating predictive accuracy, and this significantly changes our interpretation and findings. Therefore, the authors do not wish this work to be cited as reference for the project. If you have any questions, please contact the corresponding author.

studi.t: Assessment of dopaminergic neurotoxicity of CYP2E1-mediated trichloroethylene metabolites in C. elegans
studi.s: Trichloroethylene (TCE) is an industrial solvent associated with Parkinson's Disease (PD). Studies have demonstrated that TCE undergoes extensive metabolism in humans, suggesting that TCE toxicity may be attributable to its metabolites. However, knowledge of how TCE metabolites contribute to neurotoxicity in PD remains limited. We exposed Caenorhabditis elegans (C. elegans) to the TCE metabolites trichloroacetic acid (TCA) and trichloroethanol (TCEOH) to determine if exposure disrupts dopamine-dependent behaviors, such as movement and egg retention, and impairs dopamine neuron viability.

studi.t: WITHDRAWN: Managed Bee Pollination Enhances Yield and Seed Quality in Brassica napus through Flowering Duration and Agronomic Trait Modulation
studi.s: The authors have withdrawn this manuscript because we, the authors, withdraw this preprint (DOI:10.1101/2026.718066). All co-authors have agreed to this withdrawal. We have identified issues in data analysis and interpretation, and we cannot endorse the conclusions presented in this version. We plan to re-analyze the dataset and prepare a revised manuscript for future submission. Therefore, the authors do not wish this work to be cited as reference for the project. If you have any questions, please contact the corresponding author.

studi.t: A cell-based screen identifies host-directed inhibitors and nutrient-conditional antimicrobials against intracellular S. flexneri dissemination
studi.s: Multidrug-resistant S. flexneri is a World Health Organization priority pathogen for which no universally licensed vaccine is currently available. Most antimicrobial screening platforms involve planktonic bacteria replicating in nutrient-rich medium, a condition that does not reflect the intracellular niche in which S. flexneri replicates and spreads and systematically excludes compounds whose activity depends on the host environment. Here, we screened the 1,581 compounds of the National Cancer Institute Diversity Set VII for inhibitors of S.

studi.t: Cold atmospheric plasma for improved sustainability and fish welfare in recirculating aquaculture systems
studi.s: Decontamination of water is mandatory for the cultivation of aquatic species in recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS). Avoiding economic and ecological losses while ensuring safe conditions is important for the future introduction of new technologies. Therefore, the implementation of cold atmospheric plasma (CAP) within RAS was examined for the first time. For the integration of this technology two equal RAS were set up, one using CAP, the other one ultraviolet light (UV) for water decontamination.

studi.t: PTMlink: a database resource for co-variation of glycosylation and phosphorylation in human tumors
studi.s: Protein glycosylation and phosphorylation can regulate each other, but the two protein modifications are usually studied separately, and their modification-specific co-variation across tumor types remains poorly characterized. PTMlink is a database of site-resolved co-variation between glycosylation and phosphorylation in the matched glycoproteomes and phosphoproteomes of 1,211 tumor samples from cohorts of the Clinical Proteomic Tumor Analysis Consortium, complemented by studies that perturbed glycosylation in human cells to examine its crosstalk with, and functional effects on…

studi.t: Use of orthogonal split inteins to direct surface expression of specific metabotropic glutamate receptor hererodimer pairs.
studi.s: Metabotropic glutamate receptors (mGluRs) are class C G protein coupled receptors that function as obligate, covalently linked homo- and heterodimers in some combinations. The pharmacological responses of heterodimers to selective ligands are difficult to predict, and due to the tendency to homodimerize, heterodimers cannot be easily expressed in isolation.
