studi.s: A central goal of evolutionary genetics is to determine how environmental pressures maintain adaptive genetic variation and evaluate how this variation is encoded in the genome (1). Dissecting the genetic basis of local adaptation carries new urgency in an era of rapid climate change. We identified genomic regions associated with climatic adaptation, quantified the fitness consequences of allelic variation, and forecasted evolutionary responses to novel climates in the ecological model plant, Boechera stricta.

studi.t: Gaussian selection on a polygenic trait from the gene's-eye view.
studi.s: We study a polygenic trait under Gaussian selection at statistical equilibrium, where allelic effect, mutation rate and mutational bias are heterogeneous across loci. The model assumes a large number L of biallelic sites subject to reversible mutations, each allele described by its frequency in the population.

studi.t: MSGFLEX: An optimized end-to-end pipeline for proteomics and metaproteomics analysis built on MS-GF+ with a dedicated rescoring model XPECTRA
studi.s: Mass spectrometry-based proteomics workflows often face competing demands between identification sensitivity, false discovery rate (FDR) control, and computational scalability, particularly for metaproteomic datasets that require searching large and complex sequence databases. Here, we present MSGFLEX, an integrated end-to-end workflow that combines database searching, machine-learning based rescoring, and peptide-to-protein quantitative inference.

studi.t: A site-resolved post-translational modification framework for drug-response analysis
studi.s: Post-translational modifications (PTMs) regulate protein activity and treatment-associated signalling, providing functional information that can connect drug-response estimates with candidate pharmacodynamic measurements. Assessing this information requires a framework that determines its contribution beyond fixed molecular features while retaining the identity of the modified sites underlying model predictions.

studi.t: Phosphate selectivity in XPR1 is driven by direct multi-ion competition
studi.s: Inorganic phosphate (Pi) is essential for numerous cellular processes, and its intracellular concentration must be tightly regulated. In mammals, phosphate efflux is mediated by the Xenotropic and Polytropic Retrovirus Receptor 1 (XPR1/SLC53A1), the only known mammalian Pi exporter. We and others have recently proposed that XPR1 functions like a Pi channel, with the protein preferentially conducting the H2PO4- species of Pi over HPO42-. While some studies suggest that XPR1 can conduct other anions, the molecular basis of XPR1 substrate selectivity remains unknown.

studi.t: The creatine transporter SLC6A8 is an immune pressure-exposed metabolic vulnerability in acute myeloid leukemia
studi.s: Chemotherapy imposes metabolic pressure that generates persisting tumor cell states, but whether these adaptations also shape immune evasion is poorly understood. Here, we identify creatine accumulation as a conserved feature of chemotherapy-persisting acute myeloid leukemia (AML) across mouse and human models. Stable-isotope tracing and genetic perturbation show that this is driven predominantly by SLC6A8-mediated creatine uptake rather than de novo synthesis.

studi.t: Cell-autonomous self-renewal
studi.s: To self-renew, stem cells must precisely balance proliferation and differentiation. Typically, this is achieved under feedback from the niche; yet many stem cells also possess an intrinsic self-renewal program that allows them to do so autonomously, if required. However, because self-renewal implies a stable equilibrium -- in which the expected stem cell number neither increases nor decreases over time -- this seems to require fine-tuning to a critical point.

studi.t: Velocity-dependent friction in a simple two-oscillator system. II. Regions of stability
studi.s: In Part I, a gamma friction that follows theta velocity produced theta gamma phase amplitude coupling (PAC) whose strength is a closed-form function of one dimensionless number, kappa;. Here we ask when this coupling destabilizes the gamma oscillator. The friction on gamma is negative during part of every theta cycle, yet gamma stays bounded: as long as it keeps oscillating, the energy gained while theta rises is returned while theta falls, and Liouville' sformula fixes the growth over a theta cycle at the baseline decay, whatever the coupling.

studi.t: Velocity-dependent friction in a simple two-oscillator system. I. Phase amplitude coupling
studi.s: Cortical gamma oscillations often arrive in bursts locked to the phase of slower theta waves, a pattern called theta gamma phase amplitude coupling (PAC). PAC is linked to memory and altered in epilepsy, but most models tie it to particular cells or circuits. We start from a generalized Langevin equation, an equation of motion for a few collective variables in which friction and random forces stand for the unobserved neural activity, and let its stiffness and friction depend on the state.

studi.t: Tetrodotoxin-resistant NaV1.8 contributes to action potential conduction in a population of mouse and human vagal nerve fibers
studi.s: Axonal action potential (AP) conduction is dependent on voltage-gated sodium channels (NaV1s). AP conduction in the vagus nerve (which contains afferent and efferent fibers) is essential to its reflex regulation of most visceral organs. The nine isoforms of NaV1s show diverse expression patterns in vagal neurons. In rodent vagus nerves, multiple NaV1 isoforms contribute to AP conduction, with NaV1.7 playing an essential role in ~70% of fibers. Here, we investigated the contribution of tetrodotoxin-resistant (TTX-R) NaV1.8 towards vagal AP conduction ex vivo.

studi.t: Dual C5aR1 and C5aR2 deficiency uncouples neutrophilic inflammation from antibacterial host defense
studi.s: Streptococcus pneumoniae is a major cause of bacterial pneumonia and mortality worldwide. While host defense critically depends on complement activation, how C5aR1 and C5aR2 orchestrate pulmonary antibacterial immunity remains unclear. We identified alveolar type II epithelial cells as a local source of C5 and confirmed increased susceptibility of C5-deficient mice to infection.

studi.t: Allele-specific NR2F1 variants disrupt retinoic acid-associated retinal regionalization and uncover foveal hypoplasia in BBSOAS
studi.s: Pathogenic variants in the nuclear receptor NR2F1 cause Bosch-Boonstra-Schaaf optic atrophy syndrome (BBSOAS), but how distinct mutations affect retinal development and contribute to visual dysfunction remains poorly understood. Here, we identify NR2F1 as an upstream regulator of a retinoic acid (RA)-associated transcriptional program involved in retinal regionalization and cone photoreceptor patterning.

studi.t: Biochemical characterisation of fungal bioluminescence enzymes reveals substrate inhibition and secondary turnover of 3-hydroxyhispidin by H3H
studi.s: The fungal bioluminescence pathway has emerged as a versatile platform for bioimaging and synthetic biology. However, biochemical characterisation of its core enzymes remains limited. Here, we establish recombinant purification and quantitative in vitro characterisation of fungal luciferase (Luz) and hispidin-3-hydroxylase (H3H) homologues from Neonothopanus nambi and Mycena chlorophos. Complementary luminescence and mass spectrometry-based assays revealed pronounced substrate inhibition of H3H by hispidin, conserved across both homologues.

studi.t: Mapping whole-tissue spatial multi-omics at single-cell resolution with STEP
studi.s: Spatial omics technologies have revolutionized our ability to map transcriptomic, proteomic, or metabolomic profiles within tissue contexts. However, existing spatial multi-omics approaches emphasize clustering or domain identification from measured profiles, while a general framework for whole-slice mapping in measured and unmeasured areas at single-cell resolution across additional omics layers remains lacking.

studi.t: Widespread SARS-CoV-2 brain infection after intranasal challenge leads to innate and anti-viral immune response and interference with neuronal function in K18-hACE2 mice
studi.s: Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), the causative agent of the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, often spreads to the brain in K18-hACE2 transgenic mice after intranasal challenge, leading to widespread neuronal infection. Despite frequent reports of this phenomenon, the effects of SARS-CoV-2 infection on neurons have not yet been fully investigated. Therefore, using the K18-hACE2 mouse model, we performed an in-depth in situ characterisation of brain changes associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection, with a specific focus on infected neurons and glial cells.

studi.t: An H3K9me3high epigenetic state constrains neuronal activation and synaptic remodeling in the aged dentate gyrus
studi.s: How epigenetic states shape neuronal responses to experience and memory remains poorly understood. Here, using a quantitative, single-event approach, our study identifies a subset of neurons that accumulate H3K9me3 (H3K9me3high neurons) via the methyltransferase Suv39h1, specifically in the dorsal dentate gyrus (dDG) of aged mice. FACS coupled to RNA-seq showed that dDG-H3K9me3high neurons express a transcriptional state that fails to induce plasticity machinery despite engaging memory-stabilization programs.

studi.t: Oscillatory Phase Coding Emerges in Adaptive RNNS for Flexible Working Memory
studi.s: Oscillatory phase coding (OPC) is widely observed in neural systems and has been implicated in cognitive functions such as memory and sequence processing. However, its computational role and neural substrates remain largely unclear. Here, we studied OPC by training recurrent neural networks (RNNs) with adaptation to perform sequence working memory tasks with variable delays. After training, we found that OPC emerges in the RNN spontaneously: the memorized items recur at distinct phases of a shared rhythm, with oscillation amplitude encoding item identity and phase encoding serial order.

studi.t: A GPNMB-associated lysosomal program tracks neurodegeneration across the DAM continuum
studi.s: Frontotemporal dementia (FTD) and Alzheimer's disease (AD) profoundly remodel microglial states, yet how the heterogeneity of disease-associated microglia (DAM) relates to neurodegeneration remains incompletely understood. Using a progranulin (PGRN) and TMEM106B-deficient mouse model recapitulating key features of frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD), including lysosomal impairment, we demonstrated that CSF1R inhibition reduced microgliosis yet accelerated neurodegeneration, suggesting a protective microglia contribution under lysosomal stress.

studi.t: A Shared Neural Network for Highly Liked and Disliked Music
studi.s: While the neural correlates of music-induced peak moments of pleasure (e.g., chills) have been well studied, data on other types of aesthetic responses, such as judgments of beauty, goodness, or liking, are sparse. Among these, liking is of particular interest given its complex nature and its ubiquity in everyday, and musical, experiences. In this fMRI study, 26 participants listened to musical excerpts while continuously rating how much they liked the music. In addition, subjects provided an overall liking judgment at the end of each musical piece.

studi.t: From clusters to curves: A model-based alternative to cluster-based permutation tests for the analysis of time-resolved data
studi.s: Time-resolved electrophysiological measurements such as those obtained through magneto- and electroencephalography (M/EEG) offer a unique window onto the neural activity underlying cognitive processes. Researchers are often interested in determining whether and when these signals differ across experimental conditions or participant groups. The conventional approach involves mass univariate statistical testing across time and space followed by corrections for multiple comparisons or some form of cluster-based inference.

studi.t: Cortical Stimulation Strength and sgACC Connectivity Shape Neuro-Cardiac Responses to Prefrontal TMS
studi.s: Autonomic dysregulation is associated with major depressive disorder, yet how cortical stimulation strength and network connectivity shape autonomic responses to prefrontal transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) remains unclear. We combined resting-state functional MRI, individualized electric-field simulations, and electrocardiography during repetitive TMS at up to six left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) targets in 15 healthy adults.

studi.t: WITHDRAWN: Metagenomics reveals a phylogenetically informed microbial signature associated with Morgellons disease
studi.s: The authors have withdrawn this preprint because the human-participant samples underlying the study were collected without Institutional Review Board (IRB) review. In light of unresolved questions concerning research oversight, the authors recognize that public dissemination of these findings was premature. Therefore, the authors request that this preprint not be cited as these matters are addressed.

studi.t: Global inflammatory response in in vitro organ cultured testes using single-cell RNA-sequencing
studi.s: In vitro functional sperm production is important for understanding spermatogenesis and for the treatment of male infertility. Here, we describe similarities and differences between testis tissues in vivo and in vitro and clarify abnormalities in the early stage of in vitro spermatogenesis at single-cell resolution. While in vitro spermatogenesis progressed similarly to in vivo spermatogenesis until the early pachytene spermatocyte stage, a noticeable acute inflammatory response occurred in immune cells and non-immune testicular somatic cells immediately after cultivation.

studi.t: Membrane progesterone receptors spatially organize and partner with ABHD2 to mediate metabolic signaling
studi.s: Membrane progesterone receptors (mPRs) mediate rapid hormone responses, yet how they engage effectors remains poorly understood. Here, we reveal a spatially regulated partnership between mPRs and the lipid hydrolase ABHD2 that provides a mechanistic basis for the early steps of non-genomic progesterone signaling in mammalian cells. Agonist stimulation promotes mPR-dependent accumulation of predominantly intracellular ABHD2 at the plasma membrane and enhances its association with mPRs.

studi.t: Unraveling molecular mechanisms for specification of blastomere identity and neural fate in the annelid Capitella teleta
studi.s: The evolution of central nervous systems remains highly debated as we incorporate data on developmental mechanisms in understudied taxa. Yet how this process occurs in the third major bilaterian clade called Spiralia (e.g., annelids, mollusks) remains inconclusive. Using blastomere isolations, we previously found that in the annelids Capitella teleta and Platynereis dumerilii, ectodermal blastomeres fated to generate the brain and ventral nerve cord can form neural tissue after being isolated. However, in C. teleta, nerve cord formation can be inhibited or rescued by other blastomeres.

studi.t: Centimeter-sized Human Vitreous Organoids from Pluripotent Stem Cells
studi.s: The vitreous, the largest intraocular tissue, provides a transparent light path and maintains the intraocular homeostasis. The reconstitution of the vitreous in vitro or in vivo remains an unsolved biomedical challenge. Here, we discovered a common feature, the "growth edge", constituted primarily of fibroblasts and their secreted proteins in human and mouse vitreous development. By leveraging the transforming growth factor beta signaling, we then generated centimeter-scale vitreous-like organoids (VOs) through stepwise differentiation from human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs).

studi.t: Sex-dependent rewarding effects of nicotine in mice are prevented by the atypical antipsychotic aripiprazole
studi.s: Nicotine stands amongst the most commonly used drugs in contemporary societies. Preparations for nicotine consumption range from traditional tobacco products (smoking) to modern electronic cigarettes (vaping). However, its rewarding and reinforcing effects vary as a function of dose and biological sex.

studi.t: Treg- and CD8-Specific PD-1 Deficiency Reveals That CD8⁺ T Cell-Intrinsic Signaling Uniquely Restrains Pressure Overload Inflammation and Heart Failure
studi.s: Aims: PD-1 signaling limits cardiac remodeling and heart failure (HF). Whether this protection depends on PD-1 signaling intrinsic to CD8 T cells or on regulation by other immune populations, including regulatory T cells (Tregs), remains unclear. Methods and results: Using transverse aortic constriction (TAC), we studied global PD-1-knockout (KO) mice with or without CD8 T cell depletion, CD8 T cell-specific (PD1KOCD8), and Treg-specific PD-1-KO mice.

studi.t: Detection of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium and discrimination of vanA and vanB genotypes by VITEK MS Prime MALDI-TOF Mass Spectrometry and machine learning
studi.s: Rapid identification of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium (VREfm) and discrimination of resistance mechanisms (VanA and VanB) are critical for appropriate antimicrobial therapy and infection control, particularly during outbreaks. Matrix-assisted laser desorption ionization-time of flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF MS), combined with machine learning, has emerged as a promising tool for this purpose. We evaluated whether MALDI-TOF mass spectra acquired on VITEK MS PRIME, combined with machine learning, could provide this information.

studi.t: Autoinhibition and conformational activation regulate cell-wall anchoring of the bacterial type IV pilus machinery
studi.s: Type IV pili are widespread bacterial nanomachines that mediate adhesion, motility and host interactions, yet the molecular mechanism coordinating assembly of their outer-membrane channel with attachment to the bacterial cell wall has remained unknown. Here, we show that the conserved PilQ-associated protein TsaP functions as a conformationally regulated envelope adaptor linking secretin assembly to cell-wall anchoring.

studi.t: Noninvasive Cardiac Arrest Recognition Using Wearable Sensors in a Porcine Model of Ventricular Fibrillation
studi.s: Background: Wearable detection of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) could improve survival, given the prognostic importance of time to resuscitation and that 50% to 75% of events are unwitnessed. Existing systems may be limited by their form factor and by specificity achieved at the cost of sensitivity. We investigated whether the raw photoplethysmography (PPG) signal from low-cost wearable sensors contains a distinct signature of circulatory arrest.

studi.t: What's in a Story? Studying Neural Narrative Engagement with Auditory Passages Using EEG Inter-Subject Correlation
studi.s: Narrative engagement - a state implicating attention as well as emotional and sequential processing - is crucial in contexts ranging from social interaction to education. Yet we still lack an understanding of how narrative contents and listener perceptions relate to the neural responses they elicit. In this study, we investigate relationships between auditory narratives and listener responses using electroencephalography inter-subject correlation (EEG-ISC), a measure of neural synchrony that has been shown to correlate with narrative cohesion, attention, preference, and learning.

studi.t: From individual movement to ecosystem response: how landscape structure shapes herbivore impacts
studi.s: Understanding how local interactions generate large-scale ecological dynamics is a central challenge in ecology. In heterogeneous environments, consumer movement links resource distribution with exploitation, producing responses that may not be predicted from consumer abundance or resource availability alone. Here, we develop a spatially explicit stochastic individual-based model of two herbivore populations with contrasting movement and foraging strategies that share renewable resources.

studi.t: Phenotypic plasticity reshapes the evolution of species coexistence
studi.s: Modern coexistence theory (MCT) has been the mainstay of recent research on coexistence of competing species. Competition not only drives evolutionary changes in traits that affect coexistence, but also induces rapid plastic changes. However, a generalised framework that integrates plasticity and evolution into MCT is lacking. We formulate such a framework for a system of two competing species and analyse how breadth of available resources modulates the effect of competition-induced plasticity on the evolution of coexistence components (niche and fitness difference).

studi.t: Origin tracing and detection lag in the first Aedes albopictus invasion of mainland Australia and a long-term genomic dataset of mosquito incursions
studi.s: Proactive management of invasive species aims to prevent and eradicate new incursions before they establish. Genomic data can assist proactive management around how to deploy resources and when to change strategies, and has been used effectively in managing Aedes albopictus (Asian tiger mosquito) in the Australian Northern Peninsula Area over the past decade. This study characterises the first major incursion of Ae. albopictus on the Australian mainland, and contrasts this with long-term genomic monitoring of this species within the Torres Strait Islands (TSI).

studi.t: Intragenic redistribution of RNA polymerase II licenses epigenetic silencing
studi.s: Co-transcriptional chromatin regulation is widely recognized as a mechanism that reinforces active gene expression, yet transcriptionally active genes must also be able to transition into stable epigenetic silencing during developmental transitions and environmental responses. Whether and how ongoing transcription is coupled to the initiation of epigenetic silencing remains unclear. Here we show that elongating RNA polymerase II phosphorylated at Ser2 (RNAPII-Ser2P) functions as an instructive signal for epigenetic silencing initiation.

studi.t: Single-cell study of the FCG rat model and cross-species comparison reveal stronger gene regulation by sex chromosome complement in the medial septum
studi.s: Sex differences are prominent in neuropsychiatric, neurological, and neurodegenerative conditions. While both gonads (ovaries vs. testes) and sex chromosome complement (SCC; XX vs. XY) contribute to sex differences, these effects are hard to differentiate in humans and gonadal contributions have been considered dominant in the brain. The four core genotypes (FCG) mouse model distinguishes between SCC and gonadal effects but whether findings are conserved across species remains unclear.

studi.t: Pangenome-guided interpretation of k-mer GWAS inCapsicum
studi.s: Agronomic trait diversity in Capsicum is shaped by sequence variation that it is not always captured by SNPs called against a single reference genome. Reference-free k-mer GWAS can detect variants beyond SNPs, but significant k-mers are difficult to interpret as they lack genomic coordinates and annotation. In this study, we developed a pangenome-guided workflow to localize significant k-mers in a graph-based Capsicum pangenome. The workflow connects significant k-mers, identified through k-mer GWAS, to genomic positions, their annotations and homology groups.

studi.t: Combinatorial perturbation structure enables graded inference of signaling activity by CIRCE
studi.s: Cells decode external inputs into intracellular activities of varying magnitude, and inferring both input identity and strength is crucial for cell-fate engineering. However, perturbation-response models typically treat all cells exposed to a given input as a discrete class, ignoring cell-to-cell variation in response magnitude. Here, we introduce a structured-label framework that infers both input identity and strength from combinatorial perturbation screens without dose-resolved training labels.

studi.t: MDQ: A DockQ-Inspired Scoring Function for Assessing Interface Similarity and Clustering in Molecular Dynamics
studi.s: Assessing the similarity between protein-protein interfaces is essential for evaluating docking models, yet widely used metrics such as DockQ rely on a single native reference structure and yield asymmetric scores, making them unsuitable for molecular dynamics (MD) trajectories where no reference exists and frame-to-frame comparisons are required. Here, we introduce the MDQ, a fully symmetric reformulation of DockQ designed for MD trajectory analysis.

studi.t: TERRA engages MDA5 to shape the immune landscape in ALT brain tumors
studi.s: In cancer, telomere maintenance is mediated by telomerase reactivation or by the alternative lengthening of telomere (ALT) pathway. Both mechanisms contribute to cancer cell replicative immortality, but ALT, generates telomere instability and promotes inflammation, thus contributing to cancer progression also through non-cell autonomous mechanisms. How ALT telomeres modulate inflammatory signals in cancer is not fully understood, mostly because of the lack of organismal models of ALT+ cancers.

studi.t: Targeting the YAP1/TAZ-TEAD Transcriptional Axis Reveals a Therapeutic Vulnerability in Androgen Receptor Signaling Inhibitor (ARSI)-Resistant Prostate Cancer
studi.s: Therapeutic resistance remains a major barrier in advanced prostate cancer (PCa), particularly after prolonged treatment with second-generation androgen receptor signaling inhibitors (ARSIs) such as enzalutamide. Tumors can evade these drugs by escaping androgen receptor (AR) dependence through cellular plasticity and lineage transitions, but alternative resistance networks remain poorly understood. Enzalutamide-resistant (ENZ-R) PCa cells showed marked activation and nuclear enrichment of the YAP-1/TAZ-TEAD complex.

studi.t: PRC2-mediated H3K27me3 uncouples PHE1 binding from transcriptional activation at imprinted genes
studi.s: Genomic imprinting results in parent-of-origin-dependent gene expression and plays an important role in endosperm development. The type I MADS-box transcription factor PHERES1 (PHE1) has been implicated in the regulation of imprinted genes, particularly paternally expressed genes (PEGs). Silencing of the maternal alleles of PEGs is mediated by repressive histone modifications, including H3K27me3 established by the Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2).

studi.t: A standardized mosquito-to-mouse transmission assay with spatially defined bite areas
studi.s: Mosquito-borne viruses initiate infection in the skin, where interactions between viral particles, host cells, and mosquito saliva can influence early infection and subsequent viral dissemination. Investigating these events requires methods that link mosquito exposure to the precise site of inoculation. However, identifying individual bite sites during subsequent tissue collection remains a practical challenge in mosquito-to-mouse transmission models.

studi.t: Retinal Vessel Volume Density and Intraoperative Cortical Vascular Phenotypes in Moyamoya Disease
studi.s: Background Angiographic staging describes large-artery stenosis and collateral evolution in moyamoya disease but does not directly depict the cortical surface vasculature, which can vary among patients with similar Suzuki stages. We examined whether a side-matched three-dimensional retinal vascular measure was associated with intraoperative cortical vascular phenotypes after accounting for Suzuki stage.

studi.t: Early locus coeruleus tauopathy features potassium channel dysfunction and is attenuated by Kv7 activation
studi.s: Background The locus coeruleus (LC) accumulates abnormal tau early in Alzheimer's disease, yet the mechanisms linking early tauopathy to neuronal dysfunction and the potential to modify subsequent pathology remain unclear. We investigated potassium-dependent excitability control, associated molecular 5 changes and Kv7-targeted intervention. Methods We combined electrophysiology, single-cell RNA sequencing, immunohistochemistry and sleep-electroencephalographic recordings in P301S tau transgenic (PS19) mice and wild-type mice receiving local LC inoculation of synthetic human tau fibrils.

studi.t: Overexpression of α synuclein in Midbrain Dopamine Neurons Drives Learning Deficits in Mice
studi.s: Parkinson disease (PD) is diagnosed based on core motor features. However, changes in cognitive function are often already present. Cognitive symptoms include changes in executive function, including organization, planning, multi-tasking, and flexible decision-making. These early cognitive deficits have been difficult to model and remain understudied. Here, we investigated whether AAV-based overexpression of wild-type human alpha-synuclein (syn) in midbrain dopaminergic neurons can produce deficits in learning and behavioral flexibility.

studi.t: Chronic stress reduces behavioural flexibility and autonomic adaptation when aversive outcomes are controllable
studi.s: Chronic stress is associated with altered adaptation to threat, yet its effects on aversive learning under varying threat predictability and controllability remain unclear. Thirty participants with chronic stress and thirty healthy controls completed a task to learn how well visual cues predicted upcoming electric shocks (predictability) and whether correct predictions of shocks could reduce shock intensity (controllability).

studi.t: Neural mechanisms of lightness constancy
studi.s: Object-specific variables are entangled in sensory input. For example, lightness, whether a surface is white or black, not only depends on the surface reflectance but also on the incident illumination. The brain must thus perform inference to achieve a reliable percept of lightness irrespective of illumination (lightness constancy). Whether this results from simple luminance contrast operations early in the visual system or computations at higher levels remains unresolved.

studi.t: Microglia and microglia activation are protective in an LSD1-induced model of neurodegeneration
studi.s: Attempts to determine the function of microglia activation and the immune system in neurodegenerative diseases have yielded conflicting results, with some data showing a protective effect, while other data shows a detrimental effect. This discrepancy in the function of microglia activation and the immune system in neurodegeneration likely stems from differing functions during the build-up of pathological proteins versus later stage defects.

studi.t: Tumor cell-intrinsic AHR sustains IFNγ responsiveness and durable CD8 T-cell-mediated melanoma control
studi.s: The aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) regulates melanoma differentiation and progression, but its tumor cell-intrinsic role in T-cell immunotherapy remains incompletely understood. Since AHR promotes inflammation-induced melanoma dedifferentiation, we hypothesized that AHR deficiency would reduce resistance to adoptive CD8 T-cell therapy (ACT) targeting melanocytic differentiation antigens. Unexpectedly, AHR-deficient HCmel12 melanomas exhibited more frequent delayed resistance to CD8 ACT despite initially impaired tumor growth.

studi.t: The MHC requirement for αβ T-cell specification is heterochronically gated
studi.s: Major histocompatibility complex (MHC)-dependent thymic selection is a defining principle of {beta} T-cell development, yet mice lacking {beta}2m-dependent MHC class I and MHC class II retain rare {beta} T cells whose developmental significance has remained unresolved. Here we show that this residual compartment is not simply the product of failed selection. Single-cell and clonotypic profiling resolves distinct outcomes, including clonally restricted CD4-associated states and a diversified CD8 {beta} T-cell population that converges on physiological wild-type virtual memory.

studi.t: Two novel plant-derived yeast species in Thailandicola (Microbotryomycetes): comparative genomics and transformation
studi.s: Plant tissues and surfaces are among the largest microbial habitats on Earth, and commensal yeasts are common members of these communities, where they can contribute to plant-microbe interactions including the biological control of plant diseases. Here, we describe two novel species of unpigmented, basidiomycete yeasts, in the class Microbotryomycetes from the plant phyllosphere (Thailandicola erigeronia and T. cardamina) represented by three isolates from leaves of multiple hosts.

studi.t: A small molecule inhibits Neisseria gonorrhoeae pilus formation
studi.s: Neisseria gonorrhoeae is becoming increasingly antimicrobial-resistant. N. gonorrhoeae requires the Type IV pilus (T4p) for pathogenesis, wherein the T4p promotes colonization through adherence to host cells and resistance to neutrophil killing. The pilus also is required for natural transformation and twitching motility. Collectively, these critical functions make the T4p an attractive drug target. Previously, we developed a high-throughput screen to identify compounds with activity against the zinc metalloprotease Mpg, which is involved in T4p biogenesis.

studi.t: Comparative landscape of extracellular vesicles across three pathogenic trematodes identifies a key conserved miRNA cargo involved in host liver fibrosis
studi.s: Liver fibrosis caused by Schistosoma japonicum, Clonorchis sinensis, and Opisthorchis felineus represents a major global public health burden. Here, we systematically characterized extracellular vesicles (EVs) released by key stages of these parasites and uncovered, for the first time, a conserved repertoire of EV-derived miRNAs shared across all three species. By integrating animal models, single-cell RNA sequencing, and bioinformatic analyses, we comprehensively identified the targetome of miR-36-3p, a cross-species conserved miRNA cargo.

studi.t: Mutations in core Ccr4-NOT subunits manifest links to decapping rather than deadenylation in Saccharomyces cerevisiae
studi.s: The mRNA polyadenosine tail (pA-tail) is gradually shortened in the cytoplasm by two main deadenylase complexes, Ccr4-NOT and Pan2/3, eventually leading to decapping and decay. The yeast Ccr4-NOT complex contains two deadenylases, Ccr4 and Pop2, and seven non-catalytic subunits. The functions of the latter are not yet fully understood. Here, we investigate the role of Ccr4-NOT in RNA metabolism in budding yeast.

studi.t: Endogenous activation of multiple stress-response pathways during meiosis promotes gamete fitness
studi.s: Gametogenesis, the process of meiosis coupled to gamete formation, transforms diploid progenitor cells into haploid gametes through extensive cellular remodeling and rewiring of gene expression. Several stress-responsive transcription factors (TFs) are upregulated during gametogenesis, but whether the cellular mechanisms that handle environmental stress also support the success of this developmental process is largely unexplored.

studi.t: Loss of SRF-driven contractility, not lymphatic smooth muscle cell loss, is the primary driver of age-associated collecting vessel decline
studi.s: The lymphatic vasculature returns interstitial fluid to the blood circulation, a function that depends on rhythmic contraction of the smooth muscle cells (SMCs) surrounding collecting vessels. Lymph transport declines with age, a decline attributed largely to loss of SMCs from collecting vessels. We show that the principal change is not their loss but the loss of their contractile phenotype. In mouse ear collecting vessels, contractile protein expression declined with age and the vessels dilated, yet the majority of SMCs remained on the vessel wall.

studi.t: Inactive X chromosome DNA methylation erosion with age in human dermal fibroblasts
studi.s: X chromosome inactivation is an epigenetic process that establishes dosage compensation between the sexes through the monoallelic silencing of one X chromosome in karyotypically normal females. The allele that becomes inactivated is determined randomly during early development, resulting in females being mosaic with respect to whether the maternal or paternal allele is inactivated.

studi.t: Large-scale 3D stitching montage cryo-electron tomography reveals heterogeneity and connectivity of lamellipodial actin networks
studi.s: Cellular processes range from local interactions among a few proteins to micrometer-scale assemblies whose coordinated components give rise to emergent properties. A prime example is the actin cytoskeleton in protrusive structures at the leading edge of migrating cells, termed lamellipodia. Significant progress has been made in understanding the functional contributions of distinct actin-filament populations and associated proteins within lamellipodia.

studi.t: Individual symbiont strains can compensate for complex microbiome loss in the bull-headed dung beetle, Onthophagus taurus
studi.s: Many animals and plants have evolved to rely on microbiome mediated interactions with their environment. Across diverse insect groups, many are incapable of either breaking down complex carbohydrates or synthesizing essential nutrients despite consuming diets which should require one, or both, functions. Onthophagus beetles are one such host, with recent work suggesting their ability to digest their dung diet, typically rich in tough to digest polysaccharides and poor in nutrients, is likely bolstered by heritable symbionts.

studi.t: A genetic toolkit of visible mutants for Caenorhabditis briggsae
studi.s: Caenorhabditis briggsae is a widely used model for comparative genetic studies involving C. elegans. Genetic analysis in C. briggsae depends on mutations with clear, easily recognizable phenotypes, yet most mutants reported so far have been mentioned only as names and linkage groups, without underlying experimental data. This study reports 183 C. briggsae mutants belonging to 11 phenotypic classes, which represent the most comprehensive collection to date. Almost all mutants were recovered in EMS screens of the reference strain AF16.

studi.t: Evaluating cell-free RNA extraction platforms for RNA liquid biopsy via nanopore sequencing
studi.s: RNA liquid biopsies provide systemic insights into health and disease by profiling cell-free RNAs (cfRNAs) secreted into the circulation. While cfRNAs are thought to be short or fragmented, recent efforts using long-read nanopore sequencing have found that thousands of longer, full-length cfRNAs are highly abundant in plasma. However, cfRNA extraction methods have not been rigorously evaluated to assess reproducibility, cfRNA length, and transcriptome complexity.

studi.t: A recombinant expression system for the Variant Surface Glycoproteins enables structural elucidation of challenging classes of trypanosome proteins
studi.s: The African Trypanosome (Trypanosoma brucei) persists in the mammalian host by periodically altering its surface coat with antigenically distinct versions of the Variant Surface Glycoprotein (VSG). This process is called antigenic variation and produces repeated cycles of immune clearance and parasite VSG switching, leading to high morbidity and mortality in the absence of chemotherapeutic intervention. Elucidating how variant VSGs evade immune clearance is thus central to understanding trypanosomiasis.

studi.t: Molecular Conformer Sampling Beyond Generations
studi.s: Sampling the low-energy conformational states available to a molecule is a fundamental problem in computational chemistry and drug discovery, since molecular properties and downstream design decisions depend on the relevant three-dimensional geometries rather than on a single structure. Recent diffusion and flow-based generative models can efficiently sample conformer candidates from molecular graphs, but under a fixed output budget their samples do not cover the full set of relevant conformational states of a molecule, while practical benchmarks and downstream applications require a small…

studi.t: Modeling Aerobic-Anaerobic Microbial Electrolysis Cells for Multi-step Methane Conversion
studi.s: The bioconversion of methane by anaerobic methanotrophs has a higher carbon and energy efficiency compared to aerobic processes, suggesting significant potential for producing value-added chemicals and reducing green-house-gas emissions. However, their practical use still faces many challenges regarding their culturing, genetic manipulation, and integration into multi-species consortia.

studi.t: A midnight snack for spirulina: a dual-substrate kinetic model for second cheese whey supplementation of Arthrospira platensis
studi.s: Arthrospira platensis (Spirulina) is a widely used strategic cyanobacterium whose cultivation cost remains a primary barrier to large-scale production. Mixotrophic growth on dairy by-products offers a simultaneous route to increase biomass concentration and valorize industrial waste streams. Here, we investigate the effect of Parmigiano Reggiano second cheese whey supplementation on A. platensis batch cultivation under continuous and alternating photoperiods. Whey supplementation increased final biomass in a dose-dependent manner under both continuous and alternating light.

studi.t: Mass Transfer Formulations Shape Oxygen Transport and Tissue Oxygenation in Microvascular Networks
studi.s: Continuous oxygen delivery is essential for cerebral tissue function, yet its local supply characteristics remain incompletely understood. Quantifying oxygen transport in microvascular networks (MVNs) requires a physiologically consistent description of oxygen exchange between vascular compartments via mass transfer coefficients (MTCs). We investigate how different MTC formulations influence oxygen availability and hypoxic burden in realistic MVNs, and whether they produce relevant local differences in tissue oxygenation.

studi.t: Replicate libraries set the noise floor for cell-state claims in cross-sectional single-cell data: an empirical audit in drug-tolerant EGFR-mutant PC9 cells
studi.s: Claims that drug-tolerant cancer cells occupy stable states rest on single-cell snapshots with one sequencing library per condition, where a difference between conditions cannot be separated from a difference between libraries. No standard says how far a contrast must exceed replicate-library variation. We contribute a replicate-referenced framework: a distance ratio expressing a contrast as a multiple of the distance between replicate libraries of one condition, and a library-level permutation test giving exact p values by relabelling whole libraries.

studi.t: RR3DD 2.0: an expanded database for RNA three-dimensional structure classification
studi.s: RNA performs diverse biological functions by folding into specific 3D structures, which are often more conserved than their sequences. Systematic classification of RNA 3D structures is fundamental to understanding structure-function relationships. We previously established RR3DD, the first classification database based on global 3D structural similarity. However, its version 1.0 contained data only up to July 2021 and can no longer reflect the rapidly growing RNA structure space since then. Here, we present RR3DD 2.0.

studi.t: Period-Specific Remodeling of Luminal Lineages and the Mammary Microenvironment in Dairy Goats
studi.s: Milk production requires coordinated remodeling of mammary epithelial lineages and their stromal and immune niches, but this process is incompletely resolved in dairy goats. We aim to define period specific cell states and epithelial niche interactions across the dry to lactation transition. We profile mammary tissue from three peak-lactation and three dry-period Saanen goats using 10x Genomics single-cell RNA sequencing and map one peak-lactation goat with Stereo-seq. Among 44,120 cells, we identify15 populations.

studi.t: SIREN: Predicting RNA-Small Molecule Interaction using Language Models without Requiring Structure
studi.s: RNA-targeted drug discovery is constrained by the scarcity of resolved RNA tertiary structures and the conformational flexibility of RNA, which limit the applicability of structure-based virtual screening. Here, SIREN (Small molecule Interaction with RNA via sEquence-based predictioN) is presented, a sequence-based framework that ranks small molecules for a given RNA target directly from its primary sequence without requiring tertiary structure.

studi.t: Sequence-Derived Geometric Priors Enable Controllable Generation of Intrinsically Disordered Protein Ensembles
studi.s: Predicting heterogeneous conformational ensembles from sequence remains a central challenge for intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs). Sequence-to-ensemble models often entangle geometric inference with coordinate generation, obscuring error sources and limiting control over ensemble properties. Here we introduce MANTA, a C-level framework that separates these stages. An encoder derives geometric priors from protein language-model representations, and a graph-Laplacian decoder converts these priors into conformational ensembles.

studi.t: GPU handling of OPC water in GROMACS: validation by protein folding and a 1.6-fold speed-up
studi.s: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulation is one of the core computational methods of the life sciences, used to study protein folding, receptor activation and drug binding in atomic detail. The timescales it can reach depend on speed, and running each step entirely on a graphics processing unit (GPU) is now essential for fast simulation. Optimal Point Charge (OPC) water, recommended for the ff19SB protein force field, carries its negative charge on a virtual site, and in GROMACS 2026.3 virtual sites prevent the coordinate update from running on the GPU.

studi.t: Hearts in sync on a roller coaster: heart-rate responses, synchrony and psychological change in 439 amusement-park riders
studi.s: Background Shared intense experiences are thought to bring people closer, and synchronized physiology is a proposed reason. We examined heart rate and synchrony across ride phases, riders' response profiles, and whether these relate to changes in happiness, stress and closeness. Methods In this exploratory field study we recorded heart rate in 439 riders (418 with usable data) on 19 trains of the Balder roller coaster, Gothenburg, Sweden, and measured happiness, stress and closeness (0-10) just before and after the ride.

studi.t: Gene regulatory networks and the organization of cell differentiation in multicellular organisms
studi.s: Across their development, clonal multicellular organisms generate new cell types from less differentiated cell types. Differentiation pathways arrange into a hierarchical, tree-like organization: regressions from specialized to undifferentiated cell types rarely occur and undifferentiated cell types often have the potential to produce, when subject to distinct stimuli, two or more differently specialized cell types.

studi.t: Neural competition predicts speech production advantages in congenital amusia
studi.s: Mental health research has traditionally been deficit-focused, and cognitive advantages in mental conditions have almost always been documented retrospectively. Here we propose and test an a priori pathway for predicting such advantages from a conditions impaired neural basis, neural competition and brain-mind associations.

studi.t: Resident liver macrophages buffer dietary and circulating cholesterol to maintain hepatocyte homeostasis
studi.s: Cholesterol metabolism is viewed largely through the lens of hepatocytes, leaving the roles of other liver cells unclear. Using high-resolution live imaging and cholesterol tracing in intact zebrafish, complemented by genetic and clodronate-mediated macrophage depletion and single-cell analysis, we identify liver-resident macrophages (LMs) as cellular buffers of circulating and dietary cholesterol.

studi.t: Spatiotemporal Dynamics and Environmental Drivers of Maize Microbiome Structure across Diverse Agroecosystems in Georgia, USA
studi.s: The understanding of how microbial communities differ across soils, environments, plant tissues, and developmental stages is key to the improvement of crop productivity and resilience. Here, we conducted a statewide survey of maize (Zea mays L.) microbiomes across 35 fields at 16 locations in Georgia, USA, sampling soil, rhizosphere, root interior, and stalk interior at two developmental stages (600 and 1400 growing degree days, GDD). More than 38000 ASVs were produced after amplicon sequencing of 16S rRNA genes.

studi.t: Precision Fermentation Gets a New Player: Genome Assembly and Genetic Transformation of a Novel Strain, Pichia hangzhouana, for Precision Fermentation of Food Ingredients
studi.s: Precision fermentation leverages the metabolic pathways of microorganisms to produce valuable proteins and enzymes. Pichia hangzhouana, synonymous with Zygoascus hellenicus, is a non-conventional yeast with potential for food biotechnological applications. This study characterizes the CSIRO strain P. hangzhouana FRR5246, isolated from a tea beverage, to evaluate its suitability as a precision fermentation host for a variety of industrial, agricultural and food production applications. P.

studi.t: Sexual competition can select for male-only semelparity
studi.s: Semelparity, - reproducing once in a lifetime - is an extreme solution to the trade-off between reproduction and future survival and is exceedingly rare in terrestrial vertebrates. Males of the Australian genera Antechinus, Phascogale and Dasykaluta are obligately semelparous while females are iteroparous, suggesting that the sexes face such different selective pressures that they have evolved different solutions to the same trade-off.

studi.t: Caenorhabditis elegans HLH-30/TFEB has age-dependent effects on the transcriptome and is required for normal progeny number and larval survival under basal growth conditions
studi.s: Background: The transcription factor TFEB/HLH-30 is a well-established regulator of autophagy and lysosomal biogenesis during starvation and stress, and it plays important roles in development and homeostasis. Our previous work demonstrated that Caenorhabditis elegans HLH-30 also functions under basal physiological conditions in mature neurons, where it promotes the expansion of endo-lysosomal degradative capacity during early adulthood.

studi.t: Mapping Senescence Landscapes in Metabolic Liver Disease Progression
studi.s: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects more than 30% of the population, often progressing from reversible steatosis to irreversible fibrosis and cirrhosis. Although cellular senescence is implicated in driving MASLD, the evidence in human tissue and the mechanism are lacking. Here, we apply spatial transcriptomics and scRNAseq to human liver samples spanning healthy to fibrotic disease to address these knowledge gaps.

studi.t: CorridorKit: Open-source software for geometric comparison of skull base surgical corridors
studi.s: CorridorKit is open-source research software for comparing rigid surgical access corridors in physical image coordinates. Its Python engine represents finite instruments, circular portals, target samples, and protected geometry, and keeps evaluated paths linked to their reached samples, insertion depths, and clearance states through command-line, desktop, and 3D Slicer interfaces. In a reproducible 413-sample phantom, two portals reached 94 and 267 samples, with 326 in their union. Numerical verification included 82 analytical angular comparisons and 4,720 voxel-distance queries.

studi.t: Spatial metabolic ecosystems shape the architecture of IDH-mutant glioma
studi.s: The principles governing tissue organization in IDH-mutant glioma remain poorly understood, particularly in the absence of hypoxia and necrosis that define IDH-wildtype glioblastoma. Here, we integrated spatial transcriptomics, metabolomics and histology across co-registered serial tissue sections, generating a multidimensional atlas of IDH-mutant glioma. Integration with an independent spatial transcriptomics cohort and a single cell atlas (n=101 samples), enabled resolution of metabolic and cellular heterogeneity underlying tissue organization.

studi.t: Rapid enhancement of antibiotic resistance and divergent remodeling of gene expression in single cells of bacteria
studi.s: Exposing bacterial cell populations to antibiotics often results in the emergence of descendants with enhanced resistance. Phenotypic heterogeneity and global physiological responses are thought to contribute to resistance evolution. However, identifying the specific stages of drug exposure where phenotypic heterogeneity and physiological responses play critical roles remains elusive.

studi.t: A Novel Autoantibody against LAG-3 in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
studi.s: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is an autoimmune disease characterized by immune tolerance loss, although its pathogenesis remains incompletely understood. Immune checkpoint molecules maintain peripheral tolerance, and their dysregulation contributes to autoimmunity. Autoantibodies against lymphocyte activation gene-3 (LAG-3), an immune checkpoint molecule, were identified in a subset of patients with SLE. We enrolled 130 patients with SLE, 119 patients with other autoimmune diseases, and 32 healthy controls.

studi.t: Litter Microbiome Composition in Commercial Broiler Houses Under Contrasting Management: A Pilot Study
studi.s: Litter management affects broiler health, performance, and environmental impact, yet the effects of litter-applied amendments on the resident microbiome remain poorly characterized, particularly under commercial conditions. This pilot study evaluated the litter microbiome of three commercial broiler houses under contrasting management regimens. Two houses received a postbiotic litter amendment combined with sodium bisulfate (NaHSO) at 40% of the standard rate for one or two consecutive flocks, while a control house received the standard NaHSO rate alone.

studi.t: Deletion of Furin Facilitates Efficient and Versatile Coronavirus Pseudotyped Particle Generation
studi.s: Coronaviruses bring threats to both humans and animals. To initiate successful infections, coronaviruses must first navigate entry into a host cell. Coronavirus spike-bearing pseudotyped particle systems are indispensable tools for studying coronavirus entry and evaluating neutralizing antibodies and entry inhibitors. However, pseudotyped particle titers can be low when packaged particles bear coronavirus spikes that contain the furin cleavage site, and this has been a limitation for pseudotyped particle production and applications.

studi.t: Genomic Characterization of a Typical Enteropathogenic Escherichia coli Isolate from an Egyptian Fruit Bat, Rousettus aegyptiacus from Coastal Kenya
studi.s: Enteropathogenic Escherichia coli (EPEC) are responsible for significant morbidity and mortality cases among young children under the age of five, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Atypical EPEC has frequently been reported from animal hosts, however, information on the occurrence and genomic characteristics of typical EPEC in wildlife reservoirs remains limited. This study characterized an Escherichia coli isolated from an Egyptian fruit bat (Rousettus aegyptiacus) sampled in coastal Kenya using whole-genome sequencing.

studi.t: Environmental heterogeneity and microbial community architecture shape N2O fluxes in intertidal coastal sediments
studi.s: Seagrass meadows are key ''blue carbon ecosystems'', yet their contribution to nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions remains poorly constrained. We investigated environmental and microbial descriptors of N2O fluxes in intertidal sediments of Arcachon Bay, home to Europe's largest Zostera noltii meadow. At six sites, we measured in situ N2O fluxes in adjacent bare and vegetated sediments and characterized sediment properties, N2O-cycling genes using qPCR and targeted metagenomics, and microbial co-occurrence networks. Fluxes ranged from -3.7 to 8.4 mol N2O m-2 d-1.

studi.t: Multi-Cohort Blood Transcriptomic Meta-Analysis of Active Pulmonary Tuberculosis: Reproducibility of a 50-Gene Interferon Signature and Benchmarking of a 4-Gene Classifier
studi.s: Background: Most blood transcriptomic signatures for tuberculosis (TB) come from a single population or a single platform. Few have been built by meta-analysis and benchmarked against published signatures. Methods: We meta-analysed three UK blood transcriptomic datasets (two Illumina microarray, one RNA-seq; 247 samples: 87 active pulmonary TB (PTB), 160 healthy controls (HC)). GSE107991 reanalyses the Berry test set, and two discovery datasets overlap Sweeney's discovery data, so the datasets are not fully independent.

studi.t: Electron Transport Chain-inhibiting fungicides increase resistance to widely used azole antifungals
studi.s: Rising antifungal resistance in human and crop fungal pathogens poses significant challenges. Azole-based antifungals that inhibit ergosterol biosynthesis are a key first-line treatment for human fungal infections. Importantly, azole-based ergosterol-inhibiting fungicides are also widely used in agriculture alongside electron transport chain (ETC) Complex III inhibiting compounds. However, it is unknown whether the combined use of these distinct fungicides is entirely synergistic.

studi.t: Emergence of mobile fosA3-blaCTX-M-65 with mcr-1.1 and tet(X4) on conjugative plasmids in avian pathogenic Escherichia coli from industrial poultry in Pakistan
studi.s: The emergence of plasmid-mediated resistance to critically important antimicrobials poses a growing threat to global health. Here we report the first genomic evidence of plasmid-mediated fosA3 and blaCTX-M-65 coexisting with mcr-1.1 and tet(X4) in multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli from clinically healthy broiler chickens in Pakistan. Among 1,677 high-quality genomes collected through antimicrobial resistance surveillance in Punjab, Pakistan, three isolates recovered between 2022 and 2024 harboured all four resistance determinants.

studi.t: TrES-seq integrates single-cell RNA and nanobody-based histone mark profiles to decode epigenetic and transcriptional axes of cell identity
studi.s: Histone post-translational modifications and gene expression jointly shape cellular identity and activity. However, systematically assessing their heterogeneity and functional interdependence requires high-quality multimodal single-cell readouts, whose generation still faces significant technological challenges. Here, we developed TrES-seq (transcriptional and epigenetic state sequencing), a method that integrates scRNA-seq with species-specific nanobody Tn5 fusion proteins to jointly profile RNA and two histone modifications in the same cells and across multiple samples.

studi.t: ADP-ribosylation governs the repair of topoisomerase IIIβ-induced nucleic acid damage
studi.s: Abortive DNA and RNA-linked covalent cleavage complexes formed by the unique dual-activity human topoisomerase III{beta} (TOP3B) disrupt nucleic acid metabolism and can promote cancer cell death. Here, we identify poly(ADP-ribosylation) (PARylation) as a key pathway that regulates the repair and stability of both DNA- and RNA-linked TOP3B cleavage complexes (TOP3Bccs). We show that accumulated TOP3Bccs undergo rapid PARylation in a PARP1-dependent manner and that this modification is dynamically reversed by poly(ADP-ribose) glycohydrolase (PARG).

studi.t: Biotin-operated ligand trapping enables dynamic spatial redistribution of proteins and organelles in living cells
studi.s: Controlling protein localization through chemical biology tools is essential for mechanistic interrogations, functional perturbations, and therapeutic development. While existing tools cover a wide range of applications, no single approach simultaneously enables inducible trapping, controlled release, and visualization of a protein of interest (POI). To address this gap, we developed Biotin-Operated Ligand Trapping (BOLT), which combines a HaloTag-fused POI with a streptavidin trap.

studi.t: Wunen(s) help navigate Primordial Germ Cells by attenuating Hedgehog signaling
studi.s: Embryonic PGC migration in Drosophila is orchestrated by non-cell autonomous repulsive and attractive cues, controlled by Wunen(s) and, HMGCoA-reductase (Hmgcr), respectively. Hedgehog (Hh), a PGC attractant, is potentiated by Hmgcr. We demonstrate that Wunen(s) employ both nonautonomous and autonomous modes to inhibit Hh signaling.

studi.t: Onsager's relations and Ecology
studi.s: There are two complementary approaches to thermodynamics: an empirical, phenomenological representation of macroscopic states and a model-based, statistical-mechanical representation of microscopic states. When only a few energy transformation steps are involved, macroscopic quantities such as free energy and entropy can be estimated unambiguously alongside well-characterized microscopic states.

studi.t: Experimentally mimicking long term infections of Magallana gigas with the OsHV-1 virus reveals evolution through positive selection
studi.s: Ostreid herpesvirus 1 (OsHV-1) poses a significant threat to the global oyster farming industry, causing substantial economic losses due to mortality outbreaks. While OsHV-1 primarily affects the Pacific oyster Magallana gigas, it has also been associated with mortality events in various other host species. Despite progress in understanding OsHV-1 epidemiology, important knowledge gaps remain regarding its evolutionary mechanisms and adaptation to host genetic backgrounds.

studi.t: Deep learning design and in vivo validation of Müller glia-specific cis-regulatory elements
studi.s: Effective recombinant adeno-associated virus gene therapies require promoters that are compact and cell-type-specific. Ideally, promoters should also exhibit functional conservation when tested in model organisms to ensure that preclinical findings translate reliably to human patients. Here, we introduce a deep learning framework for designing cis-regulatory elements (CREs) meeting these criteria, applied to retinal Muller glia (MG).

studi.t: Identification of seven candidate structured noncoding RNA motifs in protists by comparative genomics
studi.s: Protists represent a highly diverse assemblage of predominantly unicellular eukaryotes, including protozoa, algae, and slime molds. Their essential roles in global ecosystems, along with their significance as human parasites, underscore the need for a deeper understanding of their conserved genetic elements. In this study, we employed an integrated computational approach combining CMfinder and R-scape to systematically identify and evaluate structured non-coding RNA (ncRNA) motifs across protist genomes.

studi.t: Organ context dominates cell identity across a multi-organ single-cell atlas of grapevine
studi.s: How transcriptional programs defining cell identity are maintained or remodeled across organ contexts remains a fundamental question in plant biology, particularly in long-lived perennials. We generated a multi-organ single-nucleus transcriptomic atlas of the dwarf grapevine cultivar Pixie, comprising over 220,000 nuclei from nine organs across vegetative and reproductive development, each sampled in two biological replicates.

studi.t: PAV-spotter: using signal cross-correlations to identify Presence/Absence Variation in target capture data
studi.s: High throughput sequencing technologies have become essential in the fields of evolutionary biology and genomics. When dealing with non-model organisms or genomic gigantism, sequencing whole genomes is still relatively costly and therefore reduced-genome representations are frequently obtained, for instance by target capture approaches. While computational tools exist that can handle target capture data and identify small-scale variants such as single nucleotide polymorphisms and micro-indels, options to identify large scale structural variants are limited.

studi.t: Generative design of antibody Fc interactions by deep mutational learning
studi.s: Antibodies have transformed modern medicine. Their remarkable therapeutic success stems from the fact that they do two things at once. The variable (Fab) domain recognizes a target, while the constant (Fc) domain determines how that recognition event is acted on by the immune system. The Fc carries out these instructions by interacting with a complex network of Fc-receptors expressed across diverse immune cells.

studi.t: Drug-Prot: A query system for statistical inference of drug effects and interactions in dynamic proteomic networks
studi.s: Understanding drug effects and drug-drug interactions is essential for developing combination therapies. We present Drug-Prot, a computational framework that leverages large-scale perturbation proteomics to quantify causal drug effects, drug-drug interactions, and dynamic protein relationships. Using data from 63 single drugs and 59 drug combinations applied to 16 triple-negative and 2 non-triple-negative breast cancer cell lines at 6, 24, and 48 hours, Drug-Prot estimates drug effects on protein expression and reconstructs directed temporal protein dependency networks.

studi.t: Quantitative Spatial Analysis of Matrix Remodelling in Wounds Using Digital Pathology and Fractal Analysis
studi.s: Wound healing involves spatially heterogeneous changes in matrix composition and organisation that can be difficult to capture using qualitative histological assessment alone. We developed a reproducible digital pathology workflow to quantify matrix features in cutaneous wound sections, compare them with unwounded skin, and derive an exploratory Histological Wound Index (HWI). Four normal-skin and six wound sections from patients with underlying vascular disease or diabetes were analysed using QuPath, ImageJ/FracLac and Python as a proof of principle.

studi.t: BEguided: Systematic guide and base editor evaluation for precision single-nucleotide editing
studi.s: Base editing enables precise nucleotide substitutions without introducing DNA double-strand breaks, but identifying optimal editor-guide combinations remains challenging because PAM compatibility, editing-window positioning, bystander modifications, and off-target effects must be considered simultaneously. Here, we introduce BEguided, an integrated computational platform for variant-specific guide RNA design and systematic comparison across 38 predefined base-editor profiles, with support for user-defined editors.

studi.t: A codon-sensitive conformational switch gates commitment to translation start sites
studi.s: Human translation initiation requires single-nucleotide precision to establish the reading frame, yet initiation at non-AUG codons plays key roles in gene expression. How the initiation machinery balances precision with this regulated flexibility remains unclear. Here, we define a conformational branchpoint governed by the human initiation factor eIF5 that gates commitment to start codons.

studi.t: Optimizing environmental conditions for PALM imaging of the nuclear pore complex labeled with the photoconvertible fluorescent protein mEos4b.
studi.s: Green-to-red photoconvertible fluorescent proteins (PCFPs) are smart fluorophores used in several nanoscopy approaches based on single-molecule localization microscopy (SMLM). To optimize the achievable spatial resolution and facilitate molecular counting in these approaches, PCFPs should deliver a high effective labeling efficiency (ELE).

studi.t: Shared Fine-Scale Functional Organization in the Human Subcortex Revealed by Connectivity Hyperalignment
studi.s: Subcortical structures are central to cognition, emotion, and social processing, and their dysfunction underlies a wide range of neurological and psychiatric conditions. Yet subcortical fine-scale functional organization has remained largely inaccessible to group-level fMRI analysis: nuclei are small and have low-SNR, and their functional topography varies idiosyncratically across individuals in ways that anatomical alignment cannot resolve. This idiosyncrasy carries real stakes.

studi.t: Visualizing whole-head neuronal activity and information-sharing dynamics in Caenorhabditis elegans during the transition into the anesthetized state.
studi.s: General anesthetics, such as isoflurane, induce immobility and decrease responsiveness to external stimuli. Our previous studies used C. elegans to investigate recovery from anesthesia, and established information-theory metrics characterizing how system-wide neuronal dynamics differ under these conditions. This study develops a novel technique enabling the corollary experiment: visualization of neuronal activity throughout the transition into the anesthetized state. C.

studi.t: Hyphal differentiation and cell wall remodeling in Trametes versicolor underlie a layered architecture in pure mycelium materials
studi.s: Background: Pure mycelium materials grown at the air-liquid interface are promising leather alternatives, yet they are generally treated as homogeneous sheets of fungal biomass. Because basidiomycetes differentiate their hyphae into generative, skeletal and ligative cell types, the properties of such materials may instead arise from an internal tissue organisation.

studi.t: On improving experimental binding affinity predictions with synthetic data
studi.s: The success of deep learning binding affinity prediction models depends critically on expanding experimental data with reliable synthetic data. We extend the Structurally Augmented IC50 Repository (SAIR) with {approx}80K absolute free energy perturbation (AFEP) calculations and present two distinct data splits, SAIR-FEP and SAIR-OOD (out-of-distribution), to simulate realistic drug discovery scenarios.

studi.t: A Standalone PD-1 Chimeric Switch Receptor T-Cell Platform Expands the Therapeutic Window of PD-L1 Targeting in Solid Tumors
studi.s: Programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) is a promising therapeutic target owing to its broad expression on tumor cells and immunosuppressive myeloid cells within the tumor microenvironment (TME), providing an opportunity to target both cellular compartments. However, physiological PD-L1 expression in normal tissues poses a substantial risk of on-target/off-tumor toxicity, limiting the therapeutic window and clinical translation of PD-L1-targeted cellular therapies.

studi.t: α-Synuclein and γ-Tubulin Cooperatively Regulate Activity-Evoked Presynaptic Microtubule Nucleation to Gate Dopamine Release
studi.s: How -synuclein regulates activity-dependent dopamine neurotransmission remains a longstanding question in synaptic biology. Here, we uncover a mechanism by which -synuclein couples neuronal activity to interbouton synaptic vesicle (SV) transport and the local assembly of microtubules (MTs) at boutons. Using live imaging of dopaminergic neurons, we discover that neuronal activity triggers {gamma}-tubulin-dependent MT nucleation preferentially at sites of SV fusion, promoting interbouton SV transport and striatal dopamine release.

studi.t: CYB-4/CDK-1 define temporal windows for chromosome morphogenesis during meiotic prophase in C. elegans
studi.s: Meiotic chromosome segregation requires the earlier coordination of chromosome morphogenesis with cell-cycle progression. In C. elegans, chromosome remodelling in preparation for the meiotic divisions is regulated by the master cell-cycle regulator CDK-1, but the cyclin directing its activity in prophase was unknown. Here, we identify CYB-4 as a meiosis-specific B-type cyclin that controls the timing of chromosome axis assembly and bivalent restructuring.

studi.t: Environment and host infection history jointly predict disease risk in a multi-pathogen system
studi.s: Forecasting disease epidemics may require considering both abiotic and biotic conditions. Abiotic conditions can influence pathogen dispersal, survival, and infection, while prior infection by one pathogen species can alter host susceptibility to subsequent pathogens, creating historical contingencies. Yet the relative importance of environmental conditions, within-host pathogen interactions, and their interplay in predicting seasonal disease dynamics remains underexplored.

studi.t: Assessing planktivorous fish as vectors of a plankton parasite
studi.s: According to the "healthy herd hypothesis," which posits that predators can reduce parasite prevalence in prey populations by preferentially removing infected individuals, predators are often thought to regulate disease in their prey. However, predators may also act as disease vectors, facilitating the spread of parasites. Here we investigate whether stickleback fish (Gasterosteus aculeatus) act as vectors in the transmission of the obligate bacterial parasite Pasteuria ramosa to its Daphnia host, a widespread freshwater zooplanktor. We fed infected D.

studi.t: RAD: A Read-structure Agnostic Demultiplexer for Single-Cell Long-Read Sequencing and Analysis
studi.s: Single-cell long-read sequencing (LRS) techniques enable the analysis of full transcript sequences within a cell. However, LRS introduces computational challenges for parsing information, often necessitating the development of custom workflows to handle complex read layouts, such as split combinatorial barcodes. To address these challenges, we introduce an error-robust, read-structure agnostic demultiplexer (RAD). In RAD, users can easily specify read structure, such as adapter sequence and relative barcode position, and can rapidly extract these elements for each read.

studi.t: Neural representation of action grammar structure in primate frontal cortex
studi.s: Humans and other animals rapidly solve novel problems, often on the first attempt. This capacity is hypothesized to rely on grammars, or internalized systems of abstract rules for recombining units of knowledge into novel composites. Yet, whether and how the brain realizes grammars remains unclear. Here we identify a neural population that represents the latent structure of a grammar.

studi.t: Movement refinement and cholinergic regulation of outcome-dependent updating during skilled reaching.
studi.s: Motor skill learning transforms initially variable actions into precise and reproducible movements. Because conventional measures of task success obscure the distinct processes through which this refinement occurs, we combined detailed outcome scoring and kinematic analysis of single-pellet reaching in mice to resolve how individual components of the action change with repetition. Decomposing reaching into successive stages revealed improvements in targeting and retrieval, while grasp success-rate after pellet contact did not change detectably.

studi.t: Prefrontal cortical pathways mediating cognitive control enhancement from internal capsule stimulation
studi.s: Background: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) targeting the ventral internal capsule/ventral striatum (VCVS) is an effective treatment for several psychiatric disorders, but clinical responses vary amongst patients, likely reflecting an incomplete mechanistic understanding of the brain pathways mediating response. VCVS DBS may improve cognitive control, a core deficit in multiple psychiatric disorders. Here, we investigated which prefrontal cortical pathway(s) in the internal capsule are associated with improved cognitive control task performance during VCVS DBS.

studi.t: Cross-Species Dynamics of Transposable Elements in Aging Female Visceral Adipose Tissues
studi.s: Transposable elements (TEs) make up nearly half of mammalian genomes and are increasingly implicated in genomic instability, cellular stress responses, aging, and age-related disease. Recent past research has highlighted their significant involvement in disease models such as cancer and Alzheimer's disease (AD), though much remains to be unraveled regarding these genomic insertions. In this study, we explore the involvement of TEs in aging female mouse and human visceral adipose tissue (VAT) using 10x single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) data analyzed with the computational tool SoloTE.

studi.t: Motor cortical signals predict finger velocity beyond task geometry
studi.s: Finger movements toward the same target can differ in speed. How much does motor cortical activity add to a velocity prediction once the decoder knows the starting position and the intended target? We compared predictions of finger velocity on held-out trials with and without spiking-band power from motor cortex. In 18 sessions from one macaque, neural activity reduced mean squared error by 4.92% relative to a baseline that used the target, starting position and time within the trial. The reduction was 4.63% in 20 additional sessions from the same animal, with improvement in every session.

studi.t: Opposing signaling molecules exert cortical control over dissociable behaviors that tile an aggressive state
studi.s: Neuropeptides exert broad effects across the brain to influence behavior. However, the mechanism by which neuropeptide signaling exerts top-down, cortical control over complex behavior remains poorly understood. Prolonged social isolation induces sweeping changes to behavior, including increasing aggression. Here, we find that isolation-induced aggression engages Tachykinin-2 expressing (Tac2+) neurons in the mouse medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC).

studi.t: Linking cross-species hemodynamics with neuronal activity in prefrontal cortex during abstract sequence viewing
studi.s: Humans and other primates have a remarkable ability to identify and predict abstract patterns that evolve through time, but the neural mechanisms that support this capability remain poorly understood. Lateral prefrontal cortex (LPFC) has been implicated in abstract sequence tracking in both humans and macaques, but it is unclear whether underlying processes are shared across species. Further, most existing evidence relies on hemodynamic responses, which can have variable relationships with neuronal activity.

studi.t: Ferrosome Organelles Compartmentalize a Redox-Active Ferrous Phosphate Biomineral
studi.s: Ferrosomes are recently discovered lipid bound bacterial organelles that store iron as iron phosphate biominerals, yet the chemical nature and physiological consequences of ferrosome-stored iron remain poorly understood. Here, we combined X ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), electron microscopy, inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP/MS), and physiological analyses to characterize ferrosome iron in Clostridioides difficile. We initially characterized isolated ferrosomes from a fur::CT strain that overproduces these organelles.

studi.t: Aberrant influenza virus transcription termination generatescapped cRNAs that activate RIG-I
studi.s: Host pathogen receptor retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I) detects influenza virus genome segments and non-canonical replication products. However, it has also been suggested that viral transcription products trigger innate immune responses. In this study, we investigated whether a non-canonical viral transcript is produced during infection and under what conditions this RNA is immunostimulatory.

studi.t: Copper transport is required for metabolism and persistence of Toxoplasma gondii
studi.s: Copper is a conserved cofactor, required for aerobic mitochondrial respiration and other cellular processes. Pathogens acquire copper from their hosts, however the mechanisms of uptake and role of copper within divergent eukaryotes is not well understood.
