studi.s: We have used synthetic biology recombination methods in yeast to build herpes simplex virus type-1 (HSV-1) and human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) genomes from multiple fragments. The genomes were built using transformation-associated recombination (TAR) in yeast, by virtue of overlapping sequences between the different fragments. This study demonstrates the successful assembly of the Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) genome.

studi.t: Early Ontogenetic Development of Tessellated Cartilage in Chondrichthyans
studi.s: Tessellated cartilage (TC) is a hallmark of the chondrichthyan skeleton, yet its development early in ontogeny across the four major groups (batoids, galeomorphs, squalomorphs, and holocephalans) remains poorly understood. In this study, we used micro-CT scanning to examine TC in the jaws of ten representative taxa, allowing interspecific comparison and to determine whether specialised features previously observed in mature forms had yet developed Batoids consistently exhibited well-developed, polygonal tesserae regardless of feeding mode.

studi.t: WITHDRAWN: Pathway-specific short-term synaptic dynamics and lateral inhibition shape frequency-dependent input integration and population-level pattern separation in the dentate gyrus
studi.s: The authors have withdrawn this manuscript because its main conclusions are not supported: a re-examination of the simulation code after posting showed that the near-linear summation at high input frequencies resulted from an initialization error in the simulations, that the reported gamma-band maximum of pattern separation resulted from the design of the input patterns, and that the three-layer network analyses were run on networks that differ from those described in the Methods; in addition, several cited works do not support the statements they are cited for, the two listed JSPS KAKENHI…

studi.t: Maturation-associated ERG3 and timed regulation of circuit stability
studi.s: Neural maturation remodels excitability, but how this supports stable computation remains unclear. In a layered network, unreliable transmission destabilised learning when forward and update perturbations differed. This motivated a developmental screen for conductances that could support reliable responses. Mouse Kcnh7 (human KCNH7), encoding K11.3 (ERG3), rose late postnatally. Adult single-cell data showed expression in excitatory and inhibitory populations. In a Purkinje-cell model, ERG3 raised tonic-firing threshold and broadened pre-tonic responses.

studi.t: Resting Cortical Alpha and Beta Oscillations are Continuous Across Space and Frequency
studi.s: Cortical alpha and beta oscillations are traditionally conceptualized as spatially distinct, with alpha rhythms constrained to the occipital cortex and beta rhythms to frontal cortices. Little work has tested this spatial separability empirically and explored whether the distribution of these cortical rhythms may be continuous in space and frequency.

studi.t: Pitch motor areas contribute to the perception of prosodic categories in speech
studi.s: Prosody is a fundamental aspect of speech characterized by suprasegmental features such as pitch. Prosodic pitch contours convey speakers' intentions, for example, distinguishing statements from questions. Understanding these intentions requires abstracting continuous, variable pitch information into discrete categories. The perception of segmental speech features has been proposed to recruit motor areas according to the articulatory effectors used to produce them. However, whether this principle extends to vocal pitch and prosodic category perception remains unclear.

studi.t: The transcriptional landscape of human microglia reveals strong conservation of miRNAs and preservation of function across vertebrate species.
studi.s: The central role of microglia in CNS function in health and disease has resulted in large interest in targeting microglial as treatments for neurodegenerative disease; understanding the factors that regulate microglial gene expression will be crucial to this goal. microRNAs (miRNAs) are among the most abundant post transcriptional regulators of gene expression. miRNAs suggests miRNA were likely key to significant evolutionary events as regulators of gene expression.

studi.t: Lipidome of Compact Myelin from Cortical Regions of the Aging Murine Brain
studi.s: Age-related cognitive decline has been associated with neurodegeneration in cortical white matter tracts. The trajectory of white matter degeneration over the lifespan follows a similar pattern in humans, primates and rodents including the loss of myelin integrity and concomitant loss in myelinated axonal segments. Previous studies suggest that biochemical alterations in myelin begin to occur well prior to myelin loss.

studi.t: Multiple Glycans and IFITM Proteins Mediate Human Coronavirus OC43 entry
studi.s: Human coronavirus (HCoV)-OC43 is the most prevalent seasonal coronavirus, causing colds, and occasional severe disease. HCoV-OC43 attachment is reportedly mediated by 9-O acetylated sialic acid (9-O-Ac-Sia); no proteinaceous receptor has been identified. Using genome-wide CRISPR-cas9 screens, we identify several host factors that mediate HCoV-OC43 entry. First, we identify NXPE3, an esterase, as required for HCoV-OC43 attachment and infection, both in vitro and in vivo, and demonstrate a previously unknown role for NXPE3 in 9-O-Ac-Sia synthesis.

studi.t: Pyrenophora teres f. teres uses specialized infection structures to facilitate effector-driven promotion of in planta colonization on barley
studi.s: Pyrenophora teres f. teres is a necrotrophic fungal pathogen that causes net form net blotch (NFNB) of barley. Infection of susceptible barley leaves initially causes dot-like lesions that progress to transverse and longitudinal striations, that form the net-like pattern of necrosis for which the disease was named. While the complex genetic architecture of the P. teres f.

studi.t: The splicing kinase PRPF-4 is required for somatic development and germline function in C. elegans
studi.s: Pre-mRNA splicing is essential for gene expression, yet the consequences of disrupting core spliceosomal factors during animal development remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the in vivo function of the conserved spliceosomal kinase PRPF-4 in C. elegans using endogenous reporter analysis, conditional protein depletion, and transcriptome-wide analysis of alternative splicing and gene expression.

studi.t: Stress fibers are physically and genetically linked to SPIN90 and Arp2/3 complex
studi.s: The Arp2/3 complex has long been considered to assemble only branched actin structures in the cell (lamellipodia, endocytic patches, comet tails, and many more). We show for the first time by single-molecule tracking (SMT) that the Arp2/3 complex and SPIN90, which activates Arp2/3 complex to nucleate unbranched filaments, bind to and move in the basal cortex with stress fibers (SF) and focal adhesions (FA) that, unlike known sites of Arp2/3 enrichment, employ linear actin bundles.

studi.t: Transgenic menstruating mice reveal the spatial logic of pre-menstrual uterine differentiation
studi.s: During menstruation, the superficial layer of the endometrium differentiates and sheds, while the underlying basal layer is preserved to support repeated regeneration. How differentiation is restricted to the superficial layer remains unknown. Progress in understanding menstruation has been hindered by the lack of tractable animal models, as mice and rats do not menstruate. Here, we present transgenic mouse models that use chemogenetics to induce key anatomical, functional, and transcriptional features of human menstruation.

studi.t: Functional regeneration of the Rdl-A296S mutation in Anopheles funestus decouples insecticide resistance from genetic background and isolates its life-history costs
studi.s: Resolving the genetic basis of insecticide resistance in Anopheles funestus has been limited both by the historic difficulty of germline transformation in this species and by the confounding genetic and metabolic background present in field populations. The A296S resistance-to-dieldrin (Rdl) mutation provides an informative proof-of-principle case because it has persisted at high frequency in African vector populations long after the withdrawal of dieldrin.

studi.t: High-throughput electrochemical transformation expands mass spectrometric reference space for transformation products
studi.s: Structure annotation of unknown features detected by high-resolution tandem mass spectrometry remains challenging. Spectral libraries provide confident annotation but have limited chemical space coverage. This hampers discovery of natural products and xenobiotics and often necessitates laborious isolation and characterization. We introduce a scalable high-throughput workflow combining online electrochemistry with high-resolution tandem mass spectrometry to expand the empirical spectral reference space for transformation products.

studi.t: High-Throughput Coded Aperture Raman Imaging with Total Internal Reflection
studi.s: Spontaneous Raman microscopy provides label-free molecular fingerprints of biological tissues, but its low scattering efficiency limits the throughput required for large-area hyperspectral imaging. Here we introduce total internal reflection Raman (TIRR) microscopy, an architecture that exploits repeated internal reflections within a thin sapphire substrate to generate extended evanescent excitation without dividing the incident laser power among independent illumination spots.

studi.t: Pioneer and Altimeter: Rapid and Scalable of DIA Proteomics Data Optimized for Narrow Isolation Windows
studi.s: The scale of mass spectrometry-based proteomics studies has surged due to faster instrumentation and automated sample preparation, producing terabytes of data across thousands of files and pushing analysis software to their limits. Here we introduce Pioneer and Altimeter for rapid and scalable analysis of data-independent acquisition (DIA) proteomics data. Altimeter generates in silico spectral libraries, which Pioneer uses to identify and quantify peptides and proteins.

studi.t: ARC-Impute: robust reference-guided spatial gene imputation through regularised cell-to-spot mapping
studi.s: Motivation: Reference-guided spatial imputation uses single-cell RNA sequencing references to predict genes that are unmeasured in spatial transcriptomics data. Limited shared-gene overlap can leave the mapping of reference cells to spatial locations ambiguous: different assignments may reconstruct observed genes similarly yet yield different imputed expression and cell-type estimates. This gives rise to local assignment ambiguity, source-target mismatch and reference-transfer instability.

studi.t: Quantum transduction from electron spin state to signaling in wild-type AsLOV2
studi.s: Electron spin coherence is often thought to be at odds with the warm, wet conditions of biological systems. Coherent electron-spin dynamics have been shown to modulate fluorescence in some flavoproteins, but not the chemistry by which a protein signals. The direct connection between electron spin coherence and biological function is therefore still missing. Here we show that a magnetic field modulates formation of the covalent FMN-cysteine photoadduct that constitutes the signaling state of wild-type Avena sativa LOV2 (AsLOV2), via a spin-selective radical-pair reaction.

studi.t: Glioblastoma exhibits bidirectional adaptation to treatment through JARID2-associated developmental plasticity
studi.s: Glioblastoma (GBM) exhibits bidirectional transcriptional reprogramming following standard-of-care (SoC) treatment, yet the direction cannot be predicted from primary tumours. Using independent longitudinal bulk and single-cell datasets, we show that this response is captured by a framework, the JARID2 Binding Site (JBS) axis. Tumours and cells can be positioned along this axis according to expression of JBS genes, with responder subtypes defined by movement along the axis from primary to recurrent states.

studi.t: Precision-Weighted Updating Explains Serial Dependence Across Sensory and Contextual Transitions
studi.s: Serial dependence is influenced by sensory uncertainty and by the continuity of context, but it remains controversial whether these influences reflect separate mechanisms or different expressions of a shared updating process. Across two time reproduction experiments (N = 44), we examined how motion coherence and transitions between coherence levels modulated the attraction toward the preceding duration, while controlling for central tendency. In Experiment 1, low current coherence led to stronger serial dependence than high coherence, whereas central tendency did not change.

studi.t: Real-time posterior probabilistic TMS motor mapping with robust individualized stopping criteria
studi.s: Background: Electric-field-informed regression provides high-resolution transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) motor maps, but conventional nonlinear fitting is too slow to update the map during acquisition, so sessions rely on predefined stimulation budgets, despite substantial inter-individual variability in the data required for stable localization. Objective: To develop a real-time analysis updating a posterior probability map between pulses and compare its hotspots with finger-tapping functional MRI (fMRI).

studi.t: WITHDRAWN: CA3 sparsity stabilises high-connectivity recurrent autoassociation: complementary binary and spiking computational modes in a DG->CA3 model
studi.s: The authors have withdrawn this manuscript because several of its central claims are not supported: a re-examination of the code and data after posting showed that the binary and spiking models compared in the 2 x 2 design did not share a matched dentate gyrus input, that one data point in Fig. 4B was taken from a different condition because of a plotting error, and that the statement that CA3 activity remains stable during recall collapse was based on a quantity that was not measured during recall; the claims that the product of the CA3 active fraction and the recurrent connectivity is the…

studi.t: Complex microbial consortia improve yield and physiological performance of leafy greens under deficit irrigation
studi.s: Water scarcity is an increasing constraint on agricultural productivity, particularly for high-value vegetable crops. Deficit irrigation strategies can reduce water use but frequently compromise yield and crop physiological status. Scalable, biologically based tools are needed to sustain crop performance under reduced water input without reliance on additional agrochemical inputs. Five functionally diverse microbial consortia were assembled from taxa selected to support rhizosphere colonization, soil structural stabilization, and fungal-mediated nutrient and water foraging.

studi.t: WITHDRAWN: The Sequential Threshold Model: A Unified Framework for Microbiome-Driven Periodontitis Progression
studi.s: The authors have withdrawn their manuscript because, during re-analysis during peer review, we found that we had interpreted the direction of the differential expression contrast between progressing and stable sites in reverse. We confirmed the correct direction from the original analysis objects and normalized counts. With the correct direction, inflammatory and senescence-associated genes are higher, rather than lower, at progressing sites.

studi.t: A network perspective on the role of c-di-GMP-associated protein complexes in biofilm formation.
studi.s: The secondary messenger cyclic di-GMP is a ubiquitous bacterial signal that regulates the switch from a free-swimming to a sessile biofilm-forming lifestyle. Many biofilm-forming Pseudomonas species possess numerous c-di-GMP-binding proteins (CDGs) which regulate gene expression, protein activity, and protein complexes. However, the mechanisms by which numerous CDG effectors form a coherent signaling network to coordinate lifestyle changes remain poorly understood. We addressed this knowledge gap by focusing on ten CDG proteins involved in biofilm development in P. fluorescens SBW25.

studi.t: Protein diffusion controls how single cells respond to electric fields
studi.s: Cells sense and respond to electric fields, using these fields as a guidance cue in wound healing and development. This sensing is done by redistribution of charged membrane proteins on the cell's surface ("sensors") via electrophoresis and electroosmotic flow. If membrane proteins have to physically rearrange on the cell's surface, how quickly can a cell respond to an applied signal? What limits the cell's ability to respond? Are galvanotaxing cells, like chemotaxing cells, limited by stochasticity from the finite number of molecules?

studi.t: Telomere length across land plants tracks warm season temperature and not life history
studi.s: Telomeres protect chromosome ends, yet their length varies widely among organisms. What shapes this variation is a long-standing question with implications for chromosome function and evolution. In animals, telomere length variation is explained by life-history differences related to senescence and tumorigenesis but the drivers in plants are unknown. Because plants are sessile organisms where growth depends directly on their surroundings the telomere length might be under selection from environmental factors.

studi.t: Eukaryotic 45S ribosomal RNA spacers encode an ancient layer of antiviral response
studi.s: Eukaryotic 45S ribosomal RNA genes produce internal transcribed spacers (ITSs) that are excised and discarded during ribosome biogenesis, with no established function beyond rRNA processing. Here, we uncover an unexpected antiviral role for these seemingly expendable sequences. Comparative genomic analyses reveal extensive, evolutionarily widespread sequence similarities between eukaryotic ITSs and DNA viruses, particularly between vertebrate ITSs and herpesviruses.

studi.t: LUCID: joint cell typing and neighbour-aware decontamination of segmented spatial transcriptomics
studi.s: Cell profiles in segmented spatial transcriptomics are contaminated by RNA of neighbouring cells and by segmentation errors that merge two cells. LUCID is a multinomial mixture model that jointly assigns a type to each cell, tests whether its profile mixes two types and estimates the fraction of counts coming from its neighbours. An external reference is adapted to the platform, an identifiability rule protects a cell's own signal and the test is calibrated by parametric bootstrap. LUCID works with or without a reference, runs on CPUs and returns integer counts for all genes.

studi.t: Whole-catalog reference distributions for reading one person's polygenic scores, built by an agent-optimized GPU scorer
studi.s: Objective: A polygenic score (PGS) is interpretable only as a percentile within a reference distribution, so a person who wants their risk across many diseases/traits needs every candidate model calibrated against a reference distribution. A precalculated frozen reference scoring every genome in a reference panel against every PGS model requires extensive computing resources using current software.

studi.t: WITHDRAWN: General model with biclustering for target selection in severe preeclampsia
studi.s: The authors have withdrawn their manuscript because, following the journal's peer-review process and subsequent rejection, they determined that further scientific evaluation, manuscript revisions, and final approval by all authors are necessary before public dissemination. Therefore, the authors do not wish this work to be cited as a reference for the project. If you have any questions, please contact the corresponding author.

studi.t: Lipid diffusion enhanced by membrane-associated molecular motors
studi.s: We experimentally investigate fluid lipid membranes coupled to nematic actin filament layers through myosin I motors. The motor activity of myosin I re-organizes the actin layer, modifying the morphology of +1/2 topological defects and generating spatially heterogeneous, actin-rich regions. Single-particle tracking (SPT) of lipid molecules reveal two interesting features. First, by identifying two lipid populations characterized by low- and high-speeds, it reveals an increased fraction of high-speed lipids in actin-rich regions.

studi.t: Can we measure engagement from video data based on student movement and sound level?
studi.s: Engagement is widely recognised as central to learning and academic achievement. Movement and sound level, combined with an indicator of school relevant content, can be linked to engagement through activating affect, behaviour, and cognition. Electrodermal activity (EDA) is a reliable indicator of movement and sound level, as it measures sympathetic nervous system activation. However, the high cost of wearable EDA sensors has limited its widespread application.

studi.t: Computational modeling of breast cancer metastases predicts response to dual checkpoint inhibition and reveals spatially-informed treatments
studi.s: In advanced breast cancers, the highly suppressive tumor microenvironment contributes to poor responses to immune checkpoint inhibition. The degree of suppression varies by site of disease and affects metastatic progression. To investigate this phenomenon, we developed an agent-based model of cell-cell interactions within the tumor microenvironment, specifically tuned to in vivo data from murine breast-to-lung metastases.

studi.t: A Tether-Independent Mechanism for Bacterial Outer Membrane Separation
studi.s: Gram-negative bacteria divide by coordinating the separation of two cell envelope layers: the peptidoglycan (PG) sacculus and the outer membrane (OM). In several well-studied model organisms, the OM is tightly tethered to the PG layer, causing both structures to constrict synchronously during cell division. In contrast, division of the PG and OM is uncoupled in Myxococcus xanthus, where the OM undergoes only limited invagination and remains largely unconstricted even after PG fission is complete, separating substantially later than the PG layer.

studi.t: Pili-like proteins are essential for conjugation also in Gram-positive bacteria
studi.s: Type IV secretion systems (T4SS) enable the spread of antibiotic resistance and other virulence factors. In Gram-positive bacteria, T4SSs have long been thought to lack VirB2-like proteins that form conjugative pili and instead rely on adhesins for cell-cell contacts. Yet, it has remained unclear how subsequent DNA transfer (conjugation) is mediated. Here we identify a VirB2-like protein, PrgFB2, from the clinically isolated plasmid pCF10 in Enterococcus faecalis and show that it is essential for conjugation. Structural modelling confidently predicts a pilus-like assembly for PrgFB2.

studi.t: HIV-1 Mutational Bias Shapes the Supply of Drug Resistance Mutations
studi.s: The development of durable HIV-1 therapeutics requires understanding not only which mutations confer resistance, but also how readily those mutations arise. Prior work has characterized the effects of individual mutations on viral fitness and drug or immune escape; however, the contribution of mutational bias to HIV-1 evolutionary pathways remains largely unquantified.

studi.t: Physics-Guided Neural Reconstruction of Cellular Membranes for 3D Electron Microscopy
studi.s: With advances in three-dimensional electron microscopy modalities, quantitative characterization of membrane ultrastructure has emerged as an approach to interrogate how organization of proteins and other components around the membrane drive structure and function. Hindering these efforts, the confident reconstruction of geometric features such as membrane curvature is challenging since it requires the calculation of higher-order derivatives from discrete membrane representations.

studi.t: Within-host algal symbiont turnover is not a general response to environmental change in reef corals
studi.s: Flexibility in the coral-algal symbiosis is widely proposed as a mechanism of acclimatization to environmental change. Here, I compile colony-level longitudinal data spanning 67 coral species, 26 years, and 109 reefs globally to determine the predictors of within-host symbiont turnover. Across host species, environmental change showed no consistent association with turnover likelihood at either the symbiont genus or ITS2 sequencing variant level. Instead, resident symbiont genus was the strongest predictor of turnover, and transition probabilities between genera were often asymmetric.

studi.t: Entrenchment of germline amino-acid differences in antibody affinity maturation
studi.s: Entrenchment - epistasis that locks in amino acid differences between homologous proteins, so each disfavors substitutions toward the other's state - has been demonstrated along individual protein lineages over deep evolutionary time. Antibodies offer a unique system for studying entrenchment: multiple homologous germline V gene paralogs provide diverse starting points, and the rapid somatic evolution of affinity maturation generates dense phylogenies from which selection on germline-encoded residues can be inferred.

studi.t: Norm-like vocal behavior in a nonhuman primate
studi.s: Human interlocutors have strong expectations that guide when, how, and what is communicated, but the evolutionary origins of such normative expectations remain poorly understood. Vocal accommodation in marmosets, where individuals converge their calls toward their partners, offers a model for investigating their evolutionary roots. Using a fully automated closed-loop interactive playback paradigm, we presented marmosets with partner calls that converged toward or diverged from their own call structure.

studi.t: Minute-scale single-cell transcriptomics reveals a temporal grammar of inflammatory responses
studi.s: Inflammatory stimulation triggers transient pulses, sustained activation, and repression, yet the principles organizing these distinct transcriptional kinetics remain unclear. We developed ChronoSeq, an automated microfluidic platform combining continuous live-cell sampling with molecular time barcoding for pooled, genome-wide single-cell transcriptomics at 10-minute resolution. Across distinct inflammatory contexts, gene expression trajectories repeatedly resolved into a limited set of conserved kinetic modes, despite substantial differences in their timing and gene composition.

studi.t: Inhibition of delta-1 glutamate receptor current by extracellular protons
studi.s: Decreases in brain pH are associated with numerous neurological and neuropsychiatric conditions yet the molecular mechanisms linking decreased brain pH with these disorders are incomplete. The ionotropic glutamate receptors (iGluRs) mediate the majority of excitatory neurotransmission in the brain and can be inhibited or potentiated by extracellular protons depending on receptor subtype. The effect of protons on the delta-glutamate receptor subclass of iGluRs is unknown.

studi.t: Revealing interactions between glutathione peroxidase 4 and phosphoinositides
studi.s: Glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPx4) is the primary enzyme that reduces lipid hydroperoxides to prevent membrane oxidative damage and protecting against ferroptosis. GPx4 is known to engage with lipid headgroups through electrostatic interactions, positioning the substrate for reduction. This work reveals and characterizes binding of highly anionic phosphoinositides (PIP lipids) by GPx4. PIPs are vital lipids in human cells and are central to many signaling processes, particularly in cytosolic-facing membranes.

studi.t: Local and network-level dynamics of alpha and beta rhythms during visuospatial attention in autism
studi.s: Visuospatial attention is altered in autism, yet the underlying neural mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Neural oscillatory activity coordinates distributed processes supporting attentional selection and their flexible adjustment to changing environmental demands. Altered oscillatory organization may therefore provide a mechanistic basis for atypical attentional processing in autism. We tested this theory using EEG recordings from 80 autistic and neurotypical children and youth performing a spatial cueing task with valid and invalid cues.

studi.t: Speech and music organize neural activity differently over time in human superior temporal cortex
studi.s: Speech and music engage overlapping auditory cortex. We asked whether they shape the timing of local activity in ways that regional response strength alone leaves unresolved. In intracranial recordings from 30 participants watching a film with alternating music and speech, 1-10-Hz activity in the superior temporal gyrus (STG) had higher sample entropy during music, indicating that similar short patterns were less likely to persist (mean paired difference = 0.02256, FDR q = 0.00753).

studi.t: Shox2 maintains thalamocortical neuron firing for whisker-based somatomotor responses and sleep spindles in mice
studi.s: In the mouse thalamus, thalamocortical neurons (TCNs) relay sensory information to cortex and generate rhythmic activity, including sleep spindles, through precisely timed firing. TCNs switch between tonic and burst firing modes that depend on intrinsic membrane properties, yet what maintains these properties in the mature thalamus remains unknown. Transcription factors, which regulate the ion channel genes that shape firing, are natural candidates.

studi.t: Neonatal exposure to SARS-CoV-2 spike protein in mice is associated with localized changes in cerebral cortex cell proliferation
studi.s: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) can cause acute and persistent neurological manifestations, and evidence suggests these effects may be at least partly explained by direct effects of Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) spike protein, which includes neuroinflammation, cognitive dysfunction, and persistent pain. Because the developing brain undergoes finely regulated processes of cellular proliferation, differentiation, and cerebrovascular maturation, exposure to SARS-CoV-2 or its components during this critical period may interfere with neurodevelopment.

studi.t: Evolutionarily conserved coupling of lysosomal response sensing and disease-associated microglial reprogramming scales with pathological timescales
studi.s: Background Microglia transition into disease-associated microglia (DAM) during central nervous system (CNS) injury and neurodegeneration, yet the upstream intracellular logic driving this state conversion in vivo remains unclear. The lysosome acts as a signaling hub, but whether physiological phagocytic load universally initiates and quantitatively couples to DAM reprogramming across different pathological timescales is unknown.

studi.t: Universal barcoded connectomics for massively parallel single-neuron projection mapping in diverse vertebrate species
studi.s: Neuroscience relies on diverse model species to understand animal behavior and brain function. Yet, tools for rapid, high-resolution brain connectivity mapping remain unavailable in most vertebrate species, slowing progress in many neuroscience models and rendering cross-species circuit comparisons challenging. Here, we overcome this barrier by establishing sequencing-based barcoded connectomics for rapid single-neuron tracing in seven vertebrate species ranging from frogs to birds to non-human primates.

studi.t: Web search in Latin America: language models use less local and diverse news than search engines
studi.s: AI platforms are becoming a major gateway to news and current events. This shift risks amplifying existing geographical biases that favour narratives from wealthier countries over those from the Global South. This is particularly relevant in Latin America, which accounts for the largest share of AI usage in the Global South. We examine how information about Latin America changes when users shift from conventional search engines to LLM-based search.

studi.t: Ground Truth Bias in AI-Assisted Medical Annotation: A Crossover Study Using an Independent Radiologist Reference Standard
studi.s: Behavioural evaluations of artificial-intelligence-assisted annotation score every human decision against a reference standard, so their conclusions inherit that standard's validity. We tested how far conclusions about assistance, reliance and individual differences depend on it. Fifty-one non-expert high-school students annotated 50 knee radiographs for osteoarthritis, with and without a deliberately imperfect classifier, in a crossover design; personality and non-verbal reasoning were also measured.

studi.t: Verifiable Logic in Medical LLMs: A Critical Review of Agentic Clinical Reasoning Optimization and Neuro-Symbolic Grounding
studi.s: Clinical large language models are usually judged by whether the final answer is right. Yet a model can reach a fluent, plausible output through invalid reasoning that static benchmarks do not detect, and confident hallucination, causally invalid inference, and spurious demographic shortcuts can pass conventional evaluation.

studi.t: Persistence and Change in National Production Networks
studi.s: Many country-years in multi-country input-output databases have no national table. We study the kernel of domestic intermediate transactions, the part that rescaling to new industry totals cannot update. Among 25 economies with a national table every year, the latest table misplaces 6.6 percent of the kernel one year ahead and 21.2 percent ten years ahead, while the five most similar economies misplace 24.1 to 25.0 percent at every horizon.

studi.t: Particle physics science communication with grass-roots Instagram: a success story
studi.s: Communicating science to the public is an integral part of the work of a research collaboration, not an afterthought. Institutional and collaboration-level social media accounts are often run by professional communicators rather than by practising scientists, and single-scientist ``influencer'' accounts are demanding to sustain. We describe {\em CMSatDESY}, a crowd-sourced Instagram account on which the CMS group at DESY tells its own stories, each member in their own voice.

studi.t: Embodied Human-Data Interaction
studi.s: We propose the concept of human-data interaction (HDI) as the human manipulation, analysis, and sensemaking of large, unstructured, and complex datasets. We then proceed to suggest an embodied approach to HDI to build physical reasoning environments for these difficult and polymorphic tasks. We illustrate our approach with two examples: tangible lenses for visual exploration, and an educational computer game with tangible bricks.

studi.t: From Reliance to Overreliance: Taxonomizing and Detecting Relational Risks in AI Companionship
studi.s: Companion AIs are increasingly used for emotional support, yet distinguishing meaningful engagement from harmful reliance remains difficult. We introduce the Taxonomy of Relational Risks (TRR), which operationalizes users' emotional overreliance (EO) as observable conversational behaviors and separately identifies evidence of relational harm (RH), enabling empirical examination of when reliance behaviors co-occur with adverse consequences.

studi.t: KeyMem: Temporal Occupancy Control for Robust Streaming VideoLLM Memory
studi.s: Streaming VideoLLMs retain a bounded cache of visual tokens. Yet score-based eviction lets the stream determine its own temporal occupancy, so a short salient segment can monopolize the cache and displace evidence needed later. We identify this uncontrolled temporal occupancy as a fundamental limitation and introduce KeyMem, a training-free wrapper that rank-normalizes any base score, divides the video stream into fixed-duration temporal buckets and limits how many visual tokens each bucket can retain, and optionally samples survivors with a secret key.

studi.t: MetaScanner: An Empirical Study and Proactive Defense against Deceptive UI Attacks in Social VR
studi.s: Social virtual reality (VR) platforms have surged in popularity but continue to face significant security challenges, including privacy invasion and user manipulation. Yet, the security risks posed by deceptive content remain largely unexplored. In this paper, we introduce four novel deceptive UI attacks that covertly manipulate social VR users into performing unintended actions without their awareness.

studi.t: AI-Driven Transformation of Digital Platform Work: A Task-Based Model for Measuring Labour Disruption and Vulnerability, with Early Evidence from Online Freelancing in Kenya
studi.s: Assessments of AI's impact on labour often rely on conventional occupational categories or broad market indicators. This dominant trend, however, obscures how tasks within the same occupation vary in practice across work arrangements. This limitation is particularly important in online freelancing, where workers are typically remote and devote substantial time performing unpaid tasks. This article introduces a task-based framework that distinguishes AI-driven disruption, defined as the extent of change in how work is performed, from livelihood vulnerability associated with that change.

studi.t: Design and Evaluation of Epira: An Automated Interview System for Case Investigation and Contact Tracing
studi.s: Objective: Case investigation and contact tracing are labor-intensive. Web forms struggle when respondents need clarification before disclosing contacts, and open-ended chatbots may deviate from protocols. We developed and evaluated Epira, a protocol-controlled large language model (LLM) interviewer for multi-disease case investigation and contact tracing. Materials and Methods: Epira pairs LLM dialogue with a rule-based controller enforcing required questions, safety handoffs, and a structured case record, and adapts to new diseases by questionnaire upload.

studi.t: Persona Lenses: What Makes a Vision-Language Model See Through Its Persona's Eyes?
studi.s: Vision-language models have been used to simulate where a user looks on a web page. However, a persona in the prompt reaches the simulated gaze only partly. We measure this reach as the difference in one model's gaze between two MatrAIx personas that differ in a single attribute. We introduce persona lenses, which place the persona between the model and the page: a text lens (a two-step prompt in which the model first writes what the persona would look at), a pixel lens (marks on the region matching the persona's interests) and a weight lens (a dwell reward gated to keep the scanpath…

studi.t: Coordinated Use of Large Language Models in Academic Research
studi.s: This study proposes a methodological framework for the coordinated use of multiple large language models in academic research. Its central argument is that involving more models does not in itself guarantee more reliable results; what matters is how cognitive and verification operations are organised.

studi.t: Dynamical Variational Theory of Stochastic Reaction Networks
studi.s: Discrete stochastic population dynamics describe systems ranging from biochemical reaction networks and gene regulation to epidemic spreading, ecology, and population genetics, where finite populations generate strong intrinsic fluctuations. Predicting their dynamics, including mean populations, fluctuations, time-lagged correlations, response functions, and steady states, remains challenging: the chemical master equation admits no general analytical solution, numerical solutions scale poorly with system size, and standard approximations fail at low copy numbers.

studi.t: Faithful Generative Modeling for Censored Time-to-Event Data: From Distributional Fidelity to Statistical Inference
studi.s: Synthetic data has emerged as a powerful tool for data sharing, clinical trial simulation, and digital twin development, with growing applications in biomedical research and drug development. However, limited attention has been devoted to synthetic time-to-event data, which are central to clinical trials and survival analysis. In particular, theoretical guarantees for the distributional fidelity of synthetic survival data remain largely unexplored.

studi.t: Fractional Order or False Memory: Identifiability of Caputo SIR Models from Incidence Data
studi.s: When a fractional order improves the fit of an epidemic model, it is usually taken as evidence of memory. We ask whether the order of the Caputo susceptible-infectious-removed (SIR) model can actually be recovered from incidence data. If the transmission rate is allowed to vary freely in time, as in hybrid forecasting models, every admissible order, removal rate and initial count reproduces the data exactly.

studi.t: GenAI-DBT: Evaluating a DBT-Informed Generative AI Platform for Mindfulness Skills Training: A Pilot Randomized Study
studi.s: We evaluated the feasibility, acceptability, and engagement of three digital formats for dialectical behavior therapy (DBT) mindfulness skills training. In a 30-day randomized pilot study, 45 university students were assigned to GenAI-DBT, a general-purpose large language model chatbot (Chatbot), or a static web resource (Web). Forty-two completed the study, and nine completed follow-up interviews. Usability scores were within acceptable ranges across conditions, with no significant between-group differences. GenAI-DBT showed the highest observed participant-week adherence (71.4%, vs.

studi.t: VideoTrail: Interactive Video Foraging Through Hierarchical Visualization
studi.s: People often watch videos to find information, but locating relevant moments can be difficult and time-consuming. Existing strategies like scrubbing rely primarily on visual scanning and linear search, providing limited support for goal-directed navigation. We present VideoTrail, an AI-powered browser extension that supports information seeking in videos through a hierarchical visualization. Inspired by information foraging theory, VideoTrail surfaces semantic and structural cues as information scent, creating an explorable roadmap of segments.

studi.t: Networked wealth and mortality in the Agincourt Health and Demographic Surveillance System, 2009--2018
studi.s: Background. Though resources embedded in social networks appear to shape health, past studies have not assessed this relationship directly. Using data from Agincourt Health and Demographic Surveillance System in South Africa, we examined the spillover effect of household wealth on mortality in the family network. Methods. We analysed cohort data from 2009 to 2018 to estimate the Average Total Effect (ATE) of household wealth on deaths, decomposing this into an Average Direct Effect (ADE) and Average Spillover Effect (ASE).

studi.t: When Should Deployed BCI Decoders Adapt? A Resource-Priced Ladder for Frozen EEG Trunks
studi.s: When should a deployed MI decoder spend adaptation resources-not only how to adapt under shift? We study a thin control layer outside a frozen encoder: a resource ladder (factory -> Bayesian head -> affine map, with full fine-tune as an escape hatch) governed by regime-aware gating under a utility that prices accuracy, fit time, and label cost. The head is Bayesian in the conjugate sense: a Normal-Inverse-Wishart prior over the class conditional Gaussians in embedding space, updated in closed form (no gradients) as labelled trials arrive.

studi.t: Whose Safety? Addressing Anti-Blackness in the Age of AI Safety
studi.s: "AI safety" has grown from a niche contingent of actors into the dominant framing for artificial intelligence (AI) assessment and evaluation, overshadowing AI ethics. Through political and monetary influence, AI safety has shifted political focus within the US and abroad. The focus has shifted away from harms that currently affect the public toward threats framed as "existential risks". We argue that safety cannot be achieved while anti-Blackness is left unaddressed.

studi.t: Modeling Learner-Technology Interaction Through Multilevel Gaze Transition Dynamics to Inform Usability in Online Learning
studi.s: Gaze data provide fine-grained evidence of how learners engage with instructional content and interface elements, complementing conventional usability evaluation methods. However, eye-tracking analyses often examine within-slide visual attention and across-slide navigation separately, limiting understanding of learner interaction throughout extended learning experiences.

studi.t: Knowing What You Know: A Trait Theory of Reviewer Value in Human-AI Cognitive Systems
studi.s: When a capable model and a human reviewer cooperate on the same decision, which human still adds value? We argue this is a question about a single cognitive trait, metacognitive calibration: the alignment between a reviewer's behavioral confidence and the actual correctness of their judgments. We develop a trait theory of reviewer value to make it precise.

studi.t: Mapping the AI Supply Chain: Dependencies, Vulnerabilities, and Market Concentration in the AI Ecosystem
studi.s: AI systems are built across many organizations that contribute models, data, compute, capital, talent, and other assets. While the layers of the AI stack are relatively well understood, the relationships between actors and components across layers remains sparsely documented. In this work, we focus on the organizations that make up the AI supply chain: the complex network of actors that contribute to the development and deployment of AI.

studi.t: "I Don't Think It's a Scam": A First Look at Family Intervention Barriers in Elder Abuse Discussions on Reddit and Baidu Tieba
studi.s: When older adults trust scammers despite warnings, families face obstacles to intervention. Complainants aged 60 and older reported \$4.9 billion in losses in 2024 to the U.S. Internet Crime Complaint Center. To investigate family intervention barriers to elder scams, we collected 2M Reddit posts from May 2021 to June 2026 and 2B Baidu Tieba posts from 2007 to 2026. The final corpora contain 13,082 Reddit posts and 3,933 Baidu Tieba posts, labeled using platform-specific codebooks, manual reference annotations, and LLM coding.

studi.t: Who are you? The Personal Imitation Game
studi.s: Large Language Models (LLMs) now perform strongly on Alan Turing's 1950 Imitation Game, so we propose a harder challenge, the Personal Imitation Game, which asks whether a machine can replicate a specific individual in conversation rather than a generic human. Testing with 30 participants, we establish a human baseline and report the identity signals interrogators rely on: stylometric features, personality traits, and biographical facts.

studi.t: Overlooked and Underutilized: Prototypes are the Missing Piece in Tabular XAI
studi.s: Explainable AI (XAI) is frequently applied to high-stakes tabular data, yet the field relies heavily on feature attribution methods. While these approaches offer technical transparency, evaluating dozens of isolated features demands excessive cognitive effort from non-expert users. In this paper, we argue that prototypes remain overlooked and underutilized, and should be integrated as a complementary, intuitive gateway to auditing complex machine learning models.

studi.t: A Foundation Model to Measure and Predict Human Behaviour
studi.s: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to infer psychological attributes, predict individual behaviour, and simulate human populations. However, despite generating plausible responses, they often misrepresent individuals and distort population statistics. Here we introduce Chiron, a foundation model to measure and predict human behaviour. We jointly fine-tune an LLM to represent psychological constructs, predict individual behaviour, and align population response distributions with human statistics.

studi.t: One size does not fit all: session-specific effects of deep brain stimulation on hand-motor kinematics in Parkinson's disease
studi.s: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) effectively treats motor symptoms of Parkinson's disease (PD), but it is unclear whether it changes fine hand movements in the same way for every patient. We analyzed 35 sessions of 19 patients with PD from a multi-center cohort performing the CopyDraw task, a drawing task designed to overcome the subjectivity and limited granularity of clinical assessments. Besides standard kinematics (mean velocity, acceleration, jerk, and drawing accuracy), we derived higher distributional moments and non-linear complexity measures, for 38 features in total.

studi.t: Data-driven simulation of the brain's response to stimulation: a system identification approach for closed-loop neuromodulation, piloted in adaptive deep brain stimulation
studi.s: Closed-loop neuromodulation uses a physiomarker to control stimulation. Developing such controllers requires exploring a large space of strategies and parameters, which is often not feasible with the human-in-the-loop. Simulation environments offer an alternative. Adaptive deep brain stimulation (aDBS) for Parkinson's disease is a stereotypical application: while physiomarker identification progresses rapidly, clinically available control is limited to threshold and proportional strategies.

studi.t: Bayesian Computation of Copula-based Multivariate Models with an Application to Doping Detection
studi.s: The Athlete Biological Passport (ABP) monitors athletes for doping by comparing their biomarker readings against personalized reference ranges. These are estimated via the Bayesian ADAPTIVE model, which analyzes biomarkers separately and ignores their dependence. Building on a recently proposed copula-based multivariate extension of ADAPTIVE, this paper focuses on its computational aspects, introducing a fully joint MCMC algorithm and comparing it with a two-step Bayesian IFM estimator.

studi.t: Towards Transparent Computational Agents for Air Traffic Control: Explainability, Interpretability and Trust
studi.s: We report preliminary findings from an ongoing investigation into transparency techniques for computational Air Traffic Control agents. Air Traffic Controller Officers (ATCOs) observed two types of agent in simulated air traffic controlling exercises. ATCOs found the chosen transparency techniques helpful to some extent: revealing how agents were making controlling decisions was an essential foundation for trust. However, the ATCOs' trust depended on whether they could be made sense of in a live, operational context and the agents' actions where judged to be professionally competent.

studi.t: Inferring Neural Activity Changes under Recording Uncertainty with Transformers and Variational Inference
studi.s: A difference in recorded firing rate across days may reflect a change in neuronal activity, missed spikes or recording a different neuron. We present a statistical approach that combines neuron tracking with Bayesian estimates of stationary mean recorded firing rates. Bounds under assumed differences in spike detection connect recorded rates to biological rate changes. We assess recording loss and uncertainty in rate changes in simulations, and count-model fit in recordings.

studi.t: Sex Differences in the Detection of Parkinson's Disease from Speech
studi.s: Parkinson's disease (PD) is the second most common neurodegenerative disease in the world, and 70\% to 75\% of PD patients suffer from speech disorders at some stage. Since PD affects men more frequently than women, previous publications tend to rely on unbalanced datasets that potentially introduce sex biases into trained models. This study investigates sex differences in PD detection from speech using deep learning and traditional machine learning approaches.

studi.t: Interpersonal trust, institutional trust and trust in technology in Air Traffic Control
studi.s: Air traffic control (ATC), the safe, orderly and efficient management of planes through controlled airspace is a complex task. In this article, we explore the roles that different kinds of trust play in ATC. Our study provides the essential foundations for examining the conditions that need to be satisfied if Air Traffic Controllers are to establish and sustain trust relationships with technical innovations, such as agent-based systems, and so ensure their safe and dependable embedding within ATC work.

studi.t: The Structural Number of Parties: An Electoral-Outcome-Independent Baseline for Comparing Party-System Scale
studi.s: How many parties can a country structurally sustain? Standard measures such as the effective number of parties (ENP) cannot answer this question. They are descriptive and post hoc: they summarize competition only after an election, and they depend on electoral returns that are often missing, interrupted, or unreliable in many developing democracies, particularly in Africa. They also offer no common scale for comparing the size of party registers with realized electoral fragmentation.

studi.t: Hi Gemini, Who Should I Vote For? The Benefits (and Problems) of Using LLMs As Voting Advice Applications
studi.s: Large language models (LLMs) can provide voters information about political issues, party positions, and even advise on which party to vote for. However, no previous study explores how well off-the-shelf LLMs function as voting advice applications (VAAs). In this article, we address this gap by examining how Gemini 3 Flash advises a sample of 6,022 German survey respondents on which party to vote for, based on their policy preferences and priorities alone. In brief, we find that for most respondents, following the LLM's advice would benefit voter-party policy alignment (i.e.

studi.t: A multilayer network-based modelling framework for epizootic haemorrhagic disease virus transmission in France
studi.s: Epizootic haemorrhagic disease virus serotype 8 (EHDV-8) emerged in France in September 2023 but its transmission dynamics remain poorly characterised. We adapted a stochastic, spatially explicit compartmental model developed for bluetongue to reconstruct the 2023-24 EHDV-8 epidemic in cattle in mainland France. The model represented transmission across cantons, incorporating cattle demography, pasture cover, relative Culicoides abundance and temperature-dependent vector processes.

studi.t: Negotiating Control and Accountability among Stakeholders in High-Risk AI Use Cases: Development and Evaluation of the Method ALIGN
studi.s: Characteristics of Artificial Intelligence (AI) severely restrict human control. This creates new challenges for socio-technical systems design especially in safety-critical domains, where control over risks is essential along with the accountability for any harm caused. Drawing from human factors and AI governance literature, expert interviews and participant observation in a complex high-risk AI use case from the railways, we developed ALIGN, a scenario-based method that supports the governance of and stakeholder involvement in AI development and implementation in three ways: raising…

studi.t: The Impact Of Multitasking In Video Meetings On Meeting Outcomes: Initial Results
studi.s: Multitasking in video meetings is a ubiquitous phenomenon. While extant literature has investigated the circumstances under which people multitask in video meetings, little is known about the impacts of multitasking on meeting outcomes. Building on the findings of previous studies investigating the impact of multitasking in individual non-video meeting work setups and threaded cognition theory, we present a research model that suggests that multitasking may have negative effects on meeting outcomes such as process loss and team meeting outcome satisfaction.

studi.t: What Majority Labels Hide: Annotator Disagreement and Model Errors in Multi-Dialect Arabic Sexism Detection
studi.s: Judgements of sexism are subjective and may vary across communities, yet sexism detection datasets usually reduce annotator judgements to a single majority label, obscuring disagreement and how models behave on contested cases. We introduce MuDAS, a dataset of YouTube comments in Saudi, Egyptian and Moroccan Arabic, each labelled by three native speakers of its dialect, with the individual annotations preserved. We use it to evaluate Arabic encoders fine-tuned with hard-label, soft-label and perspectivist objectives, GPT-5.6 Terra, and four Arabic-centric large language models.

studi.t: Exploring Daily Emotional Well-Being through Personalized Data Analysis
studi.s: This project analysed daily emotional well-being from a personalized perspective using records of emotional states and contextual information derived from daily life. It was based on the idea that well-being is not a fixed value, but varies from day to day, and can be better understood in relation to individual context and behaviour. The work is framed within the field of Data Science and focuses on emotional states at an individual level. The project focused on constructing an integrated daily dataset from multiple personal data sources and analysing emotional states.

studi.t: Global sensitivity analysis of transient regimes in non-Newtonian dam-break flows applied in rheometry
studi.s: Non-Newtonian dam-break flows are a classical problem with numerous engineering applications. These flows are particularly important in alternative rheometry, where they are used to rapidly and affordably estimate rheological properties, such as in the slump test and Bostwick consistometer test. However, the lifting dynamics of the containing obstacle introduce inertial effects that can compromise the accurate estimation of these properties. These effects are influenced by the lifting velocity, the fluid's viscosity, and the initial geometry of the sample.

studi.t: Exploring multimodal AI--XR interactions for software development: From expert perspectives to semantic code outlines
studi.s: AI tools can generate code quickly, but developers still need to understand and check the results. We explore how the enriched multimodal context derived from the extended reality (XR) workspace might help developers manage this information. We first interviewed 13 experts in AI, XR, and related fields to identify opportunities and design challenges (Study 1).

studi.t: Long-lasting chromatin and transcriptional states shape the maintenance of memory ensembles
studi.s: Memories of recent events are stored within minutes in neuronal ensembles in the hippocampus. Over days to weeks, these memories undergo consolidation, and later retrieval depends on reactivation of a subset of neurons within the ensemble. However, how transient experiences produce lasting molecular and cellular changes in hippocampal ensemble neurons remains unknown. Here, we profile the functional, transcriptional, and gene regulatory states of hippocampal memory ensemble neurons at single cell resolution across multiple remote timepoints following single trial contextual fear conditioning.

studi.t: Transcriptomic and Lipidomic Profiling of Human iPSC-Derived Microglia Reveals TREM2-Dependent and -Independent Processes
studi.s: TREM2 has been implicated in AD as a critical regulator of microglial functions and loss of function mutations in TREM2 increases one's risk of developing AD. Given the diverse functional roles of TREM2, we sought to unravel how it affects downstream pathways using human iPSC-derived microglia-like cells (iMGLs) derived from TREM2 knockout (KO) and isogenic control lines and assessing the response to oligomeric amyloid-{beta} 42 (oA{beta}42).

studi.t: In vivo crosslinking and cryo-EM analyses suggest a revised model of conjugative pilus biogenesis
studi.s: Bacterial conjugation requires elaboration of a conjugative pilus by membrane-embedded transport machineries known as Type IV Secretion Systems (T4SSs). Recent structural findings suggested a model of conjugative pilus biogenesis in which the pilus is assembled from the VirB6-base of the T4SS Stalk, while the VirB5-apex is projected at the pilus tip. In this study, we show that in vivo crosslinking of these two Stalk segments within the R388 T4SS has only a modest effect on conjugative transfer efficiency, inconsistent with them separating during pilus elaboration.

studi.t: In the non-canonical NF-κB pathway, binding of the initiating kinase NIK to the pathway's target, p100, serves a nonenzymatic "licensing" role
studi.s: The non-canonical NF-{kappa}B pathway plays pivotal roles in adaptive immunity. It is initiated by NIK-mediated phosphorylation of IKK1, which phosphorylates p100 and promotes processing of newly synthesized p100. However, IKK1 can also be activated by other kinases to mediate distinct functions. Why IKK1-induced p100 processing occurs efficiently downstream of NIK but not of other kinases is unknown.

studi.t: Development of synthetic genetic arrays for studying interactions between the mitochondrial and nuclear genomes
studi.s: Mitochondria, the central axis of metabolism and energy transformation has emerged as a focal point for understanding the aging process and a plethora of human diseases. Yet, how the mitochondrial and nuclear genomes communicate is still unclear. This work aims to allow the analysis of such crosstalk by developing a genome-wide platform for studying genetic interactions between the mitochondrial and nuclear genomes.

studi.t: Single-molecule tracking in the psychrophile Psychrobacter cryohalolentis reveals heat-shock-induced changes in ClpX dynamics
studi.s: Psychrophilic organisms display a series of physiological adaptations which enable them to thrive in cold environments, yet the dynamics of these processes in living cells remain largely unexplored. Here, we establish super-resolution microscopy and single-molecule tracking (SMT) in the cold-adapted bacterium Psychrobacter cryohalolentis, enabling the investigation of protein dynamics in vivo at high spatiotemporal resolution. For controlled expression of HaloTag fusions in this organism, we developed an inducible plasmid expression system based on a galactose-inducible promoter.

studi.t: Sidetrak: a de novo-designed miniprotein targets the kinesin-1 coiled-coil stalk to inhibit MAP7 binding and disrupt mitochondrial transport
studi.s: The coiled-coil domains of cytoskeletal motors contain regulatory surfaces that offer largely unexploited targets for manipulating intracellular transport. The microtubule-associated protein MAP7 promotes kinesin-1 motor activity, binding a coiled-coil surface that overlaps the TPR docking site (TDS), a regulatory interface involved in autoinhibition. Starting from an AlphaFold3 model of this relatively feature-poor surface, we used BoltzGen to design Sidetrak, a 36-amino acid miniprotein that binds kinesin-1 with nanomolar affinity.

studi.t: Repeated regeneration prolongs the juvenile stage and extends lifespan in the annelid Platynereis dumerilii
studi.s: Regeneration restores tissues lost to injury, but its consequences may extend beyond local repair. Whether regeneration produces lasting systemic effects on developmental timing and lifespan remains poorly understood. Here we investigated the long-term consequences of repeated regeneration in the marine annelid Platynereis dumerilii. To determine these consequences, we repeatedly amputated juveniles at monthly intervals, removing approximately half of the body after each regenerative cycle, and compared them with control unamputated siblings.

studi.t: A unifying framework for structured population dynamics in modern coexistence theory
studi.s: Variation within populations is ubiquitous in nature, yet many models and frameworks in community ecology assume that all individuals within a population interact with the community identically. Modern coexistence theory is no exception; however, several subfields of ecology have independently been integrating coexistence theory, each asking the same underlying question: how do structured population dynamics shape coexistence outcomes? Here, I propose a unifying framework for integrating population variation into modern coexistence theory that is applicable across all fields of ecology.

studi.t: Microeukaryotic indicators of freshwater ecosystem condition from a national river monitoring network
studi.s: Microeukaryotes are a diverse and functionally important component of river biofilms, including primary producers, consumers, decomposers, and parasites and symbionts. However, their diversity is likely underestimated, and their composition, environmental drivers, and seasonal dynamics have rarely been studied at large spatial scales. Microbiological monitoring of freshwater ecosystems has historically focused almost entirely on diatoms, so the potential of the wider microbial community as indicators of river condition is unknown.

studi.t: Genetic nurture and shared environmental effects across cognitive, educational, and mental health outcomes
studi.s: Genetic nurture, in which parental genotype predicts offspring outcomes independent of offspring genotype, operates at the between-family level, corresponding to the shared environmental effect (C) in the classical twin design. Genetic nurture represents a portion of C captured by parental genotype. The link between genetic nurture and C has not been systematically quantified across multiple trait domains.

studi.t: A large-scale multi-omics study of cortical miRNA dysregulation in Alzheimer's disease
studi.s: MicroRNAs regulate gene expression, but their roles in Alzheimer's disease pathology and downstream molecular changes remain incompletely characterized. We integrated cortical small RNA-sequencing data from seven datasets across six postmortem cohorts comprising 1,738 individuals with transcriptomic, proteomic, genetic, and single-nucleus data. Meta-analysis of 405 microRNAs identified 16 associated with advanced and four with intermediate neurofibrillary tangle pathology, with miR-132-3p significant in both comparisons.

studi.t: The genetic regulation of thyroid hormones on immune and hematopoietic homeostasis: an integrative Mendelian randomization and colocalization study
studi.s: Background: Hematological traits are closely linked to immune and inflammatory processes implicated in thyroid dysfunction. Although observational studies have reported associations between blood-cell traits and thyroid disorders, whether these relationships reflect causal mechanisms remains unclear. Methods: We performed a two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis to investigate the causal effects of 25 genetically predicted hematological traits on hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism using genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics from the UK Biobank.

studi.t: 'Silent Spring' revisited: sublethal neonicotinoid exposure suppresses birdsong
studi.s: Neonicotinoids are widely used pesticides linked to impaired reproduction and population decline in birds. However, the behavioral mechanisms connecting exposure to reduced reproduction remain unclear. Here, we examined the effects of imidacloprid, one of the most commonly used neonicotinoids, on singing in male zebra finches. Birds received sublethal doses of imidacloprid through drinking water over 30 days, followed by a 30-day washout.

studi.t: The impact of tail-cup handling as an alternative method for picking up laboratory mice
studi.s: The way that laboratory rodents are handled has a significant impact on their welfare. Picking up mice by the tail increases anxiety, reduces voluntary interaction with handlers, and reduces behavioural test reliability compared to more refined handling methods, such as picking up mice inside a handling tunnel or cupping freely on the hand. An alternative in use by the community is to restrain a mouse by the tail-base while scooping it up on the hand and supporting its weight (tail-cup method).

studi.t: Coordinated remodeling of NAD⁺ metabolic networks across the lifespan of Caenorhabditis elegans
studi.s: Changes in the metabolic network that sustain NAD+ during aging remain poorly understood. Analysis of steady state levels is insufficient to reveal whether biosynthetic or consumption pathways are perturbed or preserved. Here, we address this gap in understanding by integrating metabolomics, proteomics, gene-expression profiling, and stable-isotope tracing across the Caenorhabditis elegans adult lifespan. NAD abundance increases with age despite reductions in selected biosynthetic components.

studi.t: Daphniphyllum macropodum genome assembly and multiplexed screening unveils alkaloid modifying enzymes
studi.s: Daphniphyllum macropodum, a small shrub or tree native to East Asia, produces bioactive polycyclic alkaloids of remarkable complexity and variety, making them long-standing, attractive targets for chemical synthesis. However, the biosynthetic origins of Daphniphyllum alkaloids remain unknown, and no pathway-associated enzymes have been identified to date. Here, we report the chromosome-level genome assembly of D. macropodum, representing the first genome assembly for the Daphniphyllaceae, a family in the Saxifragales woody clade.

studi.t: Visually guided analysis of single cell proteomics data with SCP-Viz
studi.s: Single cell proteomics (SCP) is a specialized, but expanding, field of research today. One of many challenges slowing SCP adoption is the inherent instability of the proteome and the changes that can occur before getting cells to a lab for preparation and analysis. Additionally, all current interpretation tools require experienced bioinformaticians to make the step from data to interpretation. Here, we present a visual toolkit that can accept SCP data from any instrument or common data processing algorithm.

studi.t: Location of maximum bending stress in tapered hollow plants: A case study on Moso bamboo (Phyllostachys edulis)
studi.s: Many slender plants, such as trees and bamboo, have naturally tapered, axially graded forms to withstand wind loads; however, while trees feature solid cross-sections, bamboo culms are hollow. Although tapered hollow stems improve mechanical efficiency, the location at which the maximum bending stress develops remains unclear. As failure in such structures is driven by the bending-induced stress state, identifying this location is essential for understanding their structural capacities.

studi.t: MetaboRx: R Shiny application for quality assessment and preprocessing of mass spectrometry-based metabolomics data
studi.s: Introduction Metabolomics datasets offer deep insights into biological systems, yet the multi-step analytical workflow, from sample preparation through instrumental analysis, introduces unwanted variation. This variation, including signal drift and batch effects can confound true biological signals. Although rigorous quality control (QC) and data preprocessing are prerequisites for downstream analysis, existing workflows are often fragmented, time-consuming, and inaccessible to non-experts.

studi.t: TS-Zarr: a cloud-optimized Zarr layout for viewing and analyzing biomedical time series
studi.s: Background: Biomedical time series are recorded at high sampling rates for hours to days across tens to hundreds of channels. Each recording occupies gigabytes to terabytes of storage. FAIR data sharing requirements often place recordings in cloud storage. Visual analysis requires downsampling windows wider than a few seconds to the pixel width of the screen. Visualization tools therefore either read a local copy of the recording or query a dedicated resampling server in front of the data. Findings: We present TS-Zarr, a Zarr v3 layout for time series data.

studi.t: Combined nelfinavir and cisplatin treatment promotes inflammatory signaling and immunogenic cell death in ovarian cancer cells
studi.s: Platinum (Pt) based chemotherapy remains central to ovarian cancer (OC) treatment, but recurrent disease frequently develops Pt resistance and responds poorly to immune checkpoint inhibitors. Immunogenic cell death (ICD) links tumor cell killing to antitumor immunity; however, cisplatin (CDDP), widely used in OC, is an incomplete ICD inducer. We previously demonstrated that the HIV protease inhibitor nelfinavir (NFV) enhances CDDP induced OC cell death and promotes a lytic, pyroptosis associated phenotype.

studi.t: Multiomic analysis of a pleural mesothelioma organoid biobank defines gene dependencies and therapeutic vulnerabilities
studi.s: Pleural mesothelioma (PM) remains an incurable cancer with few effective therapeutic options and limited understanding of its targetable dependencies, owing in part to a scarcity of clinically relevant, scalable models. Here, we describe establishment of an annotated biobank of 26 patient-derived PM organoids that faithfully recapitulate the clinical, genomic and histopathological landscapes of their parent tumours, including driver mutations, copy-number alterations and mutational signatures.

studi.t: CD38-NAMPT-p21 signaling promotes stress adaptation in CLL
studi.s: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) is the most common adult leukemia in the United States, accounting for ~30% of new diagnoses and ~4,000 deaths annually. High CD38 expression is a well-established marker of poor prognosis, yet the mechanistic basis of CD38-mediated treatment failure has remained incompletely understood. Here, we demonstrate that CD38 functions not merely as a prognostic biomarker but as a metabolic and signaling regulator that equips CLL cells to withstand cytotoxic and hypoxic stress.

studi.t: CD3⁺CD4-CD8- (Double-Negative) T-cells Provide Inflammatory Signals That Influence Myeloid Cells and Enhance Survival in Glioblastoma
studi.s: Glioblastoma (GBM) remains resistant to immunotherapy, in part because of a profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. While investigating the consequences of conventional T-cell depletion in a murine glioma model, we unexpectedly identified a population of double-negative T-cells (DNTs; CD3CD4-CD8-) that persisted following combined depletion of CD4 and CD8 T-cells. DNT enrichment was associated with significantly prolonged survival and revealed a distinct inflammatory transcriptional program characterized by activation-associated gene expression.

studi.t: B7-H3 Orchestrates Fibro-Immune Spatial Organisation in Pancreatic Cancer
studi.s: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains one of the most lethal cancers in the western world and is largely resistant to treatment. A major barrier to effective treatment is the highly desmoplastic and immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment, where the organisation of tumour, stromal and resident immune cells limit immune infiltration. B7-H3 (CD276) is an emerging immune checkpoint marker investigated in phase I and Ib/2 clinical trials in PDAC, yet its biological role within the tumour environment remains poorly understood.

studi.t: Common early-life exposure of the colorectal epithelium to the microbiome-derived mutagen colibactin
studi.s: Colibactin is a mutagen produced by bacterial strains in the colorectal microbiomes of some healthy people. It generates somatic mutations characterised by the mutational signatures SBS88 and ID18 in normal human colorectal epithelial cells in vivo. Increasing prevalence of colibactin mutagenesis during the 20th century is hypothesised to have caused recent international increases in early-onset colorectal cancer incidence.

studi.t: ARIPA: Agentic Reasoning for Image-based Pathology Analysis
studi.s: Nuclear segmentation across patient-derived organoids (PDOs) is complicated by differences in morphology, staining, image scale, and acquisition format. We present ARIPA, an automated human-in-the-loop (HITL) system that coordinates pre-trained segmentation tools through a vision-language model (VLM)-based agentic planning, verification, and refinement loop for hematoxylin and eosin images of formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded PDOs. In contrast to existing tools, ARIPA does not require training and achieves good performance.

studi.t: Morphological Changes and Mechanistic Analysis in Osteoblasts Induced by Long-Term Exposure to Radioactive Strontium
studi.s: Radioactive strontium-89 (89Sr) is preferentially deposited in bone tissue, where it directly interacts with osteoblasts; however, the morphological and molecular consequences of sustained 89Sr exposure remain poorly characterized. In this study, mouse pre-osteoblast MC3T3-E1 cells were induced to differentiate into osteoblasts and continuously exposed to 3.7 x 103 Bq/mL 89Sr for nine consecutive passages.

studi.t: Integrating redox dynamics and gene networks reveals ROS-mediated control of Arabidopsis seed germination under water stress
studi.s: Seed germination is a critical step of plant development that is highly sensitive to water availability. During this delicate transition, water stress responses are tightly regulated by multilevel molecular networks that integrate environmental cues into developmental adaptations. Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) play a positive signaling role in seed germination, yet their influence on germination under water stress remains poorly understood.

studi.t: Expanding the SEVA plasmid toolbox for tuneable control of gene expression in Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803
studi.s: The use of cyanobacteria as biotechnological chasses is considered a key point in the circular economy due to their scarce growth requirements and its capacity of fixing atmospheric CO2. However, for obtaining the most of their potential, it is often necessary to count with tools that allow the modification of the genetic expression. In this work, we have characterized a molecular toolbox for reliable control of gene expression control through induction or repression in Synechocystis sp. PCC6803 using SEVA plasmids.

studi.t: Persistent DNA damage reprograms the cutaneous microenvironment into a stress-responsive immunometabolic pro-pigmentary niche
studi.s: Chronic ultraviolet (UV) exposure induces progressive pigmentary remodeling of the skin, yet how persistent DNA damage influences tissue-level responses remains poorly understood. Xeroderma pigmentosum complementation group C (XP-C), characterized by defective global genome nucleotide excision repair, provides a model to investigate these processes. Here, integrating chronic UVB irradiation of Xpc-deficient mice with spatial transcriptomics, multi-omics profiling, and functional analyses, we identify a coordinated multicellular response associated with persistent hyperpigmentation.

studi.t: A normalization strategy for extreme proteome regulation reveals distinct targets of eIF4A1/2 and their inhibitor silvestrol
studi.s: Cells rapidly adjust protein synthesis in response to stress, signalling and drugs, often converging on the cell's translation machinery affecting the synthesis of multiple proteins simultaneously. Nascent proteome analysis, combining pulsed SILAC labelling with enrichment of newly synthesized proteins (NSPs), can measure these changes proteome-wide. However, quantitative proteomics relies on normalization methods that assume most proteins remain unchanged.

studi.t: Developmental emergence of cue-specific fear memory parallels maturation of prefrontal-amygdala circuitry in mice
studi.s: Fear memories formed in early life are forgotten rapidly, but the circuits that delay stable memory expression are not well defined. The medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) projects to the basolateral amygdala (BLA), and both regions mature late, yet the behavior, anatomy and physiology of this pathway have rarely been examined together across development.
