studi.t: Children become accurate years before they become fast: electroencephalography dates the separate maturation of decision components
studi.s: Perceptual decisions, a hallmark of cognitive development, become faster and more accurate from early childhood to adulthood, but whether the underlying components mature together, as a single global gain in processing speed would predict, or on separate timetables remains unclear. Behaviour alone cannot distinguish whether age-related improvement reflects clearer sensory encoding, more efficient evidence accumulation, fewer attention lapses or shorter non-decision processes, and prior direct measurements have typically come from small samples spanning limited age ranges.

studi.t: Heterogeneous short-term plasticity reformats latent temporal information into an explicit population clock
studi.s: Short-term plasticity (STP) supports diverse synaptic-level computations, but how its organization across a circuit shapes emergent, network-level dynamics remains poorly understood. Here, we first characterize STP across sparse inputs to Kenyon cells in the Drosophila mushroom body, revealing an unstructured and near-random organization that could not be explained by either pre- or postsynaptic cell identity.

studi.t: Intracellular spirochete integrates into a chemosynthetic micro-consortium of a deep-sea vent mussel
studi.s: Animal-microbe interactions comprise a diverse functional landscape, spanning pathogenic to mutualistic outcomes across extracellular and intracellular niches. Within this context, spirochetes are predominantly documented as extracellular associates or transient pathogens, leaving stable, functional endosymbiosis within animal cells unverified. Here, we report the discovery of an intracellular consortium comprising a spirochete and a primary sulfur-oxidizing bacterium within gill bacteriocytes of the deep-sea hydrothermal vent mussel Gigantidas horikoshii.

studi.t: How good a predictor the in vitro antibiogram is, of in vivo antibiotic efficacy? An in vitro - in vivo integrated approach
studi.s: Conventional antimicrobial susceptibility testing, particularly the disc diffusion assay (DDA), provides a convenient means of assessing bacterial susceptibility to antibiotics. However, its ability to predict antibiotic efficacy in an infected host remains uncertain. This study investigated the relationship between DDA-derived inhibition zones and host-protective antibiotic activity using Caenorhabditis elegans infection models involving three bacterial pathogens: methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Clostridioides difficile.

studi.t: Rapidly and reproducibly building a comprehensive catalogue of resistance-associated variants for M. tuberculosis surveillance
studi.s: Background: Catalogues of genetic variants associated with resistance underpin whole-genome sequencing (WGS)-based predictions of drug susceptibility in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, and are essential for molecular diagnostics and surveillance. The current gold standard catalogues are those released by the WHO but the underlying data are not fully released and they are difficult to interpret. Open and reproducible methods would help address these problems, extending the important work already done.

studi.t: Altered age-dependent somatic mutational trajectories in ALS motor cortex neurons
studi.s: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disease in which disease onset is influenced by genetic, age-associated and environmental factors. Somatic mutations accumulate throughout life and may provide a molecular link between aging and neuronal vulnerability. Here, we investigated neuronal somatic mutational patterns in ALS and control motor cortex using three previously generated 10X single-nucleus RNA and ATAC sequencing datasets.

studi.t: Regulatory grammar design of tissue-specific enhancers across species
studi.s: Enhancers encode tissue-specific gene expression through the combinatorial identity, number, and arrangement of transcription factor motifs, collectively known as regulatory grammar. However, existing deep-learning methods directly optimize nucleotide sequences, leaving enhancer regulatory grammar implicit. Here we introduce REgulatory Grammar Architecture via reinforcement Learning (REGAL), a framework that explicitly programs enhancer grammar under sequence-to-function oracles.

studi.t: A de novo reference genome of the red seaweed Furcellaria lumbricalis
studi.s: Furcellaria lumbricalis is a red seaweed that occurs across a broad salinity gradient, ranging from the saline waters of the NE Atlantic to the brackish Baltic Sea. In the Baltic Sea, natural populations of F. lumbricalis are harvested commercially, primarily for furcellaran extraction, a sulphated polysaccharide used as a stabilizing, thickening, and gelling agent. Genomic resources for this species remain absent, constraining evolutionary, ecological, and applied research.

studi.t: Structural basis of end processing in the nucleosome by polynucleotide kinase-phosphatase
studi.s: Genomic DNA is packaged into chromatin through a fundamental repeating unit known as the nucleosome core particle. Chromatinized DNA is under constant assault from endogenous and exogenous sources of damage, which must be effectively repaired to preserve genome stability. Single-strand breaks (SSBs) with chemically heterogeneous DNA ends are one of the most prevalent forms of genomic DNA damage. These SSBs must be enzymatically processed prior to downstream gap-filling DNA synthesis and/or nick ligation during single-strand break repair (SSBR).

studi.t: Biomaterial preservation of mesenchymal stem/stromal cell fitness improves haematopoietic support in a post-leukaemic bone marrow niche model
studi.s: Mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (MSCs) are promising regenerative partners to haematopoietic stem cell (HSC) transplantation used for treatment of blood cancers. However, prolonged ex vivo expansion induces senescence and phenotypic drift that may compromise therapeutic efficacy. Here, we engineered a poly(ethyl acrylate)-laminin interface to preserve MSC fitness during expansion and investigated whether this biomaterial-controlled state influences function in a bioengineered post-leukaemic bone marrow niche model.

studi.t: BiomedCAT: Biomedical Context Analysis Tool for Supporting Mechanistic Hypothesis Generation via User-defined Contextual Subgraph Extraction
studi.s: Researchers formulate mechanistic hypotheses in slides and figures long before they write them as text, yet knowledge-graph (KG) tools expect a query in the vocabulary of the graph. We present BiomedCAT, an open-source workflow that turns biomedical slides into a subgraph of the RTX-KG2c knowledge graph shaped by the user's research profile, on a laptop and without sending the documents out.

studi.t: Systematic evaluation using SigMatch reveals how sample tissues shape transcriptomic disease relationships
studi.s: Motivation Diseases often share underlying molecular characteristics captured by transcriptional responses. Leveraging this knowledge transfer can aid in uncovering novel disease biology and drug repurposing. Large-scale transcriptomic datasets and disease signatures provide an opportunity to computationally identify these shared disease relationships based on shared genome-wide gene expression changes. However, disease signatures are strongly influenced by sample tissue, making it difficult to distinguish shared disease biology from shared tissue origin.

studi.t: XAMPGen: An Interpretable Super Intelligence Pipeline For Novel Antimicrobial Peptide Discovery
studi.s: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are short peptides with a broad spectrum of activity against bacterial pathogens, representing a promising avenue for combating the growing threat of antibiotic resistance. This study focuses on two main components: 1) generative super intelligence (GenSI) and 2) utilizing explainable super intelligence (XSI). We fine-tuned ProGen, a decoder-only protein language model, on known AMPs to generate novel peptide sequences with strong antimicrobial properties.

studi.t: ARGeement: sequence-based, versioned mapping of antimicrobial resistance gene databases
studi.s: Genomic studies of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) rely on several independently curated reference databases, which describe the same genes under different names, in different structures and with different classifications. This makes results obtained with different databases difficult to compare. ARGeement maps the entries of AMRFinderPlus, the Comprehensive Antibiotic Resistance Database (CARD) and ResFinder/DisinFinder to each other by protein sequence, independently of their names.

studi.t: Most substitutions need more than one base change and an exact test tells which deposited scans measure the route
studi.s: Design methods that reach a target through an intermediate take two substitutions at one position, and no deep mutational scan built from a single parental sequence reports the second. The detour is common, since 230 of the 380 ordered pairs of amino acids are more than one base change apart. Both substitutions are nevertheless present in the public record wherever one protein has been scanned on two parental backgrounds that differ at a position. We assemble every such comparison in MaveDB, 102,421 complete two-step routes over 65 protein clusters.

studi.t: Spinal Recurrent Inhibition Shapes the Dynamics of TMS-induced Motor-Evoked Potentials
studi.s: Background: Motor-evoked potentials (MEPs) elicited by TMS reflect the integrity of the corticospinal pathway, yet the contributions of spinal and peripheral mechanisms to the shape of individual MEP waveforms remain poorly understood. Objective: To develop a biologically grounded model of the spinal and peripheral motor pathway that can be fitted to individual MEP waveforms across TMS intensities, and to test whether Renshaw cell (RC) recurrent inhibition is required to reproduce them.

studi.t: Persistent light-induced reduction of neuronal excitability in cortical neurons
studi.s: Visible light is widely used in neuroscience, yet its direct effects on neuronal activity in the absence of optogenetic manipulation remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigated whether light stimulation can induce sustained changes in neuronal excitability. Using electrophysiological recordings in brain slices, we show that repeated pulses of blue light (5 s, 430 to 495 nm, 19 mW) produce a robust and persistent reduction in evoked firing activity in cortical neurons from both male and female mice, with an average decrease of ~60% relative to baseline.

studi.t: Overcoming subtype-specific immune resistance in small cell lung cancer through RNA-based immunotherapy
studi.s: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) comprises neuroendocrine (NE) and non-neuroendocrine (non-NE) subtypes with distinct immune landscapes and responses to therapy. Here, we established murine experimental metastases models to investigate RNA vaccination across SCLC subtypes. These exhibited distinct organotrophic properties and differ in both the magnitude and kinetics of interferon-induced MHC-I upregulation. Vaccination controlled non-NE tumors but provided limited survival benefit against NE tumors established in the lung or liver.

studi.t: Effects of drying and milling treatments on estimates of foliar functional traits with VSWIR spectroscopy
studi.s: Spectroscopy of dried, ground foliage is a cost-efficient measurement to estimate leaf biochemical traits in agricultural and ecological research. Drying removes water that obscures biochemical absorption features, and milling homogenizes samples, yet how drying and milling methods affect spectra and trait predictions is understudied. We compared two drying methods (oven-drying; flash-freezing then freeze-drying) and three milling methods (coarse and fine rotary milling; ball milling) using 61 individuals of 11 broadleaf and needle- or scale-leaved woody species.

studi.t: JEPA-SORT: World-Model Embeddings Improve Deep-Sea Multi-Object Tracking on Visually Homogeneous Fauna
studi.s: Protecting deep-sea sessile communities as Marine Protected Areas (MPAs) requires accurate estimates of their spatial distribution and abundance. Existing computer-vision detection methods require careful calibration to avoid counting errors; multi-object tracking (MOT) theoretically offers a more robust alternative. In practice, however, poor lighting and turbidity limit the efficacy of purely kinematic MOT algorithms in deep-sea environments.

studi.t: Computable Genomes: A Layered Computational Framework for Non-Coding DNA and Cellular Behavior
studi.s: Genome-wide association studies have catalogued tens of thousands of trait-associated loci, most of them in non-coding DNA, yet for most loci the path from nucleotide to phenotype remains correlational. We propose a layered computational decomposition of the genome as a complement to data-driven approaches: sequence as formal language, sequence as information-bearing signal, mobile elements as runtime, compilation to interaction networks through thermodynamic and rule-based models, and execution as cellular and multicellular dynamics.

studi.t: Spatiotemporal profiling reveals emergence of cell type-specific molecular aging and senescence programs in the spinal cord
studi.s: The spinal cord is the primary relay center between the periphery and the brain, playing a critical role in sensory, motor and autonomic function. Despite its functional importance, the cellular and molecular changes underlying spinal cord aging and their relationship to cellular senescence - a hallmark associated with aging - remain incompletely understood.

studi.t: Genome assembly for Amanita muscaria var. muscaria
studi.s: Amanita muscaria is a charismatic and widely distributed mushroom-forming fungus. Amanita muscaria comprises a species complex, and genomic resources are unevenly distributed, which may bias genetic and genomic study of the species complex. This study produces a high quality hybrid genome assembly of a specimen from New Zealand. Phylogenetic analysis shows that this belongs to Amanita muscaria var. muscaria.

studi.t: ChIMe-seq enables multimodal epigenetic profiling in single molecules and single cells
studi.s: Recent advances in single-cell and single-molecule sequencing have enabled high-resolution characterization of epigenetic states. However, methods that jointly measure multiple layers of epigenetic regulation within the same molecules and cells remain limited. Here, we developed Chromatin Immuno-Methylation sequencing (ChIMe-seq), a multimodal approach that simultaneously profiles histone modifications, DNA methylation, and nucleosome positioning genome-wide in single molecules and single cells.

studi.t: Target-enrichment sequencing reveals intergenotypic reassortment of infectious salmon anaemia virus in Atlantic Canada
studi.s: Infectious salmon anaemia virus (ISAV) causes severe disease and substantial economic losses in farmed Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar). The virus has an eight-segment, negative-sense single-stranded RNA (ssRNA) genome and is divided into European and North American genotypes. Despite their co-circulation in locations such as the Atlantic coast of Canada, reassortment between these genotypes has never been observed.

studi.t: Trunk stiffness of the American giant millipede during terrain bridging
studi.s: Slender, flexible bodies allow animals such as millipedes to regularly traverse heterogeneous, uneven terrain and complex obstacles by using their body's compliance to conform to the terrain. Orchestrating a slender body's many degrees of freedom poses a control challenge, with possible strategies ranging in complexity and cost, from complex muscle actuation patterns to simple passive compliance. Here we investigate these behavioral strategies by examining American giant millipedes (Narceus americanus) bridging between terrains of different heights.

studi.t: LUC3D: Multi-animal 3D pose tracking in the browser
studi.s: Animal behavior unfolds in three dimensions over time, yet accessible scientific tools for analyzing it in its natural form remain limited. Uncertainty from popular 2D pose methods can be refined with multi-camera approaches to produce more accurate 3D estimates. This paper presents LUC3D (Label Unification and Correspondence in 3D Annotation GUI), a browser-based 3D GUI for reducing the amount of manual labor required for labeling, proofreading, and multi-camera multi-animal tracking while requiring no installation to maximize accessibility.

studi.t: CIRCA learns identifiable cell- and niche-level programs and their interactions with tissue pathology from spatial transcriptomics
studi.s: Interactions among cells and their local microenvironments shape tissue organization and function, while their dysregulation can contribute to disease. In Alzheimer's disease (AD), the complex responses of glial cells and neurons to amyloid-{beta} pathology can both mitigate and exacerbate neuronal injury. Spatial transcriptomics enables investigation of these relationships in situ, but recovering interpretable transcriptional programs and their interactions from spatial transcriptomics remains challenging, in part because conventional nonlinear models are non-identifiable.

studi.t: Evaluation depth reshapes method rankings in proteomic co-abundance network inference
studi.s: Network inference from quantitative proteomics is usually benchmarked at a single, arbitrarily chosen number of top-ranked edges, so the influence of evaluation depth has not, to our knowledge, been systematically tested. We compared five strategies (random forest with bootstrap selection-frequency filtering, WGCNA, GENIE3, Spearman correlation and context likelihood of relatedness) across seven proteomic datasets from four quantification platforms, using harmonised preprocessing and Precision@K, the fraction of a method's K top-ranked protein pairs present in a pooled reference of curated…

studi.t: Breedbase: An Integrated Breeding Informatics System with Statistical Analysis and Decision-Support Tools
studi.s: Breeding programs are becoming increasingly data-intensive, digital and collaborative. One-stop digital breeding ecosystems, in which data storage, field workflow tools, statistical analysis and breeding decision-support tools are seamlessly integrated, are increasingly important. Breedbase (https://breedbase.org) is one of the few open-source platforms that integrate these functionalities within a single system. It provides tools for phenotypic data quality control, descriptive, inferential and predictive statistical analyses.

studi.t: SPIDER: Contextualizing Biomedical Knowledge for Evidence-Grounded Scientific Reasoning
studi.s: Aggregated relations in biomedical knowledge graphs can obscure evidence and study conditions, complicating the distinction between scientific disagreement and contextual differences. Here we introduce SPIDER, a multi-agent framework grounding biomedical relations in literature evidence and extracting study conditions for interpretation. Applied to a graph integrating 48 databases and ontologies, SPIDER analyzed 1.95 million PubMed abstracts, adding 2.31 million previously unrepresented, literature-supported entity pairs to construct SPIDER-KG.

studi.t: HARICOT: De Novo Assembly of Raw Nanopore Signals using Fuzzy de Bruijn Graphs
studi.s: Nanopore sequencing enables reading long nucleotide sequences by measuring characteristic changes in ionic current as molecules pass through a nanopore. These current measurements, known as raw signals, can be analyzed without translating them into bases (i.e., without basecalling), which provides fast and resource-efficient genome analysis. Prior work, Rawsamble, enables finding overlaps between raw nanopore signals, without basecalling them, and generating assemblies from these overlaps with off-the-shelf assemblers such as miniasm.

studi.t: A Deep Operator Network to Predict Thermal Dose on Brain Tumors in MRI-Guided Laser Induced Thermal Therapy: with Synthetic Data
studi.s: Background: MRI-guided laser interstitial thermal therapy (LITT) provides minimally invasive option for surgical treatment of recurrent brain tumors. While patient-specific prediction of thermal dose distributions would improve treatment planning, no quantitative methods currently exist for this purpose. Although conventional numerical solvers are being widely investigated, these methods are computationally expensive and often limited by accuracy and reliability. Purpose: Here we propose DeepoLITT, a rapid and accurate model to predict quantitatively heat propagation in LITT procedures.

studi.t: Timing and meaning in spoken thought relate to distinct patterns of brain dynamics
studi.s: When people think aloud, their reports vary in duration and in how closely successive thoughts are related in meaning. We asked whether these two dimensions relate to distinct patterns of brain dynamics. Using 10-minute think-aloud fMRI scans from 75 adults, we quantified timing as variability in sentence-event duration and semantic continuity as similarity between adjacent grouped thoughts.

studi.t: Stability and flexibility in the Wisconsin Card Sorting Task emerge from goal-directed inference and planning under the free-energy principle
studi.s: In goal-directed behavior, the brain has to balance stability and flexibility. Stability means keeping the current recognition of environmental context, whereas flexibility means switching to a new one. The Wisconsin Card Sorting Task (WCST) is a standard task for studying this balance. In this task, stability is keeping the category estimate after correct feedback, and flexibility is switching it after incorrect feedback. Computational models have been proposed to elucidate the mechanism behind this balance.

studi.t: Spectral and complexity-based signatures of advanced concentration absorption meditation: A high-density EEG study of jhana
studi.s: Advanced meditation provides structured and reproducible alterations of consciousness that are increasingly used as model states for the neuroscience of consciousness. Jhana-type advanced concentration absorption meditation (ACAM-J) consists of eight progressively deepening absorption states (ACAM-J1-8) in which sensory and self-referential content gradually attenuate. We applied high-density EEG and a comprehensive multidimensional battery of spectral and complexity measures to characterize each ACAM-J state individually in 20 advanced meditators, together with phenomenological ratings.

studi.t: Distinct developmental organization of intrinsic brain dynamics supports different components of inhibitory control during adolescence
studi.s: Adolescent inhibitory control develops within a changing organization of intrinsic brain activity, yet the signal properties and cortical systems associated with different control demands remain unclear. We studied 101 youths aged 8-18 years using brain entropy (BEN), amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations (ALFF), fractional ALFF (fALFF), and regional homogeneity (ReHo) derived from resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging. Voxelwise and seven-network models evaluated age associations and task-by-age interactions while adjusting for sex, head motion, and gray-matter anatomy.

studi.t: Neuronal activity regulates glycolysis to sculpt synaptic transmission
studi.s: Neuronal computation imposes rapid, localized changes in energy consumption, yet how energy production is regulated at such fine spatiotemporal scales is incompletely understood. Using two photon imaging of neuronal activity and energy metabolism in Drosophila , we show that neurons recruit glycolysis in less than a second, with cell-type and subcellular specificity. This coupling scales with neuronal activity and is regulated by AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK).

studi.t: Oligodendrocyte Development and Myelination in the 22q11.2 Deletion Syndrome
studi.s: The 22q11.2 deletion syndrome is associated with a high risk of neurodevelopmental disorders, including a 25% chance of developing schizophrenia (SCZ). SCZ is prevalent in 0.4-0.7% of the population. Evidence suggests that the cognitive deficits of SCZ may be caused by neurodevelopmental disconnection due to impaired oligodendrocyte (OL) maturation and myelination. We hypothesized that the 22q11.2 deletion syndrome impairs OL life cycle progression, halting oligodendrocytes in their immature phase and preventing advancement to the mature stage.

studi.t: Drastic improvement in MHC class I epitope prediction through training data augmentation, generative adversarial network modeling of selfness, and consideration of homology to class II epitopes.
studi.s: Accurate identification of immunogenic neoantigens is critical for personalized cancer vaccines but remains hindered by the high false-positive rates of current predictors. Here, we present DeepOmicsNeo, a modular deep learning framework that harmonizes three biological determinants of immunogenicity. The first module, DeepOmicsNeo-Binding, overcomes data scarcity in non-9mer peptide-Class I Major Histocompatibility Complex (MHC) binding prediction via a novel augmentation strategy that synthesizes pseudo-binders and non-binders by editing non-anchor residues, outperforming its competitors.

studi.t: GRABS: a content-addressed antibody-antigen binding-affinity dataset with predicted structures and a leak-free benchmark
studi.s: Machine-learning prediction of antibody-antigen binding affinity depends as much on the training data as on the model, yet public affinity measurements are scattered across databases with incompatible formats, mix genuine dissociation constants with censored or predicted values, and concentrate most of their label mass on a few heavily mutated targets.

studi.t: Pioneering Hybrid Genome Assemblies of Fusarium graminearum and Fusarium avenaceum from Indian Wheat: Insights into Virulence Frameworks and Genome Evolution
studi.s: Fusarium head blight (FHB), primarily caused by various species of Fusarium, is a destructive disease of wheat that reduces yield and contaminates grain with mycotoxins. The present study reports high-quality hybrid genome assemblies for two Indian wheat isolates, Fusarium graminearum strain TNW1 and Fusarium avenaceum strain DMW8, representing the first genome-scale comparative study of FHB associated Fusarium isolates infectious on wheat from India.

studi.t: Decline and extirpation of birds in a tropical Asian grassland ecosystem over the past century
studi.s: Grasslands are facing unprecedented habitat loss due to settler-driven agriculture during colonial expansion, conversion to tree plantations, misclassification as wastelands, absorption into megadevelopment projects, and insufficient response to climate change. Globally, grassland birds have faced the steepest declines, with many formerly common species facing rapid decline, losing much of their original ranges. In South Asia, our knowledge of how these land-use changes in grasslands have affected birds remain scant.

studi.t: Contingency and determinism in rapid adaptation shape evolutionary rescue and extinction in Drosophila
studi.s: Populations declining under anthropogenic stressors, including rising temperatures and novel chemicals, may depend on rapid adaptation to persist. Yet fundamental questions remain about what promotes and constrains such evolutionary rescue. We tracked demographic, phenotypic, and genomic dynamics in a replicated outdoor evolution experiment using Drosophila under insecticide stress, and also manipulated initial maladaptation by pre-adapting a subset of populations.

studi.t: The evolution of sexual dimorphism in the weapon system of leaf-footed bugs (Hemiptera: Coreoidea)
studi.s: The natural world contains an extraordinary diversity of morphologically elaborate traits, yet the evolutionary processes underlying the emergence and diversification of sexual dimorphism in these structures are not fully resolved. Some of the most extravagant of these traits are the mechanical weapons of sexual selection. They include such noteworthy structures as the tusks of narwals and the mandibles of stag beetles. Such traits are notoriously sexually dimorphic -- often elaborated in one sex while absent or reduced in the other sex.

studi.t: Systematic prediction of genetic variance in a line development program
studi.s: To date, predicting the genetic variance (VG) in biparental crosses has been unreliable. My objective was to determine if predicting VG via tabular analysis, which was developed assuming free recombination and having known VG in founder crosses, is effective even if these unrealistic assumptions are unmet. With line X being developed from the P1/P2 cross, the VG in X/Y was predicted as VX/Y = {lambda}1VP1/Y + {lambda}2VP2/Y, where {lambda}1 was the parental contribution of P1 to X and {lambda}2 was the parental contribution of P2 to X.

studi.t: Multimodal Structural and Regulatory Architecture of Coding and Non-Coding Variants Across the Orofacial Clefting TP63-IRF6-GRHL3 Network
studi.s: Pathogenic variation across the TP63-IRF6-GRHL3 transcriptional network causes syndromic and nonsyndromic orofacial clefts (OFCs), yet scalar sequence predictors collapse distinct failure modes and leave isoform-specific coding variants, splice-altering indels, and distal enhancer alleles unresolved. Here, we integrate 29 AlphaFold 3 (AF3) assemblies (10 wild-type, 19 mutant), thermodynamic stability ({Delta}{Delta}G) calculations, and AlphaGenome regulatory modeling across clinical, saturation-mutagenesis, and reporter benchmarks.

studi.t: Comparative metagenomics reveals diversity and metabolic heterogeneity of sediment microbes from the Great Barrier Reef
studi.s: Microbial communities in coral reefs are highly connected through benthic-pelagic coupling. Pelagic and host-associated microbiomes have recently been characterised via genome-resolved metagenomics. However, similar characterisation of sediment communities has lagged behind due to their higher complexity. Here, using short- and long-read shotgun sequence data, we characterised sediment microbial communities of Australia's Great Barrier Reef.

studi.t: MARRI: Mechanism-Aware Learning of RNA-RNA Interactions with Foundation Models
studi.s: RNA-RNA interactions (RRIs) are central to post-transcriptional regulation, yet their prediction requires accounting for structural accessibility and intermolecular base pairing beyond sequence complementarity. Pretrained RNA foundation models provide representations of individual RNAs, but translating these representations into interaction predictions requires mechanistic knowledge of interaction recognition.

studi.t: LipidRT: leveraging retention time coherence for robust lipid annotation in reversed-phase LC-MS-based lipidomics
studi.s: MS/MS data alone is often insufficient for confident lipid identification, while existing retention time (RT)-based methods, despite their promise, have limited applicability. We present LipidRT, an R-based Shiny application that uses RT coherence to validate, refine and expand lipid annotations in untargeted RPLC-HRMS lipidomics in a dataset-specific, software-agnostic manner.

studi.t: spicyR enables robust, well-powered co-localisation tests in large spatial omics cohorts
studi.s: Spatial omics technologies can now profile finely resolved cell populations in patient tissue at scale, offering a way to link their arrangement to outcomes. Yet images often differ in size, shape and cell content, and existing tests between patient groups mistake these differences for co-localisation or weight every image equally. We present spicyR v2, which avoids both problems with a fast, permutation-free test that accounts for these differences and weights each image by how precisely it measures co-localisation.

studi.t: Quantifying Homology and Length Bias in Antimicrobial Peptide Prediction
studi.s: Bacteria are becoming resistant to existing antibiotics faster than new ones are found. Antimicrobial peptides are a promising alternative, but laboratory testing is slow and costly. Candidates are therefore ranked first by a classifier, and published classifiers report near-perfect accuracy. Two controls are missing from the benchmarks behind those numbers. Training and test peptides are not separated by sequence homology. The negative class is not matched to the positive class by length.

studi.t: Learning spatial cellular state through 3D reconstruction of the cell
studi.s: Subcellular-resolution spatial transcriptomics localizes individual RNA transcripts within cells with high-precision. Existing methods for identifying spatially organized cell populations rely on cellular niches defined by neighboring cells, leaving open whether such populations can be identified from individual-cell representations alone. Moreover, representations that jointly capture transcript identity and three-dimensional (3D) spatial organization have not been systematically learned or biologically evaluated.

studi.t: Benchmarking four large language models on generating and selecting hypotheses that match published findings in 50 studies of ageing biology
studi.s: Objective We asked how often hypotheses generated by large language models for 50 research tasks matched the withheld finding of the published study, and whether model forecasts could identify the matching hypotheses. Methods We built tasks from 50 peer-reviewed studies in ageing biology published after the models' stated training cutoffs; each task gave the background and a research question and withheld the study's finding (the reference finding).

studi.t: GenVinci reconstructs 3D molecular tissue scenes from histology to map senescence across aging and disease
studi.s: Spatial omics has generated measurements at unprecedented scale, yet computational approaches remain largely confined to individual modalities and 2D representations. Here we assemble ImageOmicsNet-300M, a corpus of 300 million single-cell and spatial transcriptomic profiles, including 24.9 million H&E-predicted virtual spatial transcriptomics profiles, and 4,623 H&E sections. Of these H&E sections, we generated 1,782 from aging mouse organs and serially sectioned human skin spanning five decades, with matched spatial transcriptomics and snRNA-seq.

studi.t: Integrating disease and protein networks expands genetic support for therapeutic targets
studi.s: Human genetics guides therapeutic target selection, but direct genetic support covers few clinically investigated target-indication pairs, each linking a target to a disease. Here we introduce BRIDGE (Biological Relation-Informed Diffusion of Genetic Evidence), which propagates genetic evidence through coupled protein-protein interaction and disease-similarity networks. Each candidate's score is calibrated against scores obtained after randomly substituting similarly connected genes for genes with direct genetic support.

studi.t: ATSASfold: a web server integrating AlphaFold models with ATSAS-based SAXS analysis
studi.s: Small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) is routinely used for the structural characterization of protein monomers in solution, and computational prediction methods such as AlphaFold now provide accurate atomic models for most proteins. When a predicted model and the experimental scattering curve disagree, several refinement strategies exist, but selecting the appropriate one remains difficult, particularly for users without SAXS modeling expertise. ATSASfold is a web server developed to help analyse the results of SAXS measurements on protein monomers and select appropriate refinement strategies.

studi.t: Solanaceae-derived spirostane saponins inhibit dengue virus replication and remodel host-cell metabolism
studi.s: Flaviviruses reprogram host-cell metabolism to support viral replication. In previous work, we showed that Solanaceae-derived spirostane saponins inhibit dengue virus replication and were predicted to interact with viral enzymes. Here, we investigated whether S01, a purified solid from Solanum ovalifolium containing predominantly two characterized spirostane saponins, also modulates host-cell metabolism in association with reduced permissiveness to dengue virus serotype 2 (DENV-2).

studi.t: Commentary on the nomenclatural status of Benthoctopus Grimpe, 1921 (Cephalopoda: Octopoda) and redescription of "Vulcanoctopus" pseudonymus (Grimpe, 1922)
studi.s: The nomenclatural status of the two octopus genera Bathypolypus Grimpe, 1921 and Benthoctopus Grimpe, 1921 has been the subject of considerable, at times contentious debate since both genera were first proposed. Of these two genera, Bathypolypus has precedence, with Benthoctopus relegated to synonymy of Bathypolypus in 2002. However, the case for this synonymy was not compelling.

studi.t: Precision of sensory representations in cortex is indexed by alpha power and pupil dilation, and tracks the dynamics of correlated noise
studi.s: Sensory representations fluctuate in precision from moment to moment, shaping the fidelity of perception and memory. Population-coding theory proposes that these fluctuations are constrained by correlated variability within neural populations, yet linking these mechanisms to behaviour and brain state in humans has remained challenging. Here we combined EEG with an encoding-decoding framework to reconstruct orientation-selective population responses and quantify representational precision dynamically over time.

studi.t: PROGMF: Progressive Multimodal Fusion and Representation Learning for Incomplete Neuroimaging Data
studi.s: Multimodal neuroimaging studies often involve cohorts with partially overlapping data modalities. Many conventional multimodal fusion methods rely on participants with complete observations across the selected modalities. We introduce Progressive Multimodal Fusion (ProgMF), a novel fusion framework for learning multimodal source representations from incomplete neuroimaging data without imputing missing observations.

studi.t: Counterfactual aging in individual digital twin brains uncovers a latent dimension of resilience to aging
studi.s: Cognitive reserve concerns why the same aging causes less decline in some individuals than others, a question that digital twin brains can address by aging each individual in silico. Here we present Brain-VRNN, a connectome-constrained variational recurrent neural network trained on longitudinal multitask functional MRI. Its regenerated brain signals reproduced four functional aging markers of unseen individuals (r = 0.93-0.96) and identified each person (accuracy 0.98).

studi.t: Aging remodels the neuronal activity-dependent transcriptome
studi.s: Experience-driven neuronal activity induces coordinated transcriptional programs in neurons and glia that support plasticity and memory. How aging reshapes these activity-regulated gene (ARG) programs, and whether activity mitigates or exacerbates aging phenotypes, remain open questions with implications for cognitive decline. Here, we develop novel-environment and chemogenetic paradigms to characterize age-dependent remodeling of ARG transcriptomes in the mouse hippocampus at single-cell resolution.

studi.t: Thrombin cleavage of circulating osteopontin in the lung drives hippocampal neuroinflammation and acute delirium-like neurologic dysfunction after acute kidney injury
studi.s: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common clinical problem with high morbidity and mortality due to frequently occurring secondary organ complications, including acute neurologic dysfunction, such as delirium. Specific mechanisms responsible for this kidney-brain crosstalk are unknown but hypothesized to include uremic toxins and neuroinflammation secondary to systemic inflammation. Here we show that uremic mice with AKI show hippocampal monocytic neuroinflammation associated with acute delirium-like neurologic dysfunction only in the presence of circulating osteopontin fragments.

studi.t: Molecular analysis of 55 dopamine transporter variants from psychiatric patients reveals convergent mechanisms of dysfunction
studi.s: Rare genetic variants are increasingly recognized as contributors to neuropsychiatric disease and may reveal underlying pathobiological mechanisms. The dopamine transporter (DAT), encoded by SLC6A3, regulates dopaminergic neurotransmission through rapid dopamine (DA) reuptake. Although disease-associated DAT variants have been linked to disorders ranging from infantile parkinsonism to neuropsychiatric disease, the molecular basis of DAT dysfunction remains poorly understood. Here, we systematically investigated 55 DAT missense variants identified in the iPSYCH2012-nested case-control cohort.

studi.t: Cask dysfunction in inhibitory neurons reveals distinct synaptic and epileptic phenotypes in mouse models of CASK-related disorder
studi.s: Epilepsy is a major neurological manifestation of genetic neurodevelopmental disorders, yet how genetic disruptions produce distinct seizure phenotypes remains poorly understood. CASK-related disorder is an X-linked neurodevelopmental disorder frequently accompanied by epilepsy. It is caused by pathogenic variants in CASK, which encodes calcium/calmodulin-dependent serine protein kinase, a protein with diverse molecular functions. Here, we establish sex-specific mouse models of CASK-related disorder and identify epileptic phenotypes in both sexes.

studi.t: Modern speech recognition systems exhibit human-like word recognition but superhuman use of statistical dependencies between words
studi.s: Advances in machine learning have yielded machine systems that approach human performance on real-world perception tasks. For speech recognition, it remains unclear whether such models' behavior resembles that of humans. We addressed this question by measuring word recognition abilities in humans and models across 272 speech distortions, providing a detailed behavioral fingerprint. Three recent industry speech recognition models trained on hundreds of years of speech outperformed humans.

studi.t: Temperature and skn-1 determine whether developmental daf-2 knockdown extends C. elegans lifespan
studi.s: The evolutionarily conserved insulin/IGF-1 signalling pathway (IIS) shapes life-history traits largely through downstream transcription factors including SKN-1. Reduced IIS (rIIS) in adulthood robustly extends Caenorhabditis elegans lifespan, yet developmental rIIS has long been considered unable to extend lifespan and costly to fitness, a conclusion drawn almost entirely from experiments at 25{degrees}C, near the species' upper thermal limit. Here we knocked down daf-2 during development in wild-type and skn-1 loss-of-function nematodes across constant and fluctuating temperatures.

studi.t: Auditory bullae enlarge along an aridity gradient in a diverse subfamily of small carnivorous mammals
studi.s: The world`s arid regions are home to diverse assemblages of small mammals, many of which possess a range of physiological, behavioral, and sensory adaptations to the harsh selective pressures imposed by arid environments. The mammalian skull facilitates a range of sensory functions, meaning that arid-dwelling species likely possess distinct skull adaptations which have evolved in response to the unique selective pressures imposed by arid environments.

studi.t: The assembly and annotation of a new reference genome for the eastern mosquitofish (Gambusia holbrooki) reveal a new sex chromosome system in its invasive range
studi.s: Gambusia species, especially eastern mosquitofish - Gambusia holbrooki - are of broad relevance to evolutionary biologists aiming at understanding genomic bases of adaptation during biological invasions and rapid response to selection to heterogeneous environments including pollution. Here we used HiFi and HiC to assemble a new, high quality, chromosome scale, genome sequence for G. holbrooki in its invasive range. Both haplotypes of the nuclear genome were assembled, comprising 657.64 Mb and 651.75 Mb respectively, in 24 chromosomes and had N50s of 28.97 Mb and 28.25 Mb.

studi.t: Transposase-mediated activity is associated with accessory gene turnover and positive-selection signals in Streptococcus pyogenes
studi.s: Streptococcus pyogenes causes diseases ranging from mild pharyngitis to life-threatening invasive infection, yet the genomic determinants of this variation remain poorly understood. We analyzed 1,863 publicly available genomes, whose pangenome comprises 6,568 genes (1,392 core and soft-core, 656 shell, and 4,520 cloud), and grouped isolates into 15 genetic groups with FastBAPS. Ten groups were monophyletic on the global phylogeny, and non-monophyly of the remaining five largely reflected the placement of isolates from group 12, which is dispersed across the tree.

studi.t: A compartmentalised cochlear ageing programme: weak systemic concordance and a distinct macrophage compartment
studi.s: Whether the ageing cochlea follows the systemic ageing programmes defined by multi-organ atlases is unknown. We integrated single-nucleus RNA-sequencing data for 13,988 mouse cochlear nuclei (3, 12 and 24 months) with the Tabula Muris Senis atlas (16 droplet-based and 12 Smart-seq2 fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) sources). Cross-organ alignment of ageing programmes was quantified by genome-wide vector correlation, pre-ranked gene-set enrichment and a systemic ageing score.

studi.t: Myeloid mDIC Deficiency Remodels Adipose Macrophages to an Efferocytosis-Associated State and Improves Metabolic Homeostasis During Obesity
studi.s: Obesity-associated adipose inflammation contributes to metabolic dysfunction, yet the mechanisms linking mitochondrial metabolism to macrophage efferocytosis remain incompletely understood. The mitochondrial dicarboxylate carrier (mDIC), encoded by SLC25A10, regulates adipocyte function, but its role in macrophages remains unclear. Here, we investigated how myeloid mDIC deficiency affects mitochondrial function, macrophage heterogeneity, and metabolic homeostasis during diet-induced obesity.

studi.t: Energetic costs of osmo- and ionoregulatory responses to desiccation and recovery in a model insect
studi.s: Climate change is expected to increase the frequency, duration and intensity of weather events that cause desiccation stress to small-bodied terrestrial insects. Whether a desiccation event may cause mortality depends on the time-dependent osmo- and ionoregulation responses of insects to desiccation and their recovery. Yet these responses and their associated energetic costs are not always clear for a range of mesic species. Here, we characterised the ability of house crickets (Acheta domesticus) to physiologically resist and recover from desiccation.

studi.t: The global geometry of optimal neural representations
studi.s: Efficient coding hypothesizes that neural activity optimally represents information under resource constraints. The global structures of such optimal population codes are difficult to study theoretically, and previous works have usually resorted to either focusing on local properties like fine discrimination or placing restrictions on the parametric forms of neural tuning.

studi.t: Region-Specific Changes in the Aging Enteric Nervous System
studi.s: As human life expectancy increases, understanding the physiological changes that accompany aging becomes increasingly important. Gastrointestinal (GI) dysfunction is common with age, and age-related changes in the enteric nervous system (ENS), which regulates GI motility, may contribute to this decline in function. Studies of the aging ENS have reported contradicting results, potentially reflecting the substantial regional heterogeneity of the ENS and the fact that most studies focus on only one or two areas of the GI tract.

studi.t: Cumulative antibiograms: effects of isolate selection and stratification order on susceptibility estimates and resistance representation
studi.s: Cumulative antibiograms depend on how isolates are selected and how data are stratified. Different selection strategies may affect both the number of isolates included and the susceptibility estimates reported. We retrospectively analyzed routine microbiology records from a tertiary-care hospital in Barcelona, Spain (2022-2025). Within each patient-organism-calendar-year unit, we compared three isolate-selection strategies: first-isolate, resistance-phenotype, and susceptibility-profile.

studi.t: PYTHOCHEMICAL COMPOSITION AND ANTIMICROBIAL ACTIVITY OF LEPIDIUM SATIVUM SEED EXTRACTS AGAINST SELECTED HUMAN PATHOGENS.
studi.s: This study evaluates the antimicrobial activity of Lepidium sativum (Garden Cress) seed extracts against Staphylococcus aureus, Escherichia coli, Fusarium oxysporum, and Candida albicans using methanol and acetone as solvents. The antimicrobial effects were assessed through the zone of inhibition and minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) using serial dilution. The methanol extract exhibited the highest inhibition zones, measuring 23.6 mm for S. aureus and 21.5 mm for E. coli, while the acetone extract showed 22.9 mm and 18.3 mm, respectively. C.

studi.t: LANCE-seq: Live-tissue Analysis via Needle-encoded Capture Extraction for Spatial Transcriptomics
studi.s: Spatial transcriptomics enables the resolution of spatial heterogeneity in gene expression within tissues, yet most existing sequencing-based methods rely on ex vivo tissue processing, making it difficult to track dynamic molecular changes in the same living individual. We developed LANCE-seq (Live-tissue Analysis via Needle-encoded Capture Extraction sequencing), a live-tissue spatial transcriptomics platform based on encoded microneedle arrays that enables high-density spatial RNA capture through poly(amidoamine) (PAMAM) dendrimer-functionalized interfaces and microfluidic orthogonal…

studi.t: Native architecture of a mitochondrial oxphosome
studi.s: Mitochondrial cristae are the primary bioenergetic units of eukaryotic cells, yet the molecular principles that dictate their morphologies remain largely unknown. Using in situ cryo-electron tomography and integrative modeling, we resolve the native organization of the respiratory machinery in the diatom Phaeodactylum tricornutum. Unlike previously studied animals and green algae, diatoms possess tubular crista, a conserved membrane architecture found in diverse and globally relevant species.

studi.t: Metabolic transitions reprogram translation through sequence-dependent regulation
studi.s: Cells suppress protein synthesis during starvation, but how translation recovers upon nutrient repletion remains poorly understood. To address this gap, we followed translational recovery in budding yeast after repletion of glucose, nitrogen, or phosphate, combining time-resolved metabolomics, structural proteomics, transcriptomics, and spike-in-calibrated ribosome profiling. Nutrient addition rapidly altered ribosome occupancy in distinct, transcript-specific programs.

studi.t: A near-infrared fluorescent genetically encoded calcium ion biosensor with a direct response
studi.s: Near-infrared genetically encoded calcium ion (Ca2+) indicators (NIR GECIs) enable Ca2+ imaging at longer wavelengths than green or red fluorescent GECIs, providing reduced autofluorescence and phototoxicity, and improved compatibility with deep-tissue and multiplexed imaging applications. We have previously reported biliverdin (BV)-binding phytochrome-based NIR GECIs such as NIR-GECO2G that exhibit inverse fluorescence responses.

studi.t: The Caenorhabditis elegans pangenome elucidates hyper-divergent region gene content to reveal extensive gene copy-number variation and a novel anthelmintic resistance locus
studi.s: Caenorhabditis elegans has been a keystone model in biological research since the early 1970s, and it was the first metazoan to have its genome sequenced and assembled in 1998. Over the last few decades, the genetic and genomic resources developed for C. elegans made it one of the most powerful models for understanding metazoan biology. Recently, the C. elegans community has collected over 2,000 globally distributed wild strains, which after whole-genome sequencing, were found to contain punctuated regions of extreme genetic variation, called hyper-divergent regions (HDRs).

studi.t: Rac1-Abi-1 Signaling Links DNA Repair to Tumorigenesis
studi.s: The DNA damage response governs genomic integrity, and abnormal DNA repair can drive tumorigenesis. We previously identified a Rac1-Abi-1 signaling pathway in which Rac1 activates protein phosphatase 5, leading to Abi-1-S323 dephosphorylation and enhanced non-homologous end joining (NHEJ). Given the error-prone nature of NHEJ and its potential to promote genomic instability, we sought to determine whether Rac1-Abi-1-mediated regulation of NHEJ contributes to tumorigenesis.

studi.t: On the intra-laboratory replicability of results in animal cognition research, obtained in animals that were not exposed to, or unaffected by, experimental manipulations - Exemplified by spatial learning in pigs (Sus Scrofa Domesticus) across 12 holeboard studies
studi.s: The replicability of experimental results is considered a cornerstone of empirical research. However, the reproducibility of results from groups that have not undergone experimental manipulation - the standard against which comparisons in an experiment are made - has been almost entirely neglected in animal research. Our aim is to address this gap by exemplarily determining within-laboratory replicability using research in pigs, an increasingly popular large animal model species.

studi.t: siRNA/mRNA payload of lipid nanoparticles quantified using fluorescence microscopy and correlation spectroscopy
studi.s: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have emerged as the most promising vectors to deliver nucleic acids to mammalian cells. Advanced delivery strategies involving multiple nucleic acid species require a reliable determination of RNA payload and LNP size. Here, we use total internal reflection fluorescence (TIRF) microscopy and fluorescence correlation spectroscopy (FCS) to determine mRNA payload and siRNA/mRNA codelivered payload. Particularly, FCS proves to be a reliable method for payload determination, independently of fluorophore properties that can be altered during encapsulation.

studi.t: Optogenetic RNA relocalization reveals causal neural function in vivo
studi.s: RNA localization dictates where translation occurs, yet its disease role is unclear because most assays manipulate abundance, not position. We develop an optogenetic CRISPR-dCas13 system (Opto-CRISPR-TO) that repositions endogenous RNAs with subcellular precision, second-scale kinetics, and reversibility, enabling causal tests in vivo. In cells, Opto-CRISPR-TO routes diverse RNAs to organelles and ribonucleoprotein granules with multiplex, bidirectional control, revealing distinct RNA behaviors in centrosomes and P-bodies.

studi.t: Alpha-synuclein and neuromelanin converge to promote Parkinsons disease pathology
studi.s: Parkinsons disease (PD) is defined by the preferential degeneration of neuromelanin (NM)-containing dopamine-producing neurons in the substantia nigra (SN), accompanied by intraneuronal inclusions rich in alpha-synuclein (aSYN). However, the mechanistic relationship between NM accumulation and aSYN pathology remains unclear. Here, we reveal a bidirectional pathogenic relationship between aSYN and NM. In human post-mortem midbrain tissue, ventral nigral neurons with high NM content display increased aSYN mRNA expression and are preferentially lost in PD.

studi.t: Benchmarking Machine Learning Methods for Antimicrobial Peptide Prediction and Discovery in Ancient Microbiomes
studi.s: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) offer a promising alternative to conventional antibiotics amid the growing global threat of antimicrobial resistance. Expanding AMP discovery requires both effective computational tools to accurately identify candidate peptides and access to underexplored biological resources that may harbor novel AMPs. However, the comparative performance of existing computational methods remains poorly understood, while ancient microbiomes have received limited attention as potential reservoirs of AMPs.

studi.t: Gram-positive bacteria have different susceptibilities to the host-derived antimicrobial lysophosphatidylcholine and adapt to lysophosphatidylcholine-induced stress via distinct mechanisms
studi.s: The human lipid metabolites, lysophosphatidylcholine (LPC) and plasmenyl-LPC (pLPC), modulate both the metabolic health status and innate immunity of an individual. Previous studies reported direct antibacterial activity of LPC, while pLPC has not been evaluated. Meanwhile, some bacteria harvest LPC for producing phosphatidylcholine (PC); others produce plasmalogens under anaerobic conditions. These discoveries suggest that both LPC and pLPC can mediate host-microbe interactions.

studi.t: HIPPO signaling competency links human stromal cell states to bone forming potential and osteogenic responsiveness
studi.s: Skeletal stromal populations contribute to bone maintenance and repair, but how their molecular heterogeneity relates to bone forming potential remains incompletely understood. Whether shared transcriptional programs link this functional diversity to osteogenic responsiveness remains unresolved. We combined single-cell RNA sequencing of four human stromal clones with contrasting bone forming capacities, functional assays, and primary human stromal datasets. High bone forming clones shared oxidative metabolism and signaling-associated programs despite clone-specific expression patterns.

studi.t: Branched-chain α-keto acid metabolism is controlled by SLC25A35-mediated mitochondrial import
studi.s: Liver is considered a primary site for systemic branched-chain alpha-keto acid (BCKA) oxidation due to its abundant dehydrogenase content. However, hepatocytes rely entirely on import of substrate generated elsewhere because they lack intrinsic branched-chain transaminase activity. The mechanisms governing BCKA transit into the mitochondrial matrix remain unknown. We found that mitochondrial import, rather than dehydrogenase activity, determines hepatocellular capacity for BCKA oxidation.

studi.t: Doublecortin compacts the microtubule lattice through a DC1-dependent mechanism
studi.s: Doublecortin (DCX) is a microtubule-associated protein essential for neuronal migration during brain development, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying its function on the microtubule remain incompletely understood. Here we show that DCX compacts the microtubule lattice, with the DC1 domain serving as the main driver of lattice compaction.

studi.t: Parametric and AI-Assisted Design of Right-Handed Four-Helix Coiled Coils
studi.s: Right-handed, antiparallel -helical coiled coils are rare in nature and remain challenging targets for de novo protein design. Here, we combined parametric backbone generation with deep-learning-based sequence design and structure prediction to systematically explore this underrepresented region of coiled-coil structural space. We compared three ProteinMPNN design strategies: repeat-constrained homotetramer design, unconstrained homotetramer design, and unconstrained heterotetramer design.

studi.t: The C-terminal region of interferon-γ mediates evolutionarily tunable membrane interaction
studi.s: Interferon-{gamma} (IFN-{gamma}) is a key cytokine orchestrating innate and adaptive immunity, yet the functional significance of its highly basic C-terminal region remains poorly understood. Here, we combine evolutionary, biophysical, cellular, and computational approaches to uncover the membrane-interacting properties of this region across vertebrate IFN-{gamma} orthologs. We show that the previously described conserved KRKR motif is embedded within a broader cationic region that is highly diverse in fish but progressively reduced in terrestrial tetrapods.

studi.t: TriScan: High-Contrast Confocal Sectioning with Widefield Speed
studi.s: Modern analytical methods increasingly require fast, high-resolution, and scalable 3D fluorescence imaging with optical sectioning. We present the TriScan, a microscope that allows for compact, inexpensive, and easy-to-implement confocal imaging at very fast imaging speeds. The TriScan combines line-scan confocal imaging with a sensitive camera detector via a simple optical layout that imposes no practical limit on the scanning rate.

studi.t: Membrane voltage multistability in coupled glial cells
studi.s: Growing interest to describe the electrical behavior of glial cells, mainly astrocytes, in intact brain tissue poses more and more challenges to commonly accepted belief they only respond in a linear manner in uptake of the excess of extracellular potassium and maintenance of their network equipotentiality. Their highly conductive mutual interconnections via gap junction (GJ) connections introduce yet another class of nonlinear elements.

studi.t: How can brain-like dynamics and phonetic generalization emerge in speech representations? A study using self-supervised models
studi.s: Speech representations in the human brain do not simply mirror the instantaneous speech signal; rather, they display several properties that are hypothesized to facilitate the integration of speech sounds into words. In particular, neural encodings of speech maintain information that has dissipated from the acoustics, and have also been argued to abstract over variability in how individual speech sounds are produced. Here, we investigate how such characteristics could arise.

studi.t: A nonlinear inhibition pathway underlying cortical responses to tuned holographic optogenetic perturbations
studi.s: Optogenetics enables causal manipulation of cortical activity. Theory is essential for predicting network-mediated perturbation responses, which are often counterintuitive. Existing approaches have relied on linear approximations, which can fail for multi-neuron holographic perturbations. We develop a nonlinear theory of responses to such perturbations in networks with cell-type-specific structured connectivity.

studi.t: TGF-b/TIF1g signaling restrains CD8+ T cell expansion while preserving cytotoxic competence
studi.s: Transforming growth factor b exerts complex and often opposing effects on CD8+ T cell biology, yet the molecular mechanisms that distinguish these functions remain poorly understood. Here, we identify TIF1g (TRIM33) as a critical signal threshold regulator that couples TGF b signaling to CD8+ T cell activation and cytotoxic function. In the presence of TGF b, TIF1g deficient CD8+ T cells bypass canonical suppressive signals and acquire a transcriptional program characterized by enhanced activation and proliferation.

studi.t: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics reveal a cyst-neuron-microglia network underlying brain damage during Toxoplasma gondii infection
studi.s: Toxoplasma gondii infects approximately one-third of the world's population, and persistent brain infection links to neuropsychiatric disorders. How cysts interact with host brain cells and tissue to sustain infection and cause neuronal damage remains unclear. We combined single-nucleus RNA sequencing with Stereo-seq spatial transcriptomics to map mouse brains across acute and chronic T. gondii infection.

studi.t: Activation of the bridge-like lipid transfer protein Atg2 by Atg1-mediated phosphorylation
studi.s: Bridge-like lipid transfer proteins (BLTPs) have emerged as major contributors to lipid flux and thus cellular organization. BLTPs harbor a hydrophobic channel connecting two membranes to enable the bulk flow of lipids between them. The regulation of BLTPs is incompletely understood. Employing in vitro reconstitution, molecular dynamics simulations, and cell biology, we discovered that the BLTP Atg2, which mediates lipid transfer during autophagosome biogenesis, is activated by the Atg1 kinase. Atg1 phosphorylates two serines in the N-terminal region of Atg2.

studi.t: Paired Deep Mutational Scanning of Lck Activity and Inhibitor Sensitivity Enables the Engineering of Pharmacological Control of T Cell Receptor Signaling
studi.s: Controlling signaling enzymes with small molecules is a central goal in chemical biology and is of great utility for engineering cell-derived immunotherapies. Yet strategies for conferring selective small-molecule sensitivity without disrupting a protein's native function remain limited. Here we present a generalizable approach to engineering small molecule-controlled multidomain protein kinases.

studi.t: AmyloCore-ML: AI/Machine Learning Enabled Identification of Amyloid Fibril Core Regions Using Protein Language Models
studi.s: Identification of amyloid forming regions in proteins remains central to understanding of their aggregation behaviour, which are central to various neurodegenerative and systemic disorders. Many predictors have been designed to identify amyloid forming regions, however they may not necessarily identify total residues found in actual disease associated fibril structures. To address this, we formed a sequence-based based predictor-AmyloCore-ML to ascertain structural amyloid-core propensity.

studi.t: MtbAIM: AI/ML-guided endpoint-specific prediction of small-molecule activity across drug-susceptible and drug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis
studi.s: The emergence of drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis (M.tb) presents a major challenge to drug discovery, as compounds active against drug-susceptible (DS) isolates may not retain comparable inhibitory activity against drug-resistant (DR) isolates. Here, we developed an AI/ML workflow to independently prioritize small molecules separately against DS and DR isolates of M.tb and predict MIC, MIC90, and MIC99 as distinct quantitative endpoints.

studi.t: RETRO-URETERAL DELIVERY OF AAV-KP VECTORS FOR RENAL GENE TRANSFER AND THE ASSESSMENT OF TRANSGENE REABSORPTION IN THE KIDNEY
studi.s: Monogenic disorders cause a substantial fraction of chronic kidney disease, yet no renal gene therapy exists, partly because adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors transduce the kidney poorly after systemic delivery. Screening a barcoded library of 80 natural and chimeric AAV serotypes administered retrogradely into the mouse renal pelvis identified AAV-KP1, AAV-KP2 and AAV-KP3 as enriched in the injected kidney but not in the liver.

studi.t: BRO is a proteinaceous binding receptor for human coronavirus OC43
studi.s: Embecoviruses such as human coronavirus (HCoV) OC43 have long been viewed as sialic acid-dependent viruses that attach to cells through interactions with cell surface sialoglycans. Here, we identify a specific proteinaceous receptor that harbors the sialoglycan determinant and also contributes protein contacts for viral spike (S) recognition. Using an unbiased surfaceome CRISPR activation screen for OC43 spike binding, we discovered that the previously uncharacterized human gene C1ORF54 encodes this receptor, which we name Binding Receptor for OC43 (BRO).

studi.t: Phage VP882 possesses quorum-sensing-driven lytic induction and stress-mediated host growth suppression mechanisms
studi.s: Vibriophage VP882 launches its lytic cascade upon detection of a quorum-sensing autoinducer produced by its bacterial host. This capability enables the phage to maximize transmission by transitioning from lysogeny to lysis only at high host cell density, when abundant host cells are present to infect. Here, we show that two different pathways can be triggered upon prophage induction. When the prophage is induced via quorum sensing, Qtip, an anti-repressor, inhibits the cI lysogeny maintenance protein, driving expression of the lysis genes.

studi.t: Redefining paradigms of cellular HPV trafficking in situ
studi.s: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the most common sexually transmitted agent and causes ~4.5% of all human cancers. A complete understanding of the cellular mechanisms underlying trafficking, disassembly, and transport is still lacking. Using in situ cryo-electron tomography, we directly visualize high-risk HPV16 during infection and reveal that virions remain intact and infection-competent upon reaching lysosomes, contrary to the prevailing model of lysosomal inactivation.

studi.t: Forecasting estuarine biodiversity and population abundance for conservation: spatial scale, forecast horizon, and choice of measure
studi.s: Conservation decisions increasingly rely on forecasts, but how far ahead biodiversity and population abundance can be forecast, and at which spatial scale, is rarely known. I used monthly monitoring data on fishes and invertebrates in seven Texas estuaries to forecast biodiversity (Hill numbers, which weight rare and common species differently) and the abundance of eight common taxa, 1 to 24 months ahead, for each estuary and the coast as a whole. Each series was divided into a seasonal cycle and departures from it.

studi.t: Sex difference in the underpinnings of social fate in isogenic mice and no sex bias in precedence-based social ranking in male and female groups
studi.s: The mechanisms underlying social organization in mice have predominantly been studied in male colonies, where sociability predicts higher rank and high-ranked individuals show greater anxiety. Isogenic female mice also form stable social hierarchies. Our data indicate that greater sociability before group formation predicts high rank attainment, a trait that remains afterwards. In contrast, a consistent increased anxiety was only observed after life in colony for the same individuals.

studi.t: 3D-bioprinted skeletal muscle with tailored myofibre architecture
studi.s: Engineered skeletal muscle tissue (eSMT) contractile function strongly depends on the alignment and orientation of its myofibres, as force generation and transmission are intrinsically linked to its microstructural architecture. However, fabricating truly functional eSMT with controlled myofibre architecture remains a major challenge. Here, we present a method that combines extrusion-based 3D bioprinting with custom multi-pillar anchoring systems to guide myofibre development.

studi.t: OmniT2I: a unified table-to-image framework for survival prediction and cross-modal inference with incomplete multimodal cancer data
studi.s: Molecular profiles and histopathology provide complementary information about cancer prognosis, but these data are often incomplete for individual patients. Here we present OmniT2I, a table-to-image framework for survival prediction and cross-modal inference from incomplete multimodal cancer data. Each molecular profile was converted into a three-channel image representation with correlation-based feature placement. OmniT2I combines available molecular and histopathology embeddings through availability-aware fusion and predicts missing modalities from those observed.

studi.t: The biophysical properties of the bacterial nucleoid are dynamic, heterogeneous, and responsive to perturbations of cellular processes
studi.s: Biophysical properties play central roles in cellular function by controlling the diffusion and spatial organization of biomolecules. Because bacteria lack a nuclear membrane, biophysical measurements are often averaged over the entire cell. However, the nucleoid environment is distinct from that of the surrounding cytoplasm, and averaging also ignores local characteristics within the nucleoid. Here, we developed a microrheology framework to quantitatively characterize the bacterial nucleoid and investigate the interplay of its physical properties with cellular processes.

studi.t: AutoMorphoTrack: A modular framework for quantitative analysis of organelle morphology, tracking, and image colocalization
studi.s: AutoMorphoTrack is an open-source Python framework for analyzing organelle morphology, centroid tracking and colocalization in multichannel fluorescence microscopy. Steps in the analysis are connected by means of shared masks and persistent identities. Fifty synthetic sequences and eight publicly available microscopy studies were used in evaluation. A lack of sufficient vesicle coverage with the original, revised configuration motivated the development of a separate frozen particle pipeline.

studi.t: Stimulating neurogenesis of distinct retinal lineages in human retinal pigmented epithelium (RPE) with proneural transcription factors
studi.s: There are currently few promising approaches for treatment of photoreceptor pathologies: for example, gene therapy to augment or replace mutated genes, has proven successful in preclinical studies, and some of these therapies are moving towards the clinic. Another approach aims to unlock the inherent stem-cell potential of non-neuronal retinal cells to regenerate neurons in situ. This line of research is based on the discovery that some vertebrates can restore even severely damaged retina from RPE with all the necessary cell types to regain full functionality.

studi.t: How Much Can AI Virtual Cells Gain from Unified Perturbational Modeling?
studi.s: Predicting how individual cells respond to perturbations is a central task in artificial intelligence virtual cell (AIVC) modeling. However, integrating perturbation datasets is challenging because they differ in measured gene sets, perturbation types and cellular contexts. Existing AIVC predictors are typically developed for specific settings, limiting their applicability across heterogeneous datasets.

studi.t: Thermodynamic, Kinetic, and Structural Basis of Polyspecificity in the Malaria Sugar Transporter PfHT1
studi.s: The malaria parasite Plasmodium falciparum relies on the polyspecific sugar transporter PfHT1 for survival in diverse nutrient environments, making the molecular basis of its polyspecificity a potential avenue for antimalarial drug discovery. However, the structural, thermodynamic and kinetic basis of the emergence of polyspecificity in membrane transporters are not established in literature.

studi.t: CellVADIS: Inferring cross-tissue immune cell trafficking dynamics from single-cell snapshots
studi.s: The ability of immune cells to traffic between and enter different tissues is an important hallmark for effective immune responses. However, despite advances in high-throughput single-cell profiling, identifying circulating cell populations that drive tissue-specific immunity remains elusive. Here we present CellVADIS, an optimal transport based computational framework to infer cross-tissue immune cell dynamics.

studi.t: CD44-DT regulates p21-dependent senescence via interacting with AR-PCNA complex, revealing a therapeutic vulnerability to chimeric ncRNA-mediated AR degradation in prostate cancer
studi.s: Aberrant androgen receptor (AR) signaling driven by androgens plays a critical role in prostate cancer (PCa) progression. Interestingly, bipolar androgen therapy (BAT), a novel therapeutic strategy with cycles between near-castrate and supraphysiological androgen levels (SAL), suppresses PCa growth. SAL induces cellular senescence in various PCa models mediated by the AR, activation of AKT signaling and hypophosphorylation of pRb. Here, we show that SAL upregulates the lncRNA CD44-DT, the CD44 divergent transcript, in PCa cells linking CD44-DT to AR signaling.

studi.t: Doublecortin like kinase 1 (DCLK1) interacts with BRG1 chromatin remodeler and regulates neuronal activity-induced gene activation
studi.s: SWI/SNF-like BAF ATP-dependent chromatin remodeling complexes play important roles in neural development and plasticity by regulating neural gene expression, especially in response to neuronal stimulations. Previously, we have shown that BRG1, the core subunit of BAF, undergoes neuronal activity-induced phosphorylation, which is important for the expression of a group of activity regulated genes (ARGs). Proteomic analyses identified Doublecortin like kinase 1 (DCLK1) as a novel BRG1 interacting protein.

studi.t: Natural pest control in African agriculture: can migratory birds offset the decline of native insectivores?
studi.s: Agricultural expansion and intensification are reducing populations of resident insectivorous birds worldwide, with potentially negative consequences for natural pest control, particularly in the tropics. Many migratory insectivores spend the non-breeding season in the tropics, often favouring disturbed habitats, potentially fulfilling ecological roles once played by resident species. However, few studies have examined the relative impacts of agricultural land-use change on resident and migratory bird species, particularly in the Afrotropics.

studi.t: Toward Standardized Fucoidan Extractions from Brown Algae: Optimization of Under-Addressed Parameters to Maximize Yield and Purity
studi.s: Brown algal cell walls contain unique polysaccharides called fucoidans, which exhibit complex structural diversity and have applications across a range of industries. For these applications, fucoidan extraction methods should maximize yield while minimizing co-extracted impurities. However, extraction protocols vary widely, and their effects on yield and purity are rarely investigated. Thus, standardized and optimized fucoidan extraction methods are needed. Here, we aimed to identify optimal parameters for selected steps of a fucoidan extraction protocol.

studi.t: Force Volume Atomic Force Microscopy of THP-1 and Primary Mouse Macrophages Reveals that the Mechanical Signature of Macrophage Polarization is Model-Dependent
studi.s: Macrophages are immune cells with a rich morphological variety and markedly different biological functions when differentiated into M0 (non-activated) macrophages or polarized into M1 (pro-inflammatory) and M2 (anti-inflammatory) phenotypes. Atomic force microscopy (AFM) studies have recently associated a mechanical dimension with macrophage polarization. Herein, the elastic properties of the three phenotypes are measured and compared by force volume AFM in two less explored models: THP-1-derived macrophages (cell line) and mouse bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs, primary cells).

studi.t: Membrane Biofouling and Plasmid Conformation Shape the Retention of Antibiotic Resistance Gene-Carrying Plasmids during Ultrafiltration
studi.s: Antimicrobial resistance poses a growing threat to human and environmental health, and wastewater treatment plants are important pathways for the release of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs). Although ultrafiltration (UF) membranes effectively retain antibiotic-resistant bacteria, their capacity to remove extracellular ARGs remains less understood. Extracellular plasmids are concerning because they persist following cell lysis and may contribute to horizontal gene transfer. Unlike intact bacterial cells, these flexible DNA molecules may pass through membrane barriers.

studi.t: NXP800 suppresses HSF1 through coordinated stress signaling and GCN2-dependent translational repression in glioblastoma
studi.s: Under states of proteotoxic stress, Heat Shock Factor 1 (HSF1) serves as the primary transcription factor responsible for restoring protein homeostasis. General Control Nonderepressible 2 (GCN2) similarly alleviates cellular stress. Activated by a shortage in amino acids, GCN2 triggers the phosphorylation of eIF2 to downregulate global protein synthesis while selectively translating survival-promoting proteins like Activating Transcription Factor 4 (ATF4).
