Here we systematically compared A-rich and G-rich PAM-recognizing Cas9 editors through comprehensive analyses of ~37,000 targeting sites with about half million libraries of ~0.36 billion types of editing outcomes. We showed that the A-rich Cas9 editors exhibit stronger editing outcome predictability in comparison with the conventional Cas9 editor of the G-rich PAM.

studi.t: The crystal structure of the human SIPA1L2 PDZ domain reveals an atypically short, metazoan-conserved β2 β3 loop
studi.s: Signal - induced proliferation-associated 1-like protein 2 (SIPA1L2) is a large neuronal Rap GTPase-activating protein implicated in dynein-dependent retrograde transport of BDNF-TrkB signaling endosomes and genetically linked to Parkinson's disease. It consists of a RapGAP domain, a PDZ domain, and a coiled-coil domain separated by intrinsically disordered regions. Its compact PDZ domain mediates protein-protein interaction by binding short PDZ-binding motifs (PBM) in target proteins.

studi.t: EvoRx: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Antibiotic Resistance in Escherichia coli Using Genomic Features
studi.s: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) complicates bacterial infection management, motivating genomic approaches to predicting antibiotic susceptibility. This study assessed the predictive performance and generalisability of machine-learning models using resistance-associated genomic features from Escherichia coli. Publicly available genomic and phenotypic records yielded 446 genomes, 252 binary genomic features and 1,935 susceptibility observations across nine antibiotics.

studi.t: Recurrent astrocyte transcriptional states with spatial and functional specialization are induced by brain metastases independently of their primary tumor origin
studi.s: Reactive astrocytes have emerged as important components of the brain metastasis niche, yet a state-resolved framework for metastasis-associated astrocyte biology is still lacking. Here, we integrate single-cell and spatial transcriptomics across syngeneic breast, lung and melanoma models of brain metastases to define a state-resolved astrocyte landscape.

studi.t: An Affordable Vibrotactile Surface for Tactile Figure Recognition: Exploration Strategies of Blind and Sighted Users
studi.s: Refreshable tactile displays can make graphics accessible to blind and low-vision people, but high-resolution actuator arrays remain expensive. We study whether a low-cost vibrotactile surface can convey simple figures, and how they are read. Nine participants (four blind; five sighted, tested blindfolded then open-eyed) identified seven figures by touch, with video and timing analysis of their exploration.

studi.t: Clicks, Carbon, and Risk: Climate Attention, Persistent Financial Risk, and Real-Sector Activity
studi.s: Do shifts in public climate concern alter persistent financial risk and subsequently matter for real activity? We combine daily U.S. sectoral equity returns with a monthly Climate Concern Index (CCI) constructed from internet search intensity and decomposed into adverse and transition-oriented components. GARCH-MIDAS estimates reveal substantial heterogeneity: adverse climate concern raises persistent volatility in carbon-intensive Energy activities, while transition-oriented attention tends to reduce persistent volatility in regulated Utilities, with important differences across sub-sectors.

studi.t: Controlling Proactive Multimodal AI: Separating Perception from Participation
studi.s: Proactive multimodal AI can watch a user's screen, listen to speech, track interaction, and decide whether to enter unfolding work. Little is known about how people want to control what such AI may perceive and how far it may participate. Informed by a 14-person Wizard-of-Oz study, we built SpotMe, a design probe that senses screen, speech, and interaction; chooses Silence, Ask, or Assist; and lets users separately configure what it may perceive, how far it may participate, and what types of support it may provide.

studi.t: Plenty to FRET About: From Hazard Analysis to Formal Requirements for Robot-Assisted Dressing
studi.s: Understanding requirements for systems involving humans and robots is essential for providing robust evidence that such systems behave correctly. Requirements formalisation approaches such as the Formal Requirements Elicitation Tool (FRET) can support the transition from unstructured natural language to formal representations suitable for verification. In this paper, we formalise 146 hazard-derived natural-language requirements for a Robot-Assisted Dressing (RAD) case study, previously classified using a taxonomy of Human-Robot Teamwork (HRT) requirements.

studi.t: Fair Bubble Sort: Provably Optimal Fair Ranking with Continuous Sensitive Attributes
studi.s: Most fair-ranking methods assume categorical protected attributes, requiring continuous attributes such as age or income to be discretized into groups. This introduces arbitrary thresholds, loses fine-grained information, and ignores the natural ordering of the attribute. In this paper, we study the problem of fair ranking with continuous protected attributes without relying on thresholding.

studi.t: An AI-Driven Assistant for Human-Centric Building Digital Twin Systems: Design, Implementation, and Comparative User Evaluation
studi.s: Smart buildings generate streams of operational data, yet this richness rarely translates into accessible, decision-ready information for stakeholders who inhabit and manage them. Current Building Digital Twin Systems (BDTS) often remain oriented toward technical specialists and rely on static, one-size-fits-all interfaces.

studi.t: Anticipating or Speculating? Making Futures Pay in AI Ethics
studi.s: Philosophers have recently been trying to develop uniform decision rules for instances in which physicians' judgments diverge from the recommendations of medical artificial intelligence (AI) systems. I argue that this effort is fatally flawed because the performance and appropriate use of algorithmic recommendation systems by physicians are highly context-specific, empirical medical matters rather than epistemological ones. In such instances, general decision rules can be stipulated only to the extent that they abstract away from relevant, indeed determinative, contextual circumstances.

studi.t: OAK-Mind: Zero-Training Mental Health Change Inference from Passive Sensing via Knowledge-Grounded Multi-Agent LLMs
studi.s: Wearable and smartphone sensors capture behavioral signals associated with mental health, yet inferring mental health outcomes from these signals has traditionally relied on supervised models requiring labeled data and offering limited insight into their predictions. Large language models (LLMs) offer new opportunities to reason over behavioral evidence, but existing LLM-based approaches to passive sensing have largely continued to rely on task-specific fine-tuning or sensor-specific pretraining.

studi.t: Deep Mixture Models: A Statistical Review with R
studi.s: Deep mixture models extend finite mixture models through hierarchical latent factor structures with shared mixture parameters. This focused review examines deep Gaussian mixture models (DGMMs), robust deep mixture models (RDMMs), deep skew-$t$ mixture models (DStMMs), and mixed deep Gaussian mixture models (MDGMMs) within a common statistical framework. We compare their pathway distributions, measurement models, and latent architectures, highlighting the implications for likelihood evaluation and inference.

studi.t: Big Brains, Tiny Board: Pupavision, an Agentic Physical AI Instrument for Monitoring Drosophila Pupariation and Lifecycle Transitions
studi.s: Many biology experiments are limited by the availability and ease of use of instruments that monitor and record them. For example, the timing of pupariation in the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster, a widely used model organism, can provide biologically relevant information about growth regulation and is often recorded manually. Here, we present Pupavision, a small physical AI instrument built from a single-board Linux computer and a day/night camera for roughly 45 to 75 US dollars in parts. The key idea is that a frontier coding agent runs its agentic harness directly on the tiny board.

studi.t: ReMoE: An Interpretable Mixture-of-Experts Framework for Human Mobility Recovery Forecasting Across Disasters
studi.s: Human mobility often declines sharply following disasters and subsequently exhibits complex recovery dynamics. Effective forecasting of this recovery is critical for timely assessment and resource allocation. However, existing approaches are often developed for individual events and operate as black boxes, limiting their transferability and interpretability beyond the events they were trained on. Recent studies have identified recurring post-disaster mobility recovery types across disasters, suggesting that recovery knowledge may be transferable.

studi.t: Projected Route Cues for Bouldering: Effects of Circular, Linear, and Combined Highlighting on Route Observation and Climbing
studi.s: Before attempting a bouldering problem, climbers inspect the route to find its holds and plan their moves, which novices find difficult on walls where many routes overlap. We built a projector-camera system that projects route cues onto the wall and compared three cues: circles on the route holds, limb-colored lines connecting the holds, and both combined. Ninety-six participants, 61 of them first-time climbers, each climbed four routes, one per cue and one without projection, in a Latin-square order.

studi.t: Beyond Acuity Accuracy: A Multidimensional Framework for Evaluating Patient-Facing Emergency Triage AI Tools
studi.s: Patient-facing AI triage tools may support care-seeking and emergency department prioritization, but require evaluation beyond acuity accuracy alone. We developed SAFE-Triage, a framework integrating human review, automated metrics, LLM-as-judge evaluation, and simulation testing across clinical performance, patient interaction, and clinician-facing summary quality. We applied SAFE-Triage to 40 MIMIC-IV-derived emergency vignettes and a 10,030-case acuity analysis comparing prompted LLM triage (PLT) with rule-augmented prompted LLM triage (rPLT).

studi.t: Thinking Harder Doesn't Lead to Better Choices: Reasoning Effort Increases the Confidence but Not the Correctness of LLM Shopping Agents
studi.s: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous shopping agents that process multimodal product listings (consisting of visual and text data) and recommend purchases on behalf of consumers. Naturally, one might assume that models with more thinking power would make higher-quality purchasing decisions. To test this belief, we ask two questions about such agents: does asking a model to think harder make it choose better products, and does the confidence it reports tell us the likelihood it may be wrong?

studi.t: Supporting Researcher Control in AI-Assisted Social Media Analysis: A Mixed-Methods Study of AI4OSN
studi.s: High-quality annotated datasets are critical for advancing computational social science (CSS) research, yet collecting, curating, and analyzing large-scale data from dynamic sources such as online social networks (OSNs) remains a persistent bottleneck. Researchers must also translate substantive questions into queries, relevance criteria, and defensible interpretations. Large language models (LLMs) can assist, but they can also obscure the judgments, potentially reducing researcher oversight and critical evaluation.

studi.t: Deep Learning Models for Fractional Option Pricing
studi.s: This paper investigates whether neural networks can infer fractional option prices and the Hurst parameter directly from sequences of fractional Gaussian returns, without separately estimating the latent parameters for each new sequence. Feedforward neural networks (FNNs) and long short-term memory (LSTM) networks are trained to jointly predict European call prices, put prices, and the Hurst parameter from 252-return sequences.

studi.t: The Geoengineering Put: Ecological Debt, Termination Risk, and Asset Prices
studi.s: Solar geoengineering offers an inexpensive and fast-acting way to lower global temperatures without removing carbon from the atmosphere. As warming intensifies, climate-vulnerable countries face growing incentives to deploy geoengineering unilaterally. The economic and financial consequences of this prospect remain largely overlooked. We develop a general equilibrium macro-finance framework in which geoengineering acts as a put option on climate damages, funded by the "ecological debt" of masked warming. If deployment stops, temperatures snap back in a catastrophic termination shock.

studi.t: Assessing Distributional Covariate Balance After Weighting: A Practical Guide
studi.s: Health researchers commonly use weighting methods to improve covariate balance when estimating program and intervention effects from observational data. Standardized mean differences (SMDs) and variance ratios assess particular features of balance but may overlook residual differences elsewhere in the covariate distribution. This paper provides practical guidance for using Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS), Anderson-Darling (AD), and Cramer-von Mises (CVM) statistics as complementary distributional balance diagnostics.

studi.t: Benefits and Barriers to Human-AI Teaming for Crisis Counseling
studi.s: Background: AI systems are increasingly deployed to support mental health clinicians, yet real-world evidence remains limited. In crisis counseling, where clients often seek human connection, understanding whether AI augmentation preserves or undermines meaningful human engagement is essential. Methods: In a mixed-methods study of a counselor-facing AI copilot on a WhatsApp-based crisis hotline in India (Mar.-Oct. 2025), counselors could request, edit, and send AI messages.

studi.t: Right Reason, Wrong Advice: Evaluating Recourse in LLM Explanations of Denied Requests
studi.s: Language models increasingly write the explanations people receive when a rule system denies their request. If several rules deny the request independently, an explanation can name a true reason and still leave the person denied after they fix it. We call the missing property recourse validity: changing what the explanation cites, without changing what was asked for, can flip the decision. We compute it exactly, and a hitting-set argument predicts from the policy alone when a correct reason fails.

studi.t: Evaluating Cultural Reasoning and Robustness in LLMs for Spanish Political Discourse
studi.s: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to interpret, generate, and mediate public-facing language, which makes their reliability especially consequential in politically sensitive settings. Although sentiment analysis is a common task in this area, affective meaning in social media discourse is often conveyed through culturally situated and pragmatically indirect cues that are not well captured by label-centric evaluation alone.

studi.t: Incentive Alignment for Electricity Data Assets in China: A Blockchain-Enabled Contribution-Credit Framework
studi.s: Modern electricity markets increasingly rely on reported operational contributions to allocate incentives, recognise cooperation, and coordinate activities across multiple organisations. However, supporting evidence for many reported contributions becomes available only after subsequent metering, dispatch, settlement, or auditing processes, making it difficult to reward genuine contributions while discouraging strategic over-reporting.

studi.t: Embedding Cosine Measures Text Length Before It Measures Homogenization
studi.s: Mean pairwise cosine similarity between transformer embeddings is a standard measure of whether online discourse is converging under generative AI. When the embeddings are mean-pooled outputs of an encoder never trained for sentence similarity, this measure mostly tracks text length. In 6.06 million Reddit comments, an uncentered DeBERTa-v3 measure had suggested that only conservative discourse broke toward homogeneity after late 2022. Truncating the same comments from 10 to 150 words raises their mean cosine by eight times the reported break.

studi.t: The CYBER-BRIDGE project: An AI-Powered Platform for Cross-Border Cybersecurity, Compliance and Forensics in the EU
studi.s: Cross-border cyber attacks on European SMEs and critical-infrastructure operators expose a structural cyber-resilience gap: cybersecurity (threat sharing, detection, response), compliance (framework assessment, certification) and digital forensics (cross-jurisdictional evidence) are jointly regulated by NIS2, the CRA, GDPR and the LED, yet their tooling evolved in silos and rarely interoperates across Member States.

studi.t: Synthetic Doubt and the Integrity of Digital Proof before the International Criminal Court
studi.s: Generative artificial intelligence complicates evidentiary assessment at the International Criminal Court by enabling fabricated audiovisual material and making authentic digital evidence easier to dismiss as fake. This article calls the latter problem synthetic doubt: an objection alleging that a digital item may be AI-generated or AI-manipulated. Existing scholarship addresses digital evidence, open-source investigations and deepfakes in the ICC context.

studi.t: Shaping AI's Beliefs Before It Generates: Human Sense of Agency in Creative AI
studi.s: AI systems for creative media generation expand human capabilities yet risk diminishing human agency. A core problem is anchoring, where the user's thinking becomes anchored to a polished, generated artifact, shifting the user's role from active authoring to reactive editing. We propose pre-generation belief controls that can empower creators to inspect, revise, and steer the AI's interpretation before any media is generated, so that the initial anchor is set by the human.

studi.t: Portrait Fitness as a Pretext: Probing Implicit Demographic Bias in VLMs
studi.s: We audit face-related bias in VLMs using BALPORTRAITS, a new balanced dataset of 9,000 fictional portraits across ethnicity, gender, and age segments. Sixteen VLMs estimate portrait fitness scores for occupations, brands, activities, and banking or insurance products within an advertising-casting framework designed to avoid direct inference of protected attributes. Item-level estimations are aggregated with scenario-specific prestige scores to compare rankings across demographic groups.

studi.t: Beyond Bilingual: Studying Quadrilingual Code-Switching with Conversational AI
studi.s: Multilingual speakers choose languages by topic and conversation partner. Large language models (LLMs) support these languages unequally. Research on code-switching with conversational AI has mostly examined bilingual pairs of well-resourced languages. In Curaçao and Aruba, many people use Dutch, English, Spanish, and the low-resource Creole Papiamentu/o. In a preregistered study, 42 university students held two five-minute chatbot conversations, one about university life and one about local food and culture. Surveys assessed language background, AI use, and switching comfort.

studi.t: What's the Difference? Voice Design and Confirmation Bias in AI-Assisted Self-Diagnosis: Anthropomorphic vs. Machine-Like Voice Output
studi.s: As symptom checkers based on artificial intelligence (AI) are becoming common entry points for health information, their influence on lay users' diagnostic decisions raises questions about trust and bias. Of particular concern is confirmation bias, the tendency to favour information that supports one's existing belief while discounting information that contradicts it. One of the central design choices for such systems is the style of voice: whether they should present themselves with a human-like (anthropomorphic) or a clearly machine-like (xenomorphic) voice.

studi.t: A Crowd-Audited Atlas of Implicit Bias in LLM-Powered Agents
studi.s: Prior work has shown that large language models (LLMs) express implicit biases in high-publicity, one-off decision scenarios such as hiring and intelligence assessment. However, as people increasingly employ autonomous, LLM-powered AI agents that make decisions on their behalf in doing day-to-day tasks, it is of critical importance that we understand how implicit biases, based on sociodemographic assumptions, emerge across a broad milieu of workaday decision scenarios.

studi.t: A Game of Throngs: How Spotlight Tourism Reshapes Local Economies
studi.s: In July 2017, San Juan de Gaztelugatxe, a modest chapel in the Basque Country, appeared as "Dragonstone" in Game of Thrones, transforming a locally known site with limited tourism activity into a global tourist destination overnight. We exploit this exogenous spotlight shock to estimate its causal effects on the local economy using a novel administrative dataset and a Synthetic Control approach. We find an abrupt increase in tourism activity, far exceeding the effects documented in the literature.

studi.t: What You Post Is What You Symptom: Estimating Psychometric Networks from Social Media Discourse
studi.s: Symptom networks in psychopathology are estimated almost exclusively from self-report questionnaires, restricting inference to whatever symptom set a given instrument covers. We introduce a framework for symptom-resolved network estimation directly from social media discourse and apply the framework to depression and eating disorders, with a third anorexia corpus as cross-dataset validation.

studi.t: Share your Screen and Talk to Gemini: How Young Learners Interact with Multimodal GenAI While Solving Scratch Tasks
studi.s: Children using Scratch to learn programming can struggle with text-heavy, lengthy explanations and hints during debugging. Verbal interactions based on screen sharing or camera data may be an interesting alternative for supporting learners. We therefore explore the quality, use, and perceptions of fifth- and sixth-graders' verbal interactions with a GenAI tutor. The goal is to investigate the quality and use of the multimodal GenAI tutor in the given context. First of all, a pilot study of eight tasks conducted without students helped inform the process of the tutor's classroom evaluation.

studi.t: Who Is the Regression About? Auditing AI-Labeled Treatments When Effects Differ
studi.s: Researchers increasingly regress outcomes on treatments labeled by large language models. When effects differ, OLS averages the effect on the treated (ATT) and on the untreated (ATU), weighting the smaller group more. A label's bias then has two parts: classical attenuation from misclassification, and a selective term when its errors are correlated with the outcome. In LinkedIn postings, the model misses better-paid remote jobs: a precision check passes, yet the remote pay gap is understated by nearly 40 percent, a bias that more data cannot remove.

studi.t: PlainPairs: A Corpus Pairing the Prescriber and Patient Texts of U.S. Prescription Medicine Labels
studi.s: A prescription medicine in the United States comes with labeling written for prescribers, and many medicines also carry a text written for patients: a Medication Guide or a patient package insert. The two texts describe the same medicine for two readers, yet public resources rarely hold them side by side. I present PlainPairs, an open corpus built from the openFDA drug label files.

studi.t: Edit Recommendation: Can LLMs Anticipate Edit Requests from Users, and When?
studi.s: After a large language model (LLM) agent generates an artifact, users often send edit requests for it. This paper studies whether an LLM can anticipate these requests before they are sent. Such anticipation is useful in practice because it reduces the effort of user review and feedback. We formalize this task as edit recommendation and build EditRecBench, a benchmark for evaluating the performance of LLMs on this task, from real-world conversation logs in WildChat-4.8M.

studi.t: KuroshioVis: Hypothesis-Driven Discovery of Mesoscale Air-Sea Interaction through Coarse-to-Fine Exploration
studi.s: Mesoscale air-sea interaction occurs throughout strong sea surface temperature fronts such as the the Kuroshio Extension, but its strength is highly non-uniform and can be resolved only in kilometre-scale coupled simulations. The response of any single eddy is weak relative to synoptic variability, so evidence supporting a hypothesis of systematic air-sea coupling must be accumulated across many eddies rather than inferred from individual cases. We present KuroshioVis, a hypothesis-driven, coarse-to-fine visual analytics workflow.

studi.t: Human-AI Co-Ideation Across Socio-Technical Configurations: An Interactional Analysis of Planar and Immersive Workspaces
studi.s: Remote collaborative platforms increasingly integrate generative AI to support group ideation. These platforms are sociotechnical configurations in which spatial mediation, interaction modality, AI output format, and the mechanisms that make contributions visible to a group co-vary as properties of a deployed system. This paper examines how such configurations shape participants' collaboration and their engagement with AI during creative work.

studi.t: SWE-WhatIf: Simulating Real Users of Coding Agents from Recorded Session
studi.s: Recorded sessions between users and coding agents offer a way to evaluate how agents complete real-world tasks and interact with users. However, these sessions cannot simply be replayed with new agents, because recorded user replies may no longer apply when an agent takes a different trajectory. We introduce SWE-WhatIf, which replays recorded sessions with new agents by modeling the user's intents, the criteria for satisfying them, and the conditions under which they arise.

studi.t: Semantic Validity vs. Graphical Arrangement in Visualization Grammars
studi.s: Systems for modular, declarative and compositional specification for data visualizations, otherwise known as visualization grammars, often claim Wilkinson's Grammar of Graphics as motivation, inspiration or foundation. However, despite the shared intellectual lineage, visualization grammars can vary greatly in design scope and focus. In particular, systems that strongly adhere to domain-specific notions of correctness must trade-off expressivity for validity.

studi.t: Trade Tensions Meet the Gig Economy: Evidence from the 2025 Halving of Chinese Travel to Japan
studi.s: How do geopolitical shocks to services exports reach local labor markets? Using China's November 2025 Japan travel advisory and postings on Japan's largest spot-work platform, we provide the first such evidence for the gig economy. Posted hourly wages fall immediately and persistently in prefectures more dependent on Chinese visitors, relative to others, whereas postings, hours, and employment show no robust change. Wages fall more for early morning and daytime shifts, when hotels and shops hire, than for evening and night shifts.

studi.t: Towards wearable-scale, transition-aware sleep staging for clinical populations
studi.s: Automatic sleep staging models are predominantly developed on healthy sleepers and generalize poorly to clinical populations with fragmented sleep. Across three cohorts (patients with stroke, isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder, and other sleep disorders), we observe 2-3x more awakenings per hour, nearly twice as much N1, and less REM sleep than in healthy sleepers. We propose a label-efficient teacher-student framework for wearable-scale sleep staging.

studi.t: EE-Motion: An EEG-based Web Architecture for Live Affective Music Recommendation
studi.s: Music listening is intrinsically tied to emotion, which drifts continuously within a single session. Although modern browsers interface with wearable brain-computer interfaces, recommendation systems remain structured around discrete logs and lack the infrastructure to integrate continuous physiological signals. Furthermore, existing affect-aware models rely on static user profiles and offline training, failing to serve anonymous newcomers without model retraining. We present a web platform that resolves both challenges.

studi.t: Development of an HPLC Analytical Method Based on Large Language Models:A Case Study of the Eczema External Wash Formula
studi.s: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) formulas feature complex chemical compositions, and their HPLC quality control method development is time-consuming and experience-dependent. Large language models (LLMs) provide a promising strategy for intelligently assisting analytical method construction. Taking the Eczema External Wash Formula as the research object, this work constructed a human-machine collaborative workflow involving intelligent recommendation, experimental validation and iterative optimization for HPLC method development.

studi.t: A Unified Framework for Self-Recognition Across Monkeys, Infants, and Robots
studi.s: Self-recognition is a basic cognitive ability that indicates self-consciousness in humans. However, whether non-human agents such as monkeys and robots can possess a similar sense of self remains debated. Here, we develop a multi-scenario apparatus to examine self-recognition from different perspectives across macaque monkeys, human infants, and simulated robots.

studi.t: Emerging transient dynamics at finite observation scales
studi.s: Biogeochemical, ecological, and astronomical systems are transient. Yet, predicting dynamical shifts remains challenging because of inferential uncertainties in datasets and the limitations of asymptotic-dependent theories. To address this problem, we developed a theoretical framework that builds on the finite nature of observations.

studi.t: The key role of oxidation state and flake size in the ecotoxicological impact of industrial graphene oxide nanoflakes
studi.s: Graphene oxide (GO) is a widely used nanomaterial across various scientific and technological fields. Environmental exposure to GO and consequent ecotoxicological effects have been largely reported. Despite the significant efforts and illuminating conclusions, establishing fair pairwise correlations between material and toxicity descriptors remains challenging and controversial. Key drawbacks in GO ecotoxicological studies to date include a lack of standardized materials, poorly defined descriptors, and insufficient material variants.

studi.t: Distinct changes in brain and peripheral oxygen levels induced by synthetic opioids of the nitazene family
studi.s: Nitazenes are a category of synthetic opioids, some of which have high analgesic potential but also high toxicity, which has historically prevented their development as therapeutic drugs. Like fentanyl, nitazenes induce respiratory depression, a primary factor in their toxicity. Recently, a nitazene derivative called N-desethyl-fluornitrazene (DFNZ) was shown to have high analgesic properties with weak hypoxic effects.

studi.t: The activation-deactivation cycle of human PIEZO1
studi.s: PIEZO1 is a cation channel that is primarily activated through mechanical force, and activation has been shown to be influenced by membrane curvature. PIEZO1 is ubiquitously expressed and plays critical roles in various patho-/physiological processes such as inflammatory diseases or red blood cell volume regulation.

studi.t: Insulin signaling in pericytes is a master regulator of endocrine and vascular niches in pancreatic islets
studi.s: Insulin plays a crucial role in lowering glycemia, but it is also a powerful anabolic hormone with potent effects on the vasculature. Most studies on insulin vascular actions have focused on endothelial cells. Much less is known about its effects on the mural cells of the microvasculature known as pericytes. This gap in knowledge is particularly relevant for the pancreatic islet microvasculature which is exposed to high insulin levels and relies on local pericytes to efficiently deliver its glucoregulatory hormones.

studi.t: Cerebellar transcranial AC stimulation produces frequency and phase-dependent changes in Purkinje cell complex spike waveform
studi.s: Cerebellar transcranial alternating current stimulation (ctACS) can improve motor learning and may speed rehabilitation. The mechanisms by which ctACS induces long-term changes in brain function that underlie these effects are not known, and knowledge of them could greatly improve the application of ctACS. One potential mechanism is alteration of Purkinje cell (PC) complex spike (CS) activity, as CS activity is a key regulator of cerebellar synaptic plasticity. Thus, we investigated how ctACS modifies CS firing rates and waveform.

studi.t: Variable penetrance of schizophrenia in 22q11.2 deletion syndrome is associated with impaired, but reversible, neuronal mitophagy.
studi.s: The 22q11.2 deletion syndrome (22qDS) is a major genetic risk factor for schizophrenia (Sz). We found that iPSC-derived neurons (iNeurons) from 22qDS +Sz individuals exhibit weaker mitochondrial energetics, whereas iNeurons from individuals with the same deletion but no psychosis (22qDS -Sz) upregulate expression of mitochondrial biogenesis-related genes. Here, we investigated why the +Sz group fails to undergo this compensation, finding that 22qDS +Sz iNeurons have older and more depolarized mitochondria than 22qDS -Sz or controls.

studi.t: Early visual experience contributes to the calibration of higher-order body representations
studi.s: Higher-order body representations, including representations of body shape and size, play an important role in maintaining perceptual constancy in touch. However, whether the development of these representations depends on early visual experience remains unclear. Here, we investigated tactile distance perception in congenitally blind, late-blind, and sighted individuals. A given tactile distance is typically perceived as longer on the finger than on the forearm, reflecting distortions in cortical topography that is partially rescaled by higher-order representations of body size and shape.

studi.t: Partially shared representational space for vision and language across objects, scenes, and visual events
studi.s: Deep neural networks (DNNs) and behavioural similarity judgements of visual stimuli predict neural responses in visual cortex. Recent work shows that large language model (LLM) embeddings and similarity judgements of language descriptions also predict visual brain activity. These predictors were examined separately across modalities (vision vs language) and types (models vs human behaviour).

studi.t: Distal inhibition is recruited for action but not sensation in the primate superior colliculus
studi.s: Sensorimotor transformation requires neural circuits to coordinate excitation and inhibition, but how and whether this organization changes as the circuit transitions from processing sensation to action remain unresolved. We recorded laminar local field potentials across superior colliculus (SC) layers in four male macaques and computed current source density to resolve transmembrane currents during saccades to a target at one of eight isoradial directions. During the visual response, excitation was spatially confined to the receptive field, with little modulation at distant sites.

studi.t: Hormone therapy attenuates menopause-related impairments in motor cortical spike-timing-dependent plasticity
studi.s: The menopause marks the permanent cessation of menstruation via a decline in endogenous hormone production. This transition influences brain health, yet its effects on motor cortical excitability and spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP) are poorly understood. Across two sites, 46 females were categorised as pre-menopausal (PRE, age 28{+/-}7 years), perimenopausal (PERI, 50{+/-}3 years), post-menopausal (POST, 60{+/-}8 years), or combined continuous hormone therapy users (HT, 52{+/-}3 years).

studi.t: Chimeric antigen receptor T cell therapy targeting CD94 for cytotoxic T/NK cell malignancies
studi.s: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy against pan-B-cell antigens is highly effective, but analogous approaches for T-cell lymphomas risk prolonged T-cell aplasia. We developed a CAR-T therapy targeting a post-thymic antigen, CD94, a receptor with restricted expression in normal tissues and immune cells but enriched in cytotoxic T/NK-cell malignancies.

studi.t: Computational identification and in vitro evaluation of astragaloside II as an inhibitor of dengue virus NS1-induced endothelial hyperpermeability
studi.s: Background Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral disease in which severe cases are marked by leakage of plasma from blood vessels. The secreted nonstructural protein 1 (NS1) of dengue virus damages the endothelial barrier and is a drug target, but no approved antiviral exists. We aimed to identify compounds that target NS1 and to test whether the selected compound, astragaloside II (ASII), counteracts NS1-induced endothelial hyperpermeability.

studi.t: Long-term Epstein-Barr virus persistence in immunocompetent, primate-related Chinese tree shrews and inducible lytic reactivation in species-matched epithelial cultures
studi.s: Experimental models combining long-term Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection in immunocompetent animals with species-matched cellular systems for studying viral regulation remain limited. Chinese tree shrews combine evolutionary proximity to primates with small-animal practicality and native immunocompetence, offering a complementary nonrodent model. We serially monitored blood and oral specimens from six animals inoculated with Akata EBV. Five were followed for approximately two years, including two beyond two years, and the sixth underwent tissue collection at approximately six months.

studi.t: In vitro reduction of mineral oil hydrocarbons by Lacticaseibacillus casei DSM 20011
studi.s: Mineral oil hydrocarbons (MOH) are food contaminants of increasing concern due to their widespread occurrence in food and potential health risks. Although various physicochemical and biological strategies have been investigated to reduce chemical contaminants in food, the ability of lactic acid bacteria (LAB) to remove MOH has not previously been explored. The present study aimed to evaluate the in vitro removal of MOH by Lacticaseibacillus casei DSM 20011 under incubation 0for 4 h with shaking at 100 rpm. Following the screening of different LAB strains, L.

studi.t: TRIDENT (Taxonomic Resolution and IDentification using Environmental dNa Traces): An Optimized Algorithm for Vertebrate Taxonomic Assignments in eDNA Metabarcoding, Integrating Molecular, Taxonomic, and Ecological Criteria
studi.s: Environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding has become a powerful approach for large-scale biodiversity assessment, yet taxonomic assignment remains one of its most critical error-prone steps. Current bioinformatic pipelines rely on molecular similarity searches against reference databases, but assignment accuracy is constrained not only by short marker length and database incompleteness, but also by fundamental limitations, including recent species radiations, incomplete lineage sorting, introgression, NUMTs, and the imperfect correspondence between genetic variation and species boundaries.

studi.t: IFT20 mediates trafficking of ciliary proteins to support mammalian motile ciliogenesis in testicular efferent ductules and respiratory tract.
studi.s: Cilia are antenna-like organelles that extend from the apical cell membrane and are broadly present in eukaryotes. They are classified as primary and motile types; the later including sperm flagellum and somatic multiciliated cells present within the reproductive and respiratory systems. Intraflagellar transport (IFT) provides delivery of cargo for cilia assembly and maintenance.

studi.t: Artifact-guided restoration improves visualization of cellular ultrastructure in cryo-FIB-SEM volumes
studi.s: Cryogenic focused ion beam scanning electron microscopy (cryo-FIB-SEM) enables volumetric imaging of vitrified specimens, but charging artifacts, high noise and weak membrane contrast hinder the interpretation of biological features. Here we present a two-stage deep-learning-based framework that translates cryo-FIB-SEM images toward the domain of conventional room-temperature FIB-SEM (RT-FIB-SEM), suppressing large-scale charging artifacts and enhancing local membrane signal.

studi.t: Pleckstrin Homology-based proximity-labeling reveal lipid-associated interactomes
studi.s: Phosphoinositides (PIPs) organize membrane-associated signaling, but the proteins associated with specific PIPs and their regulation remain poorly characterized. Here, we establish a lipid-binding domain-based proximity-labeling approach to map PIP-associated proteomes in vivo, and applied it to plant cells. We identify distinct protein networks associated with PI4P and PI(4,5)P2, linking these lipids to membrane signaling, transport, and organization.

studi.t: Endogenous cAMP production within tissue fibroblasts is required for spontaneous fibrosis resolution
studi.s: Pathologic myofibroblasts (MFs) are pivotal effector cells in the development of persistent tissue fibrosis following parenchymal injury, and their activation and accumulation has been linked to a failure to phenotypically dedifferentiate and thus to resist apoptosis. The second messenger cyclic AMP (cAMP) has been shown to induce MF dedifferentiation and restore their sensitivity to apoptosis in vitro, but its endogenous role within MFs during fibrosis resolution in vivo has not been explored.

studi.t: Polarized Canine Liver Organoid Monolayers Capture Features of Western Diet-Induced Hepatic Metabolic Reprogramming Across Transcriptomic, Lipidomic, and Biogenic Amine Signatures
studi.s: Liver responses to Western-diet (WD) exposure remain incompletely defined, partly because conventional rodent models and immortalized hepatic cell lines incompletely recapitulate species-specific features of liver biology. Here, we established polarized epithelial monolayers from canine liver organoids derived from healthy beagles and beagles exposed to a WD for 8 weeks. We then used this platform to characterize diet-induced hepatic reprogramming and to explore differential responses to two SGLT2 inhibitors, dapagliflozin and bexagliflozin.

studi.t: COPS5 maintains spermatogenesis gene expression and piRNA-mediated transposon silencing
studi.s: COPS5 (CSN5/JAB1), a multifunctional subunit of the COP9 signalosome, is required for male germ cell survival, but how it acts is unclear. We combined a germ cell specific Cops5 conditional knockout (cKO) mouse model with transcriptomic, proteomic and small RNA analysis of P16 testes. Cops5 loss caused progressive spermatogenic arrest after postnatal day 16. At both the mRNA and protein levels, 59 genes were downregulated, including piRNA biogenesis factors such as PIWIL1/MIWI, PIWIL2/MILI, Tudor domain proteins, DDX4, MAEL and MOV10L1.

studi.t: Granger-causal inference to study crosstalk between two actin regulators in live cell imaging
studi.s: Dynamic actin filament assembly at the cell membrane drives cell migration. Its regulation is governed by functionally overlapping actin regulators and complex feedback loops that hinder conventional perturbation-approaches from dissecting actin regulatory pathways. Here we present an extended, perturbation-free statistical framework based on Granger causality (GC). The framework rests on statistical models that capture the interdependence among subcellular fluctuations of molecular and cell morphodynamic activities extracted from three-channel live-cell imaging.

studi.t: Re-evaluating donor-cell identity after hiPSC-RGC transplantation in mouse models of optic neuropathy
studi.s: Glaucoma is a neurodegenerative disease characterized by permanent visual field loss caused by the death of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs). Glaucoma is the leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide. We investigated the potential of transplanting human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived RGCs (hiPSC-RGCs) in two mouse models of optic nerve degeneration: N-Methyl-D-Aspartate (NMDA) and optic nerve crush (ONC), and characterized their ability to survive, integrate, and form synaptic connections in a degenerated retina.

studi.t: Cold acclimation and diapause independently improve egg cold tolerance and act through distinct mechanisms in the invasive mosquito Aedes albopictus
studi.s: 1. Phenotypic plasticity is an important mechanism by which organisms can cope with environmental change. However, there is growing recognition that phenotypic plasticity is not a single phenomenon but instead encompasses a range of responses that vary in reversibility and are predicted to evolve under different conditions. Nevertheless, few studies have disentangled the fitness effects and mechanisms of different forms of plasticity, making it difficult to predict their respective roles in promoting population persistence in the face of climate change. 2.

studi.t: Forecasting viral antigenic evolution from phylogenetic trees
studi.s: Forecasting the evolution of viral proteins can help inform pandemic preparedness and guide the development of interventions. Phylogenetic trees provide historical records of pathogen evolution, which are key for retrospective analysis, but using them to predict future genotypic changes remains challenging. We introduce antiGen, a machine learning model that learns from the evolutionary past of viruses to forecast the evolutionary future.

studi.t: Evaluating Temporal Genomic Data for Detecting and Characterizing Balancing Selection
studi.s: Balancing selection encompasses a diverse set of evolutionary mechanisms that maintain genetic polymorphism within populations. However, both detecting balancing selection and distinguishing among its underlying mechanisms remain challenging. Recent advances in the generation of temporal genetic data and the application of machine learning offer new opportunities to address these challenges.

studi.t: Phylogenetic insights into the origin of piroplasmid infection in endemic carnivores of Madagascar
studi.s: Piroplasmids (order Piroplasmida), including the genera Babesia, Theileria, and Cytauxzoon, are tick-borne protozoan parasites of medical, veterinary, and economic importance. Understanding the diversity and evolutionary history of piroplasmids infecting endangered wildlife can provide insights into their origins, natural hosts, and potential to cause severe disease. Using nuclear 18S rRNA and mitochondrial cytb gene sequences, we characterized piroplasmid parasites infecting wild carnivorans across two protected areas in Madagascar.

studi.t: Kin selection for cooperation in the honey bee microbiome
studi.s: Bacteria engage in many cooperative behaviours which provide benefits to other cells in the population. Lab experiments have suggested that these costly behaviours can be favoured by kin selection due to the benefits they provide to closely related cells. However, we know much less about the role of kin selection in natural populations. Here, we used two complementary methods to measure and compare kin selected signatures of cooperation in 19 species of bacteria found in the guts of honey bees.

studi.t: Shared characteristics establish Corynebacterium glutamicum ClpCP1P2 as a tractable model for mycobacterial orthologs
studi.s: Clp proteases are central to bacterial proteostasis, yet our biochemical understanding of actinobacterial Clp enzymes derives almost entirely from mycobacteria, where their essentiality complicates efforts to understand their physiological behavior. Here, we reconstitute and biochemically characterize the ClpCP1P2 protease from Corynebacterium glutamicum, a genetically tractable actinobacterium in which clpC and clpX are non-essential.

studi.t: Deep sequence-function mapping reveals computationally unpredictable epistatic trajectories that drive laboratory evolution
studi.s: The black-box nature of directed evolution has been constraining advances in enzyme engineering and the wider application of engineered biocatalysts. While conventional deep sequence-function mapping has delivered insights into sequence space architecture, it lacks the ability to analyse adaptive landscapes and fully grasp the long-term impact of epistasis on the accessibility of evolutionary trajectories.

studi.t: Discovery of cell-permeable inhibitors for human succinyl-CoA:glutarate-CoA transferase
studi.s: Glutaric Aciduria Type I (GA-1) is a recessive, serious neurometabolic disorder characterized by a build-up of toxic metabolites in the lysine metabolic pathway with no current pharmacological treatment. Previous mouse studies have shown that a deficiency in SUGCT attenuates the accumulation of some of these metabolites in vivo. These results highlight the potential for SUGCT as a therapeutic target in treating GA-1. We had previously identified biochemical inhibitors for SUGCT and had solved the crystal structure of the protein, both apo and bound to an inhibitor.

studi.t: De novo design of antiviral monobody binders
studi.s: Monobodies (Mobs) are a class of immunoglobulin (Ig)-like proteins that have emerged as promising therapeutic scaffolds for applications ranging from antiviral therapy to cancer treatment. Unlike conventional monoclonal antibodies (mAbs), Mobs can be readily expressed in Escherichia coli at high yields, offering important advantages in overall developability. However, discovering antigen-specific Mobs with high binding affinity traditionally requires screening large, randomized in vitro libraries.

studi.t: Programmable Imaging of Locus-Specific DNA Repair Dynamics Reveals Chromatin-Controlled Therapy Resistance in Cancer
studi.s: DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) pose a significant threat to genomic integrity, and their efficient repair is critical for cell survival. However, the spatial and temporal aspects of the repair process at specific genomic loci remain a mystery. To address this gap, we developed a novel live-cell imaging platform called Genomic Locus Imaging and DSB Repair Monitoring by Elastin-like Proteins (GLIDRE).

studi.t: QuickXL: An Open-source Ultraviolet Irradiation Device with Programmable Exposure and Active Cooling for Nucleic Acid Crosslinking
studi.s: Accessible and reproducible ultraviolet (UV) exposure is important for many chemical and biochemical applications. We describe an open-source laboratory irradiation device designed for psoralen-mediated RNA photocrosslinking, a valuable tool for nucleic acid structure determination. The device is based on 24 nominally 365-370 nm light-emitting diode modules arranged as two selectable 12-emitter series arrays with separate drivers. A Nano-compatible microcontroller, four pushbuttons and an OLED display provide user-programmable light-on and light-off intervals and an elapsed-time limit.

studi.t: Magnetic field-based actuator-sensor assembly for dynamic mechanical loading and functional analysis of engineered heart tissues in culture
studi.s: Cultured ex vivo and stem cell-derived cardiac tissues have emerged as promising tools for discovering mechanisms of human disease, for pharmacological testing and for elucidating mechanisms of genetic cardiac diseases. The current culture systems for these tissues do not fully recapitulate the mechanobiological environment of cardiac tissue or allow detailed characterization of muscle function in culture, which limits the interpretation of these models.

studi.t: Naïve Bayes taxonomic classification cost in QIIME 2 is set by the invocation rather than by sequencing depth or community richness at single-sample scale: a measured resource protocol for 16S rRNA pipelines
studi.s: Marker-gene amplicon workflows run on shared computing infrastructure, where cores, memory and wall time must be requested before a job starts. Those requests are set by convention, and the convention assumes a pipeline scales with the size of its data. For one of the two dominant stages, it does not. We measured a QIIME 2 16S rRNA workflow across nine upper-respiratory samples from a paediatric otitis media cohort.

studi.t: Joint Analysis of Common Regulatory and Rare Coding Variants for Improved Power in Kernel Association Tests
studi.s: Rare alleles arise from mutations on an existing haplotype background, yet current gene-based rare variant association tests treat low-frequency coding variants as effects independent of the common regulatory variants that surround them. The penetrance of rare coding variants can be modulated by the cis-regulatory landscape, and failing to account for this context limits the statistical power of existing methods for complex traits.

studi.t: OrthoSimulator: Empirically trained simulations for ground-truth benchmarking of orthology inference
studi.s: Orthology inference is foundational for comparative genomics, enabling the reconstruction of phylogenetic relationships and transfer of biological knowledge between species. Methods often infer different orthogroups and orthologous relationships, making robust benchmarking essential for evaluating their accuracy. Existing resources such as the Quest for Orthologs benchmark service and OrthoBench provide valuable benchmarks grounded in real biological data and expert curation.

studi.t: Survival-informed mutational network clustering reveals prognostic glioma architectures
studi.s: Cancer heterogeneity remains a major challenge for predicting patient outcomes. To address this challenge, we introduce SNOWS (Survival-iNfOrmed netWork cluStering), a probabilistic framework that integrates somatic mutations, clinical covariates and survival information to discover patient groups with distinct mutation patterns and survival profiles, using Bayesian networks to capture dependencies involving mutations and clinical variables.

studi.t: Integrating Unsupervised Clustering with Transformer-Based Models for De Novo Cell Population Identification
studi.s: Single-cell transcriptome sequencing has been widely applied across the life sciences. It enables accurate and robust identification of cell types in heterogeneous biological tissues through unsupervised clustering, shallow learning, and deep learning. While deep learning does not outperform shallow learning in classification performance, it streamlines cell type identification by eliminating cumbersome preprocessing procedures.

studi.t: Embodied schooling behavior via hydrodynamic interactions
studi.s: Collective animal behavior is commonly explained by sensory-mediated interactions among individuals, yet physical interactions between moving bodies and their environment may also contribute to coordination. In fish schooling, passive hydrodynamic interactions have long been proposed to facilitate collective organization, but biological evidence remains limited because their effects are difficult to disentangle from active sensorimotor responses.

studi.t: YAP1-2α-TAZ heterodimerization promotes BRD4-associated LLPS-like assembly at candidate super-enhancers and cancer cell malignancy
studi.s: YAP1 is a transcriptional coactivator expressed as multiple splice isoforms, but how individual isoforms specify malignant cell states remains unclear. Here, we identify YAP1-2 as an isoform that drives a distinct transcriptional state in cancer cells. The YAP1-2-TAZ heterodimer, together with TEAD, forms BRD4-associated nuclear assemblies with LLPS-like properties. These assemblies are enriched at candidate super-enhancer-associated regions and promote transcription.

studi.t: Estradiol Signaling in Regulatory T Cells Coordinates the Remodeling of the Maternal Small Intestine during Pregnancy
studi.s: Pregnancy requires coordinated maternal adaptations to support fetal growth, yet signals that couple gestation to intestinal remodeling remain poorly defined. Here, we show that pregnancy induces a reversible regenerative program in the small intestine characterized by villus elongation, increased nutrient transporter expression, and enhanced absorptive capacity driven by intestinal stem cell (ISC) hyperproliferation. Using single-cell transcriptomic and genetic approaches, we identify intestinal regulatory T (Treg) cells as required regulators of this remodeling.

studi.t: Scalable construction of near-wild-type brain atlases enables variability-aware neuronal identification in C. elegans
studi.s: Matching cells across individuals is essential for comparing cellular data but becomes challenging when cell positions vary between animals. Here we introduce a framework for constructing probabilistic neuronal atlases by integrating partially overlapping observations from sparsely labeled, near-wild-type strains to reconstruct cellular organization from incomplete observations.

studi.t: Restoring Marcenko-Pastur noise estimation and denoising of diffusion MRI under common image reconstruction
studi.s: Diffusion magnetic resonance imaging can reveal microstructure in the living brain, but the measurements are inherently noisy. Marcenko-Pastur denoising is a widely used remedy, helping to separate signal from noise under a simplified noise covariance model. However, we find that the model breaks under common image reconstructions across 28 public in vivo datasets, resulting in weaker denoising than intended. We restore the intended denoising behavior with a noise covariance model estimated from the reconstructed images, and validate the estimated model on repeated ex vivo and in vivo scans.

studi.t: "The self" as shifting coalitions of brain systems in a continuous configuration space
studi.s: Philosophers and psychologists distinguish many forms of self, yet neuroimaging results often implicate a shared core in the cortical midline or insula. We propose self-related processing arises from shifting coalitions of distributed brain systems, without a core. In a meta-analysis of 912 neuroimaging publications, titles and abstracts clustered into ten forms, including autobiographical memory, body ownership and interoception. No single location was significant in all ten associated brain maps, although each occupied different parts and amounts of midline and insular territory.

studi.t: Generalized hippocampal replay exhibits memory recall-like dynamics
studi.s: Hippocampal replay has been intensely studied for theorized roles in memory consolidation, credit assignment in reinforcement learning, and online planning. Much work in the field assumes that replayed trajectories traverse states smoothly and sequentially, in either forward or reverse order of experience. In a synthetic setting, we demonstrate that incorrect transition priors lead to systematic decoding error and show how model comparison addresses this issue.

studi.t: Transfer learning for identification of filamentous fungi using culture and microscopy images.
studi.s: Culture morphology and microscopy images are required for identification of moulds. Automated image classification is achievable in specific domains via transfer learning of pre-trained convolutional neural networks (CNNs). The study aimed to evaluate the classification accuracy of ResNet50 CNN, for image-based classification of seven commonly isolated filamentous fungi. A total of 15,400 images were collected from seven filamentous fungi. For each species, 1,100 images each were collected for two image modalities: culture front, and microscopy, resulting in 2,200 images per class.

studi.t: An Antibiotic-Treated Mouse Model Reveals the Progression of Intestinal Botulism
studi.s: Intestinal botulism, including infant botulism and adult intestinal toxemia botulism, is a life-threatening disease caused by intestinal infection with Clostridium botulinum (Cb) spores. Infants are particularly susceptible to Cb infection because of their immature gut microbiota, whereas healthy adults are generally protected by gut microbiota-mediated colonization resistance. Thus, immature gut microbiota or gut dysbiosis is thought to permit Cb colonization. However, the mechanisms underlying colonization resistance and disease progression remain poorly characterized.

studi.t: Electrostatic-hydrophobic cooperation in the mesoscale assembly of synapsin and synaptic vesicles
studi.s: Synapsin associates with synaptic vesicles. How these local contacts give rise to a connected vesicle assembly remains unclear. We used a three-dimensional Brownian agent model to vary electrostatic and hydrophobic interactions independently at fixed particle abundance and confinement. With electrostatics alone, the agents representing synapsin approached almost every vesicle early, when most vesicles still belonged to separate groups. With both interactions active, a larger connected assembly formed earlier, more of these agents were near several vesicles, and they moved more slowly.

studi.t: Co-transcriptional splicing of the Drosophila Y-loop A transcript is organized in chromatin hubs and shows variable delay which increases with spermatocyte maturation
studi.s: Splicing of the primary transcript is a major step to produce the mature mRNA. While the biochemistry of the splicing mechanism has been elucidated in detail, the dynamics and structural arrangements inside the nucleus are not clear. Biochemical and genomic studies of splicing and transcription most often lose the information about individual states and localization from the sub-nuclear to the tissue level by averaging over populations and homogenization of cells and tissues.

studi.t: Establishment and characterization of a brain cell line from bighead carp (Hypophthalmichthys nobilis)
studi.s: A wide range of pathogens continues to threaten bighead carp (Hypophthalmichthys nobilis) aquaculture. Fish cell lines allow host-pathogen interactions to be dissected and candidate control measures to be tested under defined conditions. We established and characterized the first brain-derived cell line from bighead carp, designated HnB, which is only the second cell line reported for this species. HnB cells exhibited stable proliferation in Dulbecco's Modified Eagle Medium (DMEM) containing 5-20% fetal bovine serum (FBS) at 28-32 degrees C and were serially passaged more than 50 times.

studi.t: Smooth muscle KCa3.1 limits plaque progression and alters plaque composition in mice
studi.s: Increased expression of KCa3.1 has been found in vascular smooth muscle cells (SMC), macrophages, and T cells in atherosclerotic lesions from humans and mice. While the efficacy of pharmacological inhibition and global silencing of KCa3.1 in limiting atherosclerosis has been demonstrated, the relative cell-specific contributions of KCa3.1 have not been determined. Therefore, we generated a smooth muscle (SMC) specific inducible KCa3.1-/- mouse with global Apoe-/- knockout (iSMKO) and assessed lesion development in the brachiocephalic artery (BCA) of tamoxifen vs.

studi.t: Centrosome identity drives asymmetric microtubule-dependent pushing forces, spindle positioning and daughter cell size
studi.s: Mitotic spindle positioning is essential for tissue architecture and organogenesis. In Drosophila neural stem cells, spindle positioning is attributed to apically enriched Dynein generating pulling forces on astral microtubules (MTs). Surprisingly, however, we find that the mitotic spindle consistently adopts a basal position along the apico-basal polarity axis, challenging the canonical model.

studi.t: Transit mortality and the efficiency of Tamarixia radiata releases against Diaphorina citri in metapopulation networks
studi.s: Augmentative releases of the parasitoid Tamarixia radiata are a main tool against Diaphorina citri, the vector of huanglongbing in citrus, but release models usually treat orchards as a single patch. We extended a four-compartment model of psyllid, flush, parasitoid and plant vigour with impulsive releases to networks of eight patches coupled by diffusion of psyllids and parasitoids, with optional transit mortality, and compared uniform releases with releases targeted at the outbreak patch. Without transit mortality the amount released dominated the outcome.

studi.t: Phylogenetic alpha and beta diversity of African ferns
studi.s: Ferns are widely distributed across nearly all major biomes and are indicators of ecosystem health and functioning. Therefore, their diversity and distributions can be used to elucidate the ecological and evolutionary mechanisms associated with net diversification and deep biogeographical events. Though Africa has relatively low fern species richness, the spatial patterns of fern diversity and distribution is non-random and may be indicative of the evolutionary history and paleo-ecological conditions that shape current floristic diversity on the continent.

studi.t: Language-Driven Clustering of Transfer, Persistence, Prevalence & Recovery Studies for Forensic Activity-Level Evaluation
studi.s: Transfer, Persistence, Prevalence, and Recovery (TPPR) data are essential for forensic activity level evaluations (ALE); however, concerns remain regarding the accessibility of relevant literature. This study investigated whether automated literature retrieval and natural language processing (NLP) methods could be used to identify and characterize TPPR studies. Existing forensic repositories were combined with records retrieved through the Web of Science Application Programming Interface (API) and enriched with bibliographic metadata, producing a corpus of 3,279 unique records.

studi.t: Human embryo-informed niche design enables defined bioprinting of undifferentiated hiPSCs
studi.s: Bioprinting undifferentiated human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) enables post-printing expansion and lineage specification within geometrically defined constructs, yet the biological cues required to sustain pluripotent cells in a printable 3D microenvironment remain poorly defined. To establish a biologically grounded design framework, we analyzed single-cell transcriptomes from 106 human embryos to identify niche factors associated with pluripotency maintenance.

studi.t: Circular-Arc Modal Migration for Ultrasound Imaging--Part II: Simulation and Experimental Evaluation in Compact Semicircular and Convex Arrays
studi.s: Circular-arc ultrasound imaging requires reconstruction that accounts for curvature and offset transmit sources across a wide field. This study evaluates how Circular-Arc Modal Migration (CAMM) changes point-response width, image-energy distribution, and low-echo target separation relative to delay-and-sum (DAS). CAMM combines angular modal analysis, local spectral remapping, and radial synthesis, with the offset phase evaluated through phase screens or approximated by scalar pullback.

studi.t: An apicomplexan-specific foundation model improves prediction of regulatory genomic signals in Plasmodium falciparum
studi.s: Genomic foundation models learn transferable sequence representations through self-supervision, yet their practical value is contested. In data-rich mammalian genomes, task-specific models trained from scratch can match or exceed pretrained models on many regulatory prediction tasks. Whether self-supervised pretraining provides an advantage in small, data-sparse genomes has not been directly tested. We address this in the compact, 23Mbp, A/T-rich genome of the malaria parasite, Plasmodium falciparum.

studi.t: Integrative analysis identifies LATS1 as a context-specific regulator of melanoma progression and immune response
studi.s: Malignant melanoma incidence is increasing, and survival remains poor following metastasis. The main driver oncogenes are BRAF and NRAS. Advancements in targeted agents and immunotherapies have improved survival rates, especially for patients with BRAF mutant melanoma. However, no targeted therapy options are available for patients with NRAS-mutant melanoma. Unfortunately, the development of resistance to all existing therapies remains a challenge. Recent evidence has shown that the MST2/Hippo pathway is deregulated in melanoma.

studi.t: A General Kinetic Model of Symporters Built on Cellular Homeostasis and Conformational Transitions
studi.s: General mathematical modeling of symport faces two fundamental challenges: (i) a unified kinetic description independent of protein-specific structural details; and (ii) quantitative cross-scale mapping between microscopic conformational transitions and macroscopic physiological observables. Grounded in the fundamental physiological principle of cellular homeostasis, we propose a unifying hypothesis for symporter gating: symporters actively regulate intracellular concentrations of specific solutes within thermodynamically feasible bounds.

studi.t: Dynamic multi-omics analysis of Adenovirus-induced rAAV-producing stable cell lines reveals the interplay between adenoviral infection and host cell metabolism
studi.s: Recombinant adeno-associated viruses (rAAV) are invaluable delivery vehicles for gene therapy. However, to make rAAV-based therapies more accessible, there is a need to increase rAAV titers. Here we analyze the phenotypic variation among 30 Adenovirus-induced stably-transfected human producer cell clones to identify metabolic signatures associated with high vs low rAAV production. Exometabolomic characterization revealed decreased amino acid consumption in higher producers.

studi.t: Non-canonical subthalamic nucleus projections regulate motor variability
studi.s: Regulation of motor variability is a key hallmark of motor skill learning, balancing motor exploration with optimization of identified task solutions. Nevertheless, the underlying circuit mechanisms in the mammalian brain remain largely unknown. Subnuclei of the dorsal striatum in the basal ganglia promote stereotyped or variable behavior, respectively, and deep brain stimulation of the downstream subthalamic nucleus (STN) can alter motor variability. We therefore tested whether the STN regulates motor variability via non-canonical projections to striatum.

studi.t: Selective Gut-Related Biomarker Profiles Define Parkinson Disease Trait and State
studi.s: Objective: Gut-brain-axis abnormalities are increasingly implicated in Parkinson disease (PD), but most studies examine individual biological compartments of this axis. We asked whether readily accessible stool and plasma-based biomarker profiles show broad or selective gut abnormalities in PD and whether the profiles associated with PD diagnosis (Trait) are the same as those associated with clinical severity (State). Methods: This cross-sectional study included 211 participants with PD and 204 healthy controls.

studi.t: Restrictive eating is linked to weaker recollection of food in young adults
studi.s: Affective significance often enhances episodic memory, with stronger effects on recollection than on familiarity, but prior research has focused primarily on within-person manipulations of emotional valence. Here, we tested a novel question: whether stable individual differences in the personal significance of food were associated with long-term memory across individuals, given that food ranges from highly appetitive to strongly avoided.

studi.t: Human placental stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles ameliorate loss of intestinal stem cell subtypes in experimental necrotizing enterocolitis
studi.s: Background: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is a devastating intestinal disease in premature infants with epithelial barrier disruption and loss of intestinal stem cells (ISCs). While depletion of active ISC (aISC) populations has been reported in NEC, the impact of NEC on reserve ISC (rISC) populations during early postnatal development remains poorly understood. We examined developmental and disease-associated changes in ISC subpopulations and evaluated the effects of human placental stem cell-derived extracellular vesicle (hPSC-EV) therapy on ISC preservation and recovery.

studi.t: Warming-induced sex bias underlies rapid recovery but may generate demographic imbalance in sea turtles
studi.s: Global warming threatens species with temperature-dependent sex determination (TSD) by increasing the risk of extreme offspring sex-ratio bias. In sea turtles, warmer incubation conditions produce more females. Such biases can transiently enhance population growth, while potentially generating demographic imbalance if male scarcity intensifies.

studi.t: Global indicators of climate-driven shifts in vertebrate assemblages
studi.s: We develop global indicators for tracking how species assemblages respond to climate change by estimating community climate indices based on species maximum temperature and minimum aridity niche limits. We applied them to global databases using 33.6 million occurrence records from the past half-century to track assemblage changes for 26,163 species of terrestrial vertebrates. Changes in community climate indices tracked climate changes, weakening at higher elevations and strengthening at higher latitudes.

studi.t: Population-aware computational assessment of base-editing accessibility among pathogenic variants on human chromosome 21: an African-ancestry-focused pilot study
studi.s: Background Population-aware gene-editing research requires independent evaluation of clinical variant evidence, ancestry-stratified allele observations, nucleotide correction chemistry, and sequence-level editing constraints. We developed a source-traceable chromosome 21 pilot connecting these dimensions without equating computational accessibility with therapeutic editability. Methods Reviewed ClinVar pathogenic/likely pathogenic single-nucleotide variants were matched by GRCh38 chromosome, position, REF and ALT to overall and African/African-American (AFR) gnomAD v4.1 exome allele counts.

studi.t: Sequencing of the Prnp-Prnd deletion junction in Prn-/- mouse tissues after formaldehyde fixation and >22 years at room temperature.
studi.s: In 2004, Nicolas Genoud and colleagues reported that deletion of Prnd, which encodes Doppel, prevented neurodegeneration in mice with extensive Prnp deletions. The work tested the proposal that abnormal Doppel expression in the brain caused cerebellar degeneration in mice lacking the cellular prion protein, PrP. Advances in automated image analysis have expanded scrutiny of published figures, and post-publication reviews have raised concerns about apparent figure manipulation in this work, calling its authenticity and reliability into question.

studi.t: SLIM-2PF: a miniature two-photon fiberscope for multi-depth neuroimaging in freely moving mice
studi.s: Miniaturized two-photon (2P) fiberscopes enable subcellular-resolution imaging of neural activity in freely moving rodents. However, integrating multi-depth scanning into such probes without compromising their high resolution and minimal mechanical load on the animal remains challenging. Here we report a subcellular-resolution, lightweight, multi-depth-scanning 2P fiberscope (SLIM-2PF).

studi.t: AptaRender: an interactive drawing and styling tool for 2D nucleic acid structures
studi.s: Two-dimensional (2D) diagrams are widely used to communicate nucleic acid secondary structure, yet the path from a sequence and pairing model to an editable publication figure often requires either specialized software or substantial cleanup in a general-purpose graphics editor. AptaRender (v2.3.1, available at https://yjhe99.github.io/aptarender/) is a browser-based editor that converts a set of user-supplied DNA or RNA sequences and their dot-bracket structures into an interactive 2D drawing.

studi.t: Development of Novel NPC1-Targeting Autophagy Inhibitors for the Treatment of Uveal Melanoma
studi.s: Background: Uveal melanoma (UM) is the most common primary intraocular malignancy in adults, and up to 50% of patients develop liver metastases. Metastatic UM responds poorly to conventional chemotherapy and currently available immunotherapies, highlighting the need for new therapeutic strategies. Because UM cells rely on lysosome-dependent stress-response pathways, including autophagy, we evaluated previously reported betulinic acid (BetA) derivatives and identified ALS-997 as a potent inhibitor of autophagic flux in UM cells.

studi.t: Nose-to-Brain Delivery of Cocaine in Mice: A Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetic Model Incorporating Olfactory Epithelial Transport, Mucociliary Clearance, and Blood-Brain Barrier Permeability
studi.s: Intranasal (IN) cocaine produces rapid central nervous system (CNS) effects despite generating substantially lower plasma concentrations than equivalent intravenous (IV) doses, suggesting a direct nose-to-brain pathway. The olfactory epithelium provides anatomical continuity for cocaine to pass between the nasal cavity and the brain.

studi.t: Genetic diversity, agroecosystems, and climate suitability of cacao in Panama: historical legacies and conservation priorities
studi.s: Theobroma cacao is a strategic resource for socioeconomic development and ancestral knowledge preservation in Panama. We integrated SNP genotyping, historical analysis, and climate suitability modeling to characterize the genetic resources of Panamanian cacao and inform future conservation priorities.

studi.t: Benchmarking temporal causal discovery for fully and partially observed biochemical kinetic models
studi.s: Accurately reconstructing networks of biochemical reactions is a crucial yet unsolved problem for leveraging advances in experimental techniques that track intracellular dynamics in a time-resolved fashion. This task is further challenged by the fact that we typically observe only part of the system, while many variables shaping the dynamics remain unobserved. Causal discovery methods can infer causal relations from purely observational data and account for unobserved variables.

studi.t: Cost-saving, trading, and internalization of externality: three economic strategies underlying amino acid archetypes of human metabolic enzymes
studi.s: Amino acid composition of proteome reflects principles of metabolic resource allocation. While amino acids with higher biosynthetic costs are used less frequently in the proteome of unicellular organisms, whether this pattern applies to complex multicellular life remains elusive. Here we show that amino acid composition of human metabolic enzymes does not follow a simple cost-minimizing mode but instead segregate into four distinct amino-acid composition modules each associated with specific metabolic functions, a phenomenon we term emergence of amino acid archetypes (AArchetypes).

studi.t: Preserved cognitive control with altered ventromedial prefrontal activity in lichen simplex chronicus: an fMRI study during the Multi-Source Interference Task.
studi.s: Lichen simplex chronicus (LSC) is a chronic pruritic skin condition, and one of its central features is the itch-scratch cycle. It has been hypothesized that resisting the urge to scratch, and thereby stopping this cycle, may depend on mechanisms of cognitive control. Here, we used the Multi-Source Interference Task (MSIT) during fMRI to examine whether patients with LSC (n = 9) differ from healthy controls (n = 11) in interference control or in the brain activity that supports it.

studi.t: Redox-driven control of 4-1BB interactome and signaling
studi.s: 4-1BB (CD137/TNFRSF9) is a major immunoregulatory receptor, yet the molecular principles governing its intracellular signaling remain unclear. Here we show that the conserved cytoplasmic cysteine residues of 4-1BB are critical determinants of its interactome, enabling redox-responsive engagement of TRAF2 and LANCL2.
